videos.t: Colonizing Mars
videos.s: Isaac Arthur's in-depth look at what it would take to settle and eventually terraform Mars. He covers the challenges and the scale of the work needed to make it a home for humanity.
videos.w: Recommended as a thorough, speculative-but-grounded overview of the magnitude of colonizing Mars.
videos.q: Highly recommended video on Colonizing Mars by Isaac Arthur

videos.t: The Gym of Life
videos.s: Not Just Bikes argues that people in walkable, bikeable Dutch cities stay healthy because exercise is built into daily life, which he calls the gym of life. It contrasts this with car-dependent cities that require deliberate workouts.
videos.w: HN recommends it whenever fitness, aging or cycling comes up, as the clearest statement that city design is the best public health investment.
videos.q: The best public investment to promote physical activity is designing cities to enable "the gym of life"!

videos.t: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160
videos.s: A roughly three-hour Lex Fridman podcast conversation with Brendan Eich, creator of JavaScript and co-founder of Mozilla and Brave. It covers JavaScript's rushed creation at Netscape, the browser wars, Firefox and Mozilla, and Brave's privacy approach.
videos.w: Linked as a source for first-hand JavaScript and Netscape history, with commenters pointing to specific segments like the Java versus JavaScript decision.
videos.q: a real gem of an interview, in my opinion

videos.t: Liberating Distributed Consensus - Heidi Howard
videos.s: Heidi Howard's Reactive Summit 2018 talk on generalizing Paxos by weakening its original requirements. She shows Paxos is one point on a broad spectrum of consensus approaches.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an illuminating, approachable explanation of distributed consensus.
videos.q: Heidi Howard is incredible and her work on distributed consensus is illuminating.

videos.t: Stanford Seminar - Google's Steve Yegge on GROK
videos.s: Steve Yegge's Stanford seminar on GROK, Google's internal large-scale, cross-language source code analysis system. It covers how the system helps with code search and understanding across Google's huge codebase.
videos.w: HN refers to it as the main public description of Google's internal code analysis tooling, and as a precursor of ideas like LSP.
videos.q: this talk by Steve Yegge was both entertaining and informative

videos.t: The medical test paradox, and redesigning Bayes' rule
videos.s: 3Blue1Brown explains why positive results on accurate medical tests are often false positives, and reframes Bayes' rule using likelihood ratios (Bayes factors) to update odds. It uses visual examples to make the reasoning intuitive.
videos.w: HN's go-to link whenever Bayesian reasoning, base rates or imperfect tests come up.
videos.q: is a brilliant introduction to the concept

videos.t: Rust's Journey to Async/Await
videos.s: Steve Klabnik walks through the history of Rust and how its design evolved toward async/await, including the alternatives tried and dropped. He also discusses the difficulty of adding a major feature to a language.
videos.w: HN points to it to show how deliberately the Rust team arrived at async/await and why it was chosen over alternatives like green threads.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: It will show you how meticulous the core team is and how long it took to arrive at this incredible, best in class design.

videos.t: Mike Mullane - Normalisation of deviance - IAFF - Part 1
videos.s: Astronaut Mike Mullane explains normalisation of deviance, where teams gradually come to accept violations of their own safety standards. He uses the Challenger shuttle disaster as the main case, drawing on NASA's ignored warnings before the launch. It is the first part of a talk given to a fire-fighters' association.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it whenever a thread involves ignored warnings, shortcuts or routine risk, as the clearest introduction to the concept.
videos.q: He describes how the Challenger shuttle disaster happened despite internal memos about the problem years prior.

videos.t: CppCon 2017: Louis Brandy “Curiously Recurring C++ Bugs at Facebook”
videos.s: Louis Brandy presents the most common and infamous recurring C++ bugs seen in Facebook's huge codebase, including shared_ptr data races and operator[] pitfalls. He explains the surprising complexity behind seemingly simple code.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a must-watch catalogue of C++ footguns, often cited in debates about Rust and C++ safety.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: is a great video that covers a lot of good stuff in particular this usability bug. It's worth watching in its entirety.

videos.t: Margin Call (9/9) Movie CLIP - It's Just Money (2011) HD
videos.s: A clip from the 2011 film Margin Call in which a firm's CEO, played by Jeremy Irons, tells a senior executive about the cycles of financial crashes. Kevin Spacey's character says he wants out, and the scene ends on the line that it is just money.
videos.w: HN shares it in bubble and crash threads as a memorable scene about market cycles and about information work versus physical labor.
videos.q: It's a great scene and line that's always stayed with me.

videos.t: 10 Things I Regret About Node.js - Ryan Dahl - JSConf EU
videos.s: Node.js creator Ryan Dahl discusses ten design mistakes he made in Node, including package.json, npm, and module resolution. The talk sets out the motivations behind his later project, Deno.
videos.w: HN treats it as the classic talk on why Deno exists and on lessons from design mistakes in a widely used platform.
videos.q: Ryan Dahl's great talk on design mistakes he made with node.js is something I think about all the time

videos.t: Pitfall Classic Postmortem With David Crane Panel at GDC 2011 (Atari 2600)
videos.s: David Crane, designer of Pitfall for the Atari 2600, gives a GDC 2011 postmortem on the game's design challenges. He covers how he fit a large world into the console's tiny memory. The session ends with Q&A.
videos.w: HN cites it for the story of how Pitfall's levels are generated procedurally from a seeded counter, within 4K of ROM.
videos.q: This is a great talk for those who love such things

videos.t: Matt Might - Winning the War on Error Solving the Halting Problem and Curing Cancer
videos.s: Matt Might's Curry On talk on ending errors in code, both software and the human genome. He covers conservative approximation of the halting problem via static analysis and a computational approach to precision medicine.
videos.w: Recommended as a jaw-dropping, must-see talk that gives an amazing intro to static analysis alongside Might's personal story.
videos.q: If you haven't seen it, Might's talk "Winning the War on Error: Solving the Halting Problem and Curing Cancer" is amazing, a must-see.

videos.t: Toybox vs BusyBox - Rob Landley, hobbyist
videos.s: Rob Landley compares Toybox and BusyBox and surveys options for embedded system command-line tools, including GNU. He also tells the story of leaving BusyBox, Toybox becoming Android's command line, and licensing.
videos.w: HN recommends it for the toybox intro and for Landley's candid account of software licensing and why he created the 0BSD license.
videos.q: A great talk on software licensing made by the creator of the 0BSD license

videos.t: Building Software Systems At Google and Lessons Learned
videos.s: Jeff Dean of Google describes his experiences building Google's systems and how its infrastructure evolved over time. The Stanford talk covers search, scaling tipping points and lessons from building large-scale software.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a classic look at systems engineering at Google, whose fundamentals have held up well despite its 2010 date.
videos.q: It's from 2010, but the fundamentals probably haven't changed.

videos.t: Why Air Quality Matters
videos.s: David Heinemeier Hansson explains what he learned about indoor air quality after his new house made his family sick. He covers CO2, VOCs, off-gassing, HVAC and ventilation, and cognitive effects, presented at a Basecamp meetup.
videos.w: HN points to it as a fascinating talk that convinced many to buy air quality monitors, with citations to studies.
videos.q: Fascinating talk, worth watching.

videos.t: E-paper hacking: fastest possible refresh rate
videos.s: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science explains how electrophoretic e-paper displays work and how he modified the driver firmware and waveform lookup tables of a 4.2-inch panel to reach roughly 3Hz partial refresh. It covers the tweakable constants in the refresh process and touches on colored e-ink microcapsules.
videos.w: Whenever e-ink refresh speed or driving waveforms come up, HN points to this as the clearest hands-on explanation of how these displays work and how to hack them.
videos.q: Here's a fascinating video on how these displays work, and how you can modify the firmware of the driver to get faster refresh rates

videos.t: Sid Meier's Psychology of Game Design
videos.s: Civilization creator Sid Meier's GDC 2010 talk on applying psychology to game design. He discusses player perception, randomness, and win states, and why designers must account for how players experience events.
videos.w: HN people cite it when discussing perceived randomness, luck and player experience in games, and say more designers should heed it.
videos.q: More people need to listen to what Sid Meier has said on this.

videos.t: Tested: Where Does The Tone Come From In An Electric Guitar?
videos.s: Guitarist Jim Lill methodically tests what in an electric guitar affects its tone, swapping parts on a partscaster and even trying a 2x4 body. He finds that wood and construction matter far less than people assume.
videos.w: Cited as a fun, experimental debunking of tonewood claims that shows electronics dominate electric guitar sound.
videos.q: I recently came across an excellent video where a guitarist tries to determine exactly which parts of an electric guitar affect its tone.

videos.t: How To Make Infrared Cooling Paint (Electricity Free Air Conditioning)
videos.s: NightHawkInLight shows how to make ultra-white radiative paint that cools surfaces below ambient temperature without electricity. He walks through the research papers and the household-materials process.
videos.w: HN points to it as a practical, well-researched DIY demonstration of passive radiative cooling.
videos.q: This YouTuber[0] does an excellent job recreating chemistry research from papers and improving on the techniques to be accomplished with household materials.

videos.t: James Burke Legend Connections 1 The Trigger Effect
videos.s: The first episode of James Burke's Connections series, 'The Trigger Effect', explores how modern society depends on interlinked technological systems and how quickly it breaks down when they fail, starting with a power blackout.
videos.w: Recommended whenever outages and cascading failures come up, as a classic on interdependent systems.
videos.q: You may enjoy the first episode of James Burke's Connections ("The Trigger Effect"), if you've not seen it.

videos.t: The Simple Essence of Automatic Differentiation - Conal Elliott
videos.s: Conal Elliott presents his paper on automatic differentiation, deriving a simple, generalized AD algorithm from a natural specification. Varying the representation of derivatives yields forward and reverse mode algorithms that avoid the complexity and statefulness of backpropagation.
videos.w: Cited as the more accessible companion to the paper, and as the most interesting treatment of AD via compiling to categories.
videos.q: There's a talk that Conal gives that makes the paper a bit more accessible

videos.t: Lone Star Ruby Conference 2010 Real Software Engineering by Glenn Vanderburg
videos.s: Glenn Vanderburg argues at Lone Star Ruby Conference 2010 that university-style software engineering does not work, and asks what real software engineering would look like. He revisits the waterfall model and what engineering means in other fields.
videos.w: HN recommends it for changing minds about whether programmers can be called engineers, and for its take on how waterfall was misread.
videos.q: I always thought calling programmers engineers was very weird until I watched this great talk

videos.t: The Functional Programmer's Toolkit - Scott Wlaschin
videos.s: Scott Wlaschin demystifies functional programming terms like monads, monoids, functors and catamorphisms by showing how they fit into a small toolkit. He applies them to problems such as missing data, list handling, and functional dependency injection.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the best beginner-friendly introduction to monoids, monads and other FP vocabulary.
videos.q: This was by far the best introduction to monoid, monads and few other functional programming terms.

videos.t: Is a Calorie a Calorie?  Processed Food, Experiment Gone Wrong
videos.s: Stanford Health Care hosts Christopher Gardner and Robert Lustig on whether all calories are equal, with a focus on processed food and sugar. The talk questions the idea that calories in versus calories out fully explains weight and health.
videos.w: HN points to Lustig's talk when arguing that processed food changes metabolism and that a simple calories in/out model is poor.
videos.q: Watch this video below to understand more

videos.t: GDC 2018: John McDonald (Valve) - Using Deep Learning to Combat Cheating in CSGO
videos.s: A GDC 2018 talk by Valve's John McDonald on VACNet, a deep learning system that analyzes CS:GO gameplay to detect cheaters. It covers how the model is trained on human-reviewed Overwatch cases and how its output feeds human moderation.
videos.w: HN points to it as the definitive example of server-side, behavioral, non-invasive anti-cheat using machine learning, often as a counterpoint to kernel-level anti-cheat.
videos.q: The actual presentation is worth listening to if you have the time.

videos.t: Understanding the Python GIL
videos.s: David Beazley's PyCon 2010 talk explains how the Python Global Interpreter Lock works and shows experiments where multithreaded code runs slower, even on more cores, due to lock contention and context-switching overhead.
videos.w: The canonical recommendation for understanding the GIL, praised both for its clarity and for how well it explains a deep technical topic.
videos.q: My favorite example is Beazley's GIL talk

videos.t: Humidifiers: Simpler is better?
videos.s: Technology Connections explains why humidity matters and compares the main types of humidifiers, including evaporative and ultrasonic designs. It covers how and why you would add moisture to indoor air.
videos.w: HN links it whenever humidifiers come up as the go-to explainer favoring simple evaporative designs over ultrasonic ones.
videos.q: Technology connections covers quite a bit of ground on various types of humidifiers and their up/downsides

videos.t: Vancouver Never Plays Itself
videos.s: A video essay from Every Frame a Painting about Vancouver, a major film production city that almost never appears onscreen as itself. It shows clips of films and TV shot there that pass the city off as somewhere else.
videos.w: HN points to it as a short, funny look at how cities stand in for other places on screen, and at the film industry's local effects.
videos.q: There's also a much shorter, funnier one called "Vancouver Never Plays Itself

videos.t: Talking Funny - HBO
videos.s: An HBO special in which Jerry Seinfeld, Chris Rock, Ricky Gervais and Louis CK discuss the craft of stand-up comedy. They talk about writing jokes, technique and how they handle old material.
videos.w: HN points to it as a rare look at how top comedians think about craft, motivation and process.
videos.q: is worth watching for anyone interested in that aspect of comedy

videos.t: Concurrency is not Parallelism by Rob Pike
videos.s: Rob Pike's Go talk distinguishing concurrency, the structuring of independent processes, from parallelism, their simultaneous execution. It uses Go channels and goroutines to illustrate.
videos.w: The standard link for explaining the concurrency versus parallelism distinction and the motivations behind Go's concurrency model.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: here's an excellent talk on the same subject by Rob Pike that I link all the time to people

videos.t: Dual Photography
videos.s: The SIGGRAPH 2005 demo of dual photography from Stanford, which swaps the roles of projector and camera to render a scene from the light's point of view. It includes the reveal of a hidden playing card.
videos.w: Cited whenever threads discuss recovering hidden images or non-line-of-sight imaging, as a clear demonstration of light transport.
videos.q: Skip ahead to 4:19 for a succinct demo.

videos.t: The Alt-Right Playbook: How to Radicalize a Normie
videos.s: A video essay from the Alt-Right Playbook series that explains how extremist movements draw ordinary people in, using deniable rhetoric, bad-faith games, and gradual escalation. It draws on books about the alt-right, male radicalization, and cult-style brainwashing.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it in moderation and politics threads as a clear account of why hard rules fail against dogwhistles and how isolated people get recruited.
videos.q: I think Innuendo Studios' video on this problem is one of the best explanations

videos.t: Primitive Technology: Tiled Roof Hut
videos.s: The Primitive Technology channel shows the construction of a tiled roof hut in the bush using only primitive tools and materials made in earlier videos. It includes tiles, a kiln, clay walls and underfloor heating.
videos.w: HN shares it as a mesmerizing example of building shelter and tools entirely from scratch.
videos.q: His videos are a great watch

videos.t: Thorium: An energy solution - THORIUM REMIX 2011
videos.s: A 2011 remix of over six hours of talks by Kirk Sorensen and other thorium advocates, explaining thorium as a nuclear fuel and the liquid-fluoride thorium reactor (LFTR). It argues LFTRs could produce energy without long-lived transuranic waste.
videos.w: HN users send it to anyone asking about thorium or molten salt reactors as a compact overview that answers common anti-nuclear objections.
videos.q: I highly recommend this video on liquid-fluoride thorium reactors (LFTR)

videos.t: dark matter is not a theory
videos.s: Physicist Angela Collier argues that dark matter is not a theory but a set of observations, covering rotation curves, the CMB and why modified gravity struggles to explain them.
videos.w: HN links it to correct the common misconception about dark matter and as a counterpoint to popular science coverage, though one commenter found it muddled.
videos.q: If you're interested in learning more I recommend you watch "dark matter is not a theory

videos.t: Explained: "Go Fast" UFO Video - Not Low and Not Fast - Like a Balloon!
videos.s: Mick West analyzes the Navy "Go Fast" UFO footage and shows with simple trigonometry and the data overlay that the object is slow and high up, consistent with a balloon. He explains how parallax makes it look fast and argues the original TV claims were wrong.
videos.w: HN commenters repeatedly cite it as a checkable, math-based debunking of the famous UFO clips whenever UAP stories come up.
videos.q: See for yourself. This is the most clear case of misidentification.

videos.t: The Power of belief -- mindset and success | Eduardo Briceno | TEDxManhattanBeach
videos.s: Eduardo Briceno gives a TEDx talk on mindset, contrasting fixed and growth views of ability. He argues that believing abilities can be developed encourages challenge, deliberate practice and grit.
videos.w: Recommended as a short, clear explanation of growth versus fixed mindset.
videos.q: I've found this TED talk the best explanation of growth vs. fixed mindset

videos.t: Debt Metaphor
videos.s: Ward Cunningham explains the history and intent of the debt metaphor, which he coined while refactoring the WyCash product. He says debt means code reflecting an incomplete understanding of the problem, not sloppy programming.
videos.w: HN links it as the authoritative correction to common misuse of the term technical debt, straight from its originator.
videos.q: For the best description of technical debt, you can't do better than listen to the man who first coined the term.

videos.t: Everything you think you know about addiction is wrong | Johann Hari | TED
videos.s: Johann Hari's TED talk arguing that addiction is driven largely by disconnection and environment rather than chemical hooks alone. He draws on his personal experience with addicted relatives and on research and policy examples from around the world.
videos.w: HN commenters quote it for the line that the opposite of addiction is connection, and recommend it as a more plausible account of addiction than the standard model.
videos.q: This is my favourite addiction talk.

videos.t: Civilizations at the End of Time: Black Hole Farming
videos.s: An Isaac Arthur episode on civilizations in the dark, post-stellar universe, including black hole farming, accretion disks and the Penrose process as energy sources.
videos.w: HN points to it for black hole energy and colonization ideas and recommends the whole channel.
videos.q: I highly recommend the whole channel.

videos.t: ASCII fluid dynamics -- IOCCC2012 endoh1.c
videos.s: A 3-minute demo of a tiny IOCCC 2012 winning C program that simulates fluid dynamics in an 80x25 terminal, using any text (including its own source) as input. The video shows the simulation running to Handel's Water Music.
videos.w: Commenters repeatedly point to it as an astonishing, beautiful piece of obfuscated-C code golf.
videos.q: truly a work of art

videos.t: RSA ANIMATE: Crises of Capitalism
videos.s: An RSA Animate video that illustrates a talk by geographer David Harvey on the crises of capitalism. It covers creative destruction, wage stagnation masked by credit, and the search for a more just economic order.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a quick animated introduction to Harvey's and Marx's critique of capitalism.
videos.q: Start out with this animated version of one of his talks

videos.t: Overpopulation – The Human Explosion Explained
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt explainer on why the human population exploded and why growth is slowing, drawing on Our World in Data. It argues that birth rates fall as countries develop, easing overpopulation fears.
videos.w: HN points to it in population, climate, and birth-rate threads as a clear, light-hearted overview of the demographic transition.
videos.q: Kurzgesagt has a good video on this

videos.t: Simulating an Entire Car Engine (yes, it makes noise)
videos.s: AngeTheGreat describes building a physically realistic internal combustion engine simulator in C++, drawing on fluid dynamics, physics and chemistry. It generates procedural audio for engines such as a V8.
videos.w: HN points to it as a standout example of physics-based sound synthesis and engine simulation.
videos.q: AngeTheGreat's incredible video series showing his engine simulator- absolutely worth checking out

videos.t: 34C3 -  Dude, you broke the Future!
videos.s: Charles Stross's 34C3 talk on how science fiction gets the future wrong. He argues that corporations are slow, human-powered AIs that optimize for profit, and that regulation lags behind accelerating technology.
videos.w: HN returns to it whenever corporations as paperclip-maximizer AIs or AI risk come up.
videos.q: I cannot recommend enough Charles Stross' 34C3 talk on this very topic.

videos.t: Electric car chargers aren't chargers at all – EVSE Explained
videos.s: Technology Connections explains that the so-called EV charger in an electric car's charging cable or wall unit is really an EVSE, a smart switch that safely delivers AC power. The actual charger is inside the car. The video covers the safety signaling and mechanisms involved.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the clearest introduction to what is inside an AC EV charging station and why it is much simpler than people assume.
videos.q: A quick intro into EVSE and why there is no power 'charger' in them

videos.t: Do Your Buses Get Stuck in Traffic? (The Downs-Thomson Paradox)
videos.s: Not Just Bikes explains the Downs-Thomson paradox using Amsterdam and Toronto: road widening doesn't fix congestion, and buses stuck in traffic make transit slow. It argues for giving transit its own priority infrastructure.
videos.w: HN points to it as a clear introduction to why widening roads fails and why transit-only lanes matter.
videos.q: NotJustBikes has a good introduction to it

videos.t: Identity 2.0 Keynote
videos.s: Dick Hardt's fast-paced OSCON keynote on Identity 2.0 and the move toward user-centric digital identity. It is also famous for its rapid-fire, many-slide presentation style.
videos.w: HN commenters hold it up as one of the most engaging tech talks ever given, both for its identity ideas and its slide technique.
videos.q: if you’ve never seen it, I encourage you to watch it

videos.t: Smelting Iron in Africa (A DEMONSTRATION)
videos.s: A 105-minute film of a West African smith family in Burkina Faso smelting iron from ore, from making charcoal and building the kiln to forging tools. It is a cultural recreation filmed for the camera, not current practice.
videos.w: Recommended as an amazing documentary of traditional ironmaking, often used as a baseline for the labor required.
videos.q: One of my favorite videos is a documentary of a village in Africa that goes through the process of producing iron tools from scratch

videos.t: LSTM is dead. Long Live Transformers!
videos.s: Leo Dirac explains how transformer models have replaced LSTMs in NLP. He gives background from bag of words through RNNs and LSTMs, then a technical deep dive into multi-headed self-attention and positional encoding, with sample code.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear explanation of why RNNs fall short and how transformers solve it.
videos.q: has gotten tons of compliments and keeps people watching year after year

videos.t: RustLatam 2019 - Without Boats: Zero-Cost Async IO
videos.s: Without Boats, a Rust language team member, explains the design of Rust's async/await at RustLatam 2019. He covers the history and constraints behind zero-cost, allocation-free async state machines.
videos.w: Recommended during the await syntax debates for explaining the constraints that shaped Rust's async design.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: I really loved this talk by Without Boats

videos.t: Britain peak power demand (from BBC TV series: Britain from Above)
videos.s: A clip from the BBC series Britain from Above showing UK peak power demand. It shows a grid engineer preparing for the surge as millions put the kettle on when a popular show ends.
videos.w: HN cites it as the canonical illustration of TV pickup and grid balancing, and as a must-see example of demand spikes.
videos.q: Here's a great movie illustrating how the grid is balanced

videos.t: Atari's Quadrascan Explained
videos.s: Retro Game Mechanics Explained dissects how Atari's Quadrascan vector displays and vector generator hardware drew games like Asteroids and Tempest.
videos.w: Recommended whenever Atari vector games come up as an excellent, deep technical explanation of how they worked.
videos.q: There’s an excellent video by Retro Game Mechanics Explained on how they work

videos.t: Democrats Need to Face Why Trump Won | The Ezra Klein Show
videos.s: Ezra Klein interviews Democratic pollster David Shor, who walks through survey data and charts explaining the 2024 election results. They discuss voter shifts, the education divide and what Democrats got wrong.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a data-driven explanation of the 2024 election and voter trends.
videos.q: I highly recommend this interview between Ezra Klein and Democrat strategist David Shor

videos.t: Copyright: How It Went Wrong
videos.s: CGP Grey's five-minute animated explainer on how copyright terms grew from 14 years to life plus decades. It uses Disney and Star Wars examples to argue the system has gone wrong.
videos.w: HN shares it as a short summary of why copyright length matters and the history of Disney-driven term extensions.
videos.q: CGP Grey also did a fantastic video on the history of copyright and Disney's constant involvement.

videos.t: Herbert Wolverson - Procedural Map Generation Techniques
videos.s: Herbert Wolverson's Roguelike Celebration 2020 talk surveying procedural map generation techniques, including integration of hand-crafted prefabs and vaults.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a fun, informative survey of easy-to-implement dungeon generation methods from the author of the Rust roguelike tutorial.
videos.q: My favorite from that collection on map generation is by Herbert Wolverson

videos.t: Surviving in the Siberian Wilderness for 70 Years (Full Length)
videos.s: A VICE documentary that visits Agafia Lykova, last surviving member of the Lykov family of Old Believers who fled into the Siberian taiga in 1936. It shows how she lives in remote isolation and the outside world encroaching on it.
videos.w: It is linked in threads about the Lykov family as an on-location look at the environment they survived in.
videos.q: I highly recommend it for anyone interested.

videos.t: If Brains are Computers, Who Designs the Software? - with Daniel Dennett
videos.s: Daniel Dennett's Royal Institution lecture on whether the brain is a computer and where its software comes from. He argues that minds are built by evolution and culture, with competence arising without comprehension.
videos.w: Cited as an excellent entry point to Dennett's thinking on minds, memes and competence without comprehension.
videos.q: I discovered him with the excellent Royal Institution talk

videos.t: We Hacked Flock Safety Cameras in under 30 Seconds. 🫥
videos.s: Benn Jordan details security vulnerabilities in Flock Safety license-plate-reading cameras and how easily they can be compromised. It includes citations from security researchers and discussion of police surveillance.
videos.w: HN recommends it, and Jordan's wider Flock series, as a well-documented look at the poor security of these surveillance cameras.
videos.q: This is an excellent video documenting some Flock camera vulnerabilities by Benn Jordan

videos.t: The effects of DBS on the motor symptoms of Parkinson's Disease
videos.s: Andrew, diagnosed with early onset Parkinson's at 35, shows how deep brain stimulation surgery has controlled his motor symptoms. The short video shows his tremors with the stimulator off and on.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a dramatic, moving demonstration of what deep brain stimulation can do for tremors.
videos.q: You should see this video to really understand how impressive dbs technology is.

videos.t: British Plugs Are Better Than All Other Plugs, And Here's Why
videos.s: Tom Scott explains the design of the British BS 1363 plug and socket, including fuses, shutters and safety features, and why he thinks it beats other plugs.
videos.w: HN treats it as the obligatory video to share whenever plugs and sockets come up, praised for its safety reasoning.
videos.q: There's the obligatory Tom Scott video here, which always gets shared, deservedly so

videos.t: The First Video Game
videos.s: An hour-long, carefully sourced video essay from Ahoy asking what counts as a video game and which one was truly first. It examines Tennis for Two, Spacewar, Pong, the Brown Box and a 1947 CRT device.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the thorough, well-researched answer to the first video game question.
videos.q: Here's an hour-long, meticulously sourced, rather thoughtful video on the question

videos.t: Alto System Project: Dan Ingalls demonstrates Smalltalk
videos.s: A roughly two-hour demonstration by Dan Ingalls of Smalltalk running on the Computer History Museum's restored Xerox Alto. It shows the integrated environment and language designed at Xerox PARC as personal dynamic media.
videos.w: Recommended as a vivid look at live, interactive programming environments and what Xerox PARC built on very limited hardware.
videos.q: have really been enjoying this two hour long interview / demo with Dan Ingalls on Smalltalk and the Alto

videos.t: e^(iπ) in 3.14 minutes, using dynamics | DE5
videos.s: A short 3Blue1Brown video explaining Euler's formula e^(i*pi) = -1 through dynamics, treating velocity as the thing that moves a point to a new position. It builds geometric intuition for why an exponent with i produces rotation.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a quick, visual way to understand Euler's identity.
videos.q: 3blue1brown explains it better than I could

videos.t: The Unfortunate Truth About Toyota's Hydrogen V8 Engine
videos.s: Engineering Explained examines Toyota's hydrogen-burning V8 engine built with Yamaha and explains the practical problems of hydrogen combustion vehicles. It covers efficiency, storage and distribution issues.
videos.w: HN uses it as the go-to explanation of why hydrogen internal combustion engines do not make sense.
videos.q: Here's a very factual explanation of why hydrogen internal combustion engines won't work

videos.t: [TAS] Pokémon Yellow - Arbitrary Code Execution
videos.s: A tool-assisted speedrun of Pokemon Yellow by MrWint that uses arbitrary code execution to push Game Boy hardware to its limits. Through crafted inputs it injects code and ends up running other programs, such as Tetris, inside the game.
videos.w: HN points to it as the standard demonstration of arbitrary code execution on a Game Boy, and of glitches and bugs being turned into a working computer.
videos.q: One of the crazier uses of ACE in Gameboy Pokemon games exploits

videos.t: The paradox of choice | Barry Schwartz | TED
videos.s: Psychologist Barry Schwartz argues in this TED talk that abundant choice makes people more paralyzed and dissatisfied rather than freer and happier.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the standard talk on how too many options lead to paralysis and second-guessing.
videos.q: My favourite TED talk pairing is Dan Gilbert's Surprising Science of Happiness

videos.t: George Carlin - Euphemisms
videos.s: A George Carlin stand-up bit on euphemisms, tracing how language gets softened, such as shell shock becoming PTSD, until it loses its emotional force.
videos.w: HN commenters reach for it whenever a thread involves corporate or political euphemism, using it mostly as a reference.
videos.q: George Carlin made this point brilliantly

videos.t: Carl Sagan testifying before Congress in 1985 on climate change
videos.s: Carl Sagan's December 1985 testimony to Congress on the greenhouse effect, about 15 minutes long. He lays out CO2 warming, the risk of runaway effects and the danger of continued coal burning.
videos.w: HN commenters use it as proof that the climate problem was clearly explained decades ago, and as a model of clear communication to a broad audience.
videos.q: The address Carl Sagan made in 1985 is well worth watching

videos.t: Turning Photons Into Food
videos.s: Dr. Bruce Bugbee walks through the calculations for crop yield potential when light is the limiting factor, from photosynthetic quantum yield through respiration efficiency and harvest index, using the Energy Cascade Model.
videos.w: Cited in vertical farming debates as a rigorous look at when indoor crops are economically viable.
videos.q: an extremely deep dive into the exact scientific measurements at which certain plant markets become viable at certain energy prices you will find this half hour very well spent

videos.t: Germany: Low Crime, Clean Prisons, Lessons for America | Jeff Rosen | TEDxMountainViewHighSchool
videos.s: Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen explains in a TEDx talk why Germany has lower crime and far fewer prisoners than the US, and what American criminal justice could learn from German prisons.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a comparison of German rehabilitative prisons with American retributive justice, backed by statistics.
videos.q: the whole talk is rather worthwhile to watch

videos.t: Learn Jacques Pépin's famous omelet techniques
videos.s: In this American Masters clip, Jacques Pepin shows two different techniques for making a perfect omelet, a dish he is famous for teaching America.
videos.w: HN people call it a favorite cooking video and a model of mastery, showing two omelet styles in about five minutes.
videos.q: I've watched this Jacques Pépin video countless times

videos.t: But what are Hamming codes? The origin of error correction
videos.s: 3Blue1Brown's discovery-oriented introduction to error correction codes, building up Hamming codes from the puzzle of locating a flipped bit. It explains the parity-check idea and why it is so efficient.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an invaluable, intuitive explanation of Hamming codes that pairs well with hardware-oriented treatments.
videos.q: I would strongly recommend anyone interested in the topic to check out any of these videos

videos.t: 29C3 Panel: Jesselyn Radack, Thomas Drake, William Binney on whistleblowing and surveillance
videos.s: A 29C3 panel with whistleblowers Jesselyn Radack, Thomas Drake and William Binney. They talk about what happens when exposing secret government power becomes a crime, and about surveillance abuses.
videos.w: Recommended as a first-hand account from NSA whistleblowers, often linked in surveillance and Snowden threads.
videos.q: You may be interested in watching this talk from 29c3 where Drake and Binney told their stories in their own words

videos.t: Mystery of Prince Rupert's Drop at 130,000 fps - Smarter Every Day 86
videos.s: Smarter Every Day films Prince Rupert's drops, tempered glass drops, in high-speed slow motion at 130,000 fps. It shows how the drop's heavy internal stress lets the head survive hits while the tail shatters the whole thing.
videos.w: Recommended across Prince Rupert's drop and glass threads for its striking high-speed footage.
videos.q: High speed video of one of these things exploding. Kinda blew my mind.

videos.t: Runaway Stabilizer!! How to stop MCAS.
videos.s: A Boeing 737 pilot explains the runaway stabilizer checklist, the procedure for stopping unwanted horizontal stabilizer movement such as an MCAS activation on the 737 MAX. He walks through the steps, the trim cutout switches and the jackscrew mechanism, and shows a simulator run including the manual trim wheel effort.
videos.w: During the 737 MAX crash coverage, HN commenters linked it as a clear, pilot-led demonstration of what an MCAS runaway looks like and how hard manual trim is to crank.
videos.q: I'd highly recommend anyone who wants to see what an MCAS runaway looks like

videos.t: Building Prototypes Dan Gelbart  part 1 of 18  Introduction
videos.s: First of an 18-part lecture series by engineer Dan Gelbart on building prototypes. The series covers practical mechanical design and fabrication of precision machines.
videos.w: Recommended as a gold-standard free course for anyone learning to build precision mechanical things.
videos.q: series by Dan Gelbart on YouTube which is pure gold

videos.t: Erlang: The Movie
videos.s: A short Ericsson film demoing Erlang, showing concurrent processes, debugging tools, and hot code reloading, including crashing parts of a running system while calls continue.
videos.w: A beloved classic that HN recommends as the quickest way to see why Erlang is special.
videos.q: the designers of Erlang demo some of the qualities of the Erlang system in a delightful way

videos.t: Who else benefits from the Dutch cycling infrastructure
videos.s: A short BicycleDutch episode showing how people with disabilities use Dutch cycle tracks on hand-cycles, tricycles and mobility scooters.
videos.w: HN cites it to show that cycling infrastructure also serves disabled and mobility-impaired people.
videos.q: Bike infrastructure is not only for bicycles: its for trikes, wheelchairs, mobility scooters, ebikes.

videos.t: Missing Teen's Friends Go On TV To Plead For Her Release, Gossip About Ugly Classmates
videos.s: An Onion News Network sketch in which two teenage girls appear on TV to plead for their kidnapped friend's release, then start gossiping about classmates. It is a satirical parody of teen behavior and sensational news.
videos.w: HN commenters call it one of the best and funniest Onion News Network videos and a sharp parody of teen girls.
videos.q: this parody made by The Onion is the best depiction I've ever seen

videos.t: Milton Friedman - The Real World Effects Of Unions
videos.s: An 11-minute clip of Milton Friedman explaining the incentives of unions and how they affect employment. He argues unions restrict labor supply, raising pay for some workers while hurting low-skill workers.
videos.w: HN commenters share it in union threads as a concise statement of the free-market economist's case against unions.
videos.q: Great short explanation from Milton Friedman

videos.t: Raft lecture (Raft user study)
videos.s: John Ousterhout lectures on the Raft consensus algorithm, made for the Raft user study comparing how students learn Raft and Paxos. It covers leader election and log repair.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a clearer introduction to Raft than the paper and as part of a well-designed understandability study.
videos.q: The 2 videos do an excellent job of explaining both the Paxos and Raft algorithms and the key differences between them.

videos.t: Jorge Luis Borges: This Craft of Verse Lectures - thepostarchive
videos.s: The six Norton Lectures Jorge Luis Borges gave in 1967-68, titled This Craft of Verse, on topics including the riddle of poetry, metaphor, storytelling, translation and a poet's creed. The recording runs over four hours.
videos.w: Strongly recommended as under-appreciated lectures showing Borges' erudition, delivered in a hypnotic voice from memory.
videos.q: These lectures by Borges are seriously under-appreciated

videos.t: ElixirConf 2018 - Keynote - Chris McCord
videos.s: Chris McCord's ElixirConf 2018 keynote introduces Phoenix LiveView, which renders HTML on the server and updates the page over websockets. It includes a demo showing that latency is not the bottleneck one might expect.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the original LiveView announcement and demo, a compelling argument for server-side rendering as an alternative to JavaScript front ends.
videos.q: you can't ignore it, the coolest thing happening right now about server-side rendering

videos.t: How to tie your shoes | Terry Moore
videos.s: Terry Moore's three-minute TED talk showing a better way to tie shoes, replacing the common granny knot with a square knot so laces stay tied.
videos.w: Recommended as a tiny, useful life hack many commenters adopted for good.
videos.q: You are probably tying a granny knot instead of a square knot.

videos.t: John Hughes - Testing the Hard Stuff and Staying Sane
videos.s: John Hughes, co-creator of QuickCheck, talks about property-based testing of hard systems. He shows production examples where it found very low-level bugs, including issues in the CAN bus standard.
videos.w: Recommended as the best introduction to property-based testing and cited for its examples of bugs found in the CAN standard.
videos.q: John Hughes (not the filmmaker) gives a great talk about it

videos.t: Dr. Jason Fung - 'The Aetiology of Obesity'
videos.s: Dr. Jason Fung, a nephrologist, presents his view of the causes of obesity and type 2 diabetes, focusing on hormones such as insulin rather than calories alone. The talk draws on research and his Intensive Dietary Management program.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a research-heavy introduction to how food type and hormones affect fat storage.
videos.q: Here's a good talk by a doctor, heavy on research, that's a decent introduction

videos.t: Your Mass is NOT From the Higgs Boson
videos.s: Veritasium explains that the Higgs boson accounts for only a small fraction of everyday mass. Most of a proton's mass comes from the energy of the gluon field binding its quarks.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear explanation of where mass actually comes from.
videos.q: This video explains where the mass of a proton comes from

videos.t: How to Understand What Black Holes Look Like
videos.s: Veritasium explains what a black hole should look like, using J.P. Luminet's 1979 work and a cardboard 3D model to show how light bends around it. It was made just as the first black hole image was released.
videos.w: Recommended for correctly predicting the features of the real black hole image and clearly explaining the lensing physics behind it.
videos.q: Good video that correctly predicted the image and describes why it looks the way it does

videos.t: Practical Creativity
videos.s: Raph Koster's 2014 GDC Next talk on what science says about creativity, with practical steps game designers and developers can use to be more creative. It frames creativity as applying existing patterns in new contexts.
videos.w: Recommended even to people outside game development as a useful, practical perspective on how creativity works.
videos.q: I recommend his 2014 GDC talk, "Practical Creativity" [1], even to developers who are not interested in game development.

videos.t: Blockchain 101 - A Visual Demo
videos.s: Anders Brownworth gives a basic visual introduction to blockchain using an interactive web demo, covering SHA256 hashes, blocks, chains, distribution, tokens and coinbase transactions.
videos.w: HN repeatedly recommends it as the best ground-up, non-hype introduction for people who want to understand what a blockchain actually is.
videos.q: It explains from ground up without getting complicated

videos.t: How to Find Product Market Fit - Stanford CS183F: Startup School
videos.s: Segment co-founder and CEO Peter Reinhardt recounts how his company found product-market fit, including how a product grew out of a small feature of another. It is a lecture from Stanford's Startup School course.
videos.w: HN founders recommend it as a must-watch on recognizing real product-market fit and avoiding solutions in search of problems.
videos.q: Peter Reinhardt from Segment has a must-watch talk for anyone interested in this topic

videos.t: Black hole Firewalls - with Sean Carroll and Jennifer Ouellette
videos.s: A Royal Institution event with Sean Carroll and Jennifer Ouellette on what happens if you fall into a black hole, covering the firewall paradox, the information problem and the holographic principle.
videos.w: Recommended as a high-level but clear explanation of the black hole information paradox and competing theories, by a physicist known for making quantum mechanics approachable.
videos.q: explains the paradox and several different competing theories at a high level.

videos.t: APL demonstration 1975
videos.s: A 1975 live demonstration of the APL language by Imperial College professor Bob Spence, showing a REPL on a modified typewriter terminal and APL's appeal to non-programmers.
videos.w: Recommended as a charming, from-zero introduction to APL and a window into early interactive computing.
videos.q: I think this is a good youtube video for someone starting from zero

videos.t: Dr. Bill Harris on the Omega-3 Index: Increasing Omega-3 to Promote Longevity & Transform Health
videos.s: Rhonda Patrick interviews Dr. Bill Harris, co-inventor of the Omega-3 Index and author of more than 300 papers on fatty acids. They cover EPA and DHA dosing, fish oil studies such as REDUCE-IT, and how omega-3 levels relate to health and longevity.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a researcher-led answer on omega-3 dosing, with the takeaway that most people take too little.
videos.q: it's what the dose range is: we're all underdosing.

videos.t: Joe Armstrong - Keynote: The Forgotten Ideas in Computer Science - Code BEAM SF 2018
videos.s: Erlang co-creator Joe Armstrong's Code BEAM SF 2018 keynote revisits good ideas from the history of computing that were dropped, and asks which should be revived. It also touches on Erlang and Elixir.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as a reading list of historical CS ideas worth knowing, and as a favorite among Armstrong's talks, especially after his death.
videos.q: Ted has a knack for reframing things in ways that make the arbitrariness of certain historical decisions clear

videos.t: How is this Website so fast!?
videos.s: Wes Bos breaks down the techniques behind the McMaster-Carr website's speed: server-rendered HTML, prefetching, CDN and service worker caching, preloading, critical CSS and fixed-size images. He also notes its old-school jQuery and YUI JavaScript.
videos.w: HN points to it as the clearest frontend explanation of why McMaster-Carr feels so snappy, often contrasted with slow modern UIs.
videos.q: Here is Wes Bos taking a deeper dive into the intricacies of technologies used to accomplish this

videos.t: Equipment Review: Best Carbon-Steel Skillets (Can This One Pan Do It All?) & Our Testing Winner
videos.s: America's Test Kitchen tests eight carbon-steel skillets to find the best one, asking whether a single pan can replace stainless, cast iron and nonstick. It names a winner and covers how the pans perform.
videos.w: HN people link it as a solid explainer and review of carbon steel pans, and for seasoning guidance.
videos.q: This is a solid explainer on carbon steel pans

videos.t: Prof. Thomas Seyfried - 'Cancer as a Metabolic Disease: Implications for Novel Therapies'
videos.s: A lecture by Prof. Thomas Seyfried arguing that cancer is primarily a metabolic disease rather than a genetic one. It covers the Warburg effect, mitochondrial damage and implications for therapies.
videos.w: HN people recommend it for its interesting, if contested, theory of cancer's root cause, noting the content matters more than the delivery.
videos.q: This video [1] is worth a watch to learn a bit more about cancer as a metabolic disease.

videos.t: Consistent Technical Documents Using Emacs and Org Mode
videos.s: A demo of writing technical documents in Emacs Org mode using org-babel, so that code blocks and generated content stay consistent when things change. The author shares the demo files and his dotfiles.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a practical illustration of what Org mode and literate programming can do for documentation.
videos.q: I think does a pretty good job of illustrating the power of Org.

videos.t: The Ranks of Global Billionaires: Not All Billionaires Are Made Equal
videos.s: An Economics Explained video on the different kinds of billionaires, from founders to oligarchs. It explains how wealth is held in illiquid stock and why diversification is a problem for some.
videos.w: HN recommends it to explain why comparing billionaire net worth by share price is misleading.
videos.q: fyi youtube video of why these simplistic comparisons of "net worth" based on shares-times-stockprice is meaningless

videos.t: Municipal Violations: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on municipal violations. It shows how small fines and fees escalate for people who cannot pay and how private probation and ticket revenue can ruin lives.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a clear account of how minor infractions punish the poor.
videos.q: Even more relevant is his piece on municipal violations and how they can unfairly steamroll the poor with escalating fees.

videos.t: Breakthrough with Healing Chronic Pain | Howard Schubiner | Talks at Google
videos.s: Dr. Howard Schubiner presents his research that much chronic pain comes from learned neural pathways rather than structural damage, and outlines a treatment approach based on that view.
videos.w: Recommended to people with chronic pain, fatigue or RSI as a rigorous but balanced case that pain does not always mean injury.
videos.q: The author links to Schubiner's talk on chronic pain, which I heartily recommend as the right balance of rigor and tone

videos.t: THE NVIDIA AI GPU BLACK MARKET | Investigating Smuggling, Corruption, & Governments
videos.s: A Gamers Nexus investigative documentary on the black market for Nvidia AI GPUs, following smugglers, middlemen, and buyers, including reporting from China. It examines how export-restricted chips reach their users.
videos.w: HN recommends it as real on-the-ground reporting on how banned GPUs get into China despite export controls.
videos.q: Gamers Nexus has a good video where his team travelled to China and did some actual investigative journalism

videos.t: Hacking with Andrew and Brad: tip.golang.org
videos.s: A roughly hour-long live hacking session in which Go team members Andrew Gerrand and Brad Fitzpatrick write the new version of tip.golang.org, the site serving leading-edge Go documentation. It is unedited pair programming on a real Go project.
videos.w: HN people point to it as a rare chance to watch skilled developers write real code live, pair programming and explaining as they go.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: It's just something to watch the pros doing live coding.

videos.t: Four Dimensional Maths: Things to See and Hear in the Fourth Dimension - with Matt Parker
videos.s: Matt Parker gives a hands-on Royal Institution talk on how four-dimensional shapes appear in a 3D world, with props like straw frames, Mobius strips and a knitted hat. It is a playful general-audience tour of the fourth dimension.
videos.w: Recommended as an enjoyable, accessible talk for building intuition about higher dimensions.
videos.q: I love Matt Parker's take on the fourth dimension

videos.t: Nuclear Weapons: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: A Last Week Tonight segment on the US nuclear arsenal and how poorly it is maintained and secured. It covers weapons accidents, outdated launch protocols and security problems.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a funny but sobering overview of nuclear weapons safety failures.
videos.q: John Olivers episode on it is also amazing.

videos.t: From the DMZ Into the Hermit Kingdom - Inside North Korea (Part 1/3)
videos.s: Vice founder Shane Smith travels to North Korea, speaking with refugees in South Korea before crossing the DMZ. It is part one of a three-part documentary with rare on-the-ground footage.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a rare, eye-opening look inside North Korea, though one notes such tours are staged.
videos.q: Vice has a three-part 1-hour-total documentary on North Korea with footage from the country.

videos.t: Nina Kollars - Confessions of an Nespresso Money Mule - DEF CON 27 Conference
videos.s: At DEF CON 27, Nina Kollars tells how buying Nespresso capsules on eBay led her to investigate fraudsters reselling goods bought with stolen credit cards. She describes her non-technical tracking and reporting efforts.
videos.w: HN points to it as an entertaining and informative explanation of the economics of reshipping and stolen-card resale scams.
videos.q: here's an excellent defcon talk on what these some groups do

videos.t: Why the world population won’t exceed 11 billion | Hans Rosling | TGS.ORG
videos.s: Hans Rosling uses population statistics to explain why the world population will level off rather than grow without limit. He shows that falling child mortality and rising prosperity lead to smaller families.
videos.w: Offered as an approachable, data-driven rebuttal to Malthusian overpopulation fears.
videos.q: This video might be more approachable

videos.t: FailCon 2011 - Uber Case Study
videos.s: Travis Kalanick's talk at FailCon 2011 about his earlier failed startups, given as a case study before Uber's rise. It describes lessons from those ventures.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it for insight into Kalanick's background and how his past failures shaped his mindset at Uber.
videos.q: I would really recommend watching this talk[1] TK gave at Failcon back in 2011.

videos.t: Steve Jobs on privacy, Steve Jobs at the D8 Conference (Video)
videos.s: A short clip of Steve Jobs at the 2010 D8 conference, interviewed by Walt Mossberg, defining privacy as people knowing what they are signing up for, in plain English and repeatedly. The discussion centered on location data.
videos.w: HN reaches for it constantly as evidence of Apple's long-standing privacy stance and as a yardstick for judging Apple, Facebook and others.
videos.q: Privacy means people know what they’re signing up for. In plain English, and repeatedly.

videos.t: Fantastic Quaternions - Numberphile
videos.s: Numberphile's James Grime introduces quaternions, a type of number beyond the complex numbers, building up from real and complex numbers and explaining why they are useful.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the simplest, most approachable introduction to quaternions, useful for people working in games and robotics.
videos.q: Numberphile's explanation of Quaternions is the simplest I have seen so far

videos.t: DjangoCon 2022 | From React to htmx on a real-world SaaS product: we did it, and it's awesome!
videos.s: David Guillot describes how his team replaced a two-year-old React UI of their SaaS product with Django templates and htmx in a couple of months. The talk gives concrete indicators on code size, performance and team impact.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a real-world case study of moving from React to htmx, especially in threads on boring web development and HTML over the wire.
videos.q: This recent talk from Djangocon "React to htmx on a real-world SaaS product" might be of interest

videos.t: Self and Self: Whys and Wherefores
videos.s: David Ungar of IBM Research reflects at Stanford on the Self language project and argues the real legacy of ideas is the people. He covers its history, philosophy, successes and failures.
videos.w: HN points to it as the best account of what Self made possible and what its team went on to do.
videos.q: explains the history, philosophy, successes, and failures of the Self project

videos.t: A London Accent from the 14th to the 21st Centuries
videos.s: Linguist Simon Roper reconstructs how a London accent would have sounded from the 14th to the 21st centuries, reading passages in period pronunciation. It draws on the Cambridge History of the English Language.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a captivating, accessible tour of how English pronunciation changed, including the rise and fall of the rhotic r.
videos.q: for frankly enchanting 18 minutes of viewing

videos.t: Halide Talk
videos.s: Andrew Adams, a Halide developer, presents the Halide language for image processing and tensor computation. The talk explains the separation of algorithm from schedule with illustrated examples of parallelism, locality and redundancy tradeoffs.
videos.w: Recommended as the clearest explanation of Halide's ideas and of scheduling for performance.
videos.q: The best way to understand it is probably to watch the video, which is relatively long but explains things clearly

videos.t: Vienna's Radical Idea? Affordable Housing For All
videos.s: A Bloomberg mini-documentary on how Vienna keeps housing affordable through large-scale public and social housing. It presents the city as a model strategy for others.
videos.w: HN points to it in housing-cost threads as the standard example of government-built housing keeping rents down.
videos.q: if you supply at least some public housing, it can have an outsized ability to keep rents down

videos.t: Ron Pressler - Pull Push: Please stop polluting our imperative languages with pure concepts-Curry On
videos.s: Ron Pressler's Curry On 2015 talk arguing that imperative languages should not be polluted with pure functional concepts like monads. He favors simple blocking code over non-blocking styles.
videos.w: Recommended as the case for blocking code and virtual threads over monads and async/await.
videos.q: one of my recent favorite videos generally on this topic has been from Curry On conference

videos.t: Music Software & Interface Design: MuseScore
videos.s: Tantacrul gives a detailed UX and UI design review of the MuseScore 3 notation software and compares it with Sibelius. It examines visual appeal, navigation and notation quality.
videos.w: Cited as a funny, informative teardown of bad interface design, and for the story that MuseScore hired him as head of design afterward.
videos.q: I find it very entertaining yet still informative

videos.t: Think Different
videos.c: 英倫米高 Michael in England
videos.s: Apple's classic 'Think Different' commercial, a one-minute spot celebrating creative misfits and innovators. This upload is from 2006.
videos.w: Shared as an emotionally powerful example of great advertising, especially after Steve Jobs died.
videos.q: I must admit that after watching it just now I teared up a bit.

videos.t: Keynote: Begin...End?
videos.s: David Beazley's PyData Global 2021 keynote, an oral history of early scientific Python. He tells how Python ended up running on a Connection Machine supercomputer at Los Alamos.
videos.w: Cited in threads about Python's rise as a first-hand, entertaining account of why it won in scientific computing.
videos.q: I recommend one of the recent videos by Dave Beazly

videos.t: Louis C.K. Hates Cell Phones | CONAN on TBS
videos.s: Louis C.K. on Conan explains why he won't give his kids cell phones. He argues that phones keep people from sitting with sadness and being alone with their thoughts, and that kids lose empathy when they cannot see another person's reaction.
videos.w: Commenters bring it up in threads on phones, boredom, attention and children's screen use as a funny but resonant take.
videos.q: arrived at the same conclusion much more concisely nearly a decade ago

videos.t: James Baldwin vs William F Buckley: A legendary debate from 1965
videos.s: The 1965 Cambridge Union debate between James Baldwin and William F. Buckley on race, justice and history in America. Baldwin argues that the American dream came at the expense of Black Americans.
videos.w: Held up as a classic debate with a clear winner and Baldwin's powerful oratory, still relevant today.
videos.q: he mesmerises the audience by telling them what it's like to grow up black in America not even knowing you're black

videos.t: High Altitude Leadership | Chris Warner | Talks at Google
videos.s: Climber Chris Warner talks at Google about his book on high altitude leadership and the 2007 K2 expedition, where eighteen climbers summited and two died.
videos.w: Strongly recommended as a gripping hour on K2 and on leadership and summit fever in extreme conditions.
videos.q: I highly, highly recommend listening to Chris Warner's talk on summitting K2

videos.t: Benno Rice: The Tragedy of systemd -- BSDCan 2018
videos.s: Benno Rice's BSDCan 2018 talk on why systemd exists and what it got right and wrong. It traces the history of Unix init and why Linux distributions adopted it, while asking what the BSDs should learn.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a balanced, eloquent take on the systemd debate that even skeptics find persuasive.
videos.q: One of the better videos on this subject

videos.t: Mosquito trap DIY 8,000 mosquito kill reduce ZIKA DENGUE MALARIA MaxxAir Fan CO2
videos.s: A DIY demonstration of a fan-and-screen mosquito trap that uses carbonated water as a CO2 attractant. The creator reports catching about 8,000 mosquitoes in two nights.
videos.w: HN commenters point people to it as a cheap, simple, effective way to kill mosquitoes, and some report trying it successfully.
videos.q: attach a screen (or net) to a high powered fan and catch/kill insane amount of mosquitoes.

videos.t: TasBlock at AGDQ 2017: TASBot
videos.s: A recording of the TASBot block at Awesome Games Done Quick 2017, where a robot plays games via tool-assisted speedruns, including Super Mario 64 and Portal on an SNES via arbitrary code execution, and ending with a Twitch Plays segment. It showcases console exploits and creative hardware hacking.
videos.w: HN commenters rate it a great GDQ watch and point to its feats, such as streaming video and Skype through controller ports, as inspiring hacks.
videos.q: TASBot which always makes a great GDQ watch

videos.t: 2017 ACM PPoPP Keynote: It's Time for a New Old Language
videos.s: Guy Steele's PPoPP 2017 keynote surveying the history of computer science metanotation, including BNF, inference rules, and overline notation. He argues the field's notations are inconsistent and fragmented.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an excellent talk on notation problems, useful when reading papers or designing a new metalanguage.
videos.q: an excellent talk by Guy Steele that goes over issue of notation and balkanization

videos.t: The Problem with Solar Energy in Africa
videos.s: Real Engineering looks at why Africa's abundant solar potential is hard to turn into usable power, especially for Europe. It covers the transmission, infrastructure and economic obstacles, and the pivot from concentrated solar to photovoltaics.
videos.w: Linked whenever commenters ask whether Sahara solar could power Europe, as a clear explanation of why it is impractical.
videos.q: A very good video from Real Engineering explains that no, not really

videos.t: Why Adults Can't Develop Perfect Pitch
videos.s: Rick Beato argues that adults cannot develop true perfect pitch, which he ties to critical-period brain plasticity and language acquisition. He says it can only be developed in young children, and discusses the research behind this.
videos.w: HN points to it as the standard explanation of why perfect pitch is a childhood window, in threads about absolute pitch training.
videos.q: This video convinced me that adults cannot develop or train perfect pitch.

videos.t: Building a 6800 CPU on an FPGA with nMigen (part 1)
videos.s: The first part of Robert Baruch's series on building a 6800 CPU on an FPGA with nMigen, a Python-based hardware description language. It introduces the HDL while implementing a simpler 6800 core.
videos.w: HN recommends the series as a practical introduction to nMigen and formal verification for CPU design.
videos.q: I can only recommend these Youtube series, where nMigen is used to build a full 6800 CPU

videos.t: Giant Robot Project, Part 1
videos.s: The first installment of a hobbyist's video diary documenting his build of a giant walking spider-like vehicle. The footage is casual and self-shot, following the early stages of the project.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as the start of a gripping, wonder-inducing build saga by a prolific maker of ambitious mechanical projects.
videos.q: I'm afraid I've wrecked what's left of the work day as I follow the saga.

videos.t: How the Quantum Eraser Rewrites the Past | Space Time | PBS Digital Studios
videos.s: PBS Space Time explains the quantum eraser experiment, in which erasing which-path information appears to reverse causality in a double-slit setup. It discusses what this means for quantum mechanics.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a quick introduction to the quantum eraser and delayed choice weirdness, though one commenter notes later corrections to its framing.
videos.q: a quick video from space time for those being first introduced

videos.t: "What UNIX Cost Us" - Benno Rice (LCA 2020)
videos.s: Benno Rice's linux.conf.au 2020 talk asks whether UNIX was the best design we could have had. He looks at what alternatives existed, what was gained and lost, and what could be re-learned, including the limits of treating everything as a file.
videos.w: Recommended as an insightful and entertaining critique of UNIX design choices such as file descriptors and 'everything is a file'.
videos.q: Benno Rice is an insightful, energetic, witty, and just plain enjoyable tech speaker.

videos.t: Mark DiMarco: User Interface Algorithms [JSConf2014]
videos.s: A JSConf 2014 talk visually breaking down algorithms behind everyday UI patterns, such as dropdown menus that vanish when the mouse drifts and picking the nearest target to the cursor. It shows how these are implemented in JavaScript.
videos.w: HN links it whenever menu hover problems or nearest-to-pointer selection come up, and as proof algorithms matter in front-end work.
videos.q: Algorithms do play an important role as you can see in this great presentation

videos.t: Refterm v2 - Resource usage, binary splat, glyph sizing, and more
videos.s: Casey Muratori follows up his refterm proof-of-concept, a GPU-based terminal renderer, with a second part covering memory usage, glyph sizing and correct Unicode and VT handling. It is built to show that a terminal can be fast and correct without heroic effort.
videos.w: HN points to it as proof that a small, straightforward renderer can beat Windows Terminal on speed and memory, whenever software slowness comes up.
videos.q: Casey Muratori produced a highly correct Unicode renderer with correct VT code support. Watch the video

videos.t: Entanglement and Complexity: Gravity and Quantum Mechanics
videos.s: Leonard Susskind lectures at Stanford on how gravity and quantum information theory have merged into a new way of thinking about physics. He covers entanglement and complexity, with applications from black holes to strange metals and the foundations of quantum mechanics.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a clear, characteristically engaging Susskind lecture for people trying to grasp the entanglement and gravity connection.
videos.q: Mr.Susskind has a Stanford lecture on this topic detailing the physics in his own unique & awesome way

videos.t: RetroAhoy: The Secret of Monkey Island
videos.s: A roughly 75-minute video essay from Ahoy's RetroAhoy series on the making and history of The Secret of Monkey Island. It covers the small LucasArts team, the game's development and its sequel.
videos.w: Recommended as a well-made documentary-style history that gives context around the game and inspires replays.
videos.q: Do yourself a favor and watch this wonderful video essay historique on The Monkey Island series from Ahoy

videos.t: RailsConf 2014 - Keynote: Writing Software by David Heinemeier Hansson
videos.s: David Heinemeier Hansson's RailsConf 2014 keynote argues that programming is closer to writing than to science, with clear code produced by iterating through drafts. It prioritizes clarity and craft over technical superiority.
videos.w: HN points to it in discussions of programming as a creative craft and of how to write clear software.
videos.q: I really like this[1] talk from DHH on the subject

videos.t: PFAS: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on PFAS, the 'forever chemicals' linked to health problems. It covers their widespread use in products like nonstick coatings and repellent fabrics and the limits of regulation.
videos.w: HN points to it as a well-researched, accessible overview of PFAS in PFAS-related threads.
videos.q: he does his homework

videos.t: Did SARS-Cov-2 start in a Chinese lab?
videos.s: Science journalist potholer54 examines the claim that SARS-CoV-2 came from a Wuhan lab, tracing the sources behind it and the weaknesses in the evidence.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a methodical debunking of early lab-leak claims.
videos.q: Potholer54 did a rather methodical takedown

videos.t: "Turbo Encabulator" the Original
videos.s: The earliest filmed version of the Turbo Encabulator technical-jargon parody, shot in the late 1970s with narrator Bud Haggert. It deadpans a stream of meaningless engineering language.
videos.w: Used as the canonical reference for the jargon-parody trope, and as a joke whenever technobabble appears.
videos.q: Doug Zongker's presentation similarly instructs people how to make better presentations to peers by demonstrating what not to do

videos.t: 36C3 -  BahnMining - Pünktlichkeit ist eine Zier - english translation
videos.s: David Kriesel's 36C3 talk, in an English translation, analyzes a year of scraped Deutsche Bahn data covering every stop of every long-distance train in Germany. It explores delays and how punctuality is actually measured.
videos.w: HN brings it up in any thread about German or European rail as a data-driven, entertaining analysis of why trains are late.
videos.q: There was this really great talk on the Chaos Communication Congress some time back

videos.t: Salt: Are you getting Enough?   (More Sodium & Health)
videos.s: Joseph Everett argues, drawing on the book The Salt Fix, that most people benefit from more rather than less salt, and reviews studies on sodium, potassium and blood pressure.
videos.w: HN commenters use it as a source of study references suggesting standard low-salt advice may be too restrictive.
videos.q: This is a nice video discussing some studies that show that high levels of salt is significantly better if it comes with high levels of potassium

videos.t: De-fragmenting C++: Making Exceptions and RTTI More Affordable and Usable - Herb Sutter  CppCon 2019
videos.s: Herb Sutter's CppCon 2019 talk on the split in the C++ community over exceptions and RTTI. He proposes making exceptions cheaper and more usable, including a zero-overhead, Result-like design.
videos.w: Pointed to whenever C++ exception overhead, bans on exceptions or error-handling alternatives come up.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: I can really recommend this talk

videos.t: Literate Programming in the Large
videos.s: Timothy Daly, an original author of the Axiom computer algebra system, talks about turning a large Common Lisp codebase into a literate program. He argues code should be written as readable manuals, and the talk was given at Write the Docs 2013.
videos.w: HN recommends it in literate programming threads as a rare look at applying the idea to a huge, complex codebase, though some find it meandering.
videos.q: well worth watching: it talks about real, huge comolex systems, and how lp can help bring them back under control

videos.t: What Games Are Like For Someone Who Doesn't Play Games
videos.s: Razbuten has his wife, who has never played games, try a sampling of titles and shows where she struggles. It highlights unspoken game conventions that experienced players take for granted.
videos.w: HN uses it to illustrate learned literacy in game and software UX, and how unfamiliar conventions confuse newcomers.
videos.q: The video has a bunch of other interesting observations.

videos.t: Energy From Thorium: A Nuclear Waste Burning Liquid Salt Thorium Reactor
videos.s: Kirk Sorensen's Google Tech Talk on liquid-fluoride thorium reactors, a design that could burn nuclear waste and use thorium as fuel. It draws on Oak Ridge National Laboratory work from the 1950s and 60s.
videos.w: HN used it as the go-to introduction to LFTR and thorium reactor technology in energy threads.
videos.q: If you don't know about the LFTR, check out this talk by Kirk Sorensen

videos.t: The $200M Machine that Prints Microchips:  The EUV Photolithography System
videos.s: Branch Education's animated deep dive into ASML's EUV photolithography machine and how it prints nanometer-scale transistors onto chips. It covers the system's components and the process of chip manufacturing.
videos.w: HN sends people here as the most straightforward and detailed starting point for understanding EUV lithography.
videos.q: I highly recommend watching this video about lithography and the machine that makes it all possible

videos.t: Clockmaking - How To Make A Clock In The Home Machine Shop - Part 1 - Making The Clock Frames
videos.s: The first episode of Clickspring's series building a John Wilding skeleton clock from raw stock in a home machine shop. It covers making the frames along with the tools needed for the job.
videos.w: Recommended as an absorbing masterpiece of craftsmanship, often raised in threads about watches and clockmaking.
videos.q: It's also a masterpiece, just in a different medium

videos.t: Traffic Calming is Everywhere in the Netherlands
videos.s: Not Just Bikes shows how traffic calming is built into streets across the Netherlands, from city centres to villages. Street design naturally slows cars and makes roads safer.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it in road safety and pedestrian death threads as the practical alternative to US road design.
videos.q: Consider this video on Dutch traffic calming

videos.t: Lars Andersen: A new level of archery
videos.s: Archer Lars Andersen demonstrates fast, accurate shooting techniques he says he revived from historical art and texts, arguing Hollywood archery is not historical.
videos.w: Recommended as an entertaining example of rediscovered lost skills, though some commenters note it is contested.
videos.q: Lars Andersen taking archery to the next level by using forgotten skills he learned by looking at old art and various texts. Worth a watch!

videos.t: Om Next - David Nolen
videos.s: David Nolen presents Om Next, the redesign of the ClojureScript Om library, drawing on Relay, Netflix's JSONGraph and Datomic. He covers the tradeoffs in handling the client-server boundary over immutable data.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as the lead ClojureScript developer's own account of Om's evolution, one-way data flow and single-state design.
videos.q: David Nolen does a great job talking about the trade offs and the evolution of everything in this talk

videos.t: Michael Levin: Consciousness, Biology, Universal Mind, Emergence, Cancer Research
videos.s: Curt Jaimungal interviews biologist Michael Levin of Tufts about consciousness, bioelectricity, emergence, and cancer research. The conversation challenges reductionist views of life.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a fascinating, mind-expanding interview on bioelectricity and non-reductionist biology.
videos.q: This podcast will be a shocking experience for anyone who still holds reductionist views on life.

videos.t: Lecture 1 - How to Start a Startup (Sam Altman, Dustin Moskovitz)
videos.s: The opening lecture of the How to Start a Startup course at Stanford, with Sam Altman covering ideas and products and Dustin Moskovitz discussing why to start a startup.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend the series as timeless startup advice from strong speakers, and cite specific points from Altman and Moskovitz.
videos.q: Amazing set of speakers and pretty timeless advice for starting a startup

videos.t: DEF CON 29 - Richard Henderson - Old MacDonald Had a Barcode, E I E I CAR
videos.s: A DEF CON 29 talk by Richard Henderson about encoding the EICAR antivirus test string into QR codes and barcodes and scanning them at real systems. Many systems that do not expect such input misbehave or collapse, including a parking garage system.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an entertaining demonstration of how scanners and antivirus software fail on unexpected input.
videos.q: This guy put the EICAR test string into a barcode and started to scan it on various systems, with rather funny effects.

videos.t: Building Your Own Dynamic Language
videos.s: Ian Piumarta's 2007 Stanford EE380 lecture on building a dynamic programming environment from the ground up, from the Viewpoints Research Institute's work. It covers the design of a language and system with a recursive design, parsing through code generation, and the COLA architecture.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a way to understand what the VPRI group considers core, such as supporting any syntax on one JIT compiler and removing boundaries between application and interpreter.
videos.q: There's a talk by Ian Piumarta that tries to get to the core of what the VPRI guys feel is important.
