videos.q: He gives an incredible account of his time there in the lecture (and almost stand-up-comedy act)

videos.t: Why are British place names so hard to pronounce?
videos.s: The Map Men explain why British place names are so hard to pronounce, tracing it to layers of Viking, Anglo-Saxon, Celtic and Norman influence, with a pronunciation guide.
videos.w: Recommended as an entertaining, short explanation whenever British place names or their linguistic history come up.
videos.q: The Map Men on YouTube did a short (8min) video on why pronunciation is hard and a guide

videos.t: Google Wave Developer Preview at Google I/O 2009
videos.s: The Google I/O 2009 keynote introducing Google Wave, a real-time collaborative communication and document platform. It includes a long live demo and the developer preview announcement.
videos.w: HN returns to it as the original Wave pitch, both for its wow factor and as a case study in a hyped product that was later shut down.
videos.q: their demo exhibits a wow factor that is undeniable

videos.t: Flaw in the Enigma Code - Numberphile
videos.s: Numberphile's Dr James Grime explains the flaw in the Enigma machine, namely that a letter could never be encrypted to itself, and how that helped the Allies break the code. It touches on the Bombe and Alan Turing.
videos.w: HN points to it as a short, clear explanation of why Enigma was breakable and how search-space elimination works.
videos.q: Numberphile gives a nice, succinct explanation

videos.t: The Dark Side of Counter-Strike 2
videos.s: Coffeezilla's investigation into the Counter-Strike 2 skin gambling ecosystem, covering casino sites, influencers and esports teams that profit from it. It is part of a multi-part series on Valve's skin economy and its effects on young players.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an investigative look at CS skin gambling and the exploitation of minors.
videos.q: is well worth watching if you are interested in the subject

videos.t: RailsConf 2019 - Opening Keynote by David Heinemeier Hansson
videos.s: David Heinemeier Hansson's opening keynote at RailsConf 2019 argues against the expectation of payment for open source work, drawing on his experience releasing Rails. It also includes lighter asides about the industry.
videos.w: It is the go-to reference in debates about whether open source maintainers are owed compensation, and commenters say it is worth watching even for non-Rails developers.
videos.q: Even if you're not a Rails developer it's worth watching.

videos.t: J B  Rainsberger   Integrated Tests Are A Scam HD
videos.s: J. B. Rainsberger argues that large integrated tests are a scam: they are slow, fail opaquely, and give a false sense of coverage. He advocates focused collaboration and contract tests at boundaries instead.
videos.w: HN recommends it in testing-strategy debates as the classic case for fewer integration tests and more small, well-contracted unit tests.
videos.q: JBRainsberger has an nice talk on them [1].

videos.t: Practical Common Lisp
videos.s: Peter Seibel's 2006 Google TechTalk on Practical Common Lisp, framed by the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis and Paul Graham's Blub paradox. It shows Lisp features such as condition restarts and its generic-function object system.
videos.w: HN remembers it as the memorable explanation of restarts and multiple dispatch, referenced whenever those features come up.
videos.q: I will forever think of this talk by Peter Siebel

videos.t: Don't Be a Sucker
videos.s: A 1945 US Army educational film that dramatizes how demagogues use prejudice and scapegoating to divide people. It opens with fake wrestling matches and crooked gambling games to show how con artists work, then applies the lesson to racial and religious bigotry.
videos.w: HN commenters bring it up in political threads as a classic warning about divisive agitators and fascism, and suggest it be remade for each generation.
videos.q: long, but worth a watch sometime for anyone who hasn't seen it

videos.t: Can We Pull Back From The Brink? (Episode #207)
videos.s: A Sam Harris podcast episode from June 2020 on the protests and unrest after George Floyd's death, discussing racism and police violence in America in light of the available data.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a data-oriented discussion of race and police shootings.
videos.q: Sam Harris did an excellent podcast (in my opinion) touching on the topics you mentioned.

videos.t: Are Electric Planes Possible?
videos.s: Real Engineering analyzes whether electric planes are feasible, focusing on battery energy density limits compared with jet fuel. It concludes electric flight works mainly for short ranges.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of why batteries limit electric aviation.
videos.q: did a detailed analysis of the current operating limitations with electric planes

videos.t: [4k, 60 fps] San Francisco, a Trip down Market Street, April 14, 1906
videos.s: A neural-network upscaled 4K, 60 fps version of the 1906 film of a trip down Market Street in San Francisco, shot four days before the earthquake. It shows cable cars, horse carriages, early automobiles and pedestrians sharing the street.
videos.w: Cited in threads on cars, streets and urbanism as evidence of how mixed traffic worked before cars took over.
videos.q: You can see pedestrians, horse-drawn carriages, and early automobiles all "flowing" together.

videos.t: The Only Safe Phone Is One Even the Police Can't Unlock
videos.s: A five-minute CGP Grey explainer arguing that a phone is effectively an extension of your mind, and that any backdoor or master key into encrypted devices will inevitably be abused or leaked. It frames the encryption debate as locks that are either unbreakable or absent.
videos.w: HN commenters use it as a short, persuasive primer to send to non-technical people in debates over encryption backdoors and decryption legislation.
videos.q: CGP Grey offers an easily digestible 5-minute primer

videos.t: Introduction to LibrePCB A new, powerful and intuitive EDA tool for everyone
videos.s: Urban Bruhin, LibrePCB's main author, introduces the open-source EDA tool at FOSDEM 2018. He explains why he started it and how its library concepts differ from KiCAD.
videos.w: Linked by the author and others in LibrePCB threads as the best explanation of its design rationale.
videos.q: Here's a video from FOSDEM where Urban (the main author) explains why he started LibrePCB

videos.t: Expert to Expert: Rich Hickey and Brian Beckman - Inside Clojure
videos.s: A Channel 9 Going Deep interview in which Brian Beckman talks with Rich Hickey, creator of Clojure, about the language's design. It covers Clojure's persistent data structures, reference types and its approach to concurrency on the JVM.
videos.w: HN commenters call it a fantastic introduction to Clojure and the thinking behind its design.
videos.q: It's probably the best technical video I've ever watched on YouTube.

videos.t: VLT (Very Large Telescope) HD Timelapse Footage
videos.s: A timelapse compilation of the night sky above the Very Large Telescope at Paranal, Chile, using ESO photographers' footage set to music. It shows the stars wheeling overhead and the observatory at work.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as an awe-inspiring way to feel Earth's rotation and our place in space.
videos.q: the first time I really grasped that we're all together on a rock tumbling through the vastness of space

videos.t: Is This What Quantum Mechanics Looks Like?
videos.s: Veritasium shows silicone oil droplets bouncing on a vibrating bath, a physical analogue of pilot wave theory that reproduces quantum-like behavior such as double-slit patterns.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a short, intuitive introduction to the pilot wave (de Broglie-Bohm) interpretation of quantum mechanics.
videos.q: an excellent pilot wave (de Broglie-Bohm) theory video by Veritasium[1]

videos.t: Chase Adam at Startup School 2013
videos.s: Chase Adam, founder of the nonprofit Watsi, speaks at Startup School 2013 about building a nonprofit startup.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an excellent speech from Watsi's founder, especially on keeping a nonprofit aligned with the people it serves.
videos.q: Startup School presentation (which is excellent, BTW)

videos.t: Farbrausch - fr-041: debris. [HD]
videos.s: Debris by Farbrausch, the winner of the Breakpoint 2007 demo competition. All of its 3D visuals, textures and music come from a single 177 KB executable.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the demoscene showpiece to show someone what extreme size-limited real-time graphics look like.
videos.q: If you want to really show off the demoscene, try Farbrausch - fr-041.

videos.t: Anders Hejlsberg on Modern Compiler Construction
videos.s: Anders Hejlsberg whiteboards how compilers are taught versus how modern ones are actually built. He explains the shift to compilers as services with incremental, error-tolerant, IDE-oriented design, as in Roslyn and TypeScript.
videos.w: It is the standard reference for why modern compilers and language servers differ from textbook designs, cited in rust-analyzer and parsing threads.
videos.q: I really recommend this video from Anders Hejlsberg (creator of C# and TypeScript)

videos.t: Windows 8: The Animated Evaluation
videos.s: An animated, profane rant critiquing Windows 8, especially its touch-first interface on desktop PCs. The author draws on a background in tech journalism to lay out the UX problems.
videos.w: Linked in Windows 8 threads as a funny but accurate summary of its usability problems.
videos.q: I think this video explains most of the problems with Windows 8

videos.t: Macworld Boston 1997-The Microsoft Deal
videos.s: Footage from the Macworld Boston 1997 keynote where Steve Jobs announces Apple's deal with Microsoft, with Bill Gates appearing on the big screen. The almost bankrupt Apple took Microsoft's investment, and the crowd reacted badly, including booing over Internet Explorer as the default browser.
videos.w: HN returns to it as a legendary moment in tech history and as a precedent for strategic deals between rivals, such as in the Nokia and Microsoft story.
videos.q: the legendary video of Bill Gates appearing on the big screen at the Macworld Boston Keynote 1997

videos.t: Myopia: A Modern Yet Reversible Disease — Todd Becker, M.S. (AHS14)
videos.s: Todd Becker's Ancestral Health Symposium talk arguing that myopia is driven by near-work and can be reversed, covering the biology and epidemiology and experimental evidence for reversal by using weaker lenses.
videos.w: HN commenters credit it as a life-changing talk, with some reporting reduced prescriptions after following the method.
videos.q: I'm super thankful to have found out about this life-changing video by Todd Becker on how to reverse myopia

videos.t: How to: Work at Google — Example Coding/Engineering Interview
videos.s: Two Google engineers perform a mock coding interview and then discuss best practices for candidates, including asking clarifying questions and communicating while solving.
videos.w: Cited as a realistic, well-run example of a technical interview, both for candidates preparing and interviewers calibrating.
videos.q: two of the suggestions in this excellent video from Google showing an example of a great technical interview

videos.t: AT&T Archives: Saul Bass Pitch Video for Bell System Logo Redesign
videos.s: The 1969 pitch film in which Saul Bass presents the Bell System logo redesign to AT&T, part of the largest corporate re-identity program in U.S. history.
videos.w: HN holds it up as a masterclass in explaining and selling a design.
videos.q: I always go back to the Saul Bass presentation to AT&T over their 1970 logo redesign.

videos.t: Lower Latency Graph Queries in Cypher with Redis GraphRoi Lipman, Redis LabsTim Davis, Texas A&M U
videos.s: Redis Labs and Tim Davis present RedisGraph, which uses GraphBLAS to treat graph queries in Cypher as sparse linear algebra for lower latency.
videos.w: Recommended in graph database threads as a mind-blowing case for expressing graph analysis as linear algebra.
videos.q: I think you'll find this presentation on GraphBLAS positively mind-blowing

videos.t: Graham's Number - Numberphile
videos.s: Numberphile's Tony Padilla and Matt Parker discuss Graham's number, once the largest number used in a mathematical proof, and how enormous it is.
videos.w: Recommended as the mind-melting intro to unimaginably large numbers.
videos.q: It's a pretty interesting video for seeing how quickly the numbers get unimaginably massive.

videos.t: 2. Behavioral Evolution
videos.s: Stanford biologist Robert Sapolsky lectures on the evolution of behavior, including the Prisoner's Dilemma and tit-for-tat strategies in animals. It is part of his Human Behavioral Biology course.
videos.w: Recommended in game-theory and cooperation threads, with the whole lecture series endorsed.
videos.q: This entire lecture series on Human Behavioral Biology is worth watching from the beginning

videos.t: How Overnight Shipping Works
videos.s: Wendover Productions explains how overnight shipping works, covering the hub-and-spoke logistics of companies like FedEx and UPS and the use of cargo aircraft. It touches on the economics that make next-day delivery possible.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear, accessible explainer on logistics, overnight shipping and why old planes get used for cargo.
videos.q: is a good Youtube video that discusses how overnight shipping systems like Fedex etc. have works.

videos.t: [Epilepsy Warning] Choco Mountain: The History of Mario Kart 64's Most Infamous Track
videos.s: Summoning Salt traces the speedrunning history of Mario Kart 64's Choco Mountain track and its famous shortcut, through the successive record holders and discoveries. It carries an epilepsy warning for flickering lights.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a gripping entry point into speedrunning and as a model of a well-made history video.
videos.q: I didn't realize I cared about speed-running until I saw this YouTube video from Summoning Salt

videos.t: Half-Life 2: 20th Anniversary Documentary
videos.s: Valve's two-hour documentary for Half-Life 2's 20th anniversary, with team members discussing development, nearly running out of money, being hacked, the publisher lawsuit and the birth of Steam.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an excellent inside look at Valve's history, its technology and the games industry of the time.
videos.q: the excellent YouTube documentary Valve released for Half-Life 2's 20th Anniversary

videos.t: CppCon 2016: Chandler Carruth “Garbage In, Garbage Out: Arguing about Undefined Behavior..."
videos.s: Chandler Carruth's CppCon 2016 talk tries to defuse the heated debate over undefined behavior in C and C++. He explains from the compiler writer's perspective why UB exists and how it enables optimization.
videos.w: HN points to it whenever undefined behavior comes up, as the best explanation of the reasoning behind UB, though some dispute its framing.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: Chandler Carruth's talk on the subject was really useful for my own understanding of the reasoning behind UB

videos.t: The Deadliest Being on Planet Earth – The Bacteriophage
videos.s: An animated Kurzgesagt explainer on bacteriophages, viruses that kill bacteria, covering how they infect and burst cells and their potential as therapy against antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
videos.w: HN commenters link it whenever phage therapy or antibiotic resistance comes up, as an accessible overview.
videos.q: Relevant Kurzgesagt video explaining _everything_ about bacteriophage[1].

videos.t: Your Brain: Who's in Control? | Full Documentary | NOVA | PBS
videos.s: A NOVA documentary with neuroscientist Heather Berlin exploring the subconscious and what drives our decisions. It uses sleepwalking, anesthesia, improvised rap in an MRI and game theory to probe how much of the brain's work is hidden.
videos.w: Recommended in threads on consciousness, anesthesia and perception as a fascinating look at how much of experience the brain constructs.
videos.q: Both of these videos are great resources on how much of what you experience of reality is made up or filled in by your brain

videos.t: How Wolves Change Rivers
videos.s: George Monbiot narrates how reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone after about 70 years set off a trophic cascade. The wolves changed deer behavior, vegetation recovered, and rivers changed course.
videos.w: HN cites it as the go-to example of how one keystone species can reshape an entire ecosystem.
videos.q: You need to learn about trophic cascades. Here's a quick intro

videos.t: Numberphile v. Math: the truth about 1+2+3+...=-1/12
videos.s: Mathologer examines the infamous Numberphile claim that 1+2+3+... equals -1/12, explaining what is wrong with the calculation and how it connects to real math like the zeta function and analytic continuation.
videos.w: HN points to it as the in-depth rebuttal to the Numberphile video that explains why the 'proof' is wrong yet the result is meaningful.
videos.q: Mathologer did a fairly in-depth video[1] into why this proof is wrong

videos.t: KEYNOTE / Robert Erdmann
videos.s: Robert Erdmann, a materials scientist at the Rijksmuseum, gives a PyCon keynote on the ultra-high-resolution imaging of Rembrandt's Night Watch. He covers the automated gantry camera system, the Python software that drives it, and the large volumes of image data involved.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a technically jaw-dropping talk, and it is the standard reference whenever the Night Watch gigapixel images come up.
videos.q: This was the first talk I immediately felt the urge to share with multiple co-workers & friends.

videos.t: A Portal Special Presentation- Geometric Unity: A First Look
videos.s: Eric Weinstein's roughly three-hour presentation of Geometric Unity, his proposed theory unifying physics, given as a special episode of The Portal. It includes clarifications at the end.
videos.w: HN uses it as the primary source for Weinstein's theory, though some commenters note he never published a full math paper.
videos.q: his original lecture detailing the Geometric Unity model he discussed on Rogan

videos.t: Lin Clark - A Cartoon Intro to Fiber - React Conf 2017
videos.s: Lin Clark gives an illustrated, cartoon-style walkthrough of React Fiber, the rewrite of React's reconciler, explaining its incremental rendering and scheduling at React Conf 2017.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as the clearest explanation of how Fiber and React 16 work.
videos.q: ReactConf 2017 is excellent

videos.t: Nebraska retiree uses earths's heat to grow oranges in snow
videos.s: Kirsten Dirksen visits retired mailman Russ Finch in Alliance, Nebraska, who grows oranges, figs and pomegranates in a backyard greenhouse without paying for heat. The greenhouse uses the stable temperature of the earth, with underground earth tubes, to heat and cool itself.
videos.w: HN commenters bring it up in geothermal, greenhouse and vertical farming threads as a low-tech example of growing citrus in a cold climate.
videos.q: Really interesting story/concept and I'm hoping to replicate on a small scale

videos.t: Introduction to Git with Scott Chacon of GitHub
videos.s: Scott Chacon introduces Git by showing what happens under the hood for basic commands: staging, committing, data storage, branching, merging and pushing. He contrasts it with Subversion and shows history viewing with log.
videos.w: HN commenters keep recommending it as the best video for newcomers who want to understand how Git works technically.
videos.q: This is the video that I keep recommending to new people who want to know how it works on a technical level.

videos.t: Steve Jobs on Failure
videos.s: A two-minute clip from a 1994 interview with Steve Jobs by the Santa Clara Valley Historical Association. Jobs talks about failure and about how most people never ask for help, recalling that he simply called people to ask.
videos.w: HN commenters return to it as a motivational reminder to not fear failure and to just ask for what you want.
videos.p: fear of failure and asking for help
videos.q: Whenever I feel fear of failure, I watch this video, and it might help you too.

videos.t: The Fastest Maze-Solving Competition On Earth
videos.s: Veritasium visits the Micromouse competition, where small autonomous robots race to solve mazes at extreme speed. It covers the competition's technical history, including fans and ground effect enabling very high-g turns.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a nice introduction to micromouse and maze-racing robots.
videos.q: is a nice introduction to the competition and its technical history.

videos.t: Star Trek TNG Ambient Engine Noise (Idling for 24 hrs)
videos.s: A 24-hour loop of Star Trek TNG starship engine ambience, meant as background sound for relaxing, sleeping or concentrating.
videos.w: HN people use it as background noise for coding and focus, and share it as a personal favorite.
videos.q: I just listen to the Star Trek TNG Ambient Engine Noise[1] if I'm coding or trying to focus.

videos.t: "A (Not So Gentle) Introduction To Systems Programming In ATS" by Aditya Siram
videos.s: Aditya Siram introduces ATS, a statically typed ML-like language that compiles to C and offers type-safe pointer arithmetic and a full proof language. The Strange Loop talk shows off C interop, concurrency and verification features with non-trivial examples.
videos.w: Cited in Rust and systems-language threads as the best introduction to ATS, a language claimed to go beyond Rust's safety guarantees.
videos.q: I recommend watching this presentation for a good idea of what ATS programming is like

videos.t: Desert Storm - The Air War, Day 1 - Animated
videos.s: An animated account of Day 1 of the Desert Storm air war on 17 January 1991, covering the 2,775 sorties flown against Iraqi strategic targets in the first 24 hours.
videos.w: Recommended as a deeply researched, visual series that shows how overwhelming the coalition air campaign was.
videos.q: I highly recommend watching this series about it, no one has dug into history like the Operations Room channel

videos.t: Sinclair's Soldiers in Trump's War on Media
videos.s: A Deadspin compilation of local news anchors at Sinclair-owned stations reading the same scripted message about irresponsible one-sided news. It was assembled by Timothy Burke.
videos.w: HN cites it as a vivid example of media consolidation and coordinated messaging.
videos.q: the Deadspin video of dozens of local news anchors reading the same editorial content handed down by Sinclair Broadcast Group is striking

videos.t: Stanford Seminar - Concatenative Programming: From Ivory to Metal
videos.s: Jon Purdy's Stanford EE380 seminar giving an overview of concatenative programming, from function composition theory and history down to low-level implementation and correctness benefits.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the best talk on concatenative languages and their mathematical properties.
videos.q: Jon Purdy has a great talk about this too

videos.t: Stevie Wonder - Superstition live on Sesame Street
videos.s: Stevie Wonder performs 'Superstition' on Sesame Street in 1973, with kids dancing along. It is a feel-good live music performance.
videos.w: Recommended in Sesame Street and children's TV threads as a favorite example of the show's funkier past.
videos.q: Stevie Wonder playing Superstition on Sesame Street might be my favorite

videos.t: ARCHIVE TEAM: A Distributed Preservation of Service Attack
videos.s: Jason Scott of Archive Team describes how a loose band of volunteers rushes to copy sites like Geocities, Friendster and Yahoo Video before their owners delete them. The talk covers the tactics they use and the argument that this data is history worth saving.
videos.w: HN points to it whenever a company shuts down a service and wipes user content, as an entertaining case for digital preservation.
videos.q: gave a fantastically entertaining talk about how they saved Geocities, Yahoo! Video, and Friendster

videos.t: Astroturf and manipulation of media messages | Sharyl Attkisson | TEDxUniversityofNevada
videos.s: Investigative journalist Sharyl Attkisson explains how astroturf, fake grassroots campaigns funded by corporate or political interests, manipulates media messages. The TEDx talk is about 11 minutes.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an introduction to shills, astroturfing and lobbyist influence on media, especially in threads about fake news and online forums.
videos.q: She also gave another amazing talk on corporate astroturfing and media manipulation [2]

videos.t: Rails World 2024 Opening Keynote - David Heinemeier Hansson
videos.s: DHH's opening keynote at Rails World 2024 in Toronto, where Rails 8 beta shipped. It covers built-in authentication, Propshaft, Solid Cache, Solid Queue, Solid Cable, Kamal 2 and Thruster, pitching the One Person Framework that needs no PaaS.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a primer on modern Rails and as a rebuttal to cloud 'learned helplessness', worth watching even by non-Ruby developers.
videos.q: I highly recommend you watch the first half hour of DHH Rails World talk on Rails 8 even if you aren’t a Ruby dev

videos.t: Opioids II: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's second Last Week Tonight segment on the opioid epidemic, covering the role of large companies in driving it. It touches on Purdue Pharma and the Sackler family.
videos.w: Commenters cite it, with Oliver's other two opioid segments, as a well-researched case against pharma marketing and the Purdue settlements.
videos.q: there are 3 John Oliver segments on the subject that will back up the "Good." statement

videos.t: DEF CON 30 - Sam Bent - Tor - Darknet Opsec By a Veteran Darknet Vendor
videos.s: A DEF CON 30 talk by Sam Bent, a former darknet vendor, on operational security when using Tor and the darknet. He applies the hacker mindset to staying anonymous and avoiding capture.
videos.w: HN people recommend it for a first-hand view of how Tor holds up in practice, from someone who had to rely on it.
videos.q: Here is an awesome DefCon talk about this topic from the perspective of a darknet vendor. It's amazing

videos.t: Why China Is so Good at Building Railways
videos.s: A Wendover Productions explainer on how China built the world's largest high-speed rail network so quickly and why its rail strategy differs from America's. It covers politics, social benefits and the economics of unprofitable lines.
videos.w: HN uses it as the go-to short video when threads compare Chinese and US rail and infrastructure.
videos.q: Please, I urge you to watch this.

videos.t: Scientific Studies: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on how media outlets report incomplete or untrue findings as settled science. It covers sensational headlines, small studies and pressure on researchers.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an entertaining and sophisticated primer on reading science reporting critically.
videos.q: John Oliver has a great segment called 'Scientific Studies' I'll link at the end of this post, everyone should watch this.

videos.t: Jim Jefferies -- Gun Control (Part 1) from BARE -- Netflix Special
videos.s: A clip from Jim Jefferies' Netflix special BARE in which he comedically dissects American gun culture and gun control arguments.
videos.w: Recommended as a funny but surprisingly persuasive outsider take on gun control, mainly in gun-related threads.
videos.q: I recommend listening to what Jim Jefferies had to say about gun control.

videos.t: Defcon 21 - Decapping Chips The Strike Easy Hard Way
videos.s: A DEF CON 21 talk by Adam Laurie and Zac Franken on decapping chips, covering how to remove chip packaging and image the die to read out contents such as ROM.
videos.w: Regarded as a favorite practical walkthrough of chip decapping, linked in threads on die shots, hardware backdoors and key extraction.
videos.q: One of my favourite talks is Decapping Chips the Hard Way by Adam Laurie and Zac Franken

videos.t: How to Enhance Your Gut Microbiome for Brain & Overall Health
videos.s: A Huberman Lab podcast episode on the gut-brain axis and how the gut microbiome affects the nervous system, hunger and overall health. It covers the pathways by which the gut influences the brain and practical steps for gut health.
videos.w: Recommended as an accessible neuroscientist's overview of gut microbiome science with practical takeaways.
videos.q: I would highly recommend this podcast (neuroscientist Andrew Huberman) if anyone wants to learn more about improving their gut health

videos.t: Dan Abramov   The wet codebase
videos.s: Dan Abramov's talk on the wet codebase, using visualizations to show how removing all duplication too early produces wrong abstractions that are hard to unwind.
videos.w: Recommended in DRY versus duplication debates for its visuals and its case that copy/paste can beat a wrong abstraction.
videos.q: Seeing what a premature, wrong abstraction looks like visually was eye opening.

videos.t: China & Uighurs: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on the Chinese government's treatment of the Uighur people, covering the human rights abuses in Xinjiang and why they deserve attention.
videos.w: HN points to it as an accessible, well-made mix of education and entertainment for anyone wanting to understand the Xinjiang situation.
videos.q: John Oliver did an excellent piece on the situation of the uighur last week

videos.t: Angry Voicemail We Got From an Alamo Drafthouse Customer
videos.s: Alamo Drafthouse posted an angry voicemail from a customer who was kicked out for texting in the theater. The theater turned it into a humorous in-house preview.
videos.w: It is cited as a viral example of Alamo enforcing its no-talking and no-texting rules with humor.
videos.q: This video Alamo posted to youtube of an angry customer bitching about getting kicked out for texting is amazing

videos.t: How We’re Fooled By Statistics
videos.s: A short Veritasium video explaining regression to the mean and how ignoring it leads to wrong conclusions about punishment versus reward, medical treatments and sports streaks. It uses the example of flight instructors who believed criticism works better than praise.
videos.w: HN commenters link it as the clearest short explanation of regression to the mean, especially for how it misleads people about feedback and statistics.
videos.q: Veritasium explains it better than me.

videos.t: The Death of Affordable Computing | Tariffs Impact & Investigation
videos.s: A long Gamers Nexus investigation into how volatile US tariffs affect the computer hardware industry. It interviews manufacturers and sellers about costs, margins and why moving production to the US is hard.
videos.w: HN recommends it for concrete numbers on what tariffs do to small hardware businesses.
videos.q: Best part is having a product manager show a spreadsheet of costs and margins and explain in real terms ($$$) what tariffs do to their business.

videos.t: Crow skiing down a roof
videos.s: A one-minute clip of a crow repeatedly sliding down a snowy roof on a small lid, apparently just for fun.
videos.w: Offered as vivid evidence that animals, crows in particular, play for pleasure and display intelligence beyond survival needs.
videos.q: This video of a crow repeatedly "skiing" down a roof changed my view of how animals play

videos.t: Alpha Centauri Quotes: Intro and Tech's 0-24
videos.s: Audio clips of the intro and technology quotes from the 1999 strategy game Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri, in male and female voices, covering techs 0 through 24.
videos.w: HN fans share it as a way to hear the game's philosophical, sci-fi quotes in sequence.
videos.q: I find them to be timeless, and quite heady when listened to in sequence.

videos.t: Riding the Booster with enhanced sound
videos.s: Footage from a camera on a Space Shuttle solid rocket booster from liftoff through descent, with audio enhanced by Skywalker Sound from the original camera microphones. The sound is real, not foley.
videos.w: HN recommends it for its raw, mostly natural audio and for conveying the speeds and violence of a shuttle launch and booster descent.
videos.q: I immediately had to re-watch this pretty awesome video after reading the article

videos.t: CppCon 2017: Chandler Carruth “Going Nowhere Faster”
videos.s: Chandler Carruth shows how to squeeze more performance out of already-optimized C++ code, covering how the CPU executes it. The talk goes into pipelining, branch prediction and speculative execution using benchmarks.
videos.w: Recommended as the best presentation on how modern CPUs run code, and why speculative execution matters for performance.
videos.q: The best presentation I've seen about CPU performance related to pipelining, branch prediction, and speculative execution

videos.t: How to use one paper towel | Joe Smith | TEDxConcordiaUPortland
videos.s: A short TEDx talk by Joe Smith teaching how to dry your hands with a single paper towel. It shows a simple technique for cutting waste.
videos.w: HN treats it as a tiny practical life hack some adopt for good, while others mock it as peak TED.
videos.q: I actually improved my hand drying technique after the TEDx on it

videos.t: Where Do Trees Get Their Mass?
videos.s: Veritasium asks people where a tree's mass comes from, then explains that most of a dry tree's mass originates from carbon dioxide in the air. It combines street interviews with a short explanation of photosynthesis.
videos.w: HN uses it as the go-to demonstration of how unintuitive mass conservation is, especially in weight loss and burning threads.
videos.q: Veritasium has a fun video demonstrating how unintuitive this is

videos.t: Money as Debt I - Revised Edition 2009 (Full Movie)
videos.s: An animated documentary by Paul Grignon explaining how modern money is created through bank lending as debt. This is a combined upload of the revised 2009 edition.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a cartoonish but thorough explanation of the monetary system, though some critics dispute its claims.
videos.q: is a cartoonish but thorough explanation for anyone who has the time

videos.t: "The Dangerous Truth About Protein" - Janice Stanger, Ph.D.
videos.s: A presentation by Janice Stanger arguing that protein is overhyped and that excess or the wrong kinds of protein are harmful. It promotes a whole-foods, plant-based diet.
videos.w: A few commenters cite it as a starting point for the claim that excess protein is harmful, though the claims are one-sided advocacy.

videos.t: Superpositions, Sudoku, the Wave Function Collapse algorithm.
videos.s: Martin Donald explains the Wave Function Collapse algorithm using Sudoku-like constraint solving and shows how he implemented it with Blender and Godot. It links demos and reference articles.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as the clearest way to understand WFC, especially in threads about Townscaper and tiled content generation.
videos.q: I found them hard to understand until I found this video by Martin Donald

videos.t: Michael Bay - What is Bayhem?
videos.s: An Every Frame a Painting video essay on Michael Bay's style, 'Bayhem', covering his camera movement, composition, color and editing. It argues that even if you dislike his films, they teach something about visual perception.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a short, well-produced and eye-opening piece of film analysis.
videos.q: short, easily digestible, and well-produced YouTube videos about this stuff that are eye-opening.

videos.t: Music as a Language: Victor Wooten at TEDxGabriolaIsland
videos.s: Bassist Victor Wooten argues that music should be learned the way children learn their first language: by immersion and play, without early correction or rigid academic instruction. He draws on how babies pick up speech from the people around them.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it when discussing how to teach children or beginners, as a language-like alternative to formal instruction.
videos.q: Victor Wooten gave an outstanding TED talk[1] on this topic[2]

videos.t: COVID-19 Vaccines: MODERNA | PFIZER/BIONTECH | ASTRAZENECA
videos.s: A Ninja Nerd whiteboard lecture on the Moderna, Pfizer/BioNTech and AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccines. It covers how each works, the preclinical and phase I-III trial process, and Operation Warp Speed.
videos.w: HN recommended it in late 2020 as a detailed, science-based explanation of how the different vaccines work and how they were tested.
videos.q: This is the best science based informative video I have seen on how these different Covid vaccines actually work.

videos.t: Let's #TalkConcurrency Panel Discussion with Sir Tony Hoare, Joe Armstrong, and Carl Hewitt
videos.s: A panel with Tony Hoare, Joe Armstrong and Carl Hewitt, hosted by Francesco Cesarini, on the history and future of concurrency. The three creators of CSP, Erlang and the actor model discuss their differing approaches.
videos.w: HN recommends it for getting the inventors of major concurrency models together, disagreements included.
videos.q: It was interesting hearing them discuss their different thoughts and approaches

videos.t: The REAL Story On Why Space Cadet Pinball Was Removed (ft. Windows on Itanium)
videos.s: NCommander investigates why Space Cadet Pinball disappeared from Windows Vista, building on Raymond Chen's explanation about 64-bit incompatibility. He tests it on 64-bit Windows including Itanium and walks through the debugging.
videos.w: Recommended as the detailed, entertaining history of why 3D Pinball vanished from Windows.
videos.q: If you have the time, I highly recommend checking out the NCommander's video talking about Space Cadet Pinball.

videos.t: Edgar Wright - How to Do Visual Comedy
videos.s: An Every Frame a Painting video essay analysing how Edgar Wright creates visual comedy through framing, camera movement, editing, sound effects and music.
videos.w: Recommended as a short, eye-opening piece of film analysis whenever physical or visual comedy is discussed.
videos.q: short, easily digestible, and well-produced YouTube videos about this stuff that are eye-opening.

videos.t: John Hennessy and David Patterson 2017 ACM A.M. Turing Award Lecture
videos.s: Hennessy and Patterson's 2018 Turing Award lecture at ISCA, A New Golden Age for Computer Architecture. It covers domain-specific hardware, security, open instruction sets and agile chip development.
videos.w: HN repeatedly recommends it as the best overview of the past, present and future of chip performance after Moore's law.
videos.q: I consistently recommend Hennessy and Patterson's Turing Award Talk[1] as a good overview of the past, present and future of chip performance.

videos.t: AWS re:Invent 2015 | (NET403) Another Day, Another Billion Packets
videos.s: Eric Brandwine's AWS re:Invent 2015 session on how Amazon VPC networking works. It covers the problems the design solved, why traditional approaches do not scale, and the mechanisms used for customer isolation and VPC endpoints.
videos.w: Considered a favorite deep dive into how AWS does virtual networking at L3 and why VPC hosts cannot snoop each other.
videos.q: Here's the ever excellent Eric Brandwine explaining what AWS does at L3 wrt VPC

videos.t: Driving Amazon’s ELECTRIC Delivery Vehicle: Rivian EDV
videos.s: A first-day ride-along with an Amazon delivery driver using the Rivian electric delivery van. She covers the van's new technology, how it compares to the standard Ford Transit delivery vehicles, and quirks and issues she noticed on the job.
videos.w: HN points to it as a rare review from an actual delivery driver rather than a car reviewer, showing how the van's design suits the job.
videos.q: I started watching it thinking “I’ll only watch a minute or two” and got so engrossed I watched the whole thing.

videos.t: Let Vim Do the Typing
videos.s: George Brocklehurst of thoughtbot demonstrates Vim's built-in completion mechanisms, from word, line and block completion to ctags. The aim is to type less and make fewer typos.
videos.w: HN users say it made Vim's completion system click for them.
videos.q: it "clicked" for me after watching this video

videos.t: MEETING THE ENEMY A feminist comes to terms with the Men's Rights movement | Cassie Jaye | TEDxMarin
videos.s: Documentary filmmaker Cassie Jaye explains how making The Red Pill led her, a feminist, to reevaluate her assumptions about the Men's Rights movement. She argues for listening to people you think of as the enemy.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a thoughtful account from a feminist on men's issues and the cost of saying unpopular things.
videos.q: This is a good TEDx talk from a feminist

videos.t: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum, Cryptocurrency, and the Future of Money | Lex Fridman Podcast #80
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Ethereum co-creator Vitalik Buterin about Ethereum, cryptocurrency and the future of money. The conversation also touches on technical topics such as quantum computing and mining.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a fascinating conversation showing how the Ethereum founder thinks.
videos.q: listening to the founder of Ethereum on the Lex Fridman podcast was fascinating.

videos.t: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234
videos.s: A long Lex Fridman interview with Stephen Wolfram on complexity, cellular automata, computational irreducibility and the Wolfram Physics Project.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible way into Wolfram's physics ideas and his personality.
videos.q: A good discussion that touches on these ideas in a fairly accessible way

videos.t: Stop Signs Suck and We Should Get Rid of Them
videos.s: Not Just Bikes argues that stop signs are a poor traffic control, drawing on Dutch practice and the Idaho stop to show intersections can be safer without them, especially for cyclists.
videos.w: Cited in threads about cyclist safety and traffic law as an explanation of why removing stop signs can improve safety.
videos.q: Here is a great video about life without stop signs in the Netherlands

videos.t: Epic v Apple: Judgment Day - Who Won? Who Lost? ...and Why? (VL538)
videos.s: Hoeg Law's Virtual Legality walks through the 185-page Epic v. Apple decision, covering antitrust law, relevant markets, anti-steering and who actually won. It runs well over two hours and corrects common media misreadings.
videos.w: Strongly recommended as the best explanation of the ruling, in more depth and with more accuracy than press coverage.
videos.q: I'd suggest watching the excellent video by Hoeg Law.

videos.t: Sketchpad, by Dr. Ivan Sutherland with comments by Alan Kay
videos.s: Earliest known footage of Ivan Sutherland's MIT PhD work, Sketchpad, the first computer graphics system, with commentary by Alan Kay. It shows light-pen drawing with constraints in a short clip.
videos.w: HN points people to it as the canonical demo of early interactive graphics, constraints and objects, and as one of Alan Kay's favorite things to show.
videos.q: one of Alan Kay's favorite demos over the years has been to show folks Sketchpad,

videos.t: Money as Debt - Full Documentary
videos.s: Paul Grignon's animated documentary presenting his view of how banks create money as debt and why that system requires continuous growth. It outlines the historical background of modern banking.
videos.w: Recommended as an approachable explanation of fractional reserve banking, with the caveat that it is biased.
videos.q: the first Money as Debt video [1] still makes the most sense to me

videos.t: Procedurally Crafting Manhattan for Marvel's Spider-Man
videos.s: GDC 2019 session where Insomniac's David Santiago describes the procedural systems used to build Manhattan for Marvel's Spider-Man. It covers the open-world pipeline and how each system was designed to support iteration and dependencies.
videos.w: Recommended as a prime example of large-scale procedural generation used in a shipped AAA game.
videos.q: There's a great talk about Procedurally Generating Manhattan for Spiderman that's worth watching

videos.t: Stephan T. Lavavej “Floating-Point ＜charconv＞: Making Your Code 10x Faster With C++17's Final Boss”
videos.s: Stephan T. Lavavej's CppCon 2019 talk on implementing floating-point to_chars and from_chars in Microsoft's C++ STL. It covers the history of float-string conversion and the algorithms that make it much faster.
videos.w: HN calls it a surprisingly fun, approachable talk on a hard problem and cites it in floating-point threads.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: Stephan T Lavavej also had a surprisingly fun and approachable talk on that problem

videos.t: KSP Doesn't Teach: Rocket Engine Plumbing
videos.s: Scott Manley explains the plumbing of rocket engines, including pressure-fed, gas generator, expander and staged combustion cycles. He shows why more complex designs exist and what they gain.
videos.w: Recommended whenever rocket engine cycles or turbopumps come up, as a clear introduction from a trusted explainer.
videos.q: Scott Manley has a fantastic video explaining all of this

videos.t: Email Hates the Living
videos.s: A lightning-style conference talk by Ricardo Signes about the horrors of email: its protocols, formats and decades of accumulated quirks. It is delivered with a humorous horror theme to show why handling email correctly is harder than it looks.
videos.w: HN points to it whenever someone underestimates how hard email parsing, validation or building a mail client really is.
videos.q: If you want to read about the insanity behind some of the protocols watch that talk.

videos.t: QuakeCon 2011 - John Carmack Keynote
videos.s: John Carmack's keynote at QuakeCon 2011, an hour and a half of wide-ranging talk about id Software, Rage, engine open-sourcing, patents and programming practices.
videos.w: Cited as a source for Carmack's views on static analysis, open source and languages, and praised as a captivating, conversational speaker.
videos.q: John Carmack is an absolutely brilliant speaker. Conversational, captivating and effortlessly natural.

videos.t: 1. Climate Change -- the scientific debate
videos.s: The first video in potholer54's climate series, giving a basic look at how climate scientists infer that man-made carbon gases are changing the climate. It is a short explainer meant to present the scientific evidence plainly.
videos.w: HN users point to it as a clear, evidence-based series to counter climate skepticism.
videos.q: There is a great video series on YouTube by "potholer54" that shows the scientific evidence for it better than I can.

videos.t: John Rauser keynote: "Statistics Without the Agonizing Pain" -- Strata + Hadoop 2014
videos.s: John Rauser's Strata 2014 keynote argues that programmers can learn statistics quickly by simulating random processes and shuffling data. He explains p-values through resampling rather than formulas.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an excellent programmer-friendly explanation of p-values and statistical thinking.
videos.q: This is an excellent talk I attended a while ago that explains it very well from a programmer's perspective

videos.t: Gaslighting Your Fans w/ Dolby ATMOS™
videos.s: Musician and audio engineer Benn Jordan tries Dolby Atmos as a consumer, covering the theory of immersive audio, its business model, and home theater and headphone listening. He concludes it often falls short of the pitch.
videos.w: HN points to it in Atmos and spatial audio threads as a knowledgeable critique of why the format rarely delivers.
videos.q: I found this video by Benn Jordan very enlightening about the whole Atmos nonsense

videos.t: Yuri Bezmenov: Psychological Warfare Subversion & Control of Western Society (Complete)
videos.s: A 1983 Los Angeles lecture by KGB defector Yuri Bezmenov on how the Soviets carried out ideological subversion of target societies through propaganda. He walks through demoralization and normalization stages.
videos.w: HN commenters link it to argue that cultural subversion and normalization are playing out today, though mostly as a reference in unrelated threads.
videos.q: One of the most important videos on the entire Internet

videos.t: "Energy Revolution? More like a Crawl" - Dr. Vaclav Smil
videos.c: Trottier Institute for Sustainability in Engineering and Design
videos.s: Energy scholar Vaclav Smil argues that global energy transitions are slow and that renewable targets should not rest on wishful thinking. He appraises how energy dependencies are likely to change and asks for using much less.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a grounded, data-driven counter to hype about quick energy revolutions.
videos.q: I really suggest watching this talk by Smil

videos.t: 39.08! McMurtry fan car breaks Goodwood Hill RECORD! | Festival of Speed 2022
videos.s: A short clip of the McMurtry Speirling fan car setting a new Goodwood Hill record of 39.08 seconds at the 2022 Festival of Speed, driven by Max Chilton. It beat the previous timed shootout record set in 1999 and the outright record held by the VW ID.R.
videos.w: HN points to it as a striking demonstration of fan-downforce EVs, with a run that looks glued to the track and almost sped up.
videos.q: Watching it set the record for goodwood is mind blowing

videos.t: Connections between physics and deep learning
videos.s: Max Tegmark's MIT CBMM talk on why deep learning works so well. He argues that the laws of physics and the symmetries in physical data make it compressible into small neural networks, tying physics to network structure.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear argument for why deep and cheap learning succeeds, often alongside the associated paper.
videos.q: physical data tends to have symmetries, and these symmetries make descriptions of the data very compressible into relatively small neural circuits

videos.t: How to achieve nanometer precision in space?
videos.s: Breaking Taps explains how the cryogenic mirror actuators on the James Webb Space Telescope achieve nanometer precision using flexures. It shows a 3D-printed replica and how one motor handles both coarse and fine motion.
videos.w: Commenters repeatedly recommend it in JWST threads as a great explanation of clever mechanical design that is accurate and long lasting.
videos.q: I highly recommend

videos.t: Sample Breakdown: Daft Punk - One More Time
videos.s: A short Tracklib video visualizing the disco sample that Daft Punk's One More Time is built from. It shows how the track is composed from the original material.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a striking visual breakdown of how the song was constructed.
videos.q: This video is a great visualization on how it's composed. Absolutely incredible.

videos.t: Nardwuar vs. N.E.R.D - The Extended Version
videos.s: Nardwuar interviews Pharrell and Shay of N.E.R.D. in Vancouver, using his trademark deep research and gifts. The extended version runs about ten minutes.
videos.w: HN holds it up as a model of interview preparation, where thorough research on the guest impresses the interviewee.
videos.q: This is one of the most impressive interviews I've ever experienced in my life

videos.t: Joe Rogan Experience #1080 - David Goggins
videos.s: Joe Rogan interviews David Goggins, a retired Navy SEAL and ultramarathon runner, about his path from overweight to elite endurance athlete and pushing beyond comfort zones.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an inspiring story about perseverance and getting outside one's comfort zone.
videos.q: do yourself a favor

videos.t: The Kennedy Assassination: Inside the Book Depository
videos.s: A 98-minute LEMMiNO video reconstructing what happened inside the Texas School Book Depository before, during, and after the Kennedy assassination. It draws on testimony to map people's movements and discrepancies.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a detailed, well-sourced overview that helps viewers form their own opinion.
videos.q: It's long but it gives a good overview of the sequence of events and the discrepancies.

videos.t: Maciej Ceglowski - Barely succeed! It's easier!
videos.s: Maciej Ceglowski's talk at Web Directions argues that small teams and lone programmers can build sustainable businesses without chasing Silicon Valley's grow-or-die model. He offers alternative, more achievable definitions of success.
videos.w: HN regards it as an inspiring, funny case for modest, bootstrapped success over venture-funded risk.
videos.q: Which I thought was amazing and inspiring.

videos.t: What P vs NP is actually about
videos.s: Polylog explains how algorithms can be turned into circuits and encoded as satisfiability problems, which lets you effectively run them backwards. It uses this to motivate breaking RSA, general reductions to SAT, and what P vs NP is really asking.
videos.w: Recommended as an intuitive, animated explanation of P vs NP framed around reversing computation.
videos.q: I would highly recommend giving it a watch

videos.t: Chris Sacca of Lowercase Capital - TWiST #291
videos.s: Jason Calacanis interviews investor Chris Sacca on This Week in Startups. Sacca discusses what makes a founder, his investments such as Kickstarter, and his personal story of losing money and recovering.
videos.w: HN recommends it in startup video lists for its stories and Sacca's candid background.
videos.q: My favorite, because it's so full of great stories, is the Chris Sacca interview with Jason Calacanis

videos.t: Making of "The Prodigy - Voodoo People" in Ableton by Jim Pavloff
videos.s: Jim Pavloff rebuilds The Prodigy's 'Voodoo People' in Ableton from its listed samples. The video shows how the track is assembled and how close a handmade reconstruction can sound.
videos.w: Used as an example of prototyping music and, in a Copilot copyright thread, of a handmade reconstruction that sounds like the original.
videos.q: There are legendary Prodigy tracks reconstructions by Jim Pavloff

videos.t: The Crisis in Cosmology
videos.s: PBS Space Time explains the Hubble constant tension, in which two precise, independent methods of measuring the universe's expansion rate disagree. It covers why this calls some standard cosmology into question.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear, layman-friendly explanation of the Hubble tension from a channel regarded well by physicists.
videos.q: PBS Space time has an excellent video on the topic

videos.t: Emacs From Scratch #1 - Getting Started with a Basic Usable Configuration
videos.s: The first stream in the Emacs From Scratch series, building a custom Emacs configuration from zero while teaching basics. It covers a usable baseline setup and the packages for completion, themes and productivity.
videos.w: Recommended as a thoughtful, step-by-step way to build your own Emacs config rather than starting from Doom or Spacemacs.
videos.q: System Crafters' 'Emacs from Sratch' series [0], which is incredibly well thought-out

videos.t: J.K. Rowling | ContraPoints
videos.s: A roughly 90-minute video essay by ContraPoints on J.K. Rowling and the controversy around her views on gender. It examines why many LGBTQ people and allies soured on her.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a thorough, nuanced perspective on the Rowling controversy and on cancel culture from a trans creator.
videos.q: This is a good, calm, nuanced discussion about why LGBTQ people and our allies don't like Rowling as much as we used to.

videos.t: Robust-first computing: Beyond efficiency
videos.s: Dave Ackley gives a high-level introduction to robust-first computing, which prioritizes robustness over efficiency in computer architecture. A sorting demo illustrates the idea.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a short, clear explanation of robust-first computing by its originator, and as a philosophy relevant to building with unreliable components like LLMs.
videos.q: here is a far better explanation by the terms creator

videos.t: CheerpX: a WebAssembly-based x86 virtual machine in the browser, Yuri Iozzelli
videos.s: A talk by Yuri Iozzelli at a WebAssembly meetup on CheerpX, an x86 virtual machine running in the browser. It uses a JIT compiler that emits WebAssembly at runtime to run real native applications. It covers the architecture and demos such as porting a multiplayer C++ game.
videos.w: HN points to it as an impressive look at how far WebAssembly can go, and as the explanation of the architecture behind CheerpX and its Flash support.
videos.q: This is honestly one of the coolest things I've seen

videos.t: Dr. Chris Knobbe - 'Diseases of Civilization: Are Seed Oil Excesses the Unifying Mechanism?'
videos.s: Ophthalmologist Chris Knobbe argues that excess omega-6 seed oils are a unifying cause of chronic diseases of civilization such as diabetes and macular degeneration. He presents the case at Low Carb Denver 2020.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it in nutrition threads as the strongest case against seed oils, though it is a contested claim.
videos.q: I think the best talk of the health dangers of seed oils is in the following video

videos.t: Chinampas of Mexico: Most Productive Agriculture EVER?
videos.s: Permaculture instructor Andrew Millison visits the chinampas, the floating gardens of Xochimilco in Mexico City. He looks at this ancient Aztec agricultural system and the project restoring it.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear introduction to chinampas and an example of productive agroforestry.
videos.q: who is an amazingly clear presenter about permaculture

videos.t: PRACTICE 2018: Joseph White
videos.s: Joseph White, creator of PICO-8, retraces the design of the fantasy console and how tools can shape and guide creative work. He discusses cozy, constrained design spaces and the influence of user-made cartridges.
videos.w: HN points to it for the design philosophy behind PICO-8's constraints.
videos.q: talk about the design philosophy of Pico-8

videos.t: Vaccines and Autism: A Measured Response
videos.s: hbomberguy's long video dissects the anti-vaccine movement, analyzing Andrew Wakefield's fraudulent MMR-autism study, the media's role and Wakefield's loss of his license. It combines detailed research with humor.
videos.w: HN commenters call it the definitive, thorough answer to whether vaccines cause autism and recommend it as an entertaining deep dive.
videos.q: His documentary on Andrew Wakefield has become my definitive answer to people who ask me if the MMR vaccine causes autism

videos.t: iPhone Magnifier and Voice over
videos.s: Kristy Viers demonstrates the iPhone Magnifier combined with VoiceOver to describe the user's surroundings. She shows how the built-in feature reports scenes, faces and lighting.
videos.w: HN recommends it to show what on-device accessibility features can do and how blind users actually use an iPhone.
videos.q: It describes the scene, tells you how many faces are visible, whether or not the image is focused, lighting conditions.

videos.t: Are athletes really getting faster, better, stronger? | David Epstein
videos.s: David Epstein argues in this TED talk that improving athletic records owe much to technology, training and the selection of specialized body types, not just humans getting inherently better. He gives counter-intuitive examples across sports.
videos.w: HN links it in threads about athlete body types, sports technology and record-breaking as a relevant, counter-intuitive explanation.

videos.t: Turning Smashed TVs into Realistic Artificial Daylight
videos.s: DIY Perks shows how to turn old or smashed TVs and monitors into realistic artificial window lights, using the backlight and Fresnel lens to simulate distant daylight.
videos.w: HN points to it in threads on artificial sunlight, as a buildable and surprisingly convincing artificial window.
videos.q: The result is quite stunning. I've never seen anything like it.

videos.t: I BOUGHT A WHOLE CHURCH ORGAN - Part 1 The Organs Removal
videos.s: Part one of Look Mum No Computer's series on buying a whole church pipe organ, covering how it was removed from its home. The series goes on to restoring it and rewiring it for MIDI.
videos.w: HN recommends the series as great fun, following a talented and enthusiastic amateur rebuilding a pipe organ.
videos.q: this series where a pipe organ is gradually rebuilt by an extremely talented and enthusiastic amateur is great fun!

videos.t: Is The Alcubierre Warp Drive Possible? | Space Time | PBS Digital Studios
videos.s: PBS Space Time introduces Miguel Alcubierre's warp drive, explaining how spacetime itself could be warped rather than moving a ship through it, and whether it is physically possible.
videos.w: HN points to it as a short, approachable starting point on warp drive physics from a channel commenters like.
videos.q: For a shorter 10 minute video, see this PBS Spacetime video

videos.t: Why Machines That Bend Are Better
videos.s: Veritasium explores compliant mechanisms, devices that move by flexing rather than using hinges and joints, with researchers at BYU. It covers advantages such as fewer parts and precision, including uses in nuclear weapon safety.
videos.w: HN commenters like it as a high-quality, accessible look at an under-appreciated engineering idea and bring it up in snap-fit and hinge discussions.
videos.q: Veritasium videos are pretty darn high quality.

videos.t: Terence Mckenna - Culture is your operating system
videos.s: A short edited excerpt of Terence McKenna arguing that culture acts as an operating system for the mind, set to imagery and music. It touches on psychedelics and how they change thinking.
videos.w: Cited as the origin of the 'culture/philosophy as operating system' metaphor and as a quick introduction to McKenna's ideas.
videos.q: If you want to know where the metaphor of philosophy as an operating system comes from

videos.t: The Dutch Solution for Safer Sidewalks - Continuous Sidewalks
videos.s: A short Not Just Bikes video on continuous sidewalks in the Netherlands, where the sidewalk runs unbroken across side streets so cars must visibly cross pedestrian space. It places them within Dutch sustainable safety and Vision Zero efforts.
videos.w: HN users point to it as a vivid example of how simple, intentional street design makes a big difference for pedestrian safety.
videos.q: talking about length of crossings on wide road, traffic signals, priorities, etc.

videos.t: Monad - FunFunFunction #21
videos.s: An episode of FunFunFunction explaining monads in JavaScript as functors that also implement flatMap. It builds on the preceding functor episode and works through code examples.
videos.w: Recommended to people confused by monads as a friendly, practical explanation for JavaScript developers, with one commenter saying it finally made it click.
videos.q: I saw a video by MPJ/Funfunfunction [0] and it finally made sense.

videos.t: Derren Brown - The System (Full)
videos.s: Derren Brown's TV special in which he convinces a person he has a system for predicting horse race winners, demonstrating how survivorship bias and selective outcomes can fake predictive powers.
videos.w: HN cites it as the classic demonstration of survivorship and confirmation bias in betting, trading and prediction claims.
videos.q: Here's an entertaining video from Derren Brown that shows how to use this technique to convince people you have psychic powers

videos.t: Why our IQ levels are higher than our grandparents' | James Flynn
videos.s: Moral philosopher James Flynn explains the Flynn effect, the steady rise of IQ scores across the 20th century. He argues the shift reflects a move toward abstract, hypothetical thinking as cognitively demanding professions grew.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of why generations think differently and why IQ scores have risen.
videos.q: This is an argument made by James Flynn in his amazing TED talk

videos.t: The Internet's Own Boy: The Story of Aaron Swartz | full movie (2014)
videos.s: The full documentary 'The Internet's Own Boy' about programmer and activist Aaron Swartz, with interviews with family, friends and internet figures. It covers his work on access to information and the legal case preceding his death.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the essential documentary for learning about Aaron Swartz and the case that shaped hacker culture.
videos.q: here's a must-watch documentary, especially if you belong to the hacker culture

videos.t: CIA Officer in Charge of Taking Down the AQ Khan Network | James Lawler | Ep. 125
videos.s: A long Team House podcast interview with James Lawler, a former CIA operations officer who led counterproliferation work against the A.Q. Khan nuclear network. He discusses HUMINT, WMD and how such operations were run.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an in-depth look at the mechanics of intelligence work from a veteran who ran a nonproliferation operation.
videos.q: if you want to hear someone who actively ran another incredibly successful nuclear non proliferation operation inside of CIA

videos.t: [7] Jim Keller, Silicon Wizard 🧙‍♂️
videos.s: Ian Cutress interviews chip architect Jim Keller about his time at AMD, Intel and elsewhere, management advice, design approach, Moore's Law and x86 versus Arm.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an interview dense with insight from Keller, worth hearing in full even for non-engineers.
videos.q: It’s actually important (if you’re not an engineer) to listen to the whole thing, because he drops knowledge all over the place.

videos.t: The Alt-Right Playbook: Always a Bigger Fish
videos.s: Innuendo Studios' Alt-Right Playbook episode, drawing on Corey Robin's The Reactionary Mind, argues that conservatism defends hierarchy and a shrinking in-group.
videos.w: Cited as a thoughtful video essay and for its model of in-group hierarchy in political threads.
videos.q: I think Innuendo Studios/Ian Danskin explains this mechanism very very well

videos.t: The GUI should be better.  A lot better.
videos.s: Accursed Farms' hour-plus critique of the modern desktop GUI. It argues that current interfaces are a regression from older designs such as Windows 7 and proposes principles for better ones.
videos.w: Recommended as a thought-provoking critique that makes people notice how poor everyday GUIs are.
videos.q: this video cursed me to pay far more attention on how shitty modern GUI is in my everyday interaction with the computer and phone

videos.t: Do Complex Numbers Exist?
videos.s: Sabine Hossenfelder asks whether complex numbers are just a convenient tool or necessary in physics. She discusses a recent paper arguing that quantum mechanics cannot be done with real numbers alone.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a short, accessible layperson explanation of the real-versus-complex quantum theory debate.
videos.q: I highly recommend video by Sabine Hossenfelder [1] on this topic.

videos.t: Servo Architecture: Safety and Performance
videos.s: Jack Moffitt presents the architecture of Servo, Mozilla's experimental browser engine written in Rust, focusing on parallelism across cores, GPUs and SIMD and the safety properties gained from Rust.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an exciting look at how a browser can be rebuilt for performance and safety, including the WebRender ideas that fed into Firefox Quantum.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: This video is one of the most exciting I have seen with regards to web browser performance, and it's Mozilla

videos.t: Am I still lactose tolerant? - Lactose Gene Therapy Update
videos.s: The Thought Emporium's update on the home-brewed gene therapy he took to cure his lactose intolerance. It reports how the effect held up over two years and what future versions might look like.
videos.w: Pointed to as a striking example of DIY biology and self-experimentation with gene therapy.
videos.q: His YouTube channel The Thought Emporium, is amazing.

videos.t: Republic, Lost (my favorite version)
videos.s: Lawrence Lessig's 2011 Berkeley book talk based on Republic, Lost, arguing that money in politics creates institutional corruption in Congress. He calls it his favorite version of the talk.
videos.w: HN people point to it as a starting place for understanding how money corrupts American government.
videos.q: Lawrence Lessig has some great talks about this topic, here's one of them

videos.t: Why our generals were more successful in World War II than in Korea, Vietnam or Iraq/Afghanistan
videos.s: Thomas Ricks's Nimitz Memorial Lecture at UC Berkeley asks why US generals did better in World War II than in Korea, Vietnam or Iraq and Afghanistan. A central point is the WWII practice of quickly reassigning or relieving underperforming generals.
videos.w: Used in hiring and management debates as an analysis of fast evaluation, quick dismissal without stigma, and the cost of keeping underperformers.
videos.q: Possibly the best analysis of this I have yet seen is the video

videos.t: Information, Evolution, and intelligent Design - With Daniel Dennett
videos.s: Daniel Dennett gives a Royal Institution talk toward a unified theory of information, tying together evolution, learning and engineering. He argues that design can arise bottom-up through small steps without a designer.
videos.w: Recommended for its account of competence without comprehension, relevant to evolution and to debates about AI.
videos.q: I highly recommend this Royal Institute talk

videos.t: Milton Friedman Speaks: Money and Inflation (B1230) - Full Video
videos.s: An 86-minute Milton Friedman talk arguing that inflation is a monetary phenomenon caused by money supply growing faster than goods, and that the cure is less government spending and money printing.
videos.w: Shared during inflation discussions as an accessible, layman-friendly statement of the monetarist view.
videos.q: I think is under rated talk which explains complex stuff in layman terms.

videos.t: "This Machine Greens" - Bitcoin Documentary - Online Premiere
videos.s: A documentary from Swan Bitcoin exploring Bitcoin's relationship with energy, featuring Lyn Alden and others, and arguing that mining is a net positive for the environment and not wasteful.
videos.w: Bitcoin advocates on HN cite it to rebut energy-consumption and waste criticisms, though it is an advocacy piece from a Bitcoin company.
videos.q: This video also does a great job of addressing the "waste" by elaborating on "unforgable costliness

videos.t: Lambda World 2018 - What FP can learn from Smalltalk by Aditya Siram
videos.s: Aditya Siram argues that functional programming has much to learn from Smalltalk's interactivity, using Pharo and Squeak to show live, visual, explorable programming environments.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible demonstration of what Smalltalk environments offer and a reference for advanced IDE ideas.
videos.q: I think it is the most accessible explanation of the marvel of Smalltalk

videos.t: what did you do
videos.s: Noodle explores how retro pixel art was designed for CRT displays and why games look different on LCDs, with input from pixel artists and CRT researchers.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an entertaining deep dive on CRT versus LCD rendering of retro games and the case for CRT shaders.
videos.q: This is an excellent deep dive on the issues I spoke of

videos.t: Lecture 1: Introduction to Power and Politics in Today’s World
videos.s: The opening lecture of Ian Shapiro's Yale course Power and Politics in Today's World, which examines political dynamics and institutions over the past quarter century, including inequality, declining unions and new forms of authoritarianism.
videos.w: HN recommends the lecture series as a foundational, wide-ranging grounding in modern global politics.
videos.q: Yale's Power and Politcs was created by Ian Shapiro is an excellent zoom out into global politics and how how the modern world was made.

videos.t: Growing Living Rat Neurons To Play... DOOM? | Part 1
videos.s: The Thought Emporium grows living rat neurons on an electrode array and tries to train them to play Doom. It is part of a series on biological computing.
videos.w: Cited whenever biocomputing or neurons-on-chip come up, as an accessible example of how such a system can be built.
videos.q: They run an amazing channel that covers a variety of topics. Highly recommend.

videos.t: I made a talking banana
videos.s: A maker builds a talking banana that reads YouTube and Twitch comments aloud on stream, then fights viewers who abuse it with profanity. He ends up building a pronunciation-based filter to catch bad words.
videos.w: HN shares it as a funny, technical story about phonetic profanity filtering, relevant to Soundex and content moderation threads.
videos.q: terrific little video about the battle between him and his viewers

videos.t: youtube YouTube   Stewart Lee   9   Political Correctness   41st Best Stand Up ever
videos.s: A nine-minute Stewart Lee stand-up routine about political correctness and the claim that it has gone mad. It is dry, layered British comedy that takes the complaint apart.
videos.w: HN commenters offer it as a sharp, funny answer to 'PC gone mad' and anti-woke arguments in discussions of language policy.
videos.q: there's an excellent 9-minute bit of stand-up comedy from Stewart Lee about political correctness you might want to watch

videos.t: Old Geeks Yell At Cloud (with Andrew Clay Shafer & Bryan Cantrill)
videos.s: A podcast episode of Arrested DevOps with Andrew Clay Shafer and Bryan Cantrill, featuring Cantrill's rant on integrity in companies and technology.
videos.w: HN recommends Cantrill's integrity rant when discussing corporate ethics and companies that act on principles.
videos.q: the whole thing is worth watching

videos.t: Seymour Papert 1983
videos.s: An eight-minute excerpt of a 1983 video featuring Seymour Papert, creator of Logo, on children learning programming and abstract ideas through embodied play. It shows kids acting out the Logo turtle.
videos.w: Recommended to anyone unfamiliar with Papert as a glimpse of his vision for computers in education.
videos.q: One really powerful idea he had was ensuring that we stay "somatic" with our computer instruction

videos.t: Ted Nelson in Herzog's "Lo and Behold"
videos.s: A short excerpt from Werner Herzog's film Lo and Behold in which Ted Nelson lays out his ideas about hypertext and interconnection. Herzog concludes that Nelson is the only sane person in computing.
videos.w: HN shares it as an accessible window into Ted Nelson's vision of Xanadu and linking, which commenters say gains meaning with historical context.
videos.q: I've grown to find this interview almost magical.

videos.t: A visual guide to Bayesian thinking
videos.s: Julia Galef uses pictures to explain Bayes' rule, then tells three personal stories showing how she applies it to improve her thinking.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a short, accessible intro to Bayesian reasoning and priors.
videos.q: The most important mathematical video you will ever see in your life.

videos.t: Neural Networks Demystified [Part 1: Data and Architecture]
videos.s: The first of a short series by Welch Labs on building a complete neural network in Python. It introduces the data and the architecture of a simple network before later parts cover forward propagation, gradient descent, and backpropagation.
videos.w: HN commenters point beginners to this series as one of the clearest short walkthroughs of how neural networks and backpropagation work.
videos.q: One of the clearest walkthroughs I've seen online is a short series of very short videos by Stephen C Welch [2] [3].

videos.t: GDC 2010: Sid Meier Keynote - "Everything You Know is Wrong"
videos.s: Sid Meier's GDC 2010 keynote on how players perceive probability in games, including how Civilization's odds were adjusted because players misjudged them.
videos.w: HN points to it as the best talk on how people misunderstand probabilities and how designers handle that.
videos.q: Sid Meier (Civilization) gave a great GDC keynote in 2010

videos.t: 1. A strange determinant
videos.s: Timothy Gowers thinks aloud, in real time, as he tries to understand why Pascal's determinant equals 1. He does not fully solve it in this episode, but shows his exploratory process.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it to see how a top mathematician approaches an unfamiliar problem through experiments and curiosity.
videos.q: Gowers has one of my favourite video series about how he approaches a problem he is unfamiliar with

videos.t: State of GPT | BRK216HFS
videos.s: Andrej Karpathy walks through how GPT assistants are trained, from tokenization and pretraining to supervised finetuning and RLHF, and gives practical prompting strategies and a view of the tooling ecosystem.
videos.w: Recommended as the clearest overview of how LLM assistants are built and how to use them well.
videos.q: It changed the way I use GPT-4.

videos.t: Clojure in a nutshell by James Trunk
videos.s: James Trunk introduces Clojure syntax and thinking, covering its core data structures, immutability, the thread-last macro and live data analysis in the REPL.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a clear, enjoyable introduction to Clojure and a good example of REPL-driven development.
videos.q: gave one of the most clear and enjoyable technical introductions to Clojure I've seen. Recommended!

videos.t: Old car headlights were all the same — which was a fairly bright idea
videos.s: Technology Connections explains why American cars all had the same standardized sealed-beam headlights until 1957. It covers the regulations behind the design and the effect on night visibility.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear explanation of why old headlights looked as they did, and as a case study in mandating requirements versus solutions.
videos.q: has, as so often the case, a great video about why old car headlights were the shapes they were

videos.t: REcon 2013 - The Future of RE : Dynamic Binary Visualization (Christopher Domas)
videos.s: Christopher Domas's REcon 2013 talk on dynamic binary visualization for reverse engineering. He shows how rendering binary data as interactive visual maps and trigraphs reveals structure that hex dumps hide, leading to his Cantor.dust tool.
videos.w: HN commenters say it permanently changed how they think about inspecting binary data, and point to it as the origin of visual binary analysis tools.
videos.q: after having seen Christopher Domas present "The Future of RE: Dynamic Binary Visualization" my mind was forever blown.

videos.t: Neil deGrasse Tyson - We Stopped Dreaming (Episode 1)
videos.s: A short, music-driven video built from Neil deGrasse Tyson's remarks on why advancing the space frontier matters, contrasting NASA's small budget with war spending and stressing inspiration.
videos.w: Recommended to anyone asking whether space exploration is worth the cost.
videos.q: I always recommend anyone wondering about whether or not space exploration is worth it to view the following amazing video compilations.

videos.t: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333
videos.s: Lex Fridman's long conversation with Andrej Karpathy on Tesla's self-driving approach, Optimus, neural networks, transformers, AGI and more. It also touches on his OpenAI work and working with Elon Musk.
videos.w: Cited for Karpathy's first-hand explanations of camera-only self-driving, transformers and ML trends.
videos.q: Anyone seriously interested in this question should listen to the Lex Friedman interview of Andrej Karpathy
