videos.t: Lenses, Folds, and Traversals
videos.s: Edward Kmett's talk to the NY Haskell User Group on the lens library, building from fmap and function composition up to lenses, folds and traversals. It shows how these composable combinators access and modify parts of data structures.
videos.w: HN calls it dense but mind-blowing, the go-to way to understand lenses through algebraic derivation.
videos.q: I found this talk by edward kmett incredibly helpful[0].

videos.t: A real person, a lot like you
videos.s: A three-minute video from Derek Sivers, based on his book Anything You Want, about remembering that the people you deal with online are real people. It contrasts how we treat people face to face with how we treat them online.
videos.w: Recommended in threads about online hostility as a short reminder to treat strangers as human beings.
videos.q: This is the video, I want everyone on internet to watch

videos.t: The Secret Life of the Vacuum Cleaner - Remastered
videos.s: Tim Hunkin's 1987 TV series episode on how vacuum cleaners and related household machines work, remastered and upscaled in 2021. It is part of the six-episode 'Secret Life of Machines' series with hands-on demonstrations of everyday technology.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear, charming explanation of how machines work, including a demonstration of building an electric motor.
videos.q: I cannot recommend it strongly enough.

videos.t: Thinking, Fast and Slow | Daniel Kahneman | Talks at Google
videos.s: Daniel Kahneman's Talks at Google lecture on his book Thinking, Fast and Slow, covering System 1 and System 2 thinking and the psychology of judgment and decision making.
videos.w: Recommended as a one-hour substitute for the book's opening chapters for those short on time.
videos.q: If you're short on time, watch Kahneman's talk at Google, which basically summarizes the first chapter or so.

videos.t: Using Social Media To Cover For Lack Of Original Thought - Onion Talks - Ep. 6
videos.s: A four-minute Onion Talks parody in which a social media consultant pitches never putting any effort into social marketing. It lampoons TED-style talks and marketing consultants.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as the Onion Talks parody most relevant to tech and startup culture.
videos.q: I think the social media Onion talk ( ) is the most relevant to HN (and my favourite).

videos.t: World’s Best Speakers!
videos.s: Tech Ingredients shows how to build flat panel speakers from exciters and foam board, with construction guidelines, measured SPL comparisons and a complete system playing music.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a build guide for cheap DIY speakers that sound as good as expensive ones.
videos.q: I built my own speakers for under $200 and I honestly think they are some of the best I've ever heard for a personal setup.

videos.t: Stargate Studios Virtual Backlot Reel 2009
videos.s: Stargate Studios' 2009 virtual backlot reel shows before-and-after shots in which green screen and compositing replace locations in ordinary TV dramas and comedies. It shows how much of a seemingly real show is computer generated.
videos.w: HN points to it as a demo of how routinely mundane TV scenes use green screen set replacement, even on TV budgets.
videos.q: This is an amazing demo reel of effects shots used in "mundane" TV shows

videos.t: Run containers on bare metal already!
videos.s: Bryan Cantrill's Velocity NYC 2015 talk argues for running containers directly on bare metal rather than layering them on virtual machines. He covers the history of containers and how SmartOS runs Linux workloads via syscall emulation.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an engaging and informative explanation of why containers on VMs waste resources and hurt performance.
videos.q: he's an extremely engaging speaker, so not only are you likely to watch all of that 40 minute talk

videos.t: Tesla Model 3: Inside & Out - Autoline After Hours 417
videos.s: An Autoline After Hours episode with teardown expert Sandy Munro and a panel of auto journalists. It covers his Tesla Model 3 teardown, including the battery, drive modules, build quality and manufacturing automation.
videos.w: Commenters link it in Tesla threads as an informed, hands-on engineering view of the Model 3 and its manufacturing.
videos.q: If you're interested, this video is great

videos.t: Programming is terrible—Lessons learned from a life wasted. EMF2012
videos.s: Tef's EMF 2012 talk on lessons from a career in programming, a candid and humorous look at why programming is so often terrible. Slides and a draft script are available online.
videos.w: HN lists it among its favorite programming talks and fantastic technical speeches.
videos.q: Both of these talks are in my top 5.

videos.t: Climbing SOLO with Alex Honnold   **INSANE EXPERIENCE**
videos.s: Norwegian climber Magnus Midtbo spends a day climbing with Alex Honnold on exposed routes, shot as a vlog. The video shows the stark contrast between Midtbo's visible nerves and Honnold's calm.
videos.w: Recommended for conveying viscerally just how exceptional Honnold's composure is compared to other elite climbers.
videos.q: I need to share a video [0] which helped contextualize Alex Honnold for me

videos.t: A New History for Humanity – The Human Era
videos.s: Kurzgesagt explains the Holocene or Human Era calendar, which adds 10,000 years to the current year to anchor dates to the start of human civilization. It argues this gives a more sensible frame for human history.
videos.w: Linked whenever year numbering or the Holocene calendar comes up as the accessible introduction to the idea.
videos.q: Kurtzgesagt has a really great video about the subject

videos.t: Pi and the Mandelbrot Set - Numberphile
videos.s: Numberphile with Dr Holly Krieger shows how the digits of pi surprisingly emerge from the Mandelbrot set. A short, accessible math explainer.
videos.w: Recommended whenever the Mandelbrot set comes up, as a neat and surprising result.
videos.q: My absolute favorite numberphile video is how pi occurs in a peculiar way with Riemann Zeta/Mandelbrot.

videos.t: Google I/O 2013 - High Performance Audio
videos.s: A Google I/O 2013 talk by Android audio engineers on why reliable, low-latency audio is hard on the platform. It covers problem areas across the stack, platform work underway and techniques apps can use.
videos.w: Treated as the definitive explanation of Android's audio latency problem, showing it spans the entire stack.
videos.q: is a must-watch

videos.t: James Mickens on JavaScript
videos.s: James Mickens delivers his comedic rant about JavaScript and web programming, in his usual dry, hyperbolic style. It includes his account of learning the language from the O'Reilly Definitive Guide.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a hilarious talk by a beloved speaker, and also uses it to jab at JavaScript's quirks.
videos.q: James Mickens is a national treasure. Go watch his talks on YouTube and read everything he writes.

videos.t: CppCon 2016: Dan Saks “extern c: Talking to C Programmers about C++”
videos.s: Dan Saks's CppCon 2016 talk on why C programmers resist C++ and how to talk to them about it. He argues that persuasion rarely works by arguing and examines the culture gap between the two communities.
videos.w: Recommended in C versus C++ and embedded threads as the expert view on adoption and persuasion.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: The mentioned cppcon presentation by Dan Saks is awesome. Highly recommend watching even if you are not interested in C or C++

videos.t: Oswald Acted Alone: JFK Assassination Solved (Part 1 of 2)
videos.s: The first part of a long two-part video series by historian Sean Munger arguing, with citations, that Lee Harvey Oswald assassinated President Kennedy and acted alone. It goes through the provable historical facts and addresses conspiracy theories.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as the most exhaustive, well-sourced rebuttal of JFK conspiracy theories, often when new assassination claims surface.
videos.q: there's an exhaustive two part series by Sean Munger that sets out the many interlocking lines of evidence that Oswald acted alone.

videos.t: Saving Voyager 1! - Bruce Waggoner at !!Con 2024
videos.s: Bruce Waggoner of the Voyager team describes how engineers diagnosed Voyager 1's 2023 loss of telemetry and patched its flight software from 15 billion miles away. The talk covers the spacecraft's architecture and the scarcity of old documentation.
videos.w: Recommended as an amazing blind-debugging story with deep detail on 1970s spacecraft computing.
videos.q: The talk is amazing and goes through the computer architecture of the spacecraft

videos.t: RSA ANIMATE: The Divided Brain
videos.s: An RSA Animate summary of Iain McGilchrist's lecture on the divided brain, arguing the brain's two hemispheres attend to the world differently and that this has shaped culture and society.
videos.w: Recommended as an accessible animated introduction to McGilchrist's thesis on hemispheres and narrow versus diffuse attention.
videos.q: This entire video is really excellent

videos.t: The 1751 Machine that Made Everything
videos.s: Machine Thinking argues the 1751 machine, a metal-cutting lathe associated with Vaucanson, triggered the biggest explosion of wealth in history by enabling precise manufacturing of other machines.
videos.w: HN recommends the channel and this video as an explanation of how machine tools enabled modern manufacturing.
videos.q: Also Machine Thinking's videos "The 1751 Machine that Made Everything

videos.t: Donald B. Gillies Lecture: Dr. Michael Stonebraker
videos.c: Siebel School of Computing and Data Science
videos.s: Turing Award winner Michael Stonebraker gives the 2018 Donald B. Gillies Memorial Lecture at Illinois. He discusses the gap between academic research and industry problems, publishing incentives, and the influence of large industry users on research.
videos.w: Cited in many threads about academic incentives, paper counts and why academia struggles to produce working software.
videos.q: There's a lot more, I highly recommend the talk!

videos.t: Do we need Attention? - Linear RNNs and State Space Models (SSMs) for NLP
videos.s: Sasha Rush surveys linear RNNs and state space models as replacements for attention in transformer-style models, in a talk for MLSys. It covers the foundational preliminaries and predates Mamba.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it for building intuition about state space models and the tradeoffs between transformer and SSM layers.
videos.q: I highly recommend Sasha Rush's video on it

videos.t: The Why, What, and How of Pinning in Rust
videos.s: Jon Gjengset's long live-coding stream explains Rust's Pin and Unpin types: why they exist, how they work, and how they connect to futures and async/await. It also covers moving from pre-pinning code to the new model.
videos.w: HN treats it as the definitive resource for understanding Pin semantics and lists it among async Rust learning materials.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: Jon Gjengset's stream on pin/unpin is invaluable for understanding Pin semantics

videos.t: A Narrative History of BSD, Dr. Kirk McKusick
videos.s: Kirk McKusick gives a narrative history of BSD from its start at UC Berkeley in the late 1970s through the 1980s releases and the lawsuit that led to 4.4BSD-Lite in 1992. It is full of anecdotes from a key developer.
videos.w: Recommended as an engaging, non-technical history of Unix and BSD from someone who was there, and cited for specific stories like the TCP/IP stack.
videos.q: but the whole thing is excellent.

videos.t: 8-bit CPU control logic: Part 1
videos.s: Ben Eater writes a program in a made-up machine language and walks through the control logic an 8-bit breadboard CPU needs to execute it. It is part of his build-an-8-bit-computer series.
videos.w: Recommended as the key video for understanding control logic and microcode.
videos.q: If you only have a limited amount of time I would highly recommend the control logic video

videos.t: Prius Hybrid Drive Explained
videos.s: A Blender-animated explanation of the Toyota Hybrid Synergy Drive, showing how the engine, two motor-generators, planetary gearset and battery work together as an eCVT.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the clearest visual explanation of how the Prius power-split hybrid actually works.
videos.q: here’s a great video explaining how it really works. It blew my mind...

videos.t: How to Speed up a Python Program 114,000 times.
videos.s: David Schachter describes how he made a data-collection Python program run 114,000 times faster, drawing on decades of experience. The talk covers pipelining, cache effects and other optimization lessons.
videos.w: A favorite tech talk on HN for showing that hardware knowledge and generalist skills beat simply adding machines.
videos.q: Humour, serious technical insight and a good reminder of why being a generalist is an advantage.

videos.t: 35C3 -  The Ghost in the Machine
videos.s: Joscha Bach's 35C3 talk offers an AI perspective on the soul, covering perception, mental representation, agency, consciousness and selfhood as things that can arise in a computational system like the brain.
videos.w: HN commenters call it lucid and fluff-free, and point to Bach as one of the most interesting voices on AI, consciousness and philosophy.
videos.q: the whole talk is incredibly lucid and contains zero fluff or BS

videos.t: 1,500 Slot Machines Walk into a Bar: Adventures in Quantity Over Quality
videos.s: In this 2019 GDC talk, Alex Schwartz and Ziba Scott explain how they flooded the app stores with over 1,500 auto-generated slot machine games to find the lowest bar for success. They tour the dark side of the mobile app market.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a hilarious account of mass-produced app store shovelware and cite it in threads on spam and low-quality content.
videos.q: They procedurally generated 1,500+ different iterations on top of the same Unity-based slots shovelware using noun/adjective pairs.

videos.t: The Commodordion
videos.s: Linus Akesson demonstrates the Commodordion, a fully functional 8-bit accordion built around Commodore 64 hardware with bellows made of floppy disks. He performs Scott Joplin's Maple Leaf Rag and tells the story of the build.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as the work of an unusually creative artist-engineer whose whole channel is worth exploring.
videos.q: This dude's work is incredible. His entire YouTube channel is amazing.

videos.t: THIS IS WATER! by David Foster Wallace
videos.s: A short video of David Foster Wallace's 'This Is Water' commencement speech about awareness and choosing how to think. It argues that the most obvious realities are the hardest to see, using the fish-in-water parable.
videos.w: HN commenters bring it up when urging empathy, patience and attention to the everyday instead of snap judgement.
videos.q: suggest you watch David Foster Wallace's "This is Water," and when you're done, please watch it again.

videos.t: Handmade Hero Day 001 - Setting Up the Windows Build
videos.s: Day 1 of Casey Muratori's Handmade Hero, a live-coded game built from scratch in C on Windows. It reviews C on Windows, sets up a minimal build system and WinMain entry point, and shows a first MessageBox.
videos.w: HN recommends the series as a thorough look at low-level game programming by someone with deep knowledge, offered free.
videos.q: the amount of knowledge and experience on-show was incredible

videos.t: Bret Victor - Drawing Dynamic Visualizations
videos.s: Bret Victor's talk on Drawing Dynamic Visualizations. It argues that visualization tools offer either the directness of hand drawing or the dynamics of programmed graphics, and shows a tool that combines both.
videos.w: Counted among Bret Victor's best talks and recommended to anyone exploring direct-manipulation tools.
videos.q: My favorite Bret Victor talk ever is

videos.t: Deepmind artificial intelligence @ FDOT14
videos.s: A short smartphone-recorded clip from a 2014 event in Paris where DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis presents an AI learning to play old Atari games. The system learns from only the video signal and the score. Audio quality is poor.
videos.w: HN commenters use it as the canonical demo of deep reinforcement learning, noting that watching it teaches more than an article does.
videos.q: you learn more about the tech from a youtube video than from an article

videos.t: GPT-4chan: This is the worst AI ever
videos.s: Yannic Kilcher explains how he trained a language model on three years of 4chan's /pol/ board and let it post on the site. He evaluates how good the model was and discusses the ethics and fallout.
videos.w: HN points to it as the definitive account of the GPT-4chan experiment, used in debates on LLM bias, truthfulness and bots.
videos.q: might be the coolest thing an LLM has ever done on video

videos.t: MountainWest RubyConf 2014 - But Really, You Should Learn Smalltalk
videos.s: Noel Rappin's MountainWest RubyConf talk introduces Smalltalk to Ruby programmers. He compares the two languages' object models, blocks, 1-based arrays, simple syntax and live programming environment, and walks through sample code.
videos.w: HN commenters point Rubyists and the Smalltalk-curious to it as an approachable introduction that shows the Smalltalk system browser and Pharo environment in action.
videos.q: if you enjoy Ruby, watch this

videos.t: A4 / V2 Rocket in detail: Turbopump
videos.s: A very long, detailed look at the A4/V2 rocket turbopump, the steam-turbine-driven twin propellant pump system. It covers the peroxide and permanganate catalysis that drives the turbine. This is part 1 of a series on V2 components.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend the series for its in-depth, hands-on explanation of how V2 turbopumps and peroxide decomposition work.
videos.q: this series of videos is definitely worth watching

videos.t: Colonel JD AI Codec Conversation MGS2 HD
videos.s: The final codec conversation from Metal Gear Solid 2, in which the AI 'Colonel' explains that the Patriots filter out junk information and curate truth for humanity. It plays as a dark meditation on information overload, manipulation and shared reality.
videos.w: Commenters point to it whenever AI-generated content, propaganda or internet garbage comes up, since Kojima seemed to predict it in 2001.
videos.q: You should play Metal Gear Solid 2, or at least watch the last codec call[1].

videos.t: Conlang Critic Episode Twelve: Toki Pona
videos.s: An episode of jan Misali's Conlang Critic series reviewing Toki Pona, a minimalist constructed language with about a hundred words. It is a short, humorous critique of the language's design.
videos.w: Commenters recommend the whole series as an entertaining survey of constructed languages, and this episode when Toki Pona or Lojban comes up.
videos.q: I highly recommend watching all episodes of their show

videos.t: How are holograms possible?
videos.s: 3Blue1Brown explains how holograms record a 3D scene on 2D film, using wave diffraction and phase. The video includes demonstrations of several real holograms.
videos.w: HN commenters call it the best explanation of how holograms work, and one says it transformed their understanding.
videos.q: this might be one of my most favorite videos ever single-handedly changing my understanding of holograms

videos.t: Fun with ultracapacitors!!
videos.s: Afrotechmods plays with 2600F ultracapacitors that can dump hundreds of amps, shorting them to vaporize bits of metal. Along the way he explains the three most important capacitor equations. The uploader warns that the capacitors are not designed to be shorted.
videos.w: HN commenters use it as a vivid, math-backed demonstration of what ultracapacitors can do and why shorting them is dangerous.
videos.q: This video is a good demonstration

videos.t: Abolish Copyrights and Patents? A Soho Forum Debate
videos.s: A Soho Forum debate in which patent lawyer Stephan Kinsella argues for abolishing copyright and patents against law professor Richard Epstein. Both come from libertarian perspectives.
videos.w: HN points to it as a substantive debate on intellectual property from two libertarian angles, with Kinsella as the abolitionist voice.
videos.q: Here is a debate on IP with two different libertarian perspective

videos.t: DEF CON 22 - Adrian Crenshaw- Dropping Docs on Darknets: How People Got Caught
videos.s: Adrian Crenshaw's DEF CON 22 talk gives an overview of Tor and I2P, then goes through real cases where darknet users were caught. These include Silk Road and its operator.
videos.w: HN points to it to show that most Tor busts came from poor operational security by the user rather than a flaw in Tor itself.
videos.q: in most of the cases, it was bad OpsSec by the person, and had nothing to do with Tor

videos.t: Paul Buchheit at Startup School 08
videos.s: Paul Buchheit, creator of Gmail and founder of FriendFeed, speaks at Startup School 08 about listening to users. He covers feedback, features, aiming for 100 happy users, and treating "that's impossible" as a statement of limited experience.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it for its memorable lines on advice, limited experience and early user focus, and rewatch it as a reminder not to be prescriptive.
videos.q: I watch the video every once in a while to remind myself not to be similarly prescriptive

videos.t: How Does SHA-256 Work?
videos.s: A step-by-step animated explanation of how SHA-256 works, from padding and message schedule to the compression function and final hash, with source code for the animations.
videos.w: Commenters call it clear enough to implement the algorithm from, and teachers use it in courses.
videos.q: I found this video to be an excellent explanation and sufficient to implement the algorithm

videos.t: Why Do Reversing Trucks Not Beep Any More?
videos.s: Tom Scott stands by a construction site and explains why reversing vehicles now use a white-noise hiss instead of beeping. The sound is easier to locate directionally and less annoying to neighbours.
videos.w: Cited whenever backup beepers and noise come up, as a clear explanation of the white-noise alternative.
videos.q: Tom Scott has a fascinating video that describes how this is changing

videos.t: Dune 1984 Alternative Edition Redux edited by Spicediver / Multiple Subs / 4K Upscaling by GW
videos.s: A 4K AI-upscaled, subtitled fan edit of David Lynch's 1984 Dune by Spicediver that restores deleted and lost footage to form an alternative cut.
videos.w: Recommended as the best way to watch Lynch's Dune, closer to his original vision and judged by some the best adaptation of the book.
videos.q: The Spicediver edit of Lynch's Dune proved to me that Dune is filmable. I think it remains the best adaptation of Dune.

videos.t: What 40,000 Videos Tell Us About The Trending Tab
videos.s: Coffee Break analyzes about 40,000 videos from seven months of YouTube's trending tab. It examines whether trending is biased toward mainstream media and late-night shows.
videos.w: Cited in threads on YouTube algorithms and creator complaints as a data-driven look at the trending tab.
videos.q: Here's an excellent video breaking down with extremely compelling data how the "trending" tab is very heavily manipulated

videos.t: Chernobyl 3828
videos.s: A Ukrainian documentary about the liquidators who cleaned radioactive debris off the Chernobyl reactor roof in two-minute shifts. It presents their firsthand accounts and footage of the work.
videos.w: Recommended as a moving, first-person account of the people who dealt with the worst of the Chernobyl cleanup.
videos.q: Chernobyl 3828 is about the people

videos.t: Moneyball - Firing people
videos.s: A short Moneyball clip showing a manager telling a player he has been cut, directly and without softening the news.
videos.w: HN points to it as a model for firing or laying off people clearly and respectfully.
videos.q: This is probably the greatest video clip on the subject of all time

videos.t: The Internet is Worse Than Ever – Now What?
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt video arguing that social media's problem is information flooding and tribal polarization. It suggests a return to smaller online communities and more in-person interaction.
videos.w: HN recommends it in threads about dying forums and social media as a lens on why smaller communities suit us better.
videos.q: I view social media through this lens now.

videos.t: 27c3: Reverse Engineering the MOS 6502 CPU (en)
videos.s: Michael Steil's 27c3 talk on reverse engineering the MOS 6502 from die shots into a transistor-level simulation, as in the Visual6502 project. It covers going from chip package to a digital model.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a great walkthrough of chip reverse engineering and the story of Visual 6502.
videos.q: This is a great presentation showing how this CPU is reverse engineered

videos.t: How the Higgs Mechanism Give Things Mass
videos.s: A PBS Space Time episode on how the Higgs mechanism gives particles mass, prompted by Fermilab's heavier-than-expected W boson measurement. It goes beyond the usual pop-science treatment without heavy math.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the best non-mathematical explanation of the Higgs field, deep but accessible to lay viewers.
videos.q: about as deep as a lay audience can hope to surmount

videos.t: [CVPR'21 WAD] Keynote - Andrej Karpathy, Tesla
videos.s: Andrej Karpathy, then Tesla's head of AI, gives a CVPR 2021 workshop keynote on how Autopilot's neural networks work. A large part covers the move to a vision-only stack, including why radar was dropped and how vision produces depth estimates.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it in Tesla threads as the primary-source explanation of why Tesla removed radar and how its vision depth estimation works.
videos.q: This talk was worth watching (any Karpathy or Carmack talk is imo)

videos.t: Dominic Frisby. A simple guide to land value tax
videos.s: Comedian Dominic Frisby gives a ten-minute explanation of land value tax. He argues it would fix problems of rent-seeking and the economics of land ownership.
videos.w: HN users share it as a short, accessible explainer for land value tax whenever housing, rents or inequality come up.
videos.q: Land value tax explained in 10 minutes

videos.t: Travis Oliphant: NumPy, SciPy, Anaconda, Python & Scientific Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #224
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Travis Oliphant, creator of NumPy, SciPy and Anaconda, about scientific Python and its history. It runs about three hours.
videos.w: Recommended as a firsthand history of how Python became the language of scientific computing and ML.
videos.q: I highly recommend this bit of history from NumPy creator Travis Oliphant

videos.t: Sustainable Energy - Without the Hot Air with David MacKay
videos.s: David MacKay, scientific advisor to the UK energy department, gives a Harvard talk on sustainable energy at macro and micro scale, drawn from his book Sustainable Energy Without the Hot Air. It stresses the land area renewables require.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an approachable, numbers-driven overview of what renewable energy would take.
videos.q: The author also gave a talk a few years ago that is very approachable[2].

videos.t: How Airlines Quietly Became Banks
videos.s: A Wendover Productions explainer arguing that major airlines make much of their profit from loyalty programs and co-branded credit cards rather than flying. It frames airlines as quasi-banks that sell points in bulk, using United's pandemic-era loan as a hook.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it whenever airline economics or frequent-flier miles come up, since it clearly shows loyalty programs are worth more than the airlines themselves.
videos.q: Wendover Productions had a good video about this, framed around United getting a loan during the pandemic

videos.t: ElixirConf 2023 - José Valim - The foundations of the Elixir type system
videos.s: José Valim's ElixirConf US 2023 closing keynote on the foundations of the Elixir type system, covering set-theoretic types and gradual typing with strong arrows.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the best detailed explanation from the language's creator of how Elixir's new type system works and why.
videos.q: If you're into watching talks, this will be well worth your time.

videos.t: President Trump: How & Why...
videos.s: Jonathan Pie delivers a satirical rant just after the 2016 US election, blaming the political and media establishment for the rise of Trump. It is a short, profane monologue in character as a frustrated reporter.
videos.w: Shared after the 2016 election and later as a pithy account of why Trump won and why political division needs to be moved past.
videos.q: I think Jonathan Pie encapsulated it perfectly just a few days after the election

videos.t: Math Encounters -- Five Balls, Two Hands: The Patterns of Juggling -- Colin Wright (Presentation)
videos.s: Mathematician Colin Wright demonstrates juggling and explains the mathematics of juggling patterns, including notation that led to new throwing patterns. It is a public presentation at the Museum of Mathematics aimed at a general audience.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an entertaining way to learn math through juggling.
videos.q: my fondness for this video that uses juggling to good effect to teach math in an entertaining way

videos.t: Simulating Green Beard Altruism
videos.s: Primer simulates green beard altruism, where individuals recognize and help others carrying a shared marker, and shows how imposters affect its evolution. It is an animated evolution simulation based on published papers.
videos.w: HN recommends it as part of Primer's strong series of evolution and emergence simulations.
videos.q: Primer, who's had a great string of genetic/evolution simulation videos

videos.t: A New Way to look at Networking
videos.s: Van Jacobson's 2006 Google Tech Talk argues for rethinking networking around named data rather than host-to-host connections. He gives the history and the unsolved problems of the current internet architecture.
videos.w: Recommended as the foundational talk on content-centric and named-data networking, and for its internet history stories.
videos.q: There's an old tech talk that got me out of the IP-shaped box a lot of us are trapped in

videos.t: DICKS: Do you need to be one to be a successful leader?
videos.s: Filmmaker Max Joseph's 35-minute video essay asks whether you have to be a jerk to be a successful leader. It draws on Adam Grant's givers and takers, Robert Greene and famous demanding directors.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a thoughtful critique of the great-leader-as-jerk myth in threads on difficult bosses.
videos.q: here's the best video I've found that breaks apart the idea of an "asshole"

videos.t: Robert Sapolsky: The Biology of Humans at Our Best and Worst
videos.s: A 73-minute Stanford talk by Robert Sapolsky drawn from his book Behave. It surveys the biological factors behind human behavior at its best and worst.
videos.w: HN recommends Sapolsky as an exceptional storyteller and points to this lecture on the biology of human behavior and violence.
videos.q: a talk where he explores various physical and environmental factors that influence human actions

videos.t: ClojureScript for Skeptics - Derek Slager
videos.s: Derek Slager's Clojure/conj talk argues that ClojureScript is a pragmatic choice for web development. He addresses common objections, recent improvements, tooling and use cases where it shines.
videos.w: Recommended to JavaScript skeptics as a persuasive case for ClojureScript, covering Closure Compiler optimizations and code-splitting.
videos.q: completely sold me on trying it out

videos.t: Charlie Marsh: uv: An Extremely Fast Python Package Manager
videos.s: Charlie Marsh of Astral explains how uv, a Rust Python package manager, got so fast. He covers allocators, concurrency, zero-copy tricks and the challenges of Python packaging.
videos.w: Recommended as a fascinating technical account of the optimizations behind uv's speed.
videos.q: I recently watched a talk by the author of uv that was surprisingly fascinating

videos.t: ANIME ROCK, PAPER, SCISSORS
videos.s: Corridor Digital makes a roughly seven-minute anime short using Stable Diffusion and related AI tools, based on a technique they teach in a longer tutorial. It was an early showcase of AI-assisted animation.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as an impressive example of what AI animation could do and of VFX artists adopting AI in their workflows.
videos.q: the quality of the animation (modulo some instability in shadows) is mind blowing

videos.t: Steve Jobs' 2005 Stanford Commencement Address (with intro by President John Hennessy)
videos.s: Steve Jobs' 2005 Stanford commencement address, in which he tells three stories from his life about connecting the dots, love and loss, and death. He urges graduates to follow their dreams and find opportunity in setbacks.
videos.w: HN people point to it as an inspiring, rewatchable speech, especially for anyone worrying about wasted time or direction.
videos.q: I try to watch it once a year, especially with grad students and postdocs. Gets better each time.

videos.t: The Concept of Language (Noam Chomsky)
videos.s: Noam Chomsky talks with the University of Washington's Upon Reflection about how languages change over time, why a national language is a modern idea, and how language is a system of communication rooted in human nature.
videos.w: Recommended in threads on language purity and standardization for its clear take that languages are fluid and that national languages are constructed.
videos.q: Here's my favorite talk on the subject given by Chomsky, highly recommend a listen

videos.t: SIGBOVIK 2007: Generalized Super Mario Bros. is NP-Complete
videos.s: Tom Murphy's satirical SIGBOVIK 2007 presentation, delivered under a pseudonym, proving that generalized Super Mario Bros. is NP-complete. It is a short, deadpan take on a complexity theory result.
videos.w: HN likes it as a funny, entertaining presentation, frequently linked in threads on NP-hardness of games and NES automation.
videos.q: This guy is a genius and also freakin hilarious

videos.t: Tim Minchin's Storm the Animated Movie
videos.s: Animated adaptation of Tim Minchin's beat poem 'Storm', in which he argues with a hippie at a London dinner party. It satirizes alternative medicine and defends science and reason.
videos.w: Quoted often for its line on alternative medicine that works being called medicine, and recommended as a full-length listen.
videos.q: The entirety of this song is a listen worth your time.

videos.t: Land of Lisp- The Music Video!
videos.s: A playful music video promoting the book Land of Lisp, with a song about Lisp programming.
videos.w: HN shares it as a fun, cheerful introduction to Lisp culture that people say they rewatch.
videos.q: Land of Lisp is fun, and the video is a must!

videos.t: RSA ANIMATE: First as Tragedy, Then as Farce
videos.s: An RSA Animate adaptation of a Slavoj Zizek talk on charitable giving and ethical consumerism. It argues that buying products that bundle a charity donation can sustain the system that causes the problems.
videos.w: Frequently linked in threads on philanthropy, ethical consumption and billionaire giving as a short, approachable critique of charity.
videos.q: well worth a watch (10 minutes) and approachable by those without philosophical backgrounds

videos.t: America's Iron Giants - The World's Most Powerful Metalworkers
videos.s: Machine Thinking tells the story of the Cold War Heavy Press Program, the giant forging presses that make parts for aircraft, missiles and turbines.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an excellent introduction to massive forging presses, especially in threads about gigacasting and large manufacturing machines.
videos.q: I first learned about these presses several years ago from the YouTube channel Machine Thinking which is excellent and unfortunately infrequent.

videos.t: Couldn't Care Less. Cormac McCarthy in conversation with David Krakauer
videos.s: A 2017 documentary filmed at the Santa Fe Institute in which novelist Cormac McCarthy talks with SFI's David Krakauer. They discuss isolation, mathematics, character and the nature of the unconscious.
videos.w: It is one of the few long, candid interviews with the famously reclusive McCarthy, and commenters share it whenever he comes up.
videos.q: This is my favourite interview with him so I will take this post as an excuse to share it.

videos.t: Flexbox vs. CSS Grid — Which is Better?
videos.s: Jen Simmons explains the difference between CSS Flexbox and CSS Grid, and when to use each. She makes the case that Grid does not replace Flexbox and most sites use both.
videos.w: Recommended as a short, clear rundown of one-dimensional versus two-dimensional layout.
videos.q: Here's a great explanation from Jen Simmons that really helped me understand the differences

videos.t: Work.
videos.s: Historia Civilis traces the history of work and time discipline, comparing modern working hours with those of medieval peasants and the changes brought by clocks and industrialization. It draws on works such as Schor's The Overworked American.
videos.w: HN uses it in work-hours and four-day-week threads as the source for the claim that people worked fewer hours before the industrial era.
videos.q: Here is an excellent video on the history of work.

videos.t: The Perfect Sourdough Pizza (Bread Porn)
videos.s: A short, nearly wordless demonstration of making sourdough pizza at home using a cast iron pan and the oven. It shows a Neapolitan-style result without a pizza steel or stone.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a practical, home-bakable sourdough pizza method that gets close to stone-oven quality.
videos.q: This is the best video on making neapolitan style at home with an cast iron pan and oven

videos.t: The Superheterodyne Radio: No really, that's its name
videos.s: Technology Connections explains why the superheterodyne radio has its name and how mixing frequencies lets it tune stations well. It walks through the underlying wave phenomena and algebra and why the design solved a hard tuning problem.
videos.w: HN people use it as the accessible go-to explainer for the superhet trick whenever radios or signal processing come up.
videos.q: This video is a great explainer (and I also highly recommend every other video on the channel)

videos.t: The Company that Broke Canada
videos.s: BobbyBroccoli documentary on the rise of Nortel Networks, once the dominant Canadian telecom giant, during the dot-com era. It is part one of a two-part story.
videos.w: Recommended as a well-made documentary explaining Nortel's rise and the index-fund and bubble dynamics around it.
videos.q: BobbyBroccoli on YouTube does an absolutely phenomenal job creating documentaries.

videos.t: People & Power - On a wing and a prayer
videos.s: An Al Jazeera English People & Power investigation from 2010 into safety problems with the Boeing 737NG, featuring whistleblowers on cracking parts, hand-made structural components and an alleged cover-up.
videos.w: HN resurfaces it during Boeing safety stories as early, firsthand evidence that production and management problems long predate the 737 Max.
videos.q: Here are gruesome, firsthand details about production and management problems with the 737NG in a documentary from Al Jazeera.

videos.t: Armin Ronacher - A Python for Future Generations
videos.s: Armin Ronacher's EuroPython 2017 keynote examining how the CPython interpreter's leaky abstractions affect language design and how Python could evolve, drawing on JavaScript and Rust experience.
videos.w: Recommended for explaining why Python is hard to optimize and the limits of making it fast.
videos.q: I highly recommend the two videos posted here

videos.t: Every Ruler Makes the Same Mistake When They Die
videos.s: CGP Grey, adapting The Dictator's Handbook, explains how rulers keep power and why succession causes trouble when they die. It is the sequel to his video on the rules for rulers.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a 101-level crash course on the keys to power, and says it changed how some viewers see political discourse.
videos.q: The 101-level crash-course on this is CGP Grey's video Death & Dynasties

videos.t: Do schools kill creativity? | Sir Ken Robinson | TED
videos.s: Sir Ken Robinson argues, with humor and stories such as that of choreographer Gillian Lynne, that education systems undermine creativity and should be changed. It is one of the most viewed TED talks.
videos.w: HN refers to it constantly in schooling debates, as a favorite talk or as the basis for arguments about creativity, though some commenters dispute its conclusions.
videos.q: I love this Ted talk

videos.t: How an Average Family in Tokyo Can Buy a New Home
videos.s: A mini-documentary by a Canadian living in Japan explaining how an average family can afford a new detached house in Tokyo. It covers how houses are treated as depreciating assets and how Japanese zoning and building practices keep prices low.
videos.w: It is the standard citation in HN housing debates for showing that dense cities can still have affordable single-family homes.
videos.q: a fantastic overview of housing for a nuclear family in Tokyo

videos.t: Gradient descent, how neural networks learn | Deep Learning Chapter 2
videos.s: 3Blue1Brown's second neural network chapter explains cost functions and gradient descent, showing how a network learns by minimizing error during training.
videos.w: HN recommends the series as a very accessible way to understand the math behind machine learning and LLMs.
videos.q: 3Blue1Brown which explains math in very accessible way

videos.t: Playing to Lose: AI and "Civilization" (Soren Johnson)
videos.s: Soren Johnson, a lead designer and AI programmer on Civilization games, discusses game AI design, including whether AI should cheat, behave like a human or be fun rather than strong. He uses the Civilization series as a case study.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as the key talk on why game AI is built to be fun rather than to win.
videos.q: Extremely enlightening, whether you are a gamer or not.

videos.t: Lecture 1 | The Theoretical Minimum
videos.s: Leonard Susskind opens Stanford Continuing Studies' Theoretical Minimum series with an introduction to quantum mechanics, a course for people who want real physics rather than popularization. It assumes some calculus and linear algebra.
videos.w: HN recommends the series as an entertaining, serious route into physics for self-learners comfortable with basic math.
videos.q: And he's entertaining as hell.

videos.t: Christopher Tin - Baba Yetu (Official Video) feat. Soweto Gospel Choir
videos.s: The official video for Baba Yetu, Christopher Tin's Swahili-language choral piece written as the theme to Civilization IV. It was the first video game music to win a Grammy.
videos.w: HN commenters hold it up as the greatest video game song, evoking wonder and pride in humanity.
videos.q: What about the greatest video game song ever produced (Baba Yetu)

videos.t: Will AI outsmart human intelligence? - with 'Godfather of AI' Geoffrey Hinton
videos.s: Geoffrey Hinton's 2025 Royal Institution Discourse on what AI has learned from biological intelligence and how it might surpass it. He explains neural networks and argues that human language use resembles what backpropagation-trained networks do.
videos.w: HN readers recommend it as an intuitive explanation of neural networks that shifts how people think about AI and language.
videos.q: Richard Sutton takes a different view in an interview with Dwarkesh Patel[2]

videos.t: The Incredible Sounds of the Falcon Heavy Launch (BINAURAL AUDIO IMMERSION) - Smarter Every Day 189
videos.s: Smarter Every Day shares a binaural audio recording of the SpaceX Falcon Heavy launch made by Trevor Mahlmann, with explanations of the sounds including the sonic booms of the landing boosters. It is meant to be heard with headphones.
videos.w: Recommended in launch threads as an immersive way to hear what a Falcon Heavy launch actually sounds like.
videos.q: the sonic booms of the boosters coming into land are amazing, listen with headphones!

videos.t: How does a Bowling Pinsetter Machine work? (Brunswick GS-X)
videos.s: Jared Owen's 3D animated breakdown of how a Brunswick GS-X bowling pinsetter works, showing its mechanisms for sweeping, lifting and resetting pins and balls.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an exceptionally well-made explainer of complex mechanical machinery.
videos.q: some of the best I've ever seen, and relatively recent.

videos.t: Who Is Responsible For Climate Change? – Who Needs To Fix It?
videos.s: Kurzgesagt examines who is responsible for climate change, comparing historical, current and per-capita emissions by country. It argues that individual footprints are a distraction from larger responsibility.
videos.w: Recommended as a nuanced, data-backed treatment of emissions responsibility, made with Our World in Data.
videos.q: Perhaps you and they should watch the Kurzgesagt video made in conjunction with Our World in Data

videos.t: They Shall Not Grow Old – New Trailer – Now Playing In Theaters
videos.s: The trailer for Peter Jackson's They Shall Not Grow Old, a WWI documentary built from restored, colorized archival footage and BBC interviews with British soldiers.
videos.w: HN points to it as a way to see WWI footage restored so the war feels modern and real.
videos.q: It's really incredible and makes the war (which was only 100 years ago) feel much more modern than old black and white footage.

videos.t: Why The World Relies On ASML For Machines That Print Chips
videos.s: CNBC gets a tour of ASML's cleanrooms in the Netherlands to see how its roughly $200 million EUV lithography machines are built. It covers exploding molten tin, ultra-flat optics and why only one company can make these systems.
videos.w: Frequently recommended as a good, approachable overview of ASML and semiconductor equipment.
videos.q: Good video on ASML and semiconductor fabrication equipment in general

videos.t: Future Crew - Second Reality (1993) [60fps]
videos.s: A 60fps capture of Future Crew's 1993 MS-DOS demo Second Reality, one of the best-known pieces of the demoscene. It runs about 16 minutes of real-time graphics and music effects on PC hardware of the era.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as the landmark demo of the demoscene's golden era, and this capture lets people watch it without running it under DOS.
videos.q: Future Crew's 2nd Reality demo, for those that haven't seen it

videos.t: Nokia Morph Concept (long)
videos.s: A concept video from Nokia Research Center and Cambridge Nanoscience Center showing Morph, a flexible, self-cleaning, shape-changing phone imagined through nanotechnology.
videos.w: HN brings it up as a nostalgic, exciting concept in threads on foldable phones and design, and sometimes as an example of concept videos that never shipped.
videos.q: I have just watched the video about it [2] again and I am still as excited about it as I was 11 years ago.

videos.t: ai.bythebay.io: George Hotz, Self-Driving Lessons from Comma AI
videos.s: George Hotz of Comma AI gives a 2017 conference talk on lessons from building a self-driving system. He argues about how driving should be defined and why the common approach to autonomous vehicles is flawed.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a candid, contrarian view of self-driving approaches and the real limits of the business.
videos.q: George Hotz has a killer talk about why the general approach to autonomous vehicles is flawed. I highly recommend it.

videos.t: A Complete Beginner's Guide to Electric Vehicles
videos.s: Technology Connections' hour-long guide to electric vehicles, covering costs, trade-offs and especially how little home charging power most drivers need.
videos.w: Recommended as an entertaining, in-depth beginner's guide that persuades skeptics that a wall outlet often suffices.
videos.q: I was particularly swayed by the technology connections video on this topic I watched before buying my first EV

videos.t: Bruce Hauman - Developing ClojureScript With Figwheel
videos.s: Bruce Hauman presents Figwheel, a ClojureScript tool for live, interactive development with hot code reloading. He explains the main ideas, demonstrates how it works, and shares tricks for getting the most out of it.
videos.w: HN people point to it as a very visual demonstration of what hot-reloading and interactive development can offer, and as an example of a great dev tool pitch.
videos.q: it's a very visual demonstration of what hot-reloading code and interactive development can bring

videos.t: The Ultimate AeroPress Technique (Episode #3)
videos.s: James Hoffmann demonstrates his AeroPress technique with a short recipe: 11g of coffee, 200g of just-boiled water, a 2-minute immersion, then a press. He explains why he skips rinsing, preheating and inverting.
videos.w: HN coffee fans cite it as a forgiving, repeatable recipe that gives good results.
videos.q: I've found James Hoffman's aeropress technique to be fantastic though and much more repeatable

videos.t: The "Last Lecture" by Randy Pausch
videos.s: Randy Pausch, a Carnegie Mellon computer scientist and virtual reality pioneer who was dying of cancer, gives his 'Last Lecture' about achieving childhood dreams and living well. The recording is a full-length talk of about 104 minutes.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an emotionally powerful life-advice talk and revisit it as a reminder of mortality.
videos.q: I often times revisit Randy Pausch's The Last Lecture[1] to act as a memento mori[2].

videos.t: Pipe Organ (5-story instrument)
videos.s: Rob Scallon explores a five-story pipe organ, the largest in the Midwest, with organist John Sherer. The half-hour tour covers most of the instrument and how it works.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an engaging look at how an organ works as a whole orchestra, in threads about organs and live-coding them.
videos.q: You'll want to give a watch

videos.t: Ricardo Signes - 闇のEメール伝説
videos.s: Ricardo Signes' YAPC::Asia Tokyo 2011 talk on the legends and horrors of email: how messy the SMTP and email standards are in practice. The first few minutes are Perl-specific, but the rest applies to anyone handling email.
videos.w: HN points people to it as a funny and sobering warning about why parsing, validating, or implementing email software is far harder than it looks.
videos.q: There is is awesome talk about E-Mail by Ricardo Signes

videos.t: New Horizons in Music: Polyrhythms | Loop
videos.s: Adam Neely's Ableton Loop 2017 talk links rhythm, pitch and synaesthesia. He shows that polyrhythms sped up become chords, so tempo and pitch are related by ratios.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for the mind-blowing connection between rhythm and pitch and as an approachable intro to music theory.
videos.q: Highly recommend Adam's channel if you're interested in music/music theory.

videos.t: WordTeX - A WYSIPCTWOTCG Typesetting Tool
videos.s: Tom Wildenhain's SIGBOVIK 2018 presentation of WordTeX, a Microsoft Word template that mimics LaTeX typesetting output. It is a joke research project executed with serious effort.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as an entertaining example of great effort on a trivial problem, and cite the template in LaTeX-versus-Word discussions.
videos.q: this one on WordTeX is excellent

videos.t: Sega Saturn CD - Cracked after 20 years
videos.s: A look inside Dr Abrasive's lab as he engineers a flash-card replacement for the Sega Saturn optical drive after cracking its CD protection 20 years on.
videos.w: Recommended as an inspiring story of hardware reverse engineering and persistence.
videos.q: Related and _very_ inspiring; how the Sega Saturn CD was cracked after 20 years.

videos.t: Gambling and the desire machine | Pay to Win
videos.s: A 70-minute video essay by Jimmy McGee on gambling, addiction and game design, tracing horse racing, slot machines and collectible card markets. It is the first in a series on making money from games.
videos.w: Recommended as an engaging, well-researched look at the history of gambling machines and how games borrow their psychology.
videos.q: it's a genuinely interesting exploration on the murky history of video games and gambling

videos.t: Revolution OS
videos.s: Revolution OS is a feature-length documentary on the history of free software and Linux. It covers Stallman and the GNU project, Torvalds and the kernel, and Raymond and Perens on open source, starting from the era of freely shared hobbyist code.
videos.w: Recommended as the standard documentary on the origins of GNU, the FSF and Linux.
videos.q: For those that haven't seen Revolution OS I would highly recommend it for much of the Linux backstory.

videos.t: - Startups - David H. Hansson, Partner at 37signals -TWiST #E337
videos.s: A This Week in Startups episode in which Jason Calacanis interviews David Heinemeier Hansson of 37signals. They discuss bootstrapping, company philosophy and views on the tech industry.
videos.w: Recommended to understand what the 37signals founders stand for and DHH's contrarian takes on tech business.
videos.q: People, please watch these few videos to genuinely understand what 37Signal guys (David and Jason) stand for

videos.t: The Untold Story of Online Gaming on Super Nintendo and Sega Genesis | XBAND
videos.s: A one-hour documentary on XBAND, the 1994 modem network for the Super Nintendo and Sega Genesis. It covers matchmaking, chat, email, leaderboards and how games were patched at runtime to cope with lag.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a fascinating engineering story of early console online play, including a working demo.
videos.q: Well worth watching.

videos.t: How the Fed's "Money Printer" Really Works
videos.s: Ben Felix explains how central bank money creation and quantitative easing actually work, and what they do and do not imply for asset prices and currency. He addresses the common belief that the Fed prints unlimited money and props up markets.
videos.w: HN users point to it to correct the 'money printer go brrr' view and as a clear explanation of how banks create money through loans.
videos.q: Highly recommend this video to understand and this channel in general

videos.t: Lecture 1: Probability and Counting | Statistics 110
videos.s: Lecture 1 of Harvard's Statistics 110 with Joe Blitzstein, introducing sample spaces, the naive definition of probability, counting, binomial coefficients and the sampling table.
videos.w: Recommended on Ask HN threads as a high-quality free probability course for relearning math or building an ML foundation.
videos.q: I have used and can vouch for the high quality of all of them

videos.t: Bill Hicks - It's Just A Ride
videos.s: A short clip from Bill Hicks' final special, Revelations, in which he describes life as just a ride. It is a philosophical, calming monologue.
videos.w: Offered as a pick-me-up and calming perspective when people feel lost or stressed.
videos.q: Whenever I find myself feeling like you do right now, I watch this video from Bill Hicks

videos.t: Clean Disruption - Why Energy & Transportation will be Obsolete by 2030 - Oslo, March 2016
videos.s: Tony Seba's 2016 keynote argues that batteries, electric vehicles, self-driving cars and solar will converge to disrupt energy and transportation. He predicts by 2030 all new vehicles will be electric and autonomous and that oil and other fossil fuels will be obsolete.
videos.w: Cited as a well-argued case that solar plus batteries and EVs will reach a tipping point sooner than mainstream forecasts expect.
videos.q: the linked reference is a well argued version of the near future of transportation and energy. Highly recommended

videos.t: 2017 Personality 01: Introduction
videos.s: The opening lecture of Jordan Peterson's 2017 University of Toronto personality course. He defines personality from historical, constructivist, psychoanalytic, behavioral and neuropsychological angles.
videos.w: Recommended as part of a long lecture series on psychology, complementing biology lectures, and named when HN asks for the best lecture series.
videos.q: the original Personality Lectures (2017) of Jordan Peterson are really great.

videos.t: Snarky Puppy - Lingus (We Like It Here)
videos.s: A live, overdub-free performance of 'Lingus' by Snarky Puppy, from the 'We Like It Here' DVD recorded in Utrecht. It features a Cory Henry keyboard solo.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend Snarky Puppy as proof that vibrant, progressive modern jazz is being made today.
videos.q: I highly recommend anything by Snarky Puppy.

videos.t: Here's What's Preventing You From Finishing Projects
videos.s: Zack Freedman gives advice on why makers fail to finish projects, including scrapping bad ideas, showing work publicly and writing a plan that keeps projects fun. It is aimed at hardware DIY but generalizes.
videos.w: HN finds the project-scoping rubric useful for programmers too and recommends it on finishing side projects.
videos.q: the rubric he uses is sound for programmer-y stuff too

videos.t: Steve Jobs Content vs Process
videos.s: A three-minute clip of Steve Jobs arguing that great products come from people who care about content rather than process. He says process-focused people take over and cause decline, citing IBM as an example.
videos.w: Quoted whenever HN discusses process-heavy management and companies losing their product focus.
videos.q: I wish more leaders understood this.

videos.t: The Biggest Misconception in Physics
videos.s: Veritasium explores why energy is not conserved in general relativity, using Emmy Noether's theorem linking symmetries to conservation laws. Physicists interviewed explain energy loss in an expanding universe.
videos.w: Recommended as high-quality physics communication and as an introduction to Noether and energy non-conservation in cosmology.
videos.q: thought wow this is good. Much better than the physics lectures I had at Cambridge Uni.

videos.t: John Carmack Tech Talk with UMKC-SCE
videos.c: UMKC School of Science and Engineering
videos.s: John Carmack speaks at UMKC's 2017 commencement event about the difficulties of VR, especially end-to-end latency across hardware and software. He covers why latency and buffering matter and how nausea is addressed.
videos.w: Recommended whenever latency, buffering or VR comfort comes up, as an accessible account from someone who dealt with it directly.
videos.q: a lecture where he describes the difficulties in VR in a manner that anybody with minimal programming experience can understand

videos.t: BOOKSTORES: How to Read More Books in the Golden Age of Content
videos.s: A short film by Max Joseph about his anxiety in bookstores and how to read more books amid constant streaming, social media and news. He looks for ways to rebalance his content diet in favor of reading.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as a thoughtful mini-doc on reading time and frequency in the age of social media.
videos.q: it's an interesting exploration of modern bookstores and the dynamics of reading as a pursuit in the age of social media

videos.t: Dr Russell Barkley on ADHD Meds and how they all work differently from each other
videos.s: Dr. Russell Barkley explains how different ADHD medications work and how they differ from one another, in a short clip.
videos.w: HN recommends Barkley as the best resource on ADHD, with clear explanations of what prescription ADHD drugs do.
videos.q: Dr. Russell Barkley has good explanations of what different prescription ADHD drugs do

videos.t: "Devs Play" S1E06 - Psychonauts "The SMK Speedrun" [1/1]
videos.s: In the finale of Double Fine's Devs Play, speedrunner SMK demonstrates glitches and exploits that skip entire sections of Psychonauts while Tim Schafer and the dev team watch. The developers react to and discuss the bugs as they appear.
videos.w: Recommended as an entertaining, hilarious view of developers watching a speedrunner break their game.
videos.q: They had a speedrunner running their game in front of the development team which is hilarious.

videos.t: New computers don't speed up old code
videos.s: Matthias Wandel tests old and new code on a range of PCs, including a new mini PC, to measure how much faster modern hardware really is. He also shows optimization techniques such as branchless code, with benchmark programs on GitHub.
videos.w: Used as evidence that CPU speed for branchy, dependent code has improved only modestly in 15-20 years, so software optimization matters.
videos.q: This great video [0] demonstrates how CPU performance has only increased 1.5-2x over the past 15(!) years when executing extremely branchy code.

videos.t: Safe Cycling Showdown - Good vs. Bad City Design - Plus 1 Minus 2
videos.s: Not Just Bikes compares the same cycling trip to a hardware store in Calgary and in Amsterdam, using a 'plus 1 minus 2' format. It shows how street design shapes how safe and practical cycling is.
videos.w: HN recommends the channel for understanding why North American road design makes cycling dangerous and how the Dutch approach differs.
videos.q: Watch the bicycle infrastructure get better as he get out into the Amsterdam suburbs.

videos.t: The Stealership Trap - Why We Need the Dealership "Rip Off"
videos.s: FortNine explains the economics of the dealership model, arguing that dealers absorb inventory risk and help manufacturers' finances. It looks at whether cars and motorcycles could be sold more cheaply without them.
videos.w: Offered as a well-researched counterpoint in threads complaining about car dealerships and direct sales.
videos.q: Here is a well researched youtube video on the subject.

videos.t: Defeating Ssl Using Sslstrip (Marlinspike Blackhat)
videos.s: Moxie Marlinspike's Black Hat talk presenting sslstrip, which defeats SSL in practice by intercepting the http-to-https redirect.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an entertaining talk and the original source on the stripping attack that motivated HSTS.
videos.q: Very entertaining.

videos.t: The Surprising History of Copyright and What It Means For...
videos.s: Karl Fogel's 2006 Google Tech Talk traces copyright from a 16th-century English censorship law to a distribution monopoly. It then surveys alternative economic bases for creation and distribution.
videos.w: HN uses it as the go-to history of copyright, arguing it was a gatekeeping tool and that creators don't need it.
videos.q: Karl Fogel does a great job explaining the History of copyright

videos.t: What Happens at the Event Horizon? | Space Time | PBS Digital Studios
videos.s: PBS Space Time explains what happens as you approach and cross a black hole's event horizon, using Penrose diagrams and light cones as the tool for understanding spacetime there.
videos.w: Commenters call it a short, clean, visual explanation of the infalling-particle question and of Penrose diagrams.
videos.q: I think this is the cleanest explanation with actual visual representation.

videos.t: The Closest Thing We Have to Alien Technology
videos.s: Veritasium explains how ASML's EUV lithography machines make the most advanced computer chips, covering the engineering of the light source, mirrors and the supply chain around them. It is a long-form explainer on the world's most complex commercial machine.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as the accessible deep-dive on EUV lithography and why chip manufacturing is so hard.
videos.q: The whole process was deep magic to me before I watched that video.

videos.t: EC's Big Announcement
videos.s: Essential Craftsman announces the start of a spec house build on a scenic lot, kicking off a long series. The channel covers every step of building a house from the viewpoint of a general contractor.
videos.w: HN users recommend the Spec House series as a free, extremely detailed education in how a house is actually built.
videos.q: If you're looking to build a home, do yourself a favor and watch Essential Craftsman's Spec House series

videos.t: Richard Feynman Magnets
videos.s: A short clip of Richard Feynman answering an interviewer's question about how magnets work, in which he explains why a why-question has no simple answer without a shared frame of reference.
videos.w: HN returns to it constantly as a classic on the difficulty of explaining fundamentals and the limits of analogies.
videos.q: Richard Feynman explaining magnets is one of the best layman explainers

videos.t: The Time America Almost Stopped Climate Change | Climate Town
videos.s: Climate Town tells the history of the period when the greenhouse effect was not politically controversial and the US came close to acting on climate. It covers Exxon's early climate science and the policy failures that followed.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an entertaining summary of early bipartisan climate action and corporate influence on research.
videos.q: Climate Town has a great video essay on it

videos.t: Feynman: Mirrors FUN TO IMAGINE 6
videos.s: Richard Feynman, in a clip from the BBC series Fun to Imagine, takes on the puzzle of why mirrors seem to swap left and right but not top and bottom.
videos.w: Cited as the best explanation of mirror reversal.
videos.q: Feynman has a good explanation for that

videos.t: Euler's formula with introductory group theory
videos.s: 3Blue1Brown builds intuition for Euler's formula, e^(pi i) = -1, using the core ideas of group theory. It treats exponentiation geometrically as rotation and scaling instead of repeated multiplication.
videos.w: Recommended as a mind-opening, visual explanation of why Euler's formula is true.
videos.q: check out the one he did on Euler's formula[1]. Blew my mind.

videos.t: Hillel Wayne - Beyond Unit Tests: Taking Your Testing to the Next Level - PyCon 2018
videos.s: Hillel Wayne's PyCon 2018 talk on testing beyond pytest and mypy. It introduces property-based testing with the Hypothesis library and design-by-contract with dpcontracts, and shows how to combine them with an existing test suite.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a concise, convincing case for better testing practice short of full formal methods.
videos.q: I found this talk (by the same person being interviewed) to be concise and convincing on how to do better than typical practice

videos.t: Why Planes Don't Fly Faster
videos.s: Wendover Productions explains why modern airliners fly no faster than they did decades ago, covering the economics of speed and fuel efficiency, and why supersonic travel faded.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear economic explanation of aviation tradeoffs, relevant to Concorde and supersonic startup threads.
videos.q: airplanes used to fly much faster in the 1960s than they do today.

videos.t: Loneliness
videos.s: Kurzgesagt explains why humans feel loneliness, its evolutionary role, and how modern life can turn it into a harmful downward spiral. It cites research and offers ideas on what to do about it.
videos.w: Shared in loneliness threads as a well-sourced, empathetic explanation, including for people struggling with it.
videos.q: had an excellent research report as video summarizing loneliness

videos.t: Kursk: The Epic Armored Engagement (2013)
videos.s: A panel at The National WWII Museum on the Battle of Kursk, moderated by Keith Huxen with historians Robert Citino and John Parshal. The discussion covers the armored engagement and the German, Soviet and US approaches to tank production.
videos.w: HN recommends it for its comparison of tank factory efficiency and the Soviet approach of building cheap tanks with short lifespans.
videos.q: I highly recommend it

videos.t: The Power of Big Data and Psychographics | 2016 Concordia Annual Summit
videos.s: Alexander Nix of Cambridge Analytica presents at the 2016 Concordia Summit on using big data, psychographic profiling and behavioral microtargeting in elections.
videos.w: HN points to it as the company's own pitch, used in debates about data-driven manipulation and extrapolated to today's AI.
videos.q: I urge everyone to watch this video from Cambridge Analytica about their techniques with big data and psychographic profiling

videos.t: C++Now 2018: Matt Godbolt “What Else Has My Compiler Done For Me Lately?”
videos.s: Matt Godbolt, creator of Compiler Explorer, tours surprising optimizations modern compilers perform, such as turning loops into closed-form sums and using popcount instructions. He explores what the compiler does behind the scenes.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a detailed, entertaining look at the crazy optimizations compilers do.
videos.q: Both are great presentations going into details on some of the crazy optimizations compilers will do.

videos.t: So... the minute hand shows progression — apparently we think of time in wildly different ways
videos.s: A Technology Connections video essay on how analog and digital clocks shape different mental models of time, with the minute hand acting as a progress indicator.
videos.w: HN points to it whenever analog versus digital clocks come up, as an idea that changed how commenters think about time perception.
videos.q: Technology Connections has a very good video on this, and completely changed thinking

videos.t: The Liquid Metal Battery: Innovation in stationary electricity storage
videos.s: MIT's Donald Sadoway presents the liquid metal battery as a design for grid-scale stationary electricity storage, at an Imperial College London event in 2018. He covers the grid benefits of massive-scale storage.
videos.w: HN brings it up in energy storage threads as a promising scalable grid storage technology, and calls it worth the hour.
videos.q: It's an hour long, but it's well worth the time investment.

videos.t: Dan Abramov: Beyond React 16 | JSConf Iceland
videos.s: Dan Abramov's JSConf Iceland talk on what came after React 16, with live-coded prototypes of async rendering and time slicing. It previews the ideas that became concurrent mode and suspense.
videos.w: Recommended as the clearest demo of what concurrent rendering solves, including the memorable clock animation.
videos.q: That clock animation is pure genius

videos.t: The Future of Humanity's Energy No One Knows About | Terraform
videos.s: A 20-minute S3 episode touring Terraform Industries, a startup making synthetic natural gas from air and solar power. It walks through the reactor, injection system, direct air capture and electrolyzer, plus the company's cost goals and next milestone.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a clear, short tour of Terraform's synthetic fuel approach and goals.
videos.q: Excellent S3 piece on Terraform [20min]

videos.t: J.S. Bach - Toccata and Fugue in D minor BWV 565
videos.s: Organist Hans-Andre Stamm performs Bach's Toccata and Fugue in D minor, BWV 565, on the Trost organ in Waltershausen, Germany, an instrument from 1730. The video shows the playing and footwork.
videos.w: Recommended as an expressive performance on a historically significant organ with good videography.
videos.q: Great videography, great organ and very expressive organist.

videos.t: What is Right to Repair? An introduction for curious people.
videos.s: Louis Rossmann gives a basic, non-technical introduction to right to repair legislation for people new to the issue.
videos.w: Recommended as the accessible explanation to share with non-techies, family and politicians.
videos.q: I'd highly reccomended his video "What is right to repair? An introduction for curious people." as it clears up many misconceptions about right to repair

videos.t: What Shopping On Amazon Feels Like
videos.s: A Ryan George comedy sketch about the absurdities of shopping on Amazon, including nonsense brand names, fake reviews and scammy sellers.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a funny sketch that lays bare the crazy things people have gotten used to on Amazon.
videos.q: it really lays bare a lot of the crazy stuff we've just got used to with amazon

videos.t: Google Developers Day US - Theorizing from Data
videos.s: Peter Norvig's 2007 Google talk on theorizing from data, covering what huge datasets can do for language understanding, translation, information extraction and inference. It argues that more data often beats cleverer models.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the clear explanation of why Google's statistical, data-first approach works.
videos.q: You should definitely watch it if you haven't seen it before.

videos.t: CppCon 2015: Chandler Carruth "Tuning C++: Benchmarks, and CPUs, and Compilers! Oh My!"
videos.s: Chandler Carruth walks through tuning C++ performance, from writing benchmarks to analyzing results on real CPUs and compilers. It focuses on small-scale problems such as loop kernels, data structures and algorithms, and on keeping compilers from optimizing benchmarks away.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an eye-opening primer on benchmarking and performance analysis, especially for people who have not benchmarked on Linux.
videos.q: Optimizing the Emergent Structures of C++

videos.t: Senate hearing on National Security Space Launch Programs with Elon Musk
videos.s: Video of the March 2014 Senate Defense Subcommittee hearing on National Security Space Launch programs. Elon Musk of SpaceX testifies alongside ULA's CEO, a GAO official and a policy expert, on launch contracts and Russian engines.
videos.w: HN points to it as an entertaining and informative look at the SpaceX versus ULA rivalry.
videos.q: I watched a senate hearing where Elon Musk squares off with the ULA. It's awesome.

videos.t: Understanding the Toyota RAV4 Hybrid
videos.s: Weber State's Professor Kelly explains the Toyota RAV4 Hybrid transaxle, including its planetary gearset eCVT and all nine operating modes. It also covers how the engine reaches nearly 40 percent thermal efficiency.
videos.w: HN points to it as the clearest hands-on explanation of how Toyota hybrids work.
videos.q: I understood after I watched the brilliant Weber Auto video on it, published 5 years ago[0].

videos.t: Lina Khan – FTC Chair on Amazon Antitrust Lawsuit & AI Oversight | The Daily Show
videos.s: FTC Chair Lina Khan sits down with Jon Stewart on The Daily Show to discuss the agency's work protecting consumers from unfair business practices. Topics include the FTC's antitrust lawsuit against Amazon, healthcare industry actions, and whether tech companies are racing to control AI.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a plain-language, well-conducted interview that explains what the FTC is doing about monopolization and antitrust.
videos.q: she pretty much sketched out (in the limited time she got) the main forces at work in the past 30 years of monopolization

videos.t: Nanobot (Havana Parody) | A Capella Science ft. Dorothy Andrusiak
videos.s: A Capella Science parody of Camila Cabello's Havana, retold as a song about molecular machines and nanotechnology. It features animations of rotaxanes, catenanes and molecular switches, and comes with footnotes.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a catchy, accurate piece of science edutainment, and admire its footnote practice.
videos.q: made a catchy "edutainment" song

videos.t: How Electricity Actually Works
videos.s: Veritasium explores how electrical energy actually travels in a circuit, arguing that it flows through electromagnetic fields around the wires rather than through the electrons. It builds a long-cable experiment with Caltech to test when a distant bulb lights.
videos.w: HN cites it for the field-based picture of power transfer, noting it was controversial at release but the experiment largely backed the creator.
videos.q: And why magnets work due to relativity

videos.t: Avoid These Words (And Not Just at Work)
videos.s: Adam Savage answers viewer questions on dealing with condescending colleagues, focusing on dismissive phrases such as 'why don't you just' and 'I would have'. He explains why such language undermines the person receiving it.
videos.w: HN recommends it whenever 'why don't you just...' comes up as an example of arrogant, dismissive advice.
videos.q: Adam Savage has a most excellent rant about the outrageous arrogance of the phrase, "Why don't you just..." I highly recommend it

videos.t: If Russ Ackoff had given a TED Talk...
videos.s: A 1994 talk by systems thinker Russ Ackoff, who knew W. Edwards Deming, on continuous versus discontinuous improvement. It ends with an unexpected lesson.
videos.w: HN favors it as a compact, quotable management and systems-thinking talk, often cited for doing the right thing versus doing the wrong thing right.
videos.q: this is one of my favourite management talks by Russell Ackoff

videos.t: Lecture 1 | Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning
videos.s: The first lecture of Stanford's Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning course, taught by Chris Manning and Richard Socher. It introduces NLP and word vectors, including SVD, skip-gram, CBOW, negative sampling and word2vec.
videos.w: Recommended as one of the best free courses for learning modern deep learning for NLP.
videos.q: I will suggest two brilliant courses from Stanford

videos.t: Procedural Programming: It Never Went Away — Kevlin Henney | Build Stuff
videos.s: Kevlin Henney argues that procedural programming never went away despite later paradigms such as OO and functional. He traces the history of structured programming and shows where procedural thinking still lives in modern code and why it matters for readability.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as a fascinating history lesson showing that the field keeps rediscovering ideas from the 1960s.
videos.q: tour of how all the best discoveries of the past decade or two really date back to the 1960s

videos.t: Why Do Mainframes Still Exist?  What's Inside One?  40TB, 200+ Cores, AI, and more!
videos.s: Dave Plummer tours the IBM z16 mainframe from design through factory assembly, test lab, accelerators and water cooling. He explains why mainframes still exist and what makes them reliable.
videos.w: Recommended as an accessible tour of modern mainframes that compares them sensibly to ordinary server setups.
videos.q: This is an amazing 23-minute video by the Microsoft programmer who developed the Windows NT Task Manager, among other things.

videos.t: 13 Misconceptions About Global Warming
videos.s: Veritasium debunks common climate change myths in under seven minutes, with references to NASA and published research. Topics include CO2 sources, sea ice and 1970s predictions of cooling.
videos.w: Used as a short, well-made rebuttal to common global warming arguments in climate threads.
videos.q: It's a great video, you should at least watch it.

videos.t: RailsConf 2016 - Rails to Phoenix by Brian Cardarella
videos.s: Brian Cardarella's RailsConf 2016 talk on why and how teams can move from Rails to Elixir and Phoenix. It covers performance gains without losing productivity and how to introduce Phoenix in an organization.
videos.w: HN points Rails developers to it as a real-world case for migrating to Phoenix, backed by numbers.
videos.q: A really great presentation, including numbers and real world backup data, plus conceptual overviews.

videos.t: THE SAGAN SERIES - The Frontier Is Everywhere
videos.s: A short unofficial NASA-style spot from Reid Gower's Sagan Series, setting Carl Sagan's words about humanity spreading through the Solar System to visuals and music.
videos.w: Recommended as a motivating, long-horizon vision that puts everyday concerns in perspective.
