videos.q: It gives me the motivation to work towards a goal which lies tens, hundreds, maybe a thousand years in the future.

videos.t: Do we see reality as it is? | Donald Hoffman | TED
videos.s: Cognitive scientist Donald Hoffman argues in this TED talk that evolution shaped perception to track fitness rather than truth. He uses evolutionary simulations and the Australian jewel beetle as examples.
videos.w: Cited in discussions of perception, consciousness and what is real, though some commenters find his conclusions hand-wavy.
videos.q: I encourage you to watch Donald Hoffman's 2015 TED Talk

videos.t: Fast Inverse Square Root — A Quake III Algorithm
videos.s: A walkthrough of the Quake III fast inverse square root, explaining where the constant 0x5f3759df comes from. It covers IEEE 754 floats, the bit hack that approximates a logarithm, and a Newton's method refinement.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an approachable explanation that makes the famous algorithm finally make sense.
videos.q: This video is approachable and explains it pretty well

videos.t: LED Experiments: Making Holiday Lights Less Garish
videos.s: Technology Connections experiments with filtering white and colored LEDs to make holiday lights look less garish. He explains why narrowband LED strings look harsh compared with incandescent bulbs.
videos.w: HN links it in any LED Christmas light discussion as the explanation of why they look off and how to fix it.
videos.q: we can't talk about LED christmas lights without linking to this video by tech connections

videos.t: Predatory Lending: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on payday loans and predatory lending, covering how they trap borrowers and target the elderly and military. It features Sarah Silverman.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a good overview of predatory lending and the problems with payday loans.
videos.q: I think he does a pretty good job in giving an overview of what predatory lending is.

videos.t: Alan Kay : July 2007 : A Conversation with CMU Faculty & Students
videos.s: Alan Kay visits Carnegie Mellon's School of Computer Science in 2007 for an informal conversation with faculty and students. He discusses the state of CS education and criticizes mainstream computing.
videos.w: HN recommends it for Kay's blunt critique of today's computing and standard CS curricula.
videos.q: Alan Kay, almost impolitely, tears into today's computing while talking at CMU.

videos.t: DuckDB – The SQLite for Analytics (Mark Raasveldt, CWI)
videos.s: Mark Raasveldt of CWI presents DuckDB, an embeddable analytical database described as the SQLite for analytics, in a CMU Database Group talk. He explains why it was built, what it is for, and how it works.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the definitive talk from the implementer on DuckDB's motivation and design.
videos.q: one of the implementers giving a talk to CMU students about what DuckDB is, why they made it, and how it works

videos.t: Efficient Bayesian inference with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo -- Michael Betancourt (Part 1)
videos.s: Michael Betancourt's lecture at MLSS Iceland 2014 on efficient Bayesian inference with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo. It covers MCMC concepts and motivation and the problems of sampling in high-dimensional distributions.
videos.w: HN people return to it as a clear primer on MCMC and HMC and on why high dimensions behave counterintuitively.
videos.q: it was a fantastic primer on the basic concepts and motivations of mcmc, and later hmc

videos.t: Stealing Baseball Signs with a Phone (Machine Learning)
videos.s: Mark Rober and Jabril build an app that uses machine learning to decode baseball sign sequences. The video also explains neural networks in a simple, accessible way.
videos.w: Recommended as a fun, semi-technical intro to machine learning that holds kids' attention.
videos.q: This video explains neural nets/machine learning and had my kids riveted

videos.t: Daniel Suarez: The kill decision shouldn't belong to a robot
videos.s: Novelist Daniel Suarez warns in a TED talk about autonomous robotic weapons and drones. He argues that taking the decision to kill out of human hands threatens democratic accountability and calls for a ban.
videos.w: Plugged repeatedly in AI and drone threads as a concise statement of the dangers of automated weapons.
videos.q: I often plug Daniel Suarez's great Kill Decision talk and book

videos.t: Solid Ground // Saša Jurić
videos.s: Sasa Juric's EMPEX talk demonstrates Elixir and Erlang's process model and what makes the BEAM runtime distinctive, such as fault-tolerant parallelism by design.
videos.w: Recommended as the best short overview of why the BEAM and Elixir stand apart from other runtimes.
videos.q: It perfectly articulates what sets Erlang/BEAM/Elixir apart from other runtimes/languages.

videos.t: Kedi - Full Length Documentary
videos.s: Kedi is a feature documentary following seven street cats of Istanbul and the people who care for them. It portrays the relationship between the city and its cats.
videos.w: HN users recommend it as a moving, heartwarming film whenever Istanbul's cats or cat history come up.
videos.q: Recommend it for those who haven't seen it

videos.t: Nordic.js 2014 • Douglas Crockford - The Better Parts
videos.s: Douglas Crockford's Nordic.js 2014 talk on 'the better parts' of JavaScript and programming in general. He argues against `this`, `new` and ES6 classes, and for classless, composition-based object patterns, with some broader remarks on building better structures for the future.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it whenever JavaScript classes, `this` or inheritance come up, as the clearest case for classless OOP from Crockford.
videos.q: It's possible to write javascript without `this`, a style preferred e.g. by Douglas Crockford, explained in the video below.

videos.t: The NCAA: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on the NCAA, arguing that the organization profits enormously from college athletes while insisting they remain unpaid amateurs. It covers the money in college sports, including big-school athletic spending, and the case for paying athletes.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as a sharp, accessible primer on the NCAA's amateurism model and athlete compensation, including for readers outside the US.
videos.q: John Oliver has an excellent take on NCAA salaries issue

videos.t: University of Texas at Austin 2014 Commencement Address - Admiral William H. McRaven
videos.s: Admiral William McRaven's 2014 University of Texas commencement address, built around lessons from Navy SEAL training. It famously opens with the case for making your bed every morning.
videos.w: Recommended in life-advice and motivation threads as worth watching in full, especially for its point about starting small by changing yourself.
videos.q: Worth the whole watch

videos.t: What a Japanese Moving Company in Tokyo is like
videos.s: A day-in-the-life video following a move between apartments in Tokyo using a Japanese moving company. It shows how the movers work and what the experience is like.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for the movers' rigor and discipline, which they find oddly satisfying to watch.
videos.q: Seeing their rigour and discipline is like a visual ASMR video.

videos.t: How We Made MuseScore 4 - Music App Design is Challenging!
videos.s: Tantacrul walks through how the MuseScore 4 team was built and how design decisions were made for the overhaul of a huge legacy notation app. It covers playback and engraving quality improvements.
videos.w: Recommended as a candid, in-depth look at hard UX redesign work and the limits of MIDI for notation.
videos.q: the whole video is worth watching as well

videos.t: Adam Savage's Epiphany on the Science of Measurement!
videos.s: Adam Savage shows a set of Mitutoyo ceramic gauge blocks and uses them to explain metrology, the science of measurement. He argues that accuracy and precision work differently than most people assume, which changes how you think about every measuring tool.
videos.w: Recommended as a thoughtful, enjoyable 45-minute dive into measurement and the appreciation of precision.
videos.q: I think you will thoroughly enjoy Adam Savage's (of Mythbusters fame) recent video on measurement.

videos.t: Starlink revisions, Nov 2018
videos.s: Mark Handley of UCL looks at how SpaceX's November 2018 revisions to the Starlink constellation affect network behavior. The video visualizes the orbits and routing and estimates latencies, building on his earlier video and research paper.
videos.w: HN points to Handley's simulations whenever Starlink latency comes up, as the best visualization of orbits and why laser links could beat fiber over long distances.
videos.q: this guy made an excellent youtube video modeling and visualizing the satellite orbits

videos.t: Obsidian for Beginners: Start HERE — How to Use the Obsidian App for Notes
videos.c: Linking Your Thinking with Nick Milo
videos.s: A 12-minute beginner lesson from Nick Milo's Linking Your Thinking series introducing the Obsidian note-taking app and the first steps to start using it.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an approachable start-here demo for people new to Obsidian.
videos.q: This 6-part video series by Nick Milo is a great way for newbies to get introduced to Obsidian and go up the learning curve rapidly

videos.t: C++ Seasoning
videos.s: Sean Parent's GoingNative 2013 talk surveys new and overlooked C++ features and shows how to use them for simple, correct, clear code. It stresses using standard algorithms rather than raw loops.
videos.w: Recommended whenever the STL mindset or avoiding raw loops in C++ comes up, as an enlightening talk on expressive algorithms.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: This one in particular is very enlightening

videos.t: How GPS Works, And How It Got Better Than The Designers Ever Imagined
videos.s: Scott Manley covers how GPS works and how civilian accuracy went from a planned 100 meters to about one meter. He explains the technology and the removal of restrictions that made this possible.
videos.w: Recommended as a solid history and explanation of GPS, especially when GPS outages or accuracy come up.
videos.q: Scott Manley has a nice video covering the history of GPS and how it works, well worth a watch

videos.t: Doug McLean | Common Misconceptions in Aerodynamics
videos.s: Retired Boeing Technical Fellow Doug McLean walks through common misconceptions in aerodynamics, drawing on his book Understanding Aerodynamics. He critiques popular explanations of wing lift and rocket thrust and argues for arguing from the real physics.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a credible debunking of the popular but wrong explanations of how wings generate lift.
videos.q: You might get something out of this 2013 talk by former Boeing engineer Doug McLean on misconceptions about lift.

videos.t: Lazerhawk ~ Redline Full Album
videos.s: A full-album upload of Lazerhawk's debut synthwave album Redline, with the track list and timestamps in the description.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a favorite synthwave album, good for programming and long drives.
videos.q: My favourite album from that genre is Lazerhawk's debut album Redline, awesome for programming IMO

videos.t: Hawking Radiation
videos.s: PBS Space Time explains Stephen Hawking's prediction of Hawking radiation and how black holes can emit radiation and slowly evaporate. It goes beyond the common particle-antiparticle analogy.
videos.w: Recommended as an accessible and correct explanation of Hawking radiation for non-physicists.
videos.q: explains it really well while keeping it accessible for non-physicists

videos.t: 327 - Choices, costs, and challenges in US healthcare: insurance, drug pricing, & potential reforms
videos.s: On Peter Attia's podcast, Tenet Healthcare CEO Saum Sutaria, formerly of McKinsey, walks through the structure and financial flows of the US healthcare system. They cover insurance, drug pricing, how the system evolved and possible reforms.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a detailed primer on why US healthcare is expensive and where the money goes.
videos.q: The best primer on the choices that make our healthcare expensive, and where the money goes, are in this video

videos.t: BlueHat Seattle 2019 || Guarding Against Physical Attacks: The Xbox One Story
videos.s: Tony Chen of Microsoft explains at BlueHat Seattle 2019 how the Xbox One was designed to resist physical attacks. He covers the security design and hypervisor-based OS architecture that kept the console uncracked for years.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a fascinating, authoritative account of console hardware security, often cited in threads on hardware security and anti-cheat.
videos.q: the whole talk is incredible

videos.t: Rapping, deconstructed: The best rhymers of all time
videos.s: Vox breaks down how great rappers build rhymes, from Kurtis Blow's simple bars to Biggie's smooth flow and Kendrick Lamar's dense, fast delivery. It uses on-screen visualizations of rhyme structure.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible explanation of rhyme craft that works even for people who aren't hip hop fans.
videos.q: Please consider this required watching, even if you have no interest in hip-hop music

videos.t: Do we have to accept Quantum weirdness? De Broglie Bohm Pilot Wave Theory explained
videos.s: Looking Glass Universe explains de Broglie-Bohm pilot wave theory (Bohmian mechanics) as an alternative to the standard interpretation of quantum mechanics. The video lays out the pros and cons of the theory and links to related videos on contextuality and entanglement.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend the channel as a clear, well-made source on quantum mechanics and common misconceptions about Bohmian mechanics.
videos.q: I love this series, Looking Glass Universe, on the subject [0,1].

videos.t: The User is Drunk
videos.s: A short talk by Will Dayble of Squareweave arguing that you should design software as if the user were drunk: distracted, impaired in attention and vision, and prone to misreading. It is a user experience talk built around that framing.
videos.w: HN users recommend it as a memorable, short way to build empathy for users' confusing mistakes and to design for distraction.
videos.q: There's a great short talk called "the user is drunk

videos.t: Why Snow and Confetti Ruin YouTube Video Quality
videos.s: Tom Scott explains why confetti and snow wreck video quality, using interframe compression and bitrate. He demonstrates it live by changing the quality on screen.
videos.w: Used as the clearest short demonstration of why noisy, high-motion content is hard for video compression.
videos.q: Tom Scott has a good video where turns up and down the quality live so you can see it in a single video

videos.t: How I animate 3Blue1Brown | A Manim demo with Ben Sparks
videos.s: Grant Sanderson of 3Blue1Brown shows his workflow for animating math videos with Manim, with Ben Sparks. He codes scenes live, including a Lorenz attractor, and walks through example scenes.
videos.w: Recommended as a rare detailed look at how 3b1b videos are made, including live debugging of his rendering engine.
videos.q: I want to highlight the demo video [0], where Grant explains how he works with Manim.

videos.t: Emacs Doom Episode 1 - Getting Started
videos.s: A short first episode in Zaiste's Doom Emacs series, showing how to get started with Doom, an Emacs configuration aimed at Vim users. It presents Doom as a polished, fast, batteries-included distribution.
videos.w: HN users recommend the series to newcomers learning Emacs, Doom, org-mode, projectile and magit.
videos.q: To get started I highly recommend this series by Zaiste

videos.t: Dropping the Bomb: Hiroshima & Nagasaki
videos.s: A very long video essay by Shaun on the decisions and motivations behind the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, with a detailed timeline and argument that they were not militarily necessary.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a thorough, nuanced account of why the bombings happened and what led Japan to surrender.
videos.q: Here's a thoroughly nuanced analysis of the causes and motivations leading to the bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

videos.t: Airbus A340 EMERGENCY - Engine Failure
videos.s: Cockpit footage of a Swiss Airbus A340 crew dealing with rising oil temperature in one engine on a Zurich to Shanghai flight, ending with a safety landing. It shows the pilots' procedures through the emergency.
videos.w: Recommended as a captivating look at how a professional crew calmly handles an in-flight engine problem.
videos.q: If you really want to see something captivating, watch this clip of a Swiss A340 crew handling an overheating engine in-flight.

videos.t: Simon Sinek: Why Leaders Eat Last
videos.s: Simon Sinek's 99U talk on why leaders earn trust by putting their team's safety ahead of their own, drawing on biology and anthropology. It distills the ideas of his book Leaders Eat Last into about 46 minutes.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a quick way to get the key concepts of the book and as an introduction to leadership thinking.
videos.q: watching talks by the authors, which give you the key concepts from the book in an hour

videos.t: The Halo Drive
videos.s: Astrophysicist David Kipping presents the halo drive, a proposed way to propel a starship to a good fraction of light speed by gaining energy from a black hole. The video is based on his peer-reviewed paper and explains why energy is the main obstacle to interstellar flight.
videos.w: HN readers point to it as a clear explanation of a theoretical fuel-free propulsion concept from a channel they respect.
videos.q: Prof. Kipping is well known for his Cool Worlds youtube channel, which is fantastic.

videos.t: DEF CON 31 - An Audacious Plan to Halt the Internet's Ensh*ttification  - Cory Doctorow
videos.s: Cory Doctorow's DEF CON 31 talk describes how platforms decay in a pattern he calls enshittification. He lays out a plan to stop it through antitrust, interoperability and fixing the law.
videos.w: Recommended in threads on big tech, monopolies and adversarial interoperability as the clearest statement of his argument.
videos.q: I really recommend Cory's talk at DEF CON

videos.t: Building pi in a World of Slop — Mario Zechner
videos.s: Mario Zechner explains why he built pi, a minimal coding agent, out of frustration with existing agent harnesses. He also discusses how AI agents are straining open source projects and argues for slowing down.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a first-hand argument for building your own lean agent harness instead of relying on bloated, vendor-controlled ones.
videos.q: There is a really good video by the author of pi.dev

videos.t: Should Google Go Nuclear? Clean, cheap, nuclear power (no, really)
videos.s: Robert Bussard's 2006 Google Tech Talk on inertial electrostatic confinement fusion, a compact approach he argued could be cheap and clean, using boron-hydrogen fuel without neutron radiation. It runs about 93 minutes and covers the physics, funding history and his proposed development path.
videos.w: Recommended as an intense, insightful look at Bussard's IEC fusion work, frequently cited in fusion threads for his claim that it could be developed for about $200M.
videos.q: it's an intense, fast-paced, insightful, and (likely) final public look into his mind, his work, and his character.

videos.t: The puzzle of motivation | Dan Pink | TED
videos.s: Dan Pink's TED talk argues that traditional carrot-and-stick rewards often fail for creative work, drawing on the candle problem and social science research. He points to autonomy, mastery and purpose as better motivators.
videos.w: HN cites it whenever money as an incentive comes up, as evidence that rewards can backfire for creative white-collar work.
videos.q: I highly recommend taking a look at the work of Daniel Pink related to money as an incentive.

videos.t: How To Draw Mushrooms On An Oscilloscope With Sound
videos.s: Jerobeam Fenderson shows how to draw a mushroom on an oscilloscope in XY mode using stereo audio, then animates it by modulating with a larger wave. Pd and Max4Live patches are provided.
videos.w: HN finds it mesmerizing and uses it to build intuition for waveforms and oscilloscope XY drawing.
videos.q: This was amazing to me: How To Draw Mushrooms On An Oscilloscope With Sound

videos.t: Is Nuclear Waste Really Waste?
videos.s: In a 2010 Google Tech Talk, Kirk Sorensen gives an economic analysis of what spent nuclear fuel actually contains. He argues it is mostly valuable material that can be partitioned and reused, not just waste to be isolated for 100,000 years.
videos.w: HN readers recommend it as the best explanation of what nuclear waste really is and how much of it is reusable fuel.
videos.q: This talk from 2010 is really amazing at understanding what 'nuclear waste' actually is and what it will be.

videos.t: Jancovici : Will technology save us from Climate Change ? MIT Media Lab - 23/02/2021
videos.s: Jean-Marc Jancovici gives an MIT Media Lab talk on whether technology can save us from climate change. He argues from a physical view of energy that economic growth, energy use and climate impact are tightly linked.
videos.w: Recommended in climate and energy threads as a numbers-based explanation of why energy underlies growth and emissions.
videos.q: Interesting related presentation on what is energy and how it relates to the economy from a physical point of view

videos.t: NVScene 2015 Session: How to Create Content with Signed Distance Functions (Johann Korndörfer)
videos.s: Johann Korndorfer's NVScene 2015 talk on building content with signed distance functions. It focuses on patterns that make SDF modelling more structured, arguing that SDFs capture a shape's essence like vector graphics do compared with polygons or voxels.
videos.w: Recommended as an excellent talk from a demoscene practitioner on how to build sophisticated scenes from distance functions.
videos.q: this is an excellent talk on the subject

videos.t: How secure is 256 bit security?
videos.s: 3Blue1Brown illustrates how enormous the 256-bit search space is, showing how infeasible it is to find a hash or key by guessing and checking.
videos.w: HN uses it as the go-to illustration of just how large 2^256 is.
videos.q: To comprehend how large a search space this is watch 3Blue1Brown's explanation

videos.t: 2016/2017 MUST-KNOW WEB DEVELOPMENT TECH - Watch this if you want to be a web developer
videos.s: LearnCode.academy presents a roadmap of web development technologies to learn in 2016 and 2017, spanning front-end, back-end and DevOps tools.
videos.w: Recommended to beginners asking how to start in web development as a compact survey of the toolscape of its time.
videos.q: Watch this brilliant video, I think the author nailed it

videos.t: The Biggest Chemical Coverup In History
videos.s: Veritasium investigates PFAS forever chemicals, from Teflon's history to pollution of the global water system and their presence in the US population. It covers the corporate cover-up and the host's own blood tests.
videos.w: Recommended as a good, accessible explanation of PFAS, its low safe limits and why regulation matters.
videos.q: If you want a good explanation of PFAs, Veritasium did a video on it.

videos.t: Kostya Kimlat Fools Penn & Teller // Fool Us: Penn's Favorite Card Trick
videos.s: Magician Kostya Kimlat performs a card trick on Penn & Teller: Fool Us that fooled the duo, using Penn's favorite card trick as a basis.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a trick admired for both its method and its effect.
videos.q: I like this one a lot as it is amazing on both method + effect.

videos.t: 5 steps to designing the life you want  | Bill Burnett | TEDxStanford
videos.s: TEDxStanford talk by Bill Burnett, executive director of Stanford's design program, on applying design thinking to your own life and career. He offers five practical tips such as getting curious, talking to people and trying things.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a short intro to the Designing Your Life approach when people ask about career direction and finding meaningful work.
videos.q: Highly recommend their book!

videos.t: Understanding the Job
videos.s: Clayton Christensen explains the jobs-to-be-done idea in five minutes, using the fast-food milkshake example. The point is that understanding the job a product is hired to do makes it easier to improve.
videos.w: Cited as the short, famous introduction to Jobs To Be Done and competition framing.
videos.q: well worth the 5 minute watch

videos.t: The Suburbs Are Bleeding America Dry | Climate Town (feat. @NotJustBikes)
videos.s: A snarky, comedic video essay from Climate Town, with a guest appearance by Not Just Bikes, arguing that American suburban sprawl and single-family zoning are financially and environmentally unsustainable. It covers how zoning rules shape housing and what viewers can do locally, such as attending zoning meetings.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as an entertaining but well-sourced explainer on US zoning and housing costs whenever those topics come up.
videos.q: A funny, yet very well researched video on that exact same topic of Zoning nonsense. Entertaining AND informative.

videos.t: Every Melody Has Been Copyrighted (and they're all on this hard drive)
videos.s: Adam Neely interviews Damien Riehl and Noah Rubin about their project to generate and copyright every possible melody as MIDI. The video explains their reasoning and how it bears on music copyright lawsuits.
videos.w: It is the go-to explainer whenever HN discusses brute-forcing melodies, copyright, or AI-generated content, since it features the project's creators.
videos.q: Strongly recommend watching that video! Excellent info.

videos.t: Making a Full Bridge Rectifier
videos.s: ElectroBOOM's Mehdi Sadaghdar explains how a full bridge rectifier works, the building block of AC to DC converters, with his usual humor and a demonstration of the circuit.
videos.w: Recommended as an enlightening and funny explanation of bridge rectifiers, often linked in power supply teardown threads.
videos.q: The linked video of how bridge rectifier works is enlightening, funny and terrifying.

videos.t: 23. Language
videos.s: Robert Sapolsky's Stanford lecture on language, comparing human and animal communication, ape language projects like Koko and Kanzi, and how language is acquired. It is part of his human behavioral biology course.
videos.w: HN recommends it, and the whole course, for understanding the brain and language acquisition.
videos.q: If you want to understand better how the brain works, I really recommend watching the whole course.

videos.t: The Neuroanatomy of ADHD and thus how to treat ADHD - CADDAC - Dr Russel Barkley part 3ALL
videos.s: Dr. Russell Barkley lectures on the neuroanatomy of ADHD and how to treat it, linking executive function and working memory to the disorder. It is part 3 of a CADDAC series.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it to people with ADHD for helping them understand their behavior and how their brain works.
videos.q: Watching that video helped me put my behaviors in perspective and really understand how my brain works.

videos.t: Jon Stewart On Vaccine Science And The Wuhan Lab Theory
videos.c: The Late Show with Stephen Colbert
videos.s: Jon Stewart appears on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert and discusses the pandemic, vaccine science and the Wuhan lab origin theory. He jokes that the disease shares its name with the lab.
videos.w: HN posts it in COVID origin threads as a blunt comedic take on why the lab leak question deserved investigation rather than dismissal.
videos.q: Jon Stewart's take is brilliant

videos.t: The Ultimate French Press Technique
videos.s: James Hoffmann demonstrates his technique for a clean, sludge-free cup from a French press: stir, break the crust, wait, and carefully pour. It is a four-minute guide.
videos.w: HN commenters swear by it as the best way to make French press coffee, and cite its 16:1 water-to-coffee ratio.
videos.q: IMO it produces the best coffee I've ever been able to make in a french press.

videos.t: Exposing The Dark Side of America's AI Data Center Explosion | View From Above | Business Insider
videos.s: A Business Insider investigation into the US boom in AI data centers, mapping where they are, who owns them, and how much power and water they consume. It looks at the costs borne by communities, with a focus on Virginia.
videos.w: Cited in threads on AI infrastructure as evidence of the water, power and community costs of data centers.
videos.q: Just watch that and not get hoppin' mad.

videos.t: Classic Game Postmortem: Fallout
videos.s: Timothy Cain's 2012 GDC postmortem of the original Fallout, covering how he helped build the game and set the template for open-world RPGs. He talks through production, design and programming decisions.
videos.w: Held up as an exemplary GDC postmortem and a first-hand account for fans of the original Fallout.
videos.q: GDC post mortems are amazing, especially the ones on Diablo[0] and Fallout[1].

videos.t: ZX Spectrum 1-bit music: Agent X (Tim Follin, 1985)
videos.s: A recording from real hardware of Tim Follin's multichannel 1-bit music for Agent X on the ZX Spectrum. It shows several voices coaxed out of the single-bit beeper.
videos.w: Cited as the prime example of what clever programming can do with a 1-bit audio output.
videos.q: Tim Follin's tunes for example are basically treating the beeper like a 1-bit DAC, with amazing results.

videos.t: What nobody tells you about documentation
videos.s: Daniele Procida's PyCon AU 2017 talk presents a system that divides documentation into four kinds, usually drawn as four quadrants. He explains why mixing them makes docs poor and how separating them improves writing.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the best concise introduction to a practical framework for structuring documentation, the basis of what became Diataxis.
videos.q: I highly recommend Daniele Procida's talk about this

videos.t: What is in a Lucene index? Adrien Grand, Software Engineer, Elasticsearch
videos.s: Elasticsearch engineer and Lucene committer Adrien Grand explains the design decisions inside a Lucene index and what problems it can and cannot solve. The talk goes into how Lucene stores data for fast search and analytics.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an instructive, easy-to-follow look at Lucene internals from a core committer.
videos.q: I can super highly recommend talks by Adrien Grand on Lucene and Elasticsearch.

videos.t: Chai Jing's review: Under the Dome – Investigating China’s Smog 柴静雾霾调查：穹顶之下 (full translation)
videos.s: Chai Jing's 104-minute documentary on China's smog, with full English subtitles. A former TV anchor, she investigates what smog is, where it comes from and what can be done, prompted by her daughter's health problems.
videos.w: Recommended as an accessible, powerful introduction to severe urban air pollution, remembered also for being banned in China.
videos.q: I highly recommend the documentary Under the Dome , released earlier this year and later banned in China

videos.t: THE MARS UNDERGROUND [HD] Full Movie
videos.s: A documentary following Robert Zubrin and the Mars Society as they push the Mars Direct plan for sending humans to Mars using current technology and local resources. It also covers the clash with NASA's more expensive approach.
videos.w: Recommended in Mars-mission threads as an accessible account of Zubrin's argument that Mars is feasible within a decade.
videos.q: I highly recommend this documentary

videos.t: Google Python Class Day 1 Part 1
videos.s: The first part of Google's Python Class, taught by Nick Parlante, introducing the language and its strings. It is aimed at people with some programming familiarity and comes with exercises.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a fast, accessible way to start learning Python.
videos.q: recommend it to anybody that thinks they need to learn programming

videos.t: Why is the Solar System Flat?
videos.s: A minutephysics explainer on why the planets orbit in a flat plane. It shows how conserved angular momentum flattens a collapsing cloud of matter into a disk.
videos.w: HN commenters link it as a quick, intuitive explanation of angular momentum and why spinning clumps of matter flatten.
videos.p: angular momentum and solar system formation
videos.q: I like this video from minutephysics to get an intuitive sense for it

videos.t: Moxie Marlinspike, Next Generation Threats 2014
videos.s: Moxie Marlinspike speaks at Next Generation Threats 2014 about the challenges of encrypted communication and how Signal addresses them. He also draws on American action movies as narrative for secure communications.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as a clear explanation of encrypted messaging challenges and of the thinking behind Signal.
videos.q: I got excited about signal after watching this video, which explains pretty well the challenges of encrypted communication and how Signal addresses them

videos.t: How wildlife trade is linked to coronavirus
videos.s: A Vox explainer on how the wildlife trade and wet markets are linked to coronavirus and why new diseases keep emerging in China. It stresses that most people in China do not eat wildlife.
videos.w: HN commenters shared it during early 2020 as a clear explanation of wet markets and how human encroachment on wildlife drives outbreaks.
videos.q: Vox put out a pretty good video on wet markets recently.

videos.t: Milton Friedman - Why Tax Reform Is Impossible
videos.s: Milton Friedman explains why the US tax code is enormously complex and why meaningful reform is unlikely. He argues that politicians profit from the complexity, since tax breaks are products they sell and the code works as a tool of reward and punishment. The clip is about 14 minutes from his lecture series.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it whenever a thread touches on tax complexity, loopholes, or why companies like Intuit benefit from a convoluted tax system.
videos.q: There is a good Milton Friedman video wherein he explains why tax reform won't happen in the United States.

videos.t: How to recover from depression
videos.s: Clinical psychologist Dr Michael Yapko draws on forty years of practice and research to explain skills that help people recover from, and even prevent, depression. He emphasizes cognitive and social factors beyond medication.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a comprehensive talk on depression, and one says it helped them through a bad period.
videos.q: this video helped me immensely at one point in my life

videos.t: Slavoj Žižek on "They Live" (The Pervert's Guide to Ideology)
videos.s: A short excerpt from The Pervert's Guide to Ideology in which Slavoj Zizek analyzes John Carpenter's They Live. He uses the film's fight scene and sunglasses to explain how ideology works.
videos.w: HN cites it as a concise, memorable explanation of ideology, often in threads about advertising, propaganda or AI-shaped narratives.
videos.q: it finally clicked after hearing Zizek talk about it.

videos.t: the sham legacy of Richard Feynman
videos.s: Physicist Angela Collier's nearly three-hour critique of Richard Feynman's public legacy. She examines how his books, written with Ralph Leighton, shaped a mythologized great-man image, and covers his personal behavior.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a sobering counterpoint to the Feynman myth for people whose view comes from Surely You're Joking.
videos.q: Her video on Feynman is long and detailed, and very sobering. I highly recommend it.

videos.t: How We Bought Our Abandoned House in Japan | Process, Costs, Risks, Finance, How to Find One
videos.s: The Tokyo Llama channel details how the creators found and bought an abandoned akiya minka house in Japan. It covers process, costs, taxes, financing and risks of renovation.
videos.w: Recommended as a candid look at the real costs and paperwork of buying and renovating an abandoned Japanese home.
videos.q: this video goes through the costs of buying an abandoned house in Japan

videos.t: Morris Chang, in conversation with Jen-Hsun Huang
videos.s: A 2007 Computer History Museum conversation in which Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang interviews TSMC founder Morris Chang. Chang recounts his career and the creation of the dedicated silicon foundry model.
videos.w: Recommended as a rare, inspiring history of the foundry business and the relationship between Chang and Huang.
videos.q: here's a fascinating conversation from 5 years ago between Morris Chang (founder and chairman, TSMC) and Jen-Hsun Huang (CEO, Nvidia)

videos.t: RSA ANIMATE: Smile or Die
videos.s: An RSA Animate drawing of Barbara Ehrenreich's talk on the darker side of positive thinking. It argues that forced positivity in culture, work and policy can be harmful and played a part in the financial crisis.
videos.w: HN uses it as a go-to short critique of mandatory positivity in workplaces, startups and corporate culture.
videos.q: I strongly recommend you to watch Smile or Die, a talk by Barbara Ehrenreich.

videos.t: Opioids III: The Sacklers: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on the Sackler family and how they have handled opioid lawsuits. It covers how hard they fought to defend their name and is the third of three segments on the opioid crisis.
videos.w: Recommended in threads about Purdue and Sackler immunity as a good primer on the issue.
videos.q: John Oliver had a really good video specifically about this issue

videos.t: The Mental Game of Python - Raymond Hettinger
videos.s: Raymond Hettinger's PyBay 2019 talk on the mental habits behind effective programming, drawn from coaching, teaching and StackOverflow. He covers problem decomposition, chunking, managing working memory and getting unstuck.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a Python talk with lessons that apply to any programming, especially chunking to manage complexity.
videos.q: Here's a good recent one by Raymond Hettinger on making things easier for yourself when programming

videos.t: Tom Lehrer - New Math (Animated)
videos.s: An amateur animation of Tom Lehrer's satirical song New Math, which pokes fun at 1960s math teaching and subtraction in base 8. The animation illustrates the old and new subtraction methods.
videos.w: HN brings it up whenever curriculum fads or Common Core complaints appear, as a funny precedent from the 1960s.
videos.q: My favorite Tom Lehrer song is probably New Math.

videos.t: David Reich — How one small tribe conquered the world 70,000 years ago
videos.s: Dwarkesh Patel interviews ancient-DNA geneticist David Reich about human prehistory, including the small group that left Africa around 70,000 years ago and the Yamnaya expansion.
videos.w: Recommended as a nuanced, up-to-date account of human prehistory from a leading researcher in ancient DNA.
videos.q: David Reich is probably the leading researcher in this field and his description of our best guesses is highly nuanced and open to new data.

videos.t: Cosmos - Carl Sagan - 4th Dimension
videos.s: A segment from Carl Sagan's original Cosmos explaining the fourth spatial dimension through analogy with a two-dimensional world and shadow projection.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the clearest intuitive introduction to thinking about a fourth dimension.
videos.q: brilliantly exemplified by Carl Sagan in this popular video

videos.t: John Carmack Keynote - Quakecon 2013
videos.s: John Carmack's roughly three-hour QuakeCon 2013 keynote, delivered from a few bullet points. Topics include his Haskell experiments with functional programming and static typing, game state, and cloud gaming.
videos.w: Recommended to Carmack fans as the keynote with his functional programming adventures and for his fluent, wide-ranging talk.
videos.q: Watch one of his keynotes. He sits down with some bullet points on a tablet and then talks for three hours

videos.t: Watching This Video Disqualifies You From Jury Duty for Life
videos.s: CGP Grey explains jury nullification, a juror's power to acquit despite the law, and why mentioning it can get you struck from jury selection.
videos.w: HN links it as the clearest short explainer of jury nullification and how the jury system works, often in threads on prosecutors and trials.
videos.q: Great video that explains this

videos.t: The Hobbit: A Long-Expected Autopsy (Part 1/2)
videos.s: The first part of Lindsay Ellis's video essay series on the troubled production and critical reception of The Hobbit film trilogy.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an engaging analysis of how the Hobbit films were made, in threads on CGI and Tolkien.
videos.q: Lindsay Ellis has a three-part video essay series

videos.t: Hamming, "n-Dimensional Space" (April 14, 1995)
videos.s: Richard Hamming's 1995 lecture on n-dimensional space, showing how geometric intuition about spheres and cubes breaks down in high dimensions. It is part of his course on learning to learn.
videos.w: Recommended as the source for counterintuitive high-dimensional geometry and described as an eye opener.
videos.q: This was an eye opener to me.

videos.t: Celestial Navigation (instruction video)
videos.s: A roughly 45-minute vintage US military instructional film that gives a comprehensive overview of celestial navigation, covering sextant use and the theory behind lines of position.
videos.w: HN points to it as an unusually clear teaching film on how celestial navigation works, and as an example of how good old military training material is.
videos.q: I love these military training movies, they're so good at teaching complex concepts.

videos.t: Pachelbel Rant from 2006 [Official High Quality Re-Post]
videos.s: Comedian Rob Paravonian's 'Pachelbel Rant', a comedy bit showing that the chord progression of Pachelbel's Canon underlies countless pop songs. This is a high-quality 2019 re-post of the 2006 original.
videos.w: Recommended in threads on music copyright and chord progressions as a funny, accurate demonstration that a few chords are fundamental to music.
videos.q: If you haven't seen the 'Pachelbel Rant' yet, you should, it's an entire comedy bit based on the fact that these chords are fundamental to music

videos.t: My stroke of insight | Jill Bolte Taylor | TED
videos.s: Neuroscientist Jill Bolte Taylor describes watching her own brain functions shut down during a massive stroke. She gives a first-person account of losing speech, motion and self-awareness.
videos.w: Recommended as a vivid first-person view of the right hemisphere in control, often linked to meditation and non-dual experience.
videos.q: I highly recommend this video if you want to hear about what life is when the right hemisphere is in control

videos.t: #Gamelab2018 - Jon Blow's Design decisions on creating Jai a new language for game programmers
videos.s: Jonathan Blow talks at Gamelab 2018 about the design decisions behind Jai, the programming language he is building for game programmers. He covers low-friction development, quality of life and the effects of compile times.
videos.w: Recommended for a substantive look at language design priorities and a critique of why modern programming feels broken.
videos.q: I recently watched this talk by Johnathan Blow[0] where he talks about quality of life in programming languages and spends a fair amount of time talking about compile times and their effects.

videos.t: D is for Debacle - The Crucial Story of Vitamin D and Human Health
videos.s: Ivor Cummins gives an 82-minute presentation on the history and science of vitamin D and human health. He draws on expert interviews to argue that sun exposure and vitamin D status are linked to many chronic diseases.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it in vitamin D threads as a thorough walkthrough of why deficiency may matter.
videos.q: Well worth to watch the whole video

videos.t: Neutron movie of coffee making
videos.s: A short film made with cold neutron imaging at the Paul Scherrer Institut showing a moka pot brewing coffee, sped up four times. The neutron beam makes the water and steam inside the pot visible.
videos.w: Recommended in moka pot threads as the best way to see how the pot works from the inside.
videos.q: There's also a fantastic Youtube video in a neutron beam facility of a Moka pot

videos.t: Wired Interviews Bill Gates 1996
videos.s: Unreleased 1996 footage of the Wired editors interviewing Bill Gates when he visited their office. Gates talks about software, the internet and Microsoft's thinking at the time. The video is about 53 minutes long.
videos.w: People recommend it as a rare, unpolished look at Gates's mid-90s thinking, including predictions that aged well and badly.
videos.q: I strongly recommend watching the impromptu interview Bill Gates gave back in the 90s while visiting the Wired office

videos.t: Getting GPLv2 Compliance From A Chinese Company- In Person!
videos.s: Naomi Wu visits the Shenzhen offices of smartphone maker UMIDIGI in person to get them to release source code they owed under the GPLv2, and they comply.
videos.w: Held up as a rare success story of GPL enforcement against a Chinese hardware company, and admired for the effort.
videos.q: I wish more people had the nerve to do that instead of letting it slide.

videos.t: selective attention test
videos.s: The original invisible gorilla awareness test by Daniel Simons and Christopher Chabris, in which viewers count basketball passes and often miss a gorilla crossing the scene. It demonstrates inattentional blindness.
videos.w: HN uses it constantly as the classic demonstration that attention is selective, in threads on driving, motorcycles, AI and perception.
videos.q: a longer but more relevant "motorcycle invisibility training" video

videos.t: Do Events Inside Black Holes Happen?
videos.s: A PBS Space Time episode asking what black holes really are and whether events can happen inside them. It covers event horizons, time dilation and common misconceptions about black holes.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an accessible but deep explanation of black holes that corrects popular misconceptions.
videos.q: This is mind blowing...shatters my misconception of blackholes

videos.t: Linux Kernel Development, Greg Kroah-Hartman - Git Merge 2016
videos.s: Greg Kroah-Hartman's Git Merge 2016 talk on how the Linux kernel is developed, how fast it moves, and how git and email workflows keep it manageable. He is the stable kernel maintainer.
videos.w: HN points to it as an authoritative overview of the kernel's email-and-git workflow and its development rate.
videos.q: Just dropping this gem of a talk[1], for the uninitiated.

videos.t: Ross's Game Dungeon: Deus Ex - Human Revolution
videos.s: Ross Scott's Game Dungeon episode critiques Deus Ex: Human Revolution, looking at its design, politics and visual style. It is part of his series of opinionated game reviews.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a witty critique of the game, and cite it in discussions of the yellow filter in games.
videos.q: is a delightful critique of the subject matter

videos.t: Boston Dynamics Big Dog (new video March 2008)
videos.s: Boston Dynamics' March 2008 video of BigDog, a four-legged robot, walking on ice and snow, climbing rubble and recovering from slips and kicks.
videos.w: HN returns to it as the classic jaw-dropping demo of legged robots handling rough terrain, and as a historical marker for how long such robots have existed.
videos.q: Big Dog is truly awesome.

videos.t: code::dive conference 2014 - Scott Meyers: Cpu Caches and Why You Care
videos.s: Scott Meyers explains how CPU caches work and why they matter for performance, covering cache levels, access speeds, associativity, and effects in multithreaded code. The focus is C++ and cache-aware, data-oriented programming.
videos.w: HN points to it as the go-to explanation of why memory layout beats pointer-chasing structures on real hardware.
videos.q: Scott Meyers had a very good talk which contained this information

videos.t: 56 High Speed Rail Links We Should've Built Already
videos.s: CityNerd lays out a data-driven method for deciding where high-speed rail should be built in North America and identifies 56 city pairs that justify it, based on population and distance.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a methodical argument that many US city pairs make economic sense for high-speed rail.
videos.q: CityNerd identifies 56 train segments that should be built, using data and reasonable, precedented criteria

videos.t: William Ackman: Everything You Need to Know About Finance and Investing in Under an Hour | Big Think
videos.s: A Big Think talk in which hedge-fund manager William Ackman goes through the basics of finance and investing in under an hour. It is pitched as a crash course on the most important concepts.
videos.w: HN recommends it to beginners as a quick, clear overview of finance and investing fundamentals.
videos.q: An excellent crash course for the most critical concepts.

videos.t: My Octopus Teacher: The Greatest Horror Film
videos.s: Maggie Mae Fish analyzes the documentary My Octopus Teacher as an eco-horror film, critiquing it as a story of a man projecting his own needs onto a wild animal.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a well-done critique of the documentary, sometimes in preference to watching the film itself.
videos.q: I would recommend people not to watch it and instead watch this well done critique (and criticism)

videos.t: 'Oumuamua Is Not Aliens
videos.s: PBS Space Time examines the interstellar object 'Oumuamua and the popular theories about it, including the light-sail hypothesis. It argues that a natural rock is the likeliest explanation.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a sober analysis of 'Oumuamua theories that counters the alien-spacecraft claims.
videos.q: And I really recommend this PBS Space Time Video

videos.t: New Earthships capture more energy, water & food at lower cost
videos.s: Kirsten Dirksen tours new Earthships, homes built from tires, bottles and cans that generate their own energy, collect water and grow food. The video covers the newer, cheaper Encounter model and its passive systems.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend the channel's alternative-living videos, and this one for its look at a net-zero desert home.
videos.q: this fun video about a net zero desert house

videos.t: Charlie Rose: Sir James Goldsmith Interview - 15.11.94
videos.s: Charlie Rose interviews Sir James Goldsmith in 1994 about the coming GATT free-trade agreement. Goldsmith predicts that global capital mobility will upset the balance between capital and labor.
videos.w: Recommended as a prescient interview on free trade and its social consequences, worth watching with hindsight.
videos.q: I encourage everyone who cares about this space to watch the 1994 Charlie Rose episode

videos.t: The most mind-blowing concept in music (Harmonic Series)
videos.s: Andrew Huang explains the harmonic series, which he calls the foundation of almost all music. He builds the idea up step by step, with demonstrations of overtones and how harmonies derive from them.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear, short but in-depth explanation of harmonics and overtones, useful even for musicians.
videos.q: Music producer Andrew Huang does a fantastic job demonstrating the harmonic series concepts

videos.t: Birth of BASIC
videos.s: A Dartmouth-produced documentary on how professors John Kemeny and Tom Kurtz, with a group of undergraduates, invented the BASIC language. It covers the creation of BASIC and the early time-sharing environment at Dartmouth.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the definitive documentary on BASIC's origins, and it resurfaces whenever BASIC or Kurtz comes up.
videos.q: The Birth of BASIC documentary that Dartmouth did for the 50th anniversary is excellent and features him prominently

videos.t: Lecture 7: Introduction to Galois Fields for the AES by Christof Paar
videos.c: Introduction to Cryptography by Christof Paar
videos.s: Christof Paar's university lecture introducing Galois fields and finite-field arithmetic as used in AES. It covers the mathematics behind the AES S-box.
videos.w: Recommended as a moderately formal, clear introduction to finite fields, useful beyond AES.
videos.q: this is a pretty good introduction (yes, it's for AES, but the principles are the same)

videos.t: CRDTs: The Hard Parts
videos.s: Martin Kleppmann surveys current research on CRDTs, the algorithms for merging concurrent edits across offline replicas. He covers the hard parts such as rich text, moves and merge results that are technically correct but poor.
videos.w: Recommended as an excellent first education on CRDTs and their limits.
videos.q: I found this video from him to be an excellent first education on CRDTs

videos.t: The Mind Behind Windows: Dave Cutler
videos.s: Dave Plummer interviews Dave Cutler, architect of VMS and Windows NT, in a roughly three-hour conversation about his career and the history of Windows.
videos.w: Recommended as a long, excellent first-hand interview with a legendary OS designer, though some note it is light on technical detail.
videos.q: there is an excellent 3 hour long interview with Dave Cutler on that channel.

videos.t: Errol Morris interviews mob lawyer Murray Richman - 1/3
videos.s: Part one of Errol Morris's First Person interview with Murray Richman, a New York lawyer who defends mob figures. He talks about how he sees the law and his clients.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the best interview of Morris's series and as an insight into how the law and ordinary people's minds work.
videos.q: the best one Errol Morris did with his tv series was the one with the mob lawyer.

videos.t: Let’s go whaling: Tricks for monetising mobile game players with free-to-play
videos.s: A 2016 conference talk by a mobile game CEO on the tricks of free-to-play monetization, including player profiles and how to target high-spending whales.
videos.w: HN mostly cites it critically, as an insider's blunt playbook for psychologically exploiting players in F2P and loot box games.
videos.q: Must see video for anyone interested in the topic, from someone explaining how to do these monetizations tactics

videos.t: Saša Jurić - Parsing from first principles - WebCamp Zagreb 2019
videos.s: Sasa Juric explains how to parse a language from first principles without regexes, live-coding a simple parser combinator library in Elixir. It was given at WebCamp Zagreb 2019.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a clear, dense hour on parsers and parser combinators that holds the audience.
videos.q: Saša Jurić is fantastic at condensing lots of information in a 1 hour talk without losing the audience

videos.t: Halt and Catch Fire - Sales Call [ "A16" Scene ]
videos.s: A scene from the TV drama Halt and Catch Fire in which Gordon Clark meets Joe MacMillan, who is posing as an IBM salesman, on a sales call. It includes the dialogue about IBM being the safe choice and a marketing guru telling an engineer when to stop talking.
videos.w: HN commenters post it as a favorite scene about IBM's reputation and sales psychology.
videos.q: one of my favorite scenes from Halt and Catch Fire

videos.t: Glitter Bomb 1.0 vs Porch Pirates
videos.s: Mark Rober builds a glitter-bomb booby-trapped package to take revenge on porch pirates, filming the thieves' reactions. Some reactions were later acknowledged as partially staged.
videos.w: Linked as the funny, famous porch-pirate revenge video whenever package theft comes up, with the faked-reactions caveat noted.
videos.q: watch the video on his YouTube. It's pure comedic gold.

videos.t: Alec Baldwin - Best performance
videos.s: The famous Alec Baldwin monologue from the film Glengarry Glen Ross, where his character Blake berates salesmen with the 'Always Be Closing' speech. It is a short, profane scene about sales pressure and motivation.
videos.w: HN points to it as the one scene worth watching from the movie, a classic about sales and entrepreneurship.
videos.q: Just watch this classic clip from Glengarry Glen Ross

videos.t: Build Your Own Async
videos.s: David Beazley's workshop screencast builds asynchronous programming in Python from scratch, starting from callbacks and continuations and replacing threads to show how concurrency works underneath.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as the best way to understand what async machinery actually does under the covers.
videos.q: an amazing resource to understand async at a deep level

videos.t: Oculus Connect 2: Live Coding Session with John Carmack
videos.s: John Carmack live-codes a simple VR application at Oculus Connect 2 using a Racket-based environment for rapid development and deployment on Gear VR.
videos.w: Cited for watching Carmack code fluently and for the fast iteration cycle of Racket-based VR scripting.
videos.q: it was fantastic because, first, you were showing to your audience how to work with Racket

videos.t: 8088 MPH by Hornet + CRTC + DESiRE
videos.s: 8088 MPH is a demoscene production for the original 1981 IBM PC with CGA graphics and a 4.77MHz 8088, shown with real composite output. It competed at Revision 2015 and pushes the hardware well past what it was thought capable of, breaking emulators.
videos.w: HN points to it as the standard example of what cycle-exact, hardware-level programming can achieve on ancient machines, from the colors it produces to its PC speaker audio.
videos.q: The most amazing thing I've heard done with a PC speaker is in the last part of this equally amazing demo

videos.t: The Obesity Code Lecture (Why do we get Fat?) Part 1
videos.s: Dr. Jason Fung lectures on why obesity became an epidemic since the 1970s, arguing insulin and hormones rather than calories drive weight gain. He explains why calorie counting fails and touches on low-carb eating and fasting.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a compelling alternative explanation of obesity from a prominent proponent.
videos.q: Dr. Jason Fung has a very interesting and, in my opinion, compelling explanation of obesity and weight gain.

videos.t: E-Ink on Android, and other new things!
videos.s: A Technology Connections update video in which Alec Watson tests an Onyx Boox Max e-ink Android tablet used as an external display and shares channel news. It describes his experience with large-format e-ink.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a thorough real-world account of using an e-ink tablet as a computer monitor.
videos.q: Technology Connections on youtube tried to use an eink display and thoroughly described his experiences.

videos.t: Peter Norvig - The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Data
videos.s: Peter Norvig's UBC distinguished lecture on how massive amounts of simple data, such as for language modeling, can yield understanding that hand-built models could not.
videos.w: Recommended as a favorite tech talk showing how huge data availability changes how problems are approached.
videos.q: Norvig does an especially great job in making you truly appreciate the seismic impact that the availability of massive quantities of data can have

videos.t: Andrew Sorensen Keynote: "The Concert Programmer" - OSCON 2014
videos.s: Andrew Sorensen's OSCON 2014 keynote in which he live-codes generative music on stage using his Impromptu environment while narrating his computational and musical choices. It imagines concert programmers as a performing art.
videos.w: HN commenters regard it as an inspiring, all-time favorite demonstration of live coding music.
videos.q: This video of one of his presentations on Impromptu is one of my all-time favorite programming talks

videos.t: Are Space and Time An Illusion?
videos.s: A PBS Space Time episode hosted by Gabe Perez-Giz on the nature of spacetime and whether space and time are fundamental. It builds up reference frames and causality in a short, dense format.
videos.w: HN commenters point to the PBS Space Time series as a high-quality, bite-sized way to learn modern physics concepts.
videos.q: they have an episode that would be a good place to start on warp drives

videos.t: Michael Levin: Anatomical decision-making by cellular collectives
videos.s: Michael Levin presents his lab's work on how cellular collectives use bioelectric networks to make anatomical decisions. Topics include pattern memories, regeneration and synthetic living organisms.
videos.w: HN commenters push it as an example of Levin's talks, which they think deserve far more attention.
videos.q: Almost all the talks I've seen are good, for example

videos.t: Does APL Need a Type System? by Aaron W Hsu at #FnConf18
videos.s: Aaron Hsu's FnConf18 talk asks whether APL needs a static type system. He argues that APL's expressiveness and rapid iteration already deliver the benefits usually credited to types.
videos.w: HN points to it as the main argument from the array-language camp that types are unnecessary there, and as a nuanced take on typed versus untyped programming.
videos.q: which argues that APL already provides the development ergonomics that are typically acribed to type systems.

videos.t: Lee Cronin: Origin of Life, Aliens, Complexity, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #269
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews University of Glasgow chemist Lee Cronin about the origin of life, aliens, complexity and consciousness. The conversation centers on Cronin's assembly theory.
videos.w: HN points to it in origin-of-life and complexity threads as a fascinating long-form introduction to assembly theory.
videos.p: origin of life and assembly theory
videos.q: It really changed my naive perspective of life, and the universe.

videos.t: Primitive Technology: Cord drill and Pump drill
videos.s: Primitive Technology shows building a cord drill from scratch and then upgrading it to a pump drill, using only primitive materials like a stone flywheel and cord.
videos.w: HN people link it as a satisfying demonstration of hand-powered drills being made from nothing.
videos.q: If you're interested in seeing someone make these take a look at this Primitive Technology video

videos.t: Modeling Data Concurrency w/ Asynchronous I/O in Zig - RedisConf 2020
videos.s: Zig creator Andrew Kelley's RedisConf 2020 talk on modeling data flow with asynchronous I/O in Zig. It explains how Zig's async/await avoids function coloring, and Loris Cro demonstrates OkRedis, a zero-allocation Redis client.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the clearest explanation of how Zig achieves colorless async/await.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: I highly recommend watching Andrew Kelley's video

videos.t: Chaos Theory - Awesome 64k Intro! [720p HD]
videos.s: Chaos Theory is a 64k demoscene intro by Conspiracy and CNS that took second place at Assembly 2006, generating its graphics and music from a tiny executable.
videos.w: HN people use it as a showcase of what fits in 64 kilobytes.
videos.q: probably the coolest and most impressive one

videos.t: This is Extremely Dangerous to Our Democracy
videos.s: A short supercut showing many Sinclair-owned local news anchors reading the same scripted warning about biased news, word for word.
videos.w: HN cites it as a vivid example of coordinated messaging and media consolidation, though some mentions use the title only as a quip.
videos.q: Only takes me one minute and thirty six seconds to convince anyone I meet of this point

videos.t: The Fermi Paradox: Dark Forest Theory
videos.s: Isaac Arthur examines the Dark Forest theory, Cixin Liu's proposed solution to the Fermi Paradox in which civilizations stay silent and may destroy any that reveal themselves. He tests the theory's underlying assumptions and arguments.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a well-argued rebuttal of Dark Forest axioms, and recommend his wider Fermi Paradox series.
videos.q: His entire library on the Fermi Paradox is worth watching.

videos.t: CppCon 2017: Fedor Pikus “C++ atomics, from basic to advanced.  What do they really do?”
videos.s: Fedor Pikus's CppCon 2017 talk on C++ atomics, looking at what they let the programmer express and what the hardware actually does. It covers memory ordering and lock-free programming from basic to advanced.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an enlightening explanation of atomics, caches and memory ordering from a strong presenter.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: Watching this was enlightening to say the least (and the presenter is very good)

videos.t: Principles of Natural Running with Dr. Mark Cucuzzella
videos.s: Dr. Mark Cucuzzella of the Natural Running Center gives a short instructional video on natural running form. It describes the principles of good technique, including barefoot-style mechanics.
videos.w: HN commenters call it the best video on natural running form and link it in running technique threads.
videos.q: This is the best video I have seen on natura running form

videos.t: 25c3: The Ultimate Commodore 64 Talk
videos.s: Michael Steil's 25C3 talk covers the Commodore 64's architecture, quirks and demoscene tricks in about an hour. It aims to convey everything about the machine in a compact, nostalgic tour.
videos.w: HN people treat it as the canonical C64 talk and rewatch Steil's 'Ultimate' series regularly.
videos.q: His “Ultimate Guide” talks are great and I rewatch them at least once a year.

videos.t: Ryan Dahl: Original Node.js presentation
videos.s: Ryan Dahl's first presentation of Node.js at JSConf 2009. He pitches event-driven, non-blocking I/O as the motivation, rather than JavaScript itself.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a classic dev tool pitch with palpable energy, and cites it for why Node was created.
videos.q: There is a sort of palpable energy in (Ryan Dahl) node.js original presentation.

videos.t: Have the Boomers Pinched Their Children’s Futures? - with Lord David Willetts
videos.s: Lord David Willetts argues at the Royal Institution that the post-war baby boomers gained wealth and security at the expense of younger generations. He draws on his book The Pinch, covering housing, wealth and social policy in the UK.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a clear exposition of intergenerational unfairness in housing and wages, especially from a UK angle.
videos.q: One of the best expositions of the problem I've seen is this talk

videos.t: HACKENBUSH: a window to a new world of math
videos.s: Owen Maitzen's animated hour-long introduction to Hackenbush, a simple combinatorial game, and how its strategy leads to surreal numbers and the roots of the number system.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible, well-visualized entry point to Hackenbush, surreal numbers and their link to Nim.
videos.q: I found the following video extremely useful and well-visualized

videos.t: Redoing Make - Haskell from Scratch #1
videos.s: The first episode of a screencast series building djb's redo build system from scratch in Haskell. It explains the purpose of redo, writes initial code and sets up a GitHub repository.
videos.w: Recommended to Haskell learners as a rare example of building a real program step by step beyond toy examples.
videos.q: the Jekor Redo [1] videos are fantastic, and demonstrate the slow building up of more complicated things than "reverse this string.

videos.t: Sulforaphane and Its Effects on Cancer, Mortality, Aging, Brain and Behavior, Heart Disease & More
videos.s: Rhonda Patrick of FoundMyFitness makes a case for isothiocyanates such as sulforaphane from cruciferous vegetables and broccoli sprouts. It covers cancer, aging, heart disease, brain and behavior, and neurodegeneration, with chapter timestamps.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a science-backed overview of sulforaphane's health effects, particularly for cancer.
videos.q: Here is a science-backed video talking about the benefits of a substance found in broccoli sprouts w.r.t. cancer.

videos.t: POLYBIUS - The Video Game That Doesn't Exist
videos.s: A 69-minute documentary on the Polybius arcade-game legend. It examines visual, physical and anecdotal evidence, traces the story's source, and concludes the game never existed beyond one website entry.
videos.w: HN rates it among the best gaming video essays and Ahoy as one of the best creators on the platform.
videos.q: the best gaming-related video essay produced!

videos.t: "Tackling Concurrency Bugs with TLA+" by Hillel Wayne
videos.s: Hillel Wayne's Strange Loop talk introducing TLA+ as a specification language for finding concurrency bugs in designs. It covers stalling, race conditions and dropped messages, with PlusCal examples.
videos.w: Recommended as a concise, high-level intro to what TLA+ is and when it helps.
videos.q: If you are new to TLA+ and just want to get the basic idea and use cases, I recommend the talk.

videos.t: The Story of Tetris
videos.s: Gaming Historian recounts how Alexey Pajitnov created Tetris in the Soviet Union and how a fight over publishing rights spanned the West, Mirrorsoft, Nintendo and the Cold War. It runs about an hour with chaptered parts.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an excellent documentary on Tetris and its tangled licensing history.
videos.q: excellent and fascinating documentary on the history of Tetris

videos.t: Smoother animation ≠ Better animation [read pinned comment]
videos.s: Animator Noodle explains why frame interpolation does not make animation better, covering timing, easing, smear frames and using the wrong tool for the job. A pinned correction says the video is partly outdated given later AI developments.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it in motion-smoothing and interpolation threads as an overview of why interpolation hurts animation.
videos.q: A really good video on the subject

videos.t: The Hustle
videos.s: A KRAZAM satirical sketch about hustle culture and productivity obsession in tech.
videos.w: HN posts it as a joke in productivity and focus threads, and some praise the channel as pitch-perfect satire of tech stereotypes.
videos.q: such a pitch perfect shot at a very common person in tech

videos.t: Violence | Slavoj Žižek | Talks at Google
videos.s: Slavoj Zizek discusses his book Violence in an Authors@Google talk in New York. He covers ideology, including his idea of the unknown knowns.
videos.w: Recommended as a relatively clear introduction to Zizek's thinking, especially his account of ideology and unknown knowns.
videos.q: when it comes to discussing ideology, he's doing the best outreach bar none.

videos.t: India's Water Revolution #1: Solving the Crisis in 45 days with the Paani Foundation
videos.s: Permaculture instructor Andrew Millison visits the village of Garavadi in Maharashtra, India, which took part in the Paani Foundation's Water Cup competition. It shows the water harvesting structures the villagers built in 45 days and how they restored groundwater and the local economy.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a hopeful example of land and water management restoring landscapes and livelihoods at village scale.
videos.q: they move thousands of villages from water tank dependency to self-sufficiency in their annual competition.

videos.t: I could hardly believe my eyes! - Looking Glass Holographic Monitor
videos.s: Linus Tech Tips reviews the Looking Glass 8K holographic display, a glasses-free 3D monitor. The video shows the display in action and explains how it works.
videos.w: HN uses it as a reasonably detailed overview of Looking Glass tech, including a segment showing the pixel mapping behind the 3D effect.
videos.q: Linus Tech Tips covered them before that gives a pretty good overview

videos.t: Raiden Warned About AI Censorship - MGS2 Codec Call (2023 Version)
videos.s: A fan-made Metal Gear Solid 2 codec call using AI voice synthesis, in which the Colonel warns Raiden about using AI to censor the internet and enforce digital ID. It riffs on the game's 'Selection for Societal Sanity' conversation.
videos.w: HN users post it as a meme or satirical comment in threads about AI regulation, age verification and online identity.
videos.q: which watching is in my opinion worth your time

videos.t: High Volume, Bandwidth Heavy Infrastructure On The Cheap - Kyle Drake
videos.s: Kyle Drake of Neocities explains the bandwidth pricing pitfalls of the big cloud providers. He describes how to run high-volume, bandwidth-heavy infrastructure far more cheaply, including through co-location.
videos.w: HN recommends it whenever cloud egress costs come up, since it gives concrete numbers on real bandwidth costs versus cloud pricing.
videos.q: Check out this talk by Kyle Drake that goes more into the details of bandwidth costs

videos.t: Tracy Young Speaks at Female Founders Conference 2015
videos.s: Tracy Young, a former construction engineer and cofounder of PlanGrid, speaks at the 2015 Y Combinator Female Founders Conference. She talks about building software for construction superintendents and about customer success.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a strong founder talk that shows how formidable and practical Young is, with advice delivered through a beaver metaphor.
videos.q: If you want to get an idea of how formidable Tracy Young is, watch her talk at the 2015 Female Founders Conference

videos.t: Gary Vaynerchuk Keynote at RailsConf 2010
videos.s: Gary Vaynerchuk's keynote at RailsConf 2010 in Baltimore. The Wine Library TV founder talks about building a business and audience through genuine effort and caring about customers.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an energetic, unscripted talk on creating for the long term and hustling.
videos.q: Go watch Gary Vaynerchuk's talk at RailsConf 2010

videos.t: XAYAX - Bang! (ATARI VCS 2600 demo)
videos.c: MEGA - Museum of Electronic Games & Art
videos.s: Bang! is an Atari 2600 demo by XAYAX that won first place at the Revision 2014 oldschool demo competition. It fits into a 32k ROM using F8SC bankswitching.
videos.w: Commenters hold it up as proof that 2600 programming is alive in the demoscene and as one of the most impressive demos ever made on the hardware.
videos.q: 2600 programming is alive in the demo scene. This was just created in 2014 and is completely insane

videos.t: WOKE BRANDS
videos.s: hbomberguy examines whether a product can be truly progressive, looking at brands that adopt social causes in their marketing, with the Gillette ad as a prompt. It argues the behavior is driven by profit, not politics.
videos.w: Cited in threads on corporate politics, outrage and branding as an explanation of how companies use controversy and social stances for profit.
videos.q: a very poignant discussion of the problematic underpinnings of brands adopting a particular aspect of a "personality

videos.t: Learn to Paint with Mathematics
videos.s: Inigo Quilez live-codes a painting using only mathematics in a shader, building it up step by step. The linked Shadertoy source shows the result.
videos.w: Recommended as the most beginner-friendly way into shader programming and procedural graphics.
videos.q: Watch "Learn to paint with mathematics" to see a simple shader being built gradually

videos.t: Apple's Independent Repair Program is a useless PR stunt.
videos.s: Louis Rossmann argues that Apple's Independent Repair Program is a PR stunt that misleads the public and burdens independent repair shops. He discusses parts access restrictions and program limits.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an insider account from a repair shop owner of why Apple's repair program falls short of real right to repair.
videos.q: Louis Rossmann explains it

videos.t: Clasp: Common Lisp using LLVM and C++ for Designing Molecules
videos.s: Christian Schafmeister's Google Tech Talk on Clasp and CANDO, a Common Lisp implementation on LLVM and C++ used to design molecules, including energy minimization and force-field calculations.
videos.w: Held up in Lisp threads as a striking example of Lisp powering cutting-edge science.
videos.q: I challenge anyone to watch this lecture from Christian Schafmeister and say they are not impressed

videos.t: Google Developers Day US - Python Design Patterns
videos.s: Alex Martelli's Google Developers Day talk on classic design patterns (creational, structural and behavioral) and how they appear in Python. He stresses that patterns must be studied in the context of the implementing language.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a level-headed, practical take on design patterns without Java-style verbosity.
videos.q: I found Alex Martinelli's talk on design patterns very level-headed and instructive

videos.t: Andreessen's Corollary: Ethical Dilemmas in Software Engineering - Bryan Cantrill | Craft 2019
videos.s: Bryan Cantrill's Craft 2019 talk on the ethical dilemmas software engineers face as software eats the world. He explores cases where engineering thinking conflicts with the law or personal morals, including Facebook's news feed experiments.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a good talk on ethics in software engineering, and Cantrill himself cites it as capturing his views.
videos.q: Bryan Cantrill (DTrace etc) has a good talk on ethics in software engineering[0].

videos.t: Super Mario World -- Credits Warp in 5:59.6 (First Time Ever on Console)
videos.s: SethBling performs the first credits warp in Super Mario World on a real SNES console, a glitch that plays the ending without beating Bowser. The run relies on pixel-perfect positioning and tools such as a helper ROM hack.
videos.w: Cited as a landmark of speedrunning, where a trick once limited to tool-assisted runs was pulled off live on hardware.
videos.q: his brief videos give a really nice introduction to the topic that should be accessible to most people

videos.t: The Known Universe by AMNH #datavisualization
videos.s: The American Museum of Natural History's film flies from the Himalayas out through the atmosphere and solar system to the afterglow of the Big Bang, using its Digital Universe Atlas four-dimensional map.
videos.w: HN people share it as an eye-opening, moving visualization of the scale of the universe.
videos.q: So eye opening

videos.t: Brené Brown on Empathy
videos.s: A short animated RSA piece with Dr Brene Brown's voiceover on the difference between empathy and sympathy. She argues that real connection requires getting in touch with your own vulnerability, rather than trying to fix someone's pain.
videos.w: Recommended as a quick, memorable explanation of how to support someone in pain without making it about yourself.
videos.q: the video was still useful for me. It's less than 3 minutes long.

videos.t: Why It's Impossible to Tune a Piano
videos.s: A minutephysics video explaining why a piano cannot be perfectly tuned, comparing equal temperament with just intonation and the math of harmonics.
videos.w: Commenters link it as a quick, clear explanation of why twelve notes only approximate simple ratios.
videos.q: minutephysics had a nice video about the mathematics that go behind piano tuning too.

videos.t: How We Solved the Worst Minigame in Zelda's History
videos.s: Linkus7 explains how a community reverse-engineered The Wind Waker to predict its random number generator and beat the Sploosh Kaboom battleship minigame consistently. It includes d3 animations by Peter Schmidt-Nielsen.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a rigorous, fun example of reverse engineering a game to predict and conquer its RNG.
videos.q: is a fun video about reverse-engineering Zelda to predict the randomness in a minigame

videos.t: CppCon 2015: Bjarne Stroustrup “Writing Good C++14”
