videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a nerve-wracking look at Honnold's free soloing, often when climbing, risk or van life comes up.
videos.q: The whole video is pretty interesting, but may make your hands sweat even more.

videos.t: "Programming Should Eat Itself" by Nada Amin
videos.s: Nada Amin's Strange Loop talk on programming languages that build on themselves, centered on towers of interpreters and nestable interpretation in Scheme. She shows how interpreters can be stacked and collapsed.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a quick, wonderful look at infinite towers of interpreters and what they make possible.
videos.q: Here's a wonderful demonstration of the power of nestability

videos.t: How to Age Gracefully | CBC Radio
videos.s: A five-minute CBC Radio WireTap farewell video in which people of all ages offer words of wisdom to younger people. The advice is short and funny, and keeps coming back to the point that nobody really knows what they are doing.
videos.w: Commenters bring it up in threads about life advice and aging as the best advice they have heard, namely to ignore advice and do your own thing.
videos.q: Best advice on this topic: How to Age Gracefully | CBC Radio

videos.t: Why this British crossroads was so dangerous
videos.s: Tom Scott explains why Ipley Cross in England's New Forest was one of Britain's most dangerous junctions. The angled crossroads lets a car's A-pillar hide approaching traffic and cyclists because there is no relative motion in the driver's view.
videos.w: Used as the go-to visual demonstration of A-pillar blind spots and badly designed junctions.
videos.q: Tom Scott has a good video for anyone looking for a visual of this phenomenon

videos.t: Getting Started With Org Mode
videos.s: Harry Schwartz gives a roughly hour-long tour of Emacs Org mode as an outliner, task manager, markup language and agenda tool. He demonstrates how he uses it for documents, presentations and todo lists.
videos.w: Recommended as a thorough introduction showing what Org mode can do for personal organization.
videos.q: which is a great demonstration on Emacs and Org Mode's potential as an organizational tool.

videos.t: Yanis Varoufakis with Professor Noam Chomsky at NYPL, April 16, 2016 | DiEM25
videos.s: Yanis Varoufakis and Noam Chomsky talk on stage at the New York Public Library in 2016. They cover the Greek financial crisis, European politics, neoliberalism and America's economic future, drawing on Varoufakis's book.
videos.w: Recommended as a long, insightful conversation that gives a view of how Greece was pressured during the bailouts.
videos.q: Yanis in conversation with Chomsky, long but insightful.

videos.t: Simon Peyton Jones - Linear Haskell: practical linearity in a higher-order polymorphic language
videos.s: Simon Peyton Jones presents linear types for Haskell, showing how practical linearity can fit into a higher-order polymorphic language. The talk covers motivations such as resource handling and relates the ideas to Rust.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear introduction to linear types in GHC from the language's lead designer.
videos.q: Simon Peyton Jones has a great talk on YouTube [3]

videos.t: Keynote: What is a Component (and Why)? - Luke Wagner, Distinguished Engineer, Fastly
videos.s: Luke Wagner of Fastly explains what a WebAssembly component is, how it relates to familiar concepts, and what the Component Model enables. It emphasizes security, composability and modularity.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the best starting point for understanding the Wasm Component Model and WASI direction, straight from its designer.
videos.q: I thought this keynote presentation[0] by Luke Wagner at Wasmcon was great and covered it very well.

videos.t: Quantum Entanglement and the Great Bohr-Einstein Debate | Space Time | PBS Digital Studios
videos.s: PBS Space Time explains the Bohr-Einstein debate over quantum mechanics and how quantum entanglement settled it. It covers the weirdness of measurement and nonlocal correlations.
videos.w: HN points to it as a clear, approachable explanation of quantum entanglement.
videos.q: there is a great video by the PBS space time channel explaining quantum entanglement

videos.t: Deadly Truth of General AI? - Computerphile
videos.s: A Computerphile video in which Rob Miles warns against assuming a general AI will think like a human. He uses the thought experiment of a stamp-collecting AI to show how a goal-driven system could pursue its aim with dangerous results.
videos.w: Often pointed to as an accessible first introduction to AI safety and why a superintelligent AI could be dangerous.
videos.q: There's a great Computerphile video from 2015 that introduced me to the idea of AI safety awhile ago.

videos.t: Gabe Newell: On Productivity, Economics, Political Institutions, and the Future of Corporations
videos.s: Gabe Newell of Valve speaks at UT Austin's LBJ School on productivity, economics, political institutions and the future of corporations. He discusses in-game economies and how Valve organizes work.
videos.w: Pointed to as an in-depth view of how Valve is run and how Newell thinks about workers, management and customers.
videos.q: For an understanding of what Valve are doing, here is a 1 hour talk by Gabe Newell (CEO)

videos.t: The Computer Chronicles - Gary Kildall Special (1995)
videos.s: A 1995 episode of The Computer Chronicles devoted to Gary Kildall, creator of CP/M. It works as a retrospective and tribute to the personal computer pioneer.
videos.w: HN recommends it to see what Kildall was like in real life and as a tribute to an influential figure.
videos.q: If you want to know how was he IRL I recommend watching Computer chronicles.

videos.t: How "oldschool" graphics worked Part 1 - Commodore and Nintendo
videos.s: The 8-Bit Guy explains the color limitations of 1980s computers and consoles such as the NES and Commodore 64. It shows how sprites, attributes and palettes shaped the look of old games.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear, approachable explanation of how retro graphics hardware actually worked.
videos.q: The 8-Bit Guy has some great videos about how graphics worked on the older systems

videos.t: The Five Freedoms of Aviation
videos.s: A Wendover Productions explainer on the political agreements, from the Chicago Convention onward, that determine which airlines can fly where. It lays out the five freedoms of the air.
videos.w: HN links it whenever airline route rules, cabotage or loopholes come up, as a concise background explainer.
videos.q: This video has a lot of good info on it

videos.t: Why guitarists USED TO play more in tune! (Microtonal Frets)
videos.s: Classical guitarist Brandon Acker shows how guitars with tied-on gut frets, as used 300 years ago, can play more in tune than modern fixed metal frets. He demonstrates microtonal and meantone tunings on a guitar with movable frets.
videos.w: Pointed to in tuning and temperament threads as an audible demonstration of how meantone differs from equal temperament.
videos.q: Brandon Acker gives a wonderful overview on the classical guitar

videos.t: Turning Waves Into Particles
videos.s: Huygens Optics explores the idea that space is a non-linear elastic medium, and uses simulations to show how wave energy might be confined locally into particle-like objects. It touches on inertia, the Schwinger limit and the vacuum as a medium.
videos.w: HN commenters find the hypothesis elegant and the channel consistently thought-provoking, and point to it in threads on light, particles and wave functions.
videos.q: the explanation is beautiful in its simplicity

videos.t: Elon Musk : How to Build the Future
videos.s: A 20-minute Y Combinator interview in which Sam Altman asks Elon Musk how to build the future. Topics include which problems a 22-year-old should work on, such as AI, genetics, and brain interfaces, and general advice for founders.
videos.w: Offered as a more down-to-earth Musk interview with better questions than most, and cited for his stated concerns about concentrated AI power.
videos.q: A more down-to-earth video to watch might be this one

videos.t: Dan Deacon - Bromst - In The Studio
videos.s: A Pitchfork TV documentary following Dan Deacon in Montana as he finishes his album Bromst. It shows the experimentation behind it, including pieces written for MIDI-driven player pianos.
videos.w: HN points to it in threads on black MIDI and player pianos as a look at an artist writing tuneful music beyond human playability.
videos.q: He talks about it quite in a bit in a Pitchfork TV video that documented him working on one of his albums, Bromst

videos.t: GSMT - Dan Holohan, Author: "The Lost Art of Steam Heating"
videos.c: The General Society of Mechanics and Tradesmen
videos.s: Dan Holohan, author of The Lost Art of Steam Heating, talks about the old steam heating systems he learned about from veteran tradesmen. He shares stories and practical lessons on how these systems work, including running steam at low temperatures.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an informative talk on steam heating whose advice to respect old working systems carries over to software.
videos.q: When you see something that's old and it's been there for a long time and it's working, don't laugh at it.

videos.t: Arcologies
videos.s: An Isaac Arthur episode on arcologies, self-sufficient habitats that could house whole cities, on Earth or on harsh worlds. It covers how such structures might work and what limits their size.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it in population and megacity discussions, mainly for its estimates of how many people arcologies could support and the heat, power and elevator bottlenecks.
videos.q: Isaac Arthur's YouTube channel is full of speculation and plans for all kinds of possible or nearly-possible futures

videos.t: How to Achieve Your Most Ambitious Goals | Stephen Duneier | TEDxTucson
videos.s: Stephen Duneier describes a decision-making approach that took him from struggling with simple tasks to achieving ambitious goals. The talk centers on breaking goals into small marginal adjustments.
videos.w: HN people recommend it for its simple, powerful idea of marginal adjustments and its usefulness for tackling big projects.
videos.q: The idea of marginal adjustment is both simple and powerful.

videos.t: Light Waves Visualized using Photon Sieves.
videos.s: Huygens Optics shows how DIY photon sieves shape a laser's wave front, explaining how they differ from zone plates and how aperture count affects the focal point, with time-resolved visualizations of the diffraction.
videos.w: HN points to it for a clear explanation of photon sieves versus Fresnel lenses and for showing what interference patterns actually look like.
videos.q: It shows how the interference patterns actually look.

videos.t: Noam Chomsky - Manufacturing Consent
videos.s: A nine-minute excerpt from the 1992 documentary Manufacturing Consent in which Noam Chomsky summarizes how corporate media shapes public discourse.
videos.w: Cited as a short overview of the propaganda model whenever commenters discuss media influence and consent manufacturing.
videos.q: Here's a clip from a documentary based on the book

videos.t: A Conversation with Peter Thiel and Niall Ferguson - Institute of Politics
videos.s: A 2012 Harvard Institute of Politics conversation between Peter Thiel and historian Niall Ferguson. Thiel discusses technology, politics and his stagnation hypothesis.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as one of the best single introductions to Thiel's worldview on technology and stagnation.
videos.q: Watch this if you only watch one video

videos.t: Arnold Schwarzenegger 2018 - The speech that broke the internet - Most Inspiring ever
videos.s: A motivational compilation of Arnold Schwarzenegger's 2018 speech, delivered as inspiration about work and purpose.
videos.w: HN users recommend it as practical motivation against procrastination and for people unsure what to do next.
videos.q: since watching Arnie's take on this I cannot get it out of my head and I have actually found it helpful

videos.t: You Suck at Photoshop - Distort, Warp, & Layer Effects
videos.s: An episode of the comedic You Suck at Photoshop series in which Donnie Hoyle teaches distort, warp and layer effects while vandalizing a Vanagon in the image. It won Webby awards as a how-to and comedy series.
videos.w: Recommended as a classic, funny Photoshop tutorial series with a strong comedic personality.
videos.q: Enjoy and you're welcome!

videos.t: Tesla Autonomy Day
videos.s: Tesla's roughly four-hour Autonomy Day investor event covers its in-house self-driving chip, vision-only approach, fleet data engine and robotaxi plans, with talks by Andrej Karpathy and others.
videos.w: Cited both as a primary source on Tesla's technical autonomy approach and, later, for Musk's unmet robotaxi predictions.
videos.q: Watch the presentation from 6 months ago, where they explain the decision to build their own hardware for inferring

videos.t: 12 Principles of Animation (Official Full Series)
videos.s: Alan Becker's short series on the 12 principles of animation, covering squash and stretch, anticipation, staging, timing, arcs, appeal and the rest. Each principle gets a brief animated illustration.
videos.w: Recommended as a compact starting point for making animations feel more compelling, including for UI and app developers.
videos.q: The video I linked will help the animation more compelling for the viewer.

videos.t: The Only Famous Motherboard
videos.s: Cathode Ray Dude's hour-long retrospective on the ABIT BP6, the dual-Celeron motherboard. He covers early multiprocessing, its legend, a build, running NT 4, benchmarks and the pros and cons of early SMP.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an excellent history of the famous ABIT BP6 board.
videos.q: Cathode Ray Dude's channel has a great video about the history of this amazing motherboard

videos.t: NeXT vs Sun
videos.s: A 1991 NeXT promotional video that stages a head-to-head programming contest between a NeXT computer and a Sun workstation. It shows NeXT's interface builder and object-oriented tooling producing an application far faster than traditional UNIX development.
videos.w: HN uses it as the canonical example of rapid application development and object-oriented tooling productivity, though many note it is biased marketing.
videos.q: I don't know how realistic is this video but it was interesting

videos.t: “What is Success?” by Evan Czaplicki
videos.s: Elm creator Evan Czaplicki's 2018 Elm Europe talk on how to define success for an open source project and language community. It argues against judging projects by GitHub activity and touches on community expectations.
videos.w: Cited in debates over Elm's direction and open source health, with some praising its points about metrics and others finding its tone toward unhappy users hard to watch.
videos.q: he raises some interesting points about how measuring projects by Github activity is strongly biased

videos.t: The Antique Microwave Oven that's Better than Yours
videos.s: Technology Connections examines an old feature-rich microwave and shows how it uses a humidity or steam sensor and lookup data to cook food well, arguing it beats many modern ones.
videos.w: Cited again and again in microwave and smart-appliance threads as proof that older appliances were smarter, especially for steam-sensor cooking.
videos.q: it explains how microwaves use a humidity probe to sense steam escaping from say a microwave-popcorn bag to determine when its done.

videos.t: Why Alien Life Would be our Doom - The Great Filter
videos.s: A short Kurzgesagt animation explaining the Great Filter, the idea that finding alien life might be bad news because it implies something usually destroys civilizations. It connects the concept to the Fermi paradox.
videos.w: HN links it as a concise, accessible explainer whenever the Fermi paradox or Great Filter comes up, though one commenter criticized its lack of source attribution.
videos.q: There is also a good video from Kurzgesagt explaining the great filter

videos.t: Teenage engineering OP1 - Live looping  [Thoj]
videos.s: Musician Thoj performs a live looping session on the Teenage Engineering OP-1 synthesizer, building a deep house track layer by layer.
videos.w: HN points to it as a demonstration of the OP-1, a well-designed instrument and an accessible way to start making music.
videos.q: The OP-1 in action

videos.t: The Truth About Electric Towing
videos.s: Aging Wheels tests how towing trailers affects the range of electric trucks, including a Silverado EV. It shows that trailer aerodynamics matters far more than added weight.
videos.w: HN cites it as data-backed evidence that weight has little effect on EV range while air resistance from trailers does.
videos.q: The YouTube channel Aging Wheels has two good videos on this.

videos.t: Games, Schools, and Worlds Designed for Violence
videos.s: Jacob Geller's video essay examines how architecture in schools and in video games, such as cover shooters, is shaped by violence. It touches on brutalism, campus policing and protests.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an informed look at architecture in games and at how school design relates to shooter maps and Columbine.
videos.p: architecture of violence in games and schools
videos.q: Jacob Geller did a really interesting video essay

videos.t: Joe Armstrong & Jeremy Ruston - Intertwingling the Tiddlywiki with Erlang | Code Mesh LDN 18
videos.s: Joe Armstrong, creator of Erlang, and Jeremy Ruston, creator of TiddlyWiki, discuss hypertext, Ted Nelson's idea of intertwingled knowledge, and a way to combine TiddlyWiki with Erlang. It is a Code Mesh LDN 2018 talk.
videos.w: Recommended in note-taking and personal wiki threads for its enthusiasm about granular, densely linked notes and TiddlyWiki.
videos.q: great talk by its creator Jeremy Ruston and the late creator of Erlang, Joe Armstrong

videos.t: Buster Keaton - The Art of the Gag
videos.s: An Every Frame a Painting video essay on Buster Keaton's visual comedy, examining how he built and framed his gags. It uses clips from his silent films to show the thinking behind them.
videos.w: Recommended as a short, excellent analysis of Keaton and visual comedy.
videos.q: a great Every Frame a Painting film essay on his work

videos.t: This AI actually WORKS!!! - NVIDIA RTX Voice
videos.s: A ShortCircuit (Linus Tech Tips) review of Nvidia's RTX Voice, which uses GPU-based neural networks to remove background noise from microphone audio. It demonstrates how well the filtering works.
videos.w: Cited as a demo of GPU-powered noise suppression that works remarkably well, in threads on mic muting and speech enhancement.
videos.q: It's really pretty impressive, here's a demo

videos.t: Ricky Jay - Amazing Card Trick/Manipulation
videos.s: A three-minute clip of magician Ricky Jay performing a card manipulation routine, including table faro shuffles. The routine builds in intensity and ends with a surprising finish.
videos.w: HN people share it as a classic example of sleight-of-hand mastery whose ending is mind-blowing.
videos.q: The manipulations are pretty amazing and then at the end it's mindblowing.

videos.t: Growing Human Neurons on a Home Made Electrode Array
videos.s: The Thought Emporium builds a homemade multi-electrode array, grows human neurons on it and attempts to take readings. It is the first part of a series aimed at connecting living neurons to a computer.
videos.w: HN cites it as an impressive garage-science example of neuron-computer interfaces and hard-science DIY biology.
videos.q: Seeing a dude grow human neurons directly connected to a computer chip to make a "human AI", all from his garage

videos.t: China’s Vanishing Muslims: Undercover In The Most Dystopian Place In The World
videos.s: VICE News reporter Isobel Yeung goes undercover as a tourist in Xinjiang, documenting heavy surveillance, policing and internment of Uighurs. It also covers children taken into state-run institutions.
videos.w: HN cites it as first-hand, independent reporting on Xinjiang that does not rely on state-sanctioned access.
videos.q: here's a very thorough look from an established news source

videos.t: An Intro to KiCad – Part 1: How PCBs Are Made | DigiKey
videos.s: Shawn Hymel of DigiKey introduces KiCad and explains how printed circuit boards are manufactured. It is the first part of a beginner series that builds a 555 badge project.
videos.w: Recommended as a friendly starting point for people who want to learn PCB design with free tools.
videos.q: Digikey actually makes really nice YouTube tutorials on how to use KiCAD

videos.t: What's a Memory Allocator Anyway? - Benjamin Feng
videos.s: A Zig SHOWTIME talk by Benjamin Feng on what a memory allocator is, followed by an interview. It covers allocation strategies and different allocator types in Zig.
videos.w: Recommended as a quick, clear overview of allocators and arenas that also shows how Zig approaches allocation.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

videos.t: Amazing! Bird Sounds From The Lyre Bird - David Attenborough  - BBC Wildlife
videos.s: A short BBC clip in which David Attenborough shows a lyrebird imitating sounds, including camera shutters, car alarms and chainsaws. It comes from the BBC natural history series Life on Earth.
videos.w: Brought up whenever threads touch on mimicry, voice cloning or bird vocalization, and people say the ending is startling.
videos.q: The end of this BBC clip blew my mind the first time I saw it.

videos.t: The Most Common Cognitive Bias
videos.s: A Veritasium video that runs the 2-4-8 rule-guessing puzzle on people to show how they test only examples that confirm their hypothesis. It uses this to illustrate confirmation bias and falsification.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear demonstration of confirmation bias and the value of trying to break your own hypothesis.
videos.q: I would suggest this video by Veritasium, which also touches on this, at a very fundamental level

videos.t: 3D Gaussian Splatting! - Computerphile
videos.s: A Computerphile video in which Dr Mike Pound and PhD student Lewis Stuart explain 3D Gaussian splatting, a quick technique that turns photos of a scene into a 3D model without much compute. It includes a demo and compares the approach to NeRFs.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible introduction to Gaussian splats, made by people who understand the subject.
videos.q: Here's a much better explainer from some people who seem to actually understand the subject matter and not just the buzzwords

videos.t: The rigs we've created for chipsynth MD's emulation.
videos.s: A Plogue developer shows the custom electronic test rigs built to measure the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis sound chip (YM2612) for the chipsynth MD emulation. It covers the years of testing and reverse engineering needed to reproduce the chip's quirks accurately.
videos.w: Recommended in threads on chip emulation as a look at how hard it is to emulate vintage sound hardware accurately.
videos.q: This video shows some insight into the development process

videos.t: Applied Sciences Group: High Performance Touch
videos.s: A Microsoft Research demo from TechFest 2012 of a lab touch system that lets viewers feel the effect of different input latencies, down to about 1 ms. It shows how much more responsive dragging feels compared with typical 100 ms touch delay.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it whenever input latency comes up, as the demonstration that people can perceive touch delay down to 1 ms.
videos.q: It shows the difference between from >100ms to ~1ms. It's mind baffling.

videos.t: Jonathan Haidt: The moral roots of liberals and conservatives
videos.s: Psychologist Jonathan Haidt presents his moral foundations research in a TED talk. He argues that liberals and conservatives weigh a different set of moral values, which helps explain political divides.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible way to understand why people across the political spectrum disagree and to better understand opposing views.
videos.q: Jonathon Haidt has actually done some great scientific work on the real differences between liberals and conservatives.

videos.t: Fluorine - Periodic Table of Videos
videos.s: Periodic Videos visits a fluorine expert to show how reactive the element is in action. It also includes a discussion of fluoride and tooth enamel.
videos.w: Recommended in fluoride and fluorine threads as a short, fun demonstration of how nasty fluorine is.
videos.q: tooth chat at 5:10, but the whole video is interesting

videos.t: Principles of economics, translated
videos.s: Economist-comedian Yoram Bauman delivers a humorous translation of Mankiw's ten principles of economics for the uninitiated. It was presented at the AAAS humor session in 2007.
videos.w: HN points to it as a short, funny and genuinely informative take on economic principles such as trade and opportunity cost.
videos.q: a great 5min video

videos.t: Introduction to Julia - Part 1 | SciPy 2014 | David Sanders
videos.s: David Sanders gives the first part of a two-part introduction to the Julia programming language at SciPy 2014. It walks through the language's basics and its appeal for scientific computing.
videos.w: HN commenters point newcomers to it as a solid starting point for getting to know Julia.
videos.q: I've found these talks useful as a starting point

videos.t: EEVblog #1132 - The 3 Cent Microcontroller!
videos.s: Dave Jones of EEVblog looks at a sub-3-cent microcontroller from Padauk and other obscure Chinese manufacturers. He shows how to find such parts and where to buy them in stock.
videos.w: Cited as the go-to demo that full microcontrollers now cost about three cents, replacing things like the 555 timer.
videos.q: Dave Jones' EEVBlog recently posted a video on cheap microcontrollers (<0.03USD)

videos.t: Homebrew NMOS Transistor Step by Step - So Easy Even Jeri Can Do It
videos.s: Jeri Ellsworth shows step by step how to make an NMOS transistor at home using a kiln, rust remover, spin-on dopant, eBay wafers and vinyl stickers.
videos.w: HN points to it as the classic example of home-made semiconductors and a fun way to go down to the transistor level.
videos.q: If you want to go further down, check out Jeri Ellsworth's old videos where she built a transistor at home

videos.t: The largest campaign ever to stop publishers destroying games
videos.s: Ross Scott of Accursed Farms lays out a campaign to stop publishers from permanently shutting down games, using The Crew as the test case. He covers government initiatives and the legal options, and the stopkillinggames.com site.
videos.w: HN points to it as the original statement of the Stop Killing Games campaign.
videos.q: Here's the original intro to Stop Killing Games by Ross

videos.t: Why Google Stores Billions of Lines of Code in a Single Repository
videos.s: Rachel Potvin describes the scale of Google's codebase and its custom monolithic source repository. She explains the reasons for the monorepo model, the tooling that makes it workable, and its tradeoffs.
videos.w: The go-to reference in monorepo and trunk-based development discussions, recommended as a firsthand account of how Google manages source control.
videos.q: I'd recommend this video that describes it.

videos.t: Tested: Where Does The Tone Come From In A Guitar Amplifier?
videos.s: Guitarist Jim Lill spends a year testing where guitar amplifier tone comes from, swapping tubes, rectifiers and bias types. He finds that much of it can be reproduced with EQ and distortion in different orders.
videos.w: Recommended as a systematic, surprising experiment, often cited in audio and gear-obsession threads.
videos.q: check out this guy who ran a much more systematic set of experiments

videos.t: Parsing JSON Really Quickly: Lessons Learned
videos.s: Daniel Lemire's QCon talk on how simdjson parses gigabytes of JSON per second. It covers SIMD vectorization, branch prediction and the lessons learned building a fast parser.
videos.w: HN points to it as the best explanation of simdjson internals and of why fast parsing is rarely disk-bound.
videos.q: It's worth looking at if you're into this sort of thing.

videos.t: The Secret Reason Horses Let Us Ride Them
videos.s: CGP Grey explains why horses could be ridden and why other animals like zebras and bears were never domesticated for war or riding. It is a follow-up on the topic of animal domestication.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a classic on why some animals are suited to farming and domestication and others are not.
videos.q: CGP Grey has a great video [0] that goes into why some animals are better to farm/breed/eat than others.

videos.t: Reynolds Number - Numberphile
videos.s: Numberphile with Tom Crawford of Oxford explains the Reynolds number, the second of three videos on Navier-Stokes and fluid flow, with demonstrations of laminar versus turbulent behavior.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible layperson's introduction to the Reynolds number and fluid dynamics scales.
videos.q: I think this is a good lay-person's introduction to basis of Kolmogorov's length scale, specifically the Reynold's number

videos.t: How Modern SQL Databases Come up with Algorithms that You Would Have Never Dreamed Of by Lukas Eder
videos.s: Lukas Eder's Devoxx talk on how modern cost-based SQL optimizers rewrite and plan queries in ways developers would not expect. It argues that declarative SQL, used well, can run complex queries very fast.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it to developers unfamiliar with how much leverage and intelligence there is in a SQL database.
videos.q: I'd suggest watching this video to get a flavor of how much leverage using the database can give you

videos.t: Hacking at Quantum Speed with Shor's Algorithm | Infinite Series
videos.s: PBS Infinite Series explains how Shor's algorithm lets a quantum computer break RSA encryption, building on earlier episodes about cryptography and the math of quantum computers. It works through the idea step by step.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear, worked explanation of Shor's algorithm for building intuition.
videos.q: I thought this example of Shor's algorithm was pretty good

videos.t: PTVS 2.0 Beta: Mixed-Mode Python/C/C++ Debugging overview
videos.s: An overview of the PTVS 2.0 beta feature for debugging Python and C/C++ together in one session in Visual Studio.
videos.w: Linked whenever mixed Python and C++ debugging came up as a neat PTVS feature.
videos.q: if you want to get a feel for an advanced feature, try

videos.t: Visualising software architecture with the C4 model - Simon Brown, Agile on the Beach 2019
videos.s: Simon Brown's Agile on the Beach 2019 talk presents the C4 model, a lightweight approach to diagramming software architecture with a shared vocabulary and simple notation.
videos.w: Recommended as the introduction to C4 when people ask how to visualize and communicate software architecture.
videos.q: If C4 is new to you too, I recommend their intro video

videos.t: Invisibility Training for Motorcyclists
videos.s: FortNine's tongue-in-cheek guide to why drivers fail to see motorcyclists and how riders can make themselves more visible. It touches on perception psychology, including the role of saccades.
videos.w: Cited in threads on motorcycle and cyclist safety to explain why drivers look and still miss them.
videos.q: a longer but more relevant "motorcycle invisibility training" video

videos.t: Everything is a Remix (2023 Edition)
videos.s: Kirby Ferguson's updated four-part video essay arguing that creativity is built on copying, transforming and combining existing work. It covers examples from film, music and technology and touches on generative AI.
videos.w: Pointed to in copyright and AI debates as a compelling case that all culture is remix.
videos.q: It highlights how essentially everything in culture is a remix of some previous version of the culture

videos.t: Inside Africa's Food Forest Mega-Project
videos.s: Permaculture instructor Andrew Millison travels with the UN World Food Programme to Niger to see land recovery within the Great Green Wall, where rainwater harvesting is boosting food security and restoring the ecosystem.
videos.w: Recommended in regreening and desertification threads as an optimistic, constructive example of land restoration.
videos.q: A few good ones that I watched: - Inside Africa's Food Forest Mega-Project

videos.t: The KGB, The Computer and Me - The Cuckoo’s Egg Story
videos.s: A 57-minute account of Clifford Stoll's tracking of a KGB-linked hacker through Lawrence Berkeley Lab computers in 1986, the story of The Cuckoo's Egg. It covers the FBI and Chaos Computer Club involvement.
videos.w: Recommended as a documentary telling the early hacking and spy-hunting story, with the original people involved.
videos.q: It's quite amazing to see the original people involved recreating events just a few years after they took place

videos.t: DEF CON 26  - Christopher Domas - The Ring 0 Facade Awakening the Processors Inner Demons
videos.s: Christopher Domas's DEF CON 26 talk on secret processor registers that vendors reserve for third parties holding trusted keys. He examines how users are locked out of parts of their own CPUs.
videos.w: HN commenters call his x86 internals talks spectacular and mention them whenever low-level processor surprises come up.
videos.q: I remember watching his Defcon talks on x86 shenanigans[^1][^2] and being amazed at what he's been able to discover

videos.t: Emulating the DX7 the HARD way
videos.s: An episode of Plogue's chipresearch series on emulating the Yamaha DX7 from the hardware up. It covers the sub CPU and main CPU, address map investigation, cartridges, firmware analysis and a skeleton MAME driver.
videos.w: Recommended in DX7 reverse-engineering threads as a look at the effort behind bit-accurate emulation.
videos.q: a YouTube video about the reverse engineering process from David at Plogue

videos.t: Erlang Factory SF 2016 Keynote  Phoenix and Elm – Making the Web Functional
videos.s: A joint Erlang Factory 2016 keynote by Phoenix creator Chris McCord and Elm creator Evan Czaplicki on using the two together, including Phoenix.Presence design and PubSub optimizations.
videos.w: Pointed to as the best source on Phoenix Presence internals and for combining Phoenix with Elm.
videos.q: My Erlang Factory keynote also goes into the design considerations and PubSub layer optimizations that sits underneath Phoenix.Presence

videos.t: Bitcoin Is Protecting Human Rights Around the World
videos.s: A Reason TV segment, drawing on Alex Gladstein of the Human Rights Foundation, argues that Bitcoin works as an escape hatch for people living under authoritarian governments and inflating currencies.
videos.w: HN commenters use it in crypto debates as evidence that Bitcoin matters for people in unstable-currency countries.
videos.q: Actually it's pretty important for many

videos.t: Seymour Papert
videos.s: A short vintage film clip of Seymour Papert, creator of Logo, on using computers to spark children's imagination and learning.
videos.w: Recommended as a glimpse of Papert's vision of computers as tools for learning, shared especially after his death.
videos.q: I firmly believe that we'd all be better off if THIS guy had been the one to introduce computers to the common man

videos.t: Killing a Toyota Part 1 | Top Gear | BBC
videos.s: Top Gear episode in which Jeremy Clarkson and team try to destroy a Toyota Hilux pickup through water, fire, and a demolished building. It is the first part of the 'Killing a Toyota' series.
videos.w: HN uses it as the go-to evidence for Toyota pickup durability, and as a benchmark in discussions of truck toughness.
videos.q: It's a worthwhile watch if you want to see truck survive after being drowned in water, fire, and the rubble of a demolished skyscraper.

videos.t: The Maths of General Relativity (1/8) - Spacetime and Worldlines
videos.s: The first of an eight-part ScienceClic series building general relativity, covering worldlines, proper time and coordinate systems with animated visualizations.
videos.w: Praised for its visualizations and pedagogy in threads about physics and differential geometry.
videos.q: it covers it with incredible visualizations and pedagogical approach

videos.t: Pranks Destroy Scam Callers- GlitterBomb Payback
videos.s: Mark Rober and collaborators build glitter bomb traps and other pranks to fight phone scam call centers, and share evidence about the operations.
videos.w: Offered as a satisfying example of fighting back against scam call centers.
videos.q: Here is Mark Rober basically bringing the war to their shores with incredible pranks

videos.t: McMurtry Speirling BREAKS Goodwood Hillclimb Record!! 39.08!
videos.s: Coverage of the McMurtry Speirling fan car breaking the Goodwood hillclimb record with a 39.08 second run driven by Max Chilton. It beat the Volkswagen ID.R and the 1999 McLaren time.
videos.w: Shared as a striking example of a fan car using powered ground effect, with an eye-popping launch, in EV and motorsport threads.
videos.q: Take a look at the Speirling at Goodwood Festival of Speed for an awfully mean fan car.

videos.t: history of the entire world, i guess
videos.s: A fast, absurdist 19-minute animated run through the history of the whole world, narrated and scored by Bill Wurtz in his distinctive style. It compresses millennia of events into jokes, songs and quick visuals.
videos.w: HN commenters list it among favorite long-form, info-dense YouTube videos and as a representative piece of Wurtz's quirky creativity.
videos.q: history of the entire world, i guess

videos.t: Cordyceps: attack of the killer fungi - Planet Earth Attenborough BBC wildlife
videos.s: A three-minute clip from BBC's Planet Earth narrated by David Attenborough about Cordyceps, the fungus that infects insects and takes over their behavior. It shows an infected ant and its demise.
videos.w: HN links it as the quick introduction to zombie-ant fungi whenever the topic comes up.
videos.q: For anyone else not familiar with cordyceps fungi, here's a three-minute clip from BCC Planet Earth

videos.t: Who’s Taking America’s Water? | Climate Town
videos.s: A Climate Town episode on who uses America's water, particularly Western water. It looks at agriculture such as alfalfa and animal feed, and at water-rights rules that discourage conservation.
videos.w: HN points to it in Colorado River and water-use threads as an accessible explainer of why the Western water shortage keeps getting worse.
videos.q: Climate Town has a good explainer

videos.t: How to write cuneiform with Irving Finkel and @preservethings I Curator's Corner S4 Ep9
videos.s: British Museum curator Irving Finkel teaches how to write cuneiform, with a colleague following along. It is a short, lively introduction to the script.
videos.w: Recommended as the best short, funny and approachable introduction to cuneiform on YouTube.
videos.q: It's short enough for an introduction, funny and entertaining

videos.t: How the US Postal Service reads terrible handwriting
videos.s: Tom Scott visits the USPS Remote Encoding Center in Salt Lake City, where keyers decipher mail images machines cannot read. It shows the lengths taken to decode bad handwriting.
videos.w: Recommended in address and OCR threads as a look at the last human mail-coding operation.
videos.q: This Tom Scott video shows some of the surprising (to me) lengths to which the USPS does go to figure out the right address

videos.t: Kinesin protein walking on microtubule
videos.s: A very short animation of a kinesin motor protein walking along a microtubule inside a cell, carrying cargo.
videos.w: Shared as a vivid illustration of molecular machines at work inside cells.
videos.q: Take a look at dynein and kinesin walking along microtubules while dragging along their cargo. It's pretty neat.

videos.t: Badness 0 (Apostrophe‛s version)
videos.s: Tom 7's pilot episode of a series that plays with type systems and absurd programming, presented as a parody of the GPL v3 license. It mixes a typesetting experiment with a long, story-driven intro on the origin of TeX. Source code and papers are linked from the author's site.
videos.w: HN readers point to it as an example of Tom7's ridiculous-but-brilliant programming projects, here tied to license parody and typesetting.
videos.q: this fun experiment in Typesetting which starts off with the amazing TeX origin story

videos.t: Elon Musk Interview: 1-on-1 with Sandy Munro
videos.s: Sandy Munro interviews Elon Musk at Boca Chica about Tesla production, mega-castings, seats, structural battery packs and the difficulty of mass production.
videos.w: HN uses it as a primary source on Tesla manufacturing and engineering decisions and Musk's grasp of product detail.
videos.q: Check out this video of Musk and Sandy Munro (former Chief Engineer at Ford) talking about it

videos.t: A Physics Professor Bet Me $10,000 I'm Wrong
videos.s: Veritasium recounts a $10,000 bet with a UCLA physics professor over whether a vehicle can travel downwind faster than the wind. He presents the professor's reasoning and demonstrations, including one without aerodynamics.
videos.w: Linked as clear demonstrations that make the counterintuitive faster-than-wind result click.
videos.q: The small demonstration that made it click for me is from that video

videos.t: Shared memory parallelism in Julia | Kiran Pamnany | Cambridge Julia Meetup (May 2018)
videos.s: Kiran Pamnany's Cambridge Julia Meetup talk on Julia's shared memory parallelism and its new task scheduler. It argues that fork-join and work-stealing models nest poorly and presents depth-first scheduling for composable parallelism.
videos.w: Recommended in Julia threading threads as an insightful, simple explanation of the new task scheduler.
videos.q: I found his talk to be an insightful overview of this work

videos.t: Terence Tao on the cosmic distance ladder
videos.s: Terence Tao and Grant Sanderson of 3Blue1Brown walk through the cosmic distance ladder, showing how humans measured distances from the Earth to the Moon, Sun, planets and beyond. It includes animations and the history behind each step.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an excellent explanation of how we know cosmic distances.
videos.q: For details, watch the video, it is really good.

videos.t: I Solved Klotski
videos.s: 2swap explains how he solved the Klotski sliding-block puzzle by mapping its full state space as a graph and visualizing it. The video includes footage of the Guinness world-record solve and links to an interactive graph.
videos.w: HN people point to it for intuition about why some games are hard to navigate and for its Rush Hour and graph visualizations.
videos.q: the state space of the game can produce some intuition on why certain games are hard

videos.t: Y Combinator's Paul Graham sits down with Jason at LAUNCH Festival 2014
videos.s: A fireside chat at LAUNCH Festival 2014 where Paul Graham tells Jason Calacanis why he is handing Y Combinator's presidency to Sam Altman. He also shares startup advice drawn from nine years and 500+ startups.
videos.w: HN people link it for Paul Graham's candid views on startups, Aaron Swartz, and investing selection.
videos.q: PG definitely gives up lots of great success tips, so worth watching it all.

videos.t: Modern Times Streetwise - part 1/4 - 1996 BBC Documentary how become a London cabbie.
videos.s: Part one of a 1996 BBC Modern Times documentary on the training to become a London black cab driver. It follows candidates learning the Knowledge and facing stressful repeated exams with Public Carriage Office examiners.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it whenever London cabbies and the Knowledge come up, as an interesting if slightly dated look at the process.
videos.q: there is an excellent (albeit slightly dated) BBC documentary on the subject

videos.t: The Complete History of the A Button Challenge
videos.s: A five-hour documentary history of the Super Mario 64 A button challenge, which aims to beat the game with as few A presses as possible. It covers the bugs and exploits discovered over the years.
videos.w: Recommended as a deep-dive rabbit hole showing extraordinary knowledge of game internals.
videos.q: The amount of knowledge and abuse of bugs these guys are performing is insane.

videos.t: CppCon 2018: Stoyan Nikolov “OOP Is Dead, Long Live Data-oriented Design”
videos.s: A CppCon 2018 talk arguing that OOP has failed to deliver on reuse and performance, and presenting data-oriented design for C++ with practical worked examples from real systems.
videos.w: HN cites it as a concrete, worked example of data-oriented design and as an alternative to OOP in performance-sensitive code.
videos.q: a more recent video on it from CppCon 2018 where the presenter goes over a specific worked example.

videos.t: Spherical Geometry Is Stranger Than Hyperbolic - Hyperbolica Devlog #2
videos.s: CodeParade's short devlog on how spherical geometry looks in 2D and 3D and why it feels so unusual, part of the Hyperbolica series on a non-Euclidean game.
videos.w: Recommended among the nice visual explorations and tech demos of non-Euclidean geometry for games.
videos.q: One of the better ones, in my opinion, because it has "normal" objects in it

videos.t: Ichthyology: Phishing as a Science
videos.s: Karla Burnett presents real phishing campaigns run against a Bay Area tech company, including conversion rates and how existing protections were bypassed. She argues for evidence-based techniques to prevent credential phishing, not just mitigate it.
videos.w: HN people cite it to show even technical users fall for phishing and that hardware security keys are the real fix.
videos.q: shows just how easy it is to phish even users who think they are too good to be fooled.

videos.t: Solaris | SCIENCE FICTION | FULL MOVIE | directed by Tarkovsky
videos.s: Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 film Solaris, in which a psychologist is sent to a space station orbiting a planet with an alien intelligence and meets his dead wife there. It is the full movie, uploaded by Mosfilm.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a masterpiece of emotional, contemplative science fiction, and draws analogies between its alien ocean and AI.
videos.q: the film's a masterpiece that I highly recommend

videos.t: Induced Demand & Roadway Widening: Everything You Always Wanted to Know (and Weren't Afraid to Ask)
videos.s: CityNerd Ray Delahanty explains induced demand and what happens when freeways are widened. He walks through the economics of supply and demand applied to traffic and asks how much new traffic appears and whether congestion returns.
videos.w: HN commenters link it as a clearer explanation of induced demand for people who have not studied the topic.
videos.q: Anyway, Ray explains it better than I could and he agrees that the term is bad

videos.t: Navy pilots describe encounters with UFOs
videos.s: A 60 Minutes segment in which Navy pilots describe encounters with unidentified aerial phenomena, ahead of a report due to Congress.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as eyewitness testimony and multi-radar evidence in UFO threads, though some dispute it.
videos.q: At least watch this 60 Minutes short piece about this phenomenon

videos.t: The Best Easy Way to Capture Analog Video (it's a little weird)
videos.s: Technology Connections shows a cheap method for capturing analog video: a composite-to-HDMI upscaler feeding an HDMI capture dongle, aimed at digitizing home movies and VHS tapes.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as an affordable, good-quality way to digitize analog video.
videos.q: does some good coverage of capturing/converting analogue video - hardware choices make huge difference.

videos.t: 35C3 -  The year in post-quantum crypto
videos.s: Daniel J. Bernstein and Tanja Lange survey recent highlights in post-quantum cryptography at 35C3, covering the NIST competition, network protocol experiments, and broken candidates.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a good overview of the NIST candidates and the state of post-quantum crypto.
videos.q: This talk by djb and Tanja Lange is a good overview of the NIST candidates and the current state of pqcrypto

videos.t: Causal understanding of water displacement by a crow
videos.s: A silent PLOS ONE video of New Caledonian crows solving Aesop's Fable puzzles by dropping objects to raise water and reach food. It shows example trials from experiments testing causal understanding of water displacement.
videos.w: Used as vivid evidence of crow intelligence and animal physical reasoning in discussions of cognition.
videos.q: This video is a startling verification.of the crows mental capabilities.

videos.t: Your Body Killed Cancer 5 Minutes Ago
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt animation about how the immune system constantly detects and kills cells that are turning cancerous. It explains what cancer cells are and why stopping them is so hard.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear, accessible introduction to cancer and the immune system.
videos.q: I found Kurzgesagt has a very good ELI5 on how cancer grows in the body

videos.t: Thank You For Your Feedback - Don't Say Velcro
videos.s: Velcro's follow-up to its "Don't Say Velcro" ad responds to viewer feedback, with a humorous take on trademark usage and alternative names for hook and loop fasteners.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a delightful sequel to the original ad, brought up in threads on trademarks and the original campaign.
videos.q: it's hilarious and worth watching

videos.t: Let's port Diablo to SerenityOS!
videos.s: Andreas Kling ports the game Diablo to SerenityOS, his from-scratch Unix-like operating system, using the devilutionX project. The roughly 80-minute session shows what porting third-party software to the OS involves.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a demonstration of SerenityOS's hackability and fast iteration across all layers of the system.
videos.q: the video on porting Diablo to SerenityOS in an hour is pretty interesting to watch

videos.t: "Swift as C++ Successor in FoundationDB" by Konrad Malawski (Strange Loop 2023)
videos.s: Konrad Malawski's Strange Loop 2023 talk shows how the FoundationDB team adopted Swift incrementally in a C++ codebase. It covers Swift's C++ interoperability, which let them move single functions or entire types over one at a time.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as the main resource on Swift as an incremental successor to C++ and on how the interoperability works in practice.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: The fairly recent presentation about starting to move FoundationDB to Swift[0] was also very interesting.

videos.t: The Immune System Explained I – Bacteria Infection
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt animation of how the immune system responds to a bacterial infection, depicting immune cells as an army defending the body.
videos.w: HN suggests it as a simple, layman-friendly explanation of the immune system, especially during COVID vaccine discussions.
videos.q: Here's a nice video on the immune system that might help you out.

videos.t: PHP doesn't suck (anymore)
videos.s: Aaron Francis walks through how PHP has changed from 2012 to 2023, covering traits, array destructuring, generators, typed properties and more. It is a quick chaptered tour of modern PHP features.
videos.w: HN commenters share it to show that modern PHP is much better than its reputation.
videos.q: I was quite surprised to see how far PHP has come since I used it many years ago

videos.t: 50 Years Ago, This Was a Wasteland. He Changed Everything | Short Film Showcase
videos.s: An 8-minute National Geographic short film about David Bamberger, who bought 5,500 overgrazed acres in the Texas Hill Country and restored the land and its aquifers over about 50 years.
videos.w: Cited in climate and water threads as an encouraging example of large-scale landscape restoration.
videos.q: National Geographic did a really good 8-minute video on it

videos.t: James Tour: The Mystery of the Origin of Life
videos.s: Synthetic organic chemist James Tour gives a lecture arguing that origin-of-life research is far from explaining how life began. The talk was published by the Discovery Institute and drew sharp criticism.
videos.w: Recommended by some as a blunt expert critique of origin-of-life research, while others question its claims and length.
videos.q: Here's a talk by one of the world’s top synthetic organic chemists offering a blunt assessment of the current state of origin of life research

videos.t: DollarShaveClub.com - Our Blades Are F***ing Great
videos.s: Dollar Shave Club's low-budget launch ad, in which the founder jokes his way through the case for cheap mail-order razors.
videos.w: HN holds it up as a great example of a funny, viral company video that frames the razor market well.
videos.q: is absolutely amazing for how low budget it is

videos.t: Tutorial: New and Updated - Everything You Always Wanted to Know About Optical Networking
videos.s: A two-hour NANOG tutorial by Richard Steenbergen aimed at network engineers, covering optical networking technologies. This is the updated 2017 edition of a recurring talk.
videos.w: Commenters call it an invaluable, approachable way to learn how optical networking actually works.
videos.q: proved invaluable to me in learning optical networking

videos.t: Here's Why Your Static Website Needs HTTPS
videos.s: Troy Hunt argues that even static, non-secret websites need HTTPS, demonstrating attacks such as injected content and China's Great Cannon. It accompanies his blog post of the same name.
videos.w: Cited as a must-watch persuasive case for HTTPS everywhere.
videos.q: The linked video is a must watch to those who still doubt HTTPS

videos.t: BBS The.Documentary Part 4 - Fidonet
videos.s: Part 4 of the BBS: The Documentary series, covering FidoNet, the amateur network that linked dial-up bulletin board systems together to relay messages and files worldwide.
videos.w: Recommended as a great documentary on FidoNet's rise, with interviews with figures like Tom Jennings.
videos.q: A great documentary on FidoNet's rise with superb music and universal themes

videos.t: Shawn Douglas - Nanoscale Instruments for Visualizing Small Proteins & Bret Victor - Dynamicland
videos.s: A Foresight Institute workshop video with two talks: Shawn Douglas on nanoscale instruments for visualizing small proteins, and Bret Victor on Dynamicland. Victor's part shows biomolecular design built in his Realtalk system with physical objects.
videos.w: HN points to Bret Victor's segment as a recent, concrete demonstration of Dynamicland's ideas applied to a specific scientific domain.
videos.q: It shows just how far the Dynamicland concept can be pushed into a hyperspecific feature set customized to fit a single domain

videos.t: AI Slop Is Destroying The Internet
videos.s: Kurzgesagt examines how AI-generated content is flooding the internet, from video and music to news and books. It looks at how this makes verifying what is real harder.
videos.w: HN uses it as a reference for AI slop, LLMs citing LLM output, and the growing difficulty of fact checking.
videos.q: Kurzgesagt made a great video on how this stuff gets generated

videos.t: Mars DOS demo by Tim Clarke (1993)
videos.s: A one-minute capture of Tim Clarke's 1993 'Mars' DOS demo, a roughly 5 KB program that renders a navigable terrain landscape in real time.
videos.w: Remembered fondly as a tiny, efficient demo that inspired graphics programmers and is a benchmark for modern terrain rendering.
videos.q: I saw Mars demo which hooked me forever on the path of graphics programming.

videos.t: DEF CON 23 - Zoz - And That's How I Lost My Other Eye...Explorations in Data Destruction (Fixed)
videos.s: Zoz's DEF CON 23 talk explores practical, often explosive ways to destroy data and hard drives quickly. It tests methods such as thermite and other physical techniques for rapid destruction.
videos.w: HN points to it whenever hard drive destruction or fast physical data wiping comes up, as an empirical test of what actually works.
videos.q: Take a look at this talk from DEF CON 23 on what it takes to safely destroy HDDs

videos.t: Jeff Hawkins: Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #25
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Jeff Hawkins, founder of Numenta and author of On Intelligence, about the Thousand Brains Theory and reverse-engineering the neocortex. They also cover Hierarchical Temporal Memory and brain-inspired AI architectures.
videos.w: HN people send others here to hear Hawkins explain his theory in his own words, including reference frames and the old versus new brain.
videos.q: Highly recommend the Lex Fridman interview to listen to Jeff explain live

videos.t: Gacha Drama and the Korean Gender War
videos.s: A video essay from lawyer-turned-YouTuber Moon Channel on the South Korean gender war, tracing its historical roots and modern origins through the lens of a gacha game controversy. It is the first part of a two-part series.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it, along with its sequel, as an enlightening explanation of the economic and cultural roots of gender friction in South Korea.
videos.q: i found this video [0] and its sequel [1] very enlightening.

videos.t: Effective ML
videos.s: Yaron Minsky of Jane Street gave this talk to Harvard's OCaml-based CS51 class in 2010. It collects advice on being an effective ML programmer in an industrial setting.
videos.w: It is the go-to source for the idea of making illegal states unrepresentable through types, with the key moment at 28:02.
videos.q: Richard Feldman dives deeper into the topic with a lot more examples in

videos.t: Homemade Transistor Demonstration
videos.s: Jeri Ellsworth demonstrates a PMOS transistor she fabricated herself in a home chip lab. She shows some of its electrical characteristics.
videos.w: HN likes Ellsworth as a hardware tinkerer, and cites the video as proof that transistors can be made with low-tech, DIY fabrication.
videos.q: One of my favorite channels as she's done many projects I've had interest in.

videos.t: BFS-Auto: High Speed Book Scanner at over 250 pages/min
videos.s: A University of Tokyo lab demonstrates a book scanner that flips pages automatically and scans over 250 pages per minute. It uses real-time 3D recognition of the flipped pages and then restores each one to a flat image.
videos.w: HN commenters bring it up in book-scanning threads as an impressive non-destructive method that is not commercially available.
videos.q: very very impressive but to my knowledge not commercially available

videos.t: Enterprise Sales | Startup School
videos.s: Y Combinator partner Pete Koomen, who led Optimizely to $100M ARR, walks through the enterprise sales funnel. Chapters cover prospecting, outreach, qualification, pricing, closing, procurement and implementation.
videos.w: Recommended as a compact, practical summary of enterprise SaaS sales for technical founders.
videos.q: I find this video about enterprise sales from Pete Koomen (YC Partner) to be the best summary

videos.t: Four Languages from Forty Years Ago - Scott Wlaschin
videos.s: Scott Wlaschin's NDC Oslo talk on four 1970s languages, SQL, Prolog, ML and Smalltalk. It explains their philosophies and what practical principles they still offer modern developers.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a sampling of truly different programming paradigms beyond mainstream OOP.
videos.q: Check out this fantastic talk by Scott Wlaschin to get a sampling of truly different language paradigms

videos.t: Zach Oakes - Making Games at Runtime with Clojure
videos.s: Zach Oakes explains why Clojure suits making games at runtime, so designers can experience their work as they build it. He combines abstract discussion with live demonstrations, drawing on his play-clj library and Nightmod tool.
videos.w: Recommended as a great talk on live, functional-style game programming.
videos.q: here is his presentation on this subject at the last Conj (great talk)

videos.t: Alexis King -  “Effects for Less” @ ZuriHac 2020
videos.s: Alexis King's ZuriHac 2020 talk on how effect systems in Haskell can be implemented efficiently. It looks at the performance cost of effect libraries and how to reduce it.
videos.w: HN commenters call it among the best talks of 2020 for understanding Haskell effect systems.
videos.q: the best one I did watch this year was Alexis King's 'Effects for Less' (Haskell).

videos.t: Sam Altman - How to Succeed with a Startup
videos.s: A 16-minute Y Combinator Startup School talk in which Sam Altman lays out what makes a startup succeed. It covers building a product people tell friends about, exponential markets, real versus fake trends, and having an ambitious vision.
videos.w: Recommended as the single Startup School video worth watching, a short and dense talk on what makes a startup work; one commenter dismisses it as platitudes.
videos.q: If you watch one SUS video ever then watch this 16 minute video from Sam Altman

videos.t: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Speedrun in 22:38, live at AGDQ2013
videos.s: Cosmo's 22:38 Ocarina of Time speedrun, performed live at AGDQ 2013. The runner uses a complex exploit to skip much of the game.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a showcase of the deep reverse-engineering and glitch knowledge behind speedrunning, and cite it for the wrongwarp trick.
videos.q: The level of reverse-engineering is impressive.

videos.t: BahnMining - Pünktlichkeit ist eine Zier (David Kriesel)
videos.s: David Kriesel's 36C3 talk, in German, analyzes a year of scraped data on every stop of every long-distance train in Germany. It shows how Deutsche Bahn delay statistics hide cancellations and delays.
videos.w: Recommended in threads on German rail as the data-backed explanation of how reported punctuality understates real delays.
videos.q: there's the great talk from David Kriesel on the 36C3 [1] about how Deutsche Bahn is... "doing statistics" to hide their delays. It's well worth the hour!

videos.t: Hartverdrahtet - Akronyme Analogiker | 4k Revision 2012
videos.s: Hartverdrahtet by Akronyme Analogiker, the winning PC 4k intro at Revision 2012. It is a realtime demo with music and fractal visuals in 4096 bytes.
videos.w: Cited as a showcase of what fits in 4k, in discussions of code size limits and the demoscene.
videos.q: So then I'm going to post my favorite 4k [1], which even if you ignore the file size, is just a very cool use of fractals.

videos.t: Deception, Lies, and Valve
videos.s: Coffeezilla investigates Counter-Strike skin gambling, the role of Valve and the legal and PR response, including effects on minors.
videos.w: Pointed to in threads on CS skin economy and Valve as an investigation arguing Valve is complicit in underage gambling.
videos.q: I highly recommend the videos.

videos.t: Deus Ex Morpheus Conversation [1080p Widescreen]
videos.s: A 1080p widescreen capture of the Deus Ex conversation between JC Denton and the AI Morpheus. It is a philosophical exchange that includes surveillance as a replacement for God.
videos.w: Commenters call it one of the game's best dialogues and bring it up in discussions of mass surveillance.
videos.q: My favorite conversation in the game is probably the one with the AI Morpheus

videos.t: 37C3 -  Operation Triangulation: What You Get When Attack iPhones of Researchers
videos.s: A 37C3 talk by Kaspersky researchers on Operation Triangulation, a zero-click iPhone attack that targeted their own colleagues. They describe capturing every stage of the chain, four zero-days and a previously unknown spyware active for years.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a gripping look at what nation-state attackers can do, used as the primary source in threads about iPhone security and Kaspersky.
videos.q: was a rollercoaster of a ride. If you have the time to watch it I highly recommend it!

videos.t: Manipulating the YouTube Algorithm - (Part 1/3) Smarter Every Day 213
videos.s: Part 1 of Smarter Every Day's three-part series on manipulating the YouTube algorithm. It features Renee DiResta and examples of how social media platforms can be manipulated.
videos.w: Referenced in threads on social media manipulation and junk content as an interesting miniseries, though one commenter criticized its ExpressVPN ad read.
videos.q: Destin Sandlin explores how YouTube, Twitter, and Facebook are being used as a sort of vanguard in a meta-game to undermine our trust

videos.t: Nicholas Carlini - Black-hat LLMs | [un]prompted 2026
videos.s: Nicholas Carlini of Anthropic talks at [un]prompted 2026 about how adversaries could misuse current LLMs for attacks. He shows recent models finding zero-day vulnerabilities in heavily tested software, including a SQL injection in Ghost.
videos.w: HN cites it as a concrete demonstration that LLMs have suddenly become strong at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities.
videos.q: This talk changed my view on where we're actually at

videos.t: How to Design Impenetrable Airport Security
videos.s: A Wendover Productions explainer on how airport security is designed, covering screening layers, x-ray scanning, and the contrast with Israel's profiling-based approach. It walks through the logic behind why security works the way it does.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a well-researched primer when airport security theatre and Israeli-style screening come up.
videos.q: If you actually want to be informed on the subject I highly recommend

videos.t: Making Mushroom Ketchup - 18th Century Cooking
videos.s: The Townsends channel shows how to make mushroom ketchup, a popular 18th-century sauce, in period style. It includes the history and a recipe and links to a blog post on whether George Washington used ketchup.
videos.w: HN commenters who have cooked it recommend it as a reliable, delicious recipe and a good historical explanation of pre-tomato ketchup.
videos.q: The Mushroom Ketchup recipe is one I repeatedly go back to -- it's just that good

videos.t: The Greatest Shot In Television
videos.s: A one-minute clip from James Burke's 1978 BBC series Connections in which he walks past a Saturn V rocket and a timed take-off happens behind him in a single shot, with no green screen.
videos.w: Held up as an iconic, perfectly timed piece of television whenever Burke or Connections comes up.
videos.q: the totally iconic piece of one shot perfectly timed tv

videos.t: Brave New World vs Nineteen Eighty-Four featuring Adam Gopnik and Will Self
videos.s: An Intelligence Squared debate in which Will Self argues for Brave New World and Adam Gopnik for Nineteen Eighty-Four as the better dystopian warning. It includes acted excerpts and is chaired by Jonathan Freedland.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a good long debate for the recurring question of whether Orwell or Huxley was right.
videos.q: this debate between will self and adam gopnik on 'brave new world' vs '1984' is really good if anybody has 1.5 hours to indulge.

videos.t: Yes Minister — Why Britain Joined the European Union
videos.s: A short Yes Minister clip in which the civil servant explains why Britain joined the European Union, delivered as satire of British foreign policy.
videos.w: HN posts it, often jokingly, as a prescient and witty explanation of Britain's ambivalent stance toward Europe, especially around Brexit.
videos.q: The best explanation of this

videos.t: The Rivian Electric Amazon Delivery Van Is Highly Innovative and Incredibly Cool
videos.s: Doug DeMuro reviews the Rivian electric delivery van built for Amazon, walking through its quirks, features and design innovations. It is a long, detailed tour of the vehicle inside and out.
videos.w: HN points to it as the most thorough walkthrough of the Amazon Rivian van, useful for seeing its real size and delivery-specific design.
videos.q: This is a thorough tour, and I want one

videos.t: Horrific USB power supply fault.  (Electrocution risk.)
videos.s: Electronics hobbyist bigclivedotcom tears down a cheap USB power supply with a manufacturing fault that carries full mains voltage to the USB ports, showing the risk of electric shock.
videos.w: Cited in threads about cheap chargers as proof of why proper certified and isolated power supplies are worth paying for.
videos.q: He earned my respect from a video on a USB charger with an electrocution risk

videos.t: 3dfx Oral History Panel with Ross Smith, Scott Sellers, Gary Tarolli, and Gordon Campbell
videos.s: A Computer History Museum oral history panel with four 3dfx founders on the company's rise with Voodoo Graphics and Glide, and its fall into bankruptcy. It runs about two and a half hours.
videos.w: Recommended as the definitive retrospective on 3dfx, with first-hand stories about engineering hacks and design philosophy.
videos.q: This is a really great retrospective on 3dfx from four of the founders.

videos.t: Michael Jordan "Failure" Nike Commercial
videos.s: A Nike commercial in which Michael Jordan lists the shots he missed and games he lost, saying that repeated failure is the reason he succeeds.
videos.w: HN invokes it as the classic illustration of learning through repeated failure and iterating, often in startup threads.
videos.q: which everyone should see

videos.t: Philip Glass - Sesame Street - Geometry of Circles.mp4
videos.s: A Sesame Street animation from 1979 with music composed by Philip Glass, showing geometric circle patterns.
videos.w: Mentioned as an example of Sesame Street respecting children's intelligence and as an early gateway to modern classical music.
videos.q: Philip Glass scored an animation for Sesame Street.

videos.t: "Understanding Burnout," Prof. Christina Maslach (U.C. Berkeley)
videos.s: A Berkeley lecture by psychologist Christina Maslach, a leading burnout researcher, on what burnout is and what causes it. It covers common misunderstandings and the job and workplace factors involved.
videos.w: HN uses it as the expert primer on burnout that dispels common misconceptions.
videos.q: There is this excellent talk by Maslach, "Understanding Burnout" which dispels most misunderstandings

videos.t: The surprising science of happiness | Dan Gilbert
videos.s: Psychologist Dan Gilbert argues in this TED talk that our psychological immune system lets us become happy even when things do not go as planned. He challenges the idea that we will be miserable if we do not get what we want.
videos.w: HN cites it as one of the best TED talks and as evidence that people adapt to and come to like outcomes they cannot change.
videos.q: is one of the best TED talks of all time

videos.t: “I’m Not a Robot” (2025 Academy Award Winner) | The New Yorker Screening Room
videos.s: Victoria Warmerdam's Oscar-winning Dutch short film in which a woman fails a series of Captcha tests and is plunged into a strange new reality. It is a dark, Black Mirror-like sci-fi comedy.
videos.w: HN brings it up in threads about captchas, bots and AI agents as an excellent short film about being a robot.
videos.q: there is an excellent short movie online called "I'm not a Robot".

videos.t: Data Oriented GUI in Rust by Raph Levien - Bay Area Rust Meetup
videos.s: Raph Levien presents his new Rust GUI framework, built on data-oriented design and ideas from entity component systems, for the Xi editor. He weighs the approach against alternatives and discusses pros and cons.
videos.w: HN people point to it as an excellent, inspirational talk on Rust GUI architecture, and it led many to the Druid project.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: I found this excellent talk to be complementary to my talk[1] on data-oriented GUI in Rust

videos.t: Journalist Vincent Woo reflects on his piece, "Lambda School's Misleading Promises" | E1039
videos.s: Journalist Vincent Woo discusses his New York Magazine piece on Lambda School's misleading promises, including its income share agreements and placement claims, in an interview on This Week in Startups. The host questions him pointedly.
videos.w: HN cites it in Lambda School threads as a revealing interview that lends credibility to Woo's reporting.
videos.q: It's a great watch.

videos.t: Sabine Schmitz's Nurburgring Van CHALLENGE | Top Gear - Part 2
videos.s: In Top Gear's second part, racing driver Sabine Schmitz tries to lap the Nurburgring in a Ford Transit van in under ten minutes. She finishes just over the mark.
videos.w: Shared in threads about the Nurburgring and after Schmitz's death as a charming showcase of her skill.
videos.q: If you havent watched her take a van around the ring in a smidge over 10 minutes it is worth a watch.

videos.t: DARK GOTHIC MAGA: How Tech Billionaires Plan to Destroy America
videos.s: A political commentary video arguing that tech billionaires such as Thiel, Musk and Andreessen, along with figures like Yarvin, are using the new administration to push their agenda. It connects Yarvin's ideas with Project 2025.
videos.w: HN commenters share it during DOGE and government-cuts threads as a summary of the billionaires' aims, though many only cite it as a reference.
videos.q: This video breaks down who those people are as well as what their motivations are

videos.t: If You Eat Meat You Should Know This
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt video on the conditions in which most farm animals are raised. It argues that cruelty is for cheaper rather than better meat, and that a small price increase per meal could avoid most of the suffering.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear, evidence-backed introduction to the economics of animal welfare in meat and egg production.
videos.q: I highly recommend this Kurzgesagt video on how paying just a bit more for meat or eggs drastically improves animals' living conditions

videos.t: Andy Bell – Be the browser’s mentor, not its micromanager
videos.s: Andy Bell's 2022 talk on hinting the browser rather than micromanaging it, using progressive enhancement, CSS layout, fluid type and space, and modern CSS to build resilient front-ends.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a practical case for intrinsic, fluid CSS that cuts down on media queries and selectors.
videos.q: I'd really encourage you to watch this talk by Andy

videos.t: Keynote - Karen Sandler
videos.s: Karen Sandler's keynote at Linux.conf.au 2012 on the software running inside medical devices such as her own pacemaker-defibrillator. She discusses the difficulty of learning what code runs in life-sustaining devices and why open source matters there.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it in threads about medical device security and software transparency as an excellent, personal case for open source in implants.
videos.q: here's a really excellent talk by Karen Sandler.

videos.t: Web 2.0 ... The Machine is Us/ing Us
videos.s: Michael Wesch's five-minute video about Web 2.0, showing how the read/write web, XML and user-generated content change how people create and share information.
videos.w: Cited as a classic, compact explanation of the read/write web and open data, invoked in threads on the semantic web and open APIs.
videos.q: Just going to leave this gem of a video[0] here.

videos.t: Lawyer.  Passport.  Locksmith.  Gun.  (A Talk About Risk & Preparedness)
videos.s: Deviant Ollam gives a long talk on risk and preparedness: get a lawyer, passport, locksmith and other resources before you need them. It covers practical steps to build defenses against serious problems in life.
videos.w: Recommended as a thorough preparedness talk, and cited for specifics such as lawyers, password managers and gun ownership.
videos.q: it's worth an hour of your time.

videos.t: How to Build a Startup Without Funding by Pieter Levels @ Dojo Bali
videos.s: Pieter Levels talks at Dojo Bali about building startups without venture capital through bootstrapping, persistence and learning many skills as a generalist. He reviews his own past projects.
videos.w: Pointed to as an inspiring talk for solo makers turning side projects into profitable businesses.
videos.q: Probably the best startup talk I've seen in a while.

videos.t: Robert F. Kennedy challenges Gross Domestic Product
videos.s: A short video of Robert F. Kennedy's 1968 speech criticizing Gross Domestic Product as a measure of progress, saying it counts everything except what makes life worthwhile.
videos.w: Quoted in economics threads about growth, work and basic income as a classic critique of GDP.
videos.q: the best way to acknowledge that is to watch this speech from Robert F Kennedy

videos.t: Modular Micro-Reactors – The Future of Nuclear Energy?
videos.s: Professor Ruzic explains modular micro-reactors: self-contained nuclear units with passive safety whose fuel lasts about 20 years. He covers their use for process and district heat and where they can compete with diesel generation.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear technical explanation of micro-reactor fuel, safety and economics, from a channel HN trusts on nuclear topics.
videos.q: His videos are great. Worth your time.

videos.t: George Hotz | Programming | Livecoding SLAM | twitchslam | Part1
videos.s: A long livestream of George Hotz live-coding a toy SLAM implementation, twitchslam, over two days in May 2018. It is an unedited session of Python programming with computer vision and visualization.
videos.w: Recommended as informal, long-form live coding to watch, though some commenters criticize his style.
videos.q: The guy's a certified legend.

videos.t: The War on Sensemaking, Daniel Schmachtenberger
videos.s: Daniel Schmachtenberger discusses why the information ecology is damaged and what healthy public sensemaking would take. The conversation ties this to the meaning crisis and to improving discourse.
videos.w: Recommended to people interested in propaganda, misinformation and how to improve public discourse.
videos.q: It may change the way you think about people that question the narrative.

videos.t: Terence Tao: The Cosmic Distance Ladder, UCLA
videos.s: Terence Tao's AMS Einstein Public Lecture at UCLA on the cosmic distance ladder, the chain of methods astronomers use to measure distances from the Earth to distant galaxies. It is aimed at a general audience.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible and elegant tour of how indirect reasoning builds up cosmic measurements, with one commenter calling it their favorite Tao work.
videos.q: Tao’s oft given talk about the cosmic distance ladder has always been my favorite thing he has done.

videos.t: There’s No Wave Function? | Jacob Barandes
videos.s: Physicist Jacob Barandes discusses his view that quantum mechanics can be formulated without wave functions, using a stochastic, probabilistic approach. The long interview covers measurement, the foundations of quantum theory and the history of the field.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a credible, clearly explained alternative take on quantum foundations from a Harvard physicist.
videos.q: Barandes is excellent at clearly articulating complex ideas in very simple, concise terms.

videos.t: The Addictive Cost Of Predatory Videogame Monetization (The Jimquisition)
videos.s: A Jimquisition episode examining the human cost of predatory videogame monetization, focusing on loot boxes and microtransactions. It features testimonials from people harmed by gambling-style game mechanics.
videos.w: Pointed to in threads on loot boxes, gacha games and exploitative monetization as a damning overview.
videos.q: especially the section where he quotes from a talk by one such developer [2].

videos.t: Mikey Dickerson Velocity NY 2014 Keynote: "One Year After healthcare.gov..."
