videos.s: Mikey Dickerson's keynote at Velocity NY 2014, one year after the healthcare.gov launch failure. He recounts how a small team rescued the site and what the episode showed about government IT contracting.
videos.w: HN cites it as a firsthand account of how dysfunctional large IT projects can be, with about 50 contractors and no one in charge.
videos.q: I saw Mikey Dickerson give a great talk about his experience leading the completion of healthcare.gov

videos.t: Vaccines: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on vaccines, arguing that the benefits far outweigh the minuscule risks and discussing why some parents still doubt their safety.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible, funny explanation of why vaccines matter.
videos.q: Last Week Tonight has a nice episode on Vaccines

videos.t: Why Doing Taxes Is So Hard | Patriot Act with Hasan Minhaj | Netflix
videos.s: An episode of Patriot Act with Hasan Minhaj exposing how tax-prep companies like TurboTax make filing confusing and costly even though many Americans can file for free. It combines comedy with reporting on lobbying and dark patterns.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible explanation of how Intuit's lobbying and deceptive design undermine free tax filing.
videos.q: There's a very good Patriot Act episode [1] regarding devious patterns in the US tax industry.

videos.t: The Cannonball Run Countach: Supercar Legend | Full Documentary
videos.s: A Hagerty documentary on a 1979 Lamborghini Countach LP400 S and how it ended the Cannonball Baker Sea-to-Shining-Sea Memorial Trophy Dash. It tells the story of the illicit race started by Brock Yates and its Hollywood adaptation.
videos.w: Recommended as a history-rich look at the Cannonball Run and the rebellious philosophy behind it.
videos.q: You really need to watch the documentary on Cannonball Run

videos.t: How Toy Story 2 Almost Got Deleted: Stories From Pixar Animation: ENTV
videos.s: Pixar staff tell the story of how Toy Story 2 was almost deleted from the studio's computers and was saved by a home computer backup.
videos.w: HN shares it as a classic backup and operations cautionary tale.
videos.q: which I highly recommend if you are in storage, DevOps or SRE

videos.t: The new Windows Terminal
videos.s: Microsoft's short announcement video for the new Windows Terminal, a modern terminal app for Command Prompt, PowerShell and WSL. It is a stylized trailer for the unreleased project.
videos.w: Mentioned for its unusually polished, nerdy trailer style, and as an example of a good developer tool announcement.
videos.q: this advertisting video is super cool and nerdy.

videos.t: Bret Victor Inventing on Principle
videos.s: Bret Victor's talk "Inventing on Principle" argues that creators should find a guiding principle to fight for. He shows demos of immediate-feedback tools, such as live-updating code and animation editors.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an inspiring talk on immediate feedback and on living by a principle.
videos.q: This gave me a sharp moment of clarity, thank you so much for this!

videos.t: Practical Deep Learning for Coders: Lesson 1
videos.s: Lesson 1 of fast.ai's Practical Deep Learning for Coders, taught by Jeremy Howard. It takes coders from running code in a Jupyter notebook straight into training a real image model.
videos.w: HN considers the course one of the best hands-on ways into deep learning, praising the code-first teaching style.
videos.q: The lectures are super hands on - Jeremy actually fires up a jupyter notebook and runs code which often surprises him

videos.t: A Tour of Prolog
videos.s: Markus Triska tours Prolog's most distinctive features, including its use as a database and query language, rule processing, constraint solving and compile-time rewriting. It also covers concise meta-interpreters.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the best short introduction to what makes Prolog unique.
videos.q: check out this video introduction by Markus Triska about what makes Prolog unique

videos.t: Where's the 'Collusion'?
videos.s: The Real News Network interview between Aaron Mate and Guardian reporter Luke Harding about Russiagate and Harding's book on alleged Russian collusion.
videos.w: HN mostly uses it as a reference for a skeptical take on Russiagate media coverage, and some link it to give context on the reporter.

videos.t: Amputee Makes History with APL’s Modular Prosthetic Limb
videos.s: Johns Hopkins APL shows Les Baugh, a bilateral shoulder-level amputee, controlling two Modular Prosthetic Limbs by thought after a short training period. Nerves rerouted to his chest drive the arms.
videos.w: HN cites it as an astonishing glimpse of advanced thought-controlled prosthetics.
videos.q: This particular thing from Johns Hopkins is just incredible

videos.t: GitHub Actions Feels Bad
videos.s: A fasterthanlime video essay arguing that GitHub Actions is a poorly designed system, with a history of personal computing and CI, and a look at how it works behind the scenes. It is sponsored by Brilliant.
videos.w: Pointed to in GitHub Actions threads as a well-argued critique of how brittle and confused the platform is.
videos.q: This video really highlighted just how brittle the whole thing is even behind the scenes

videos.t: DEF CON 19 - Artem Dinaburg - Bit-squatting: DNS Hijacking Without Exploitation
videos.s: Artem Dinaburg's DEF CON 19 talk on bit-squatting, where DRAM bit flips cause DNS requests to go to domains one bit off from the intended one. It shows how hardware faults can be exploited for hijacking without any software exploit.
videos.w: Recommended as a fun, practical talk on why bit flips matter for security, and cited in ECC memory discussions.
videos.q: A really fun DefCon talk on bitsquatting.

videos.t: Cambridge Ideas - Professor Risk
videos.s: David Spiegelhalter, Professor of the Public Understanding of Risk, uses statistics to weigh everyday risks such as bacon sandwiches and cycling. The six-minute piece introduces micromorts as a way to compare the risk of dying.
videos.w: Recommended as a short, fun introduction to micromorts and thinking about risk.
videos.q: Here is great video by Cambridge Ideas about the risk of dying from various activities (measured in micromorts)

videos.t: How I Fixed a 10 Year Old Guitar Hero Bug Without the Source Code
videos.s: A reverse engineer walks through fixing a ten-year-old bug in Guitar Hero III without access to its source code, using a disassembler and decompiler. It is technical but explained step by step.
videos.w: Held up as a favorite tech talk and a great hard-debugging story about patching a game binary.
videos.q: One of the best though, for me, has to be this one on fixing a Guitar Hero bug

videos.t: Philip Wadler  - Propositions as Types (Lambda Days 2016)
videos.s: Philip Wadler's Lambda Days talk on propositions as types, the link between logic and computation that underlies theorem provers and programming language design.
videos.w: Recommended as an exceptional whirlwind tour of the foundations of computer science.
videos.q: This is a very good lecture series[4].

videos.t: Holy Post -  Race in America
videos.s: Phil Vischer of VeggieTales and Holy Post gives an 18-minute history of racial injustice in America, covering why anger persists despite civil rights laws. It is told from an evangelical Christian perspective and adapted from a class he co-taught.
videos.w: Recommended as a concise, broad-strokes history of racial injustice, including the lasting effects of redlining.
videos.p: history of racial injustice in america
videos.q: There’s a great 18-minute video from Bob the Tomato, AKA Phil Vischer, which lays out the sordid history in broad detail.

videos.t: Dynamic Languages Wizards Series - Panel on Language Design
videos.s: A 2001 panel with Paul Graham, John Maeda, Jonathan Rees and Guy Steele on programming language design, part of the Dynamic Languages Wizards Series.
videos.w: HN users mine it for design wisdom and history from luminaries, and often quote Guy Steele's remarks.
videos.q: I'd also highly recommend that anyone interested in this kind of thing listen to all three of the Dynamic Languages Wizards Series panels

videos.t: Rocker Jack White - Serious Jibber-Jabber with Conan O'Brien | Team Coco
videos.s: Conan O'Brien interviews Jack White in a Serious Jibber-Jabber episode shot on 35mm film. They discuss White's creative process, his use of constraints and his approach to music and art.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an inspiring interview about passion, minimalism and deliberately imposing restrictions on creative work.
videos.q: I highly recommend the interview with Conan

videos.t: Hacker Interviews: Larry Wall
videos.s: Jonathan Schiefer interviews Larry Wall, creator of Perl, in a 33-minute conversation. Wall discusses his self-designed linguistics degree and how language and programming overlap.
videos.w: Recommended as an enjoyable look at the hacker mindset and a thoughtful interview worth rewatching.
videos.q: I really enjoyed this interview with Larry Wall (of Perl fame)

videos.t: Back to the Future | VFXcool (1/2)
videos.s: Captain Disillusion explains the visual effects behind the Back to the Future trilogy. He covers ILM's motion-control, computer-controlled camera work and clever pre-CGI tricks.
videos.w: Recommended as a succinct documentary on motion control and practical-effects ingenuity.
videos.q: is a really good yet succinct documentary on it

videos.t: Maximizing Productivity, Physical & Mental Health with Daily Tools
videos.s: A long Huberman Lab episode laying out science-based daily tools for focus, sleep, exercise and mental and physical health, organized around a 24-hour day.
videos.w: Commenters credit it for practical routines, such as morning walks and circadian timing, and for helping with burnout recovery.
videos.q: I followed the Huberman protocol for sleep [1] and daily tools [2], with profound results.

videos.t: Max Headroom 20 minutes into the future 1985
videos.s: The 1985 Channel 4 TV film 'Max Headroom: 20 Minutes into the Future', the origin of the computer-generated TV host Max Headroom, with a soundtrack by Midge Ure and Chris Cross.
videos.w: Recommended in Max Headroom threads as a surprisingly good, short original film.
videos.q: you are in for a serious treat. It is so much better than I ever expected

videos.t: Disruptive Innovation - Clayton Christensen (Part 2)
videos.s: Clayton Christensen explains disruptive innovation using the steel industry, showing how mini-mills beat incumbents from the low end. He argues disruption is not about stupid or bad management.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an amazing, clear explanation of why incumbents move upmarket and lose to low-end challengers.
videos.q: Here's part of a great talk from Christensen describing the same logic but in the Steel industry

videos.t: Beware online "filter bubbles" | Eli Pariser
videos.s: Eli Pariser's TED talk argues that personalized web services trap users in filter bubbles, limiting exposure to challenging information. He says this is bad for individuals and for democracy.
videos.w: Cited as an early, prescient warning about algorithmic personalization, echo chambers and social media feeds.
videos.q: The Filter Bubble Ted talk is what motivated me to dump social media.

videos.t: Super Mario World Ending Theme sight-read by Tom Brier
videos.s: Pianist Tom Brier sight-reads a piano arrangement of the Super Mario World ending theme, working from a first-draft score by Keeper1st. He takes some liberties with the score as he plays.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a showcase of remarkable sight-reading and a favorite when sight-reading or notation comes up.
videos.q: He's a rare gem and a treat to the ears.

videos.t: The Miniature Microcars of Amsterdam
videos.s: Not Just Bikes looks at the tiny microcars such as the Canta seen around Amsterdam. It discusses how they serve people with mobility issues, can use bike paths under certain rules, and where they fit in a 21st century city.
videos.w: Linked in self-driving and car-dependence threads as an example of small vehicles that help disabled and elderly people without full-size cars.
videos.q: Please, please watch the videos I linked.

videos.t: Secret Life Of Machines 104 The Washing Machine
videos.s: An episode of Tim Hunkin's The Secret Life of Machines that explains how a washing machine works, using models, cut-aways and animations. It was first aired in 1988.
videos.w: Recommended as a humorous and clear explanation of everyday machines, including why washing machine balancing works.
videos.q: Cartoonist Tim Hunkin explains how machines work, with lots and lots of models and cut-aways of real life devices.

videos.t: Interview with an Agile Coach - Sprint1
videos.s: Kai Lentit's comedy sketch parodying an interview with an agile coach, lampooning scrum, sprints and kanban jargon. It is a few minutes of programmer humor.
videos.w: Recommended as a funny parody that resembles agile as practiced at large companies.
videos.q: A funny enough YouTube video (comedy)

videos.t: Charlie Brooker's Screenwipe - Reality TV Editing
videos.s: A clip from Charlie Brooker's BBC show Screenwipe showing how reality TV uses editing to manufacture emotion and narrative. It demonstrates how the same footage can be cut to give very different impressions.
videos.w: HN people cite it as a vivid demonstration of how editing shapes perception in documentaries and reality television.
videos.q: here is an awesome video that shows how editing can do wonders for how we perceive things(1).

videos.t: Why Women Are Stripey
videos.s: Veritasium explains X-chromosome inactivation, where different cells in a woman's body switch off different X chromosomes, giving a mosaic pattern. It uses animation from the WEHI institute and connects to calico cat coloring.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as the best short explanation of X inactivation and why calico cats and some human traits are mosaics.
videos.q: Veritasium has a fantastic video that discusses the genetics behind the random color patterns of calico cats

videos.t: Beats That Defy Boxes | Reggie Watts | TED
videos.s: Reggie Watts performs at TED 2012, blending vocal looping, beatboxing, poetry and comedy across musical genres in a larger-than-life improvised set.
videos.w: HN points to it as a memorable performance that doubles as a parody of TED talks and a showcase of live vocal looping.
videos.q: His TED talk is one for the ages

videos.t: Public Service Broadcasting - Go!
videos.s: Music video for Public Service Broadcasting's "Go!" from the album The Race For Space, built from NASA audio and archival material of Apollo-era voices.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an energizing space-themed song, and references it when Apollo go/no-go calls come up.
videos.q: One of my favorite songs to listen to that can get a pumped up feeling

videos.t: Black Hat 2013 - OPSEC Failures of Spies
videos.s: Matthew Cole's Black Hat 2013 talk on operational security failures by CIA operatives. It covers the Abu Omar case and how sloppy tradecraft with cell phones exposed officers through call records and metadata.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as a compelling demonstration that metadata identifies people, and as a great watch on sloppy CIA tradecraft.
videos.q: This is one of the best videos I have ever seen countering this argument.

videos.t: The Super-Fast Logistics of Delivering Blood By Drone
videos.s: A Wendover Productions documentary-style video on how Zipline delivers blood and medical supplies by drone in Rwanda. It covers the catapult launch, parachute drop and the logistics behind it.
videos.w: Offered as a clear, well-made look at a real, working drone-delivery system, often in answer to skepticism about delivery drones.
videos.q: Wendover Productions did a great video detailing this a few years back.

videos.t: John Carmack Facebook Connect 2021 Keynote
videos.s: John Carmack's keynote at Facebook Connect 2021, where he speaks candidly about VR, Quest, and Meta's metaverse plans. He pushes back on hype and discusses retention and latency.
videos.w: Commenters praise it as clear, honest thinking from Carmack and recommend it to technical people interested in VR and the metaverse.
videos.q: As always, John is a master of communication and clear thought.

videos.t: Geographical limit between Balkan and Central Europe
videos.s: A one-minute clip of Slavoj Zizek showing what he calls the official geographical limit between the Balkans and Central Europe, standing at a river in Ljubljana. It is a short, absurd and funny piece of cultural geography.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as one of the best short clips on YouTube for illustrating Balkan versus Central European identity.
videos.q: this short clip [1] of Zizek explaining the geography that separates Central Europe from the Balkans is one of the best things on YT

videos.t: REBL - Stuart Halloway
videos.s: Stuart Halloway introduces REBL, a graphical, interactive tool for browsing Clojure data, extracted from Datomic tools. The talk is from Clojure/conj 2018.
videos.w: Recommended as a must-watch Conj talk and as the intro for people who haven't seen REBL, often compared to Jupyter-style tooling.
videos.q: People who have not heard of the REBL, can check out this video

videos.t: Sensor Fusion on Android Devices: A Revolution in Motion Processing
videos.s: David Sachs of InvenSense explains how gyroscopes, accelerometers and compasses work on their own and together, demonstrated on a modified Android handset. He covers sensor fusion algorithms and why rotation math such as Euler angles matters.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the definitive talk on mobile motion sensing, including why integrating acceleration twice drifts so badly.
videos.q: I'm always happy to share this incredible lecture from many many years ago

videos.t: How to  Properly Heat a Pan
videos.s: A two-minute Rouxbe cooking-school demo of how to heat a pan properly before cooking. It uses the Leidenfrost effect, where water beads and skates across a hot pan, to show when a stainless steel pan is ready.
videos.w: HN people cite it as a practical test for pan temperature and as the way to get a stainless steel pan relatively non-stick.
videos.q: This youtube video explains the process

videos.t: What Makes This Song Great? "Into You" MAX MARTIN
videos.s: Rick Beato analyzes the music and production of Max Martin through Ariana Grande's Into You, breaking down its layering and songwriting craft.
videos.w: HN points to it as an explanation of how Max Martin builds hit songs.
videos.q: My favourite video of his is about the most accomplished songwriter most people have never heard of - Max Martin

videos.t: LIVE Coding "Happy Jumping"
videos.s: Inigo Quilez live-codes the "Happy Jumping" animated scene in a Shadertoy GLSL shader over about six hours. He builds the raymarched character step by step, explaining the math and procedural techniques, with checkpoints linked for each stage.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a patient, full-length walkthrough of how a raymarched shader is built from scratch.
videos.q: is fantastic, yes it's five hours but worth it.

videos.t: The Chinese Student Crisis
videos.s: PolyMatter examines how universities, especially in the West, depend on foreign and Chinese student tuition and how rankings and incentives distort institutions around that money.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it in college-ranking and higher-ed threads as an explanation of why rankings are a hustle for foreign student revenue.
videos.q: Polymatter recently had a great video on the way the college ranking system is a hustle for foreign student money

videos.t: Hjernevask - Brainwashing (Eng Sub) Part 1 - The Gender Equality Paradox
videos.s: First episode of the Norwegian documentary series Hjernevask, in which Harald Eia interviews researchers on the nature versus nurture debate. It focuses on the gender equality paradox and gender differences in career choice.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it, especially during the Google memo debate, as expert testimony on biological contributions to gender differences.

videos.t: Noam Chomsky - "The machine, the ghost, and the limits of understanding"
videos.s: Noam Chomsky's 2011 University of Oslo lecture on Newton's contributions to the study of mind. He argues Newton abandoned mechanical explanation and lowered the bar for scientific intelligibility, with consequences for the limits of human understanding. Q&A starts at 45:33.
videos.w: Recommended as a lucid, insightful lecture on the limits of human knowledge and the study of mind, one commenter calling it among the best lectures ever.
videos.q: Chomsky's surprisingly insightful thinking on the limits of human knowledge, and the consequences

videos.t: Why is this number everywhere?
videos.s: Veritasium explores why the number 37 turns up so often, drawing on Tom Magliery's collection of 37 sightings and a poll of about 200,000 people asked to pick a random number. It covers how humans choose numbers and why 37 stands out.
videos.w: HN cites it in LLM randomness and number-picking threads as evidence that humans are also biased and predictable when asked for random numbers.
videos.q: humans are fairly predictable when trying to come up with random numbers, for example, have a look at this Veritasium video

videos.t: 2017 Personality 18: Biology & Traits: Openness/Intelligence/Creativity I
videos.s: A Jordan Peterson university lecture on the Big Five trait openness to experience, covering creativity and intelligence. It explains how IQ is measured, how well it predicts life success, and the Pareto distribution of creative output.
videos.w: Recommended as a solid introduction to personality and IQ research, and cited as the source for factor-analysis claims about personality and intelligence.
videos.q: For anybody interested in personality research, I warmly recommend this lecture series, by the way.

videos.t: ARROWS vs ARMOUR - Medieval Myth Busting
videos.s: Tod's Workshop fires full-weight medieval arrows from a 160lb English warbow at reproduced medieval armour. Armour curator Dr Tobias Capwell, an archer and bowyer give historical context and discuss the results.
videos.w: HN considers it the key experimental evidence on how effective longbows really were against armour.
videos.q: I believe the video from Tod's Workshop with actual experimentation is a must see

videos.t: Free To Choose 1980 - Vol. 01 The Power of the Market - Full Video
videos.s: The first episode of Milton Friedman's 1980 Free To Choose series, on how markets and voluntary exchange organize economic activity and the price system. It includes visits to Hong Kong, the U.S. and Scotland and a panel discussion with critics.
videos.w: Commenters say it made market economics click for them and find it an interesting documentary relevant to welfare and UBI debates.
videos.q: What really made it click was Milton Friedman's

videos.t: "How to Think about Parallel Programming: Not!" - Guy L. Steele Jr. (Strange Loop 2010)
videos.s: Guy Steele's Strange Loop 2010 talk argues that programmers should not have to think about parallelism, and that languages should support algorithms built on independence and divide-and-conquer. He also recounts fitting a program onto a single punch card.
videos.w: Recommended as a fantastic talk, valued both for its parallelism ideas and for the punch-card story.
videos.q: It's a fantastic talk in its own right

videos.t: Always/Never: The Quest for Safety, Control, and Survivability - Part 1
videos.s: Part one of Sandia National Labs' first-person documentary on the use control, detonation safety and survivability of US nuclear weapons. It covers nuclear sharing in NATO and how control of use was separated from possession, leading to the always/never problem.
videos.w: Strongly recommended in nuclear-accident and weapons-history threads as an excellent documentary on how nuclear weapons were made safe and secure.
videos.q: I highly recommend this three-part series produced by Sandia National Laboratory

videos.t: How I hacked a hardware crypto wallet and recovered $2 million
videos.s: Joe Grand recounts being hired to hack a Trezor One hardware wallet and recover $2 million of cryptocurrency. He describes three months of experimentation, voltage glitching, failures and high-stakes attempts with only one chance to get it right.
videos.w: Recommended as a gripping real-world hardware hacking story and a showcase of Joe Grand's skill.
videos.q: a cool video about someone hacking a Trezor One. Very enjoyable watch.

videos.t: Aamer Rahman (Fear of a Brown Planet) - Reverse Racism
videos.s: Aamer Rahman of Fear of a Brown Planet delivers a stand-up routine on so-called reverse racism, arguing about power imbalance and why criticism of a dominant group is not equivalent to racism.
videos.w: Pointed to as a comedic but clear explanation of power dynamics in discussions of race and diversity in tech.
videos.q: the very best explanation is long-form stand-up comedy. If you don't understand, you really should watch this.

videos.t: How Analog Color TV Works:  The Beginnings
videos.s: Technology Connections explains the early history of analog color television, from the 1954 start of modern color broadcasting, and how shadow masks work in CRTs. It is the first in a series on how analog color TV works.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an especially good explanation of analog TV and CRT shadow masks.
videos.q: This one on "how analog tv works" I thought was especially good.

videos.t: TSP #133 - Keysight UXR 110GHz BW, 256GS/s, 10-bit Real-Time Oscilloscope Teardown & Experiments
videos.s: Shahriar of The Signal Path tears down and experiments with Keysight's UXR real-time oscilloscope, which offers 110GHz bandwidth and 256GS/s sampling, and compares architectures from Keysight, LeCroy and Tektronix.
videos.w: Recommended as part of a channel with deep teardowns of extreme test equipment, valuable for anyone interested in electronics or RF.
videos.q: If you even have a passing interest in electronics or radio, I can't recommend his channel enough.

videos.t: Native Advertising: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: A John Oliver Last Week Tonight segment on native advertising, showing how ads are disguised as editorial content in news media, including BuzzFeed and major newspapers.
videos.w: Recommended as a funny, clear explanation of native advertising whenever sponsored content in media is discussed.
videos.q: I highly recommend taking the next 11 minutes to watch John Oliver talk about native advertising

videos.t: OCaml Workshop 2020 - State of the OCaml Platform 2020
videos.s: A one-hour OCaml Workshop 2020 talk on the state of the OCaml Platform, covering IDE support, next steps for the tooling and plans for 2020-2021.
videos.w: HN points to it as the latest progress report on OCaml tooling and the community push to improve the platform.
videos.q: Here's the latest progress report, in case you're interested

videos.t: Power Satellites & Space Based Solar Power
videos.s: Isaac Arthur explores space-based solar power, in which satellites beam energy down via microwaves to rectennas on Earth. He discusses feasibility, profitability and its role in spurring space colonization.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as the best overview of power satellites, with pros and cons beyond the construction cost.
videos.q: Issac Arthur usually has the best overview of topics like this

videos.t: Matter to Mind:Bioelectricity, Body Intelligence, Future of Regenerative Medicine- Dr. Michael Levin
videos.s: Developmental and synthetic biologist Michael Levin speaks at a Harvard Extension student event on bioelectricity, body intelligence and regenerative medicine. He discusses how cell electrical networks guide growth and form.
videos.w: Recommended as an approachable look at Levin's work on regrowth and collective cellular intelligence, and used as an example of intelligence beyond brains.
videos.q: Do watch his lectures, it's some really fascinating stuff.

videos.t: Why “No Problem” Can Seem Rude: Phatic Expressions
videos.s: Tom Scott explains phatic expressions such as hello, thank you and how are you, which carry social meaning rather than information, and why replies like no problem can seem rude to some people.
videos.w: HN uses it as the short, clear explainer when discussions about greetings and small talk come up.
videos.q: Tom Scott has an excellent video that addresses this very issue.

videos.t: Gary Vaynerchuk: Building Personal Brand Within the Social Media Landscape - Web 2.0 Expo NY
videos.s: Gary Vaynerchuk's Web 2.0 Expo keynote on building a personal brand in social media. He urges keeping a day job while building something on the side, with passion and persistence, in a loud and profane style.
videos.w: Recommended in Ask HN career threads as motivational advice to use spare hours to start building.
videos.q: One of the best inspirational videos that got me through that time

videos.t: Carbon Offsets! Can't we just buy our way out of climate change?
videos.s: Climate Town's comedic explainer on carbon offsets and whether companies can buy their way out of climate change. It argues that offsets won't save us, while granting they are not bad in principle.
videos.w: HN shares it as an entertaining, well-argued critique of carbon offsetting in threads on greenwashing.
videos.q: i'm taking the chance to share some content by people that present their points of view on this issue much better than i do

videos.t: Saw Stop - This guy puts a finger into an active table saw blade & comes away without a scratch!
videos.s: A short clip showing a person touching an active table saw blade with a finger and walking away unharmed, thanks to SawStop's system that stops the blade within milliseconds of skin contact.
videos.w: Linked as the canonical demo of a safety technology that stops a blade before it injures a finger.
videos.q: The demo also never gets old. Just too badass.

videos.t: Gopherfest 2017 | Upspin with Rob Pike
videos.s: Rob Pike presents Upspin at Gopherfest 2017, an experimental framework for naming and sharing files and data securely and uniformly across a global namespace. It is a project written in Go rather than about Go.
videos.w: Cited as the talk that introduced Upspin, and called fascinating and really good by commenters.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: It's a fascinating talk. I really enjoyed it.

videos.t: Lecture by Douglas Hofstadter: Albert Einstein on Light; Light on Albert Einstein
videos.s: Douglas Hofstadter lectures at Uppsala University on how analogy and daring thinking drove Einstein's discovery of light quanta. He argues deep insight in physics comes from imaginative leaps rather than rigid logic.
videos.w: Cited in discussions of analogy-making in science, and revisited by fans of Hofstadter.
videos.q: that I often revisit

videos.t: [60 fps] The Flying Train, Germany, 1902
videos.s: Neural-network upscaled, 60 fps, stabilized and colorized version of 1902 footage of the Wuppertal Schwebebahn suspended railway in Germany. The source film comes from MoMA. It gives a vivid view of an early-1900s city and a train system that still runs.
videos.w: HN commenters share it as a favorite example of upscaled vintage footage that makes the early 1900s feel present, though some find the colorization off.
videos.q: I've really come to enjoy these sorts of upscaled videos that allow a view of various cities in the early 1900's.

videos.t: Barliman: trying the halting problem backwards, blindfolded - William Byrd, Greg Rosenblatt
videos.s: A Clojure/conj 2016 talk demoing Barliman, a prototype smart editor that does program synthesis. Given a partial program and tests, it completes the program using a relational interpreter written in miniKanren.
videos.w: HN people point to it as an amazing demonstration of relational programming and program synthesis that still looks exciting after LLM code generation.
videos.q: I work on miniKanren, which is a logic programming language with a complete search that doesn't hit the nontermination issues you mention.

videos.t: Best Speech You Will Ever Hear - Gary Yourofsky
videos.s: Gary Yourofsky's 2010 lecture at Georgia Tech arguing for veganism on ethical, health and environmental grounds. It is a long, forceful animal-rights speech.
videos.w: Some commenters credit it with persuading them to go vegan, while others dismiss parts of it as pseudoscience.
videos.q: the logical inconsistencies become very apparent

videos.t: Epic 2014
videos.s: Epic 2014 is a short science-fiction film that imagines the media landscape merging into a personalized, computer-generated news service. It is a fictional history of 'Googlezon' and the decline of traditional newspapers.
videos.w: HN returns to it as an uncannily prescient prediction of tech consolidation and AI-written, personalized news.
videos.q: Rewatching it now gives me this uncanny feeling.

videos.t: Honest Government Ad | Anti Encryption Law
videos.s: A satirical 'honest' government ad from The Juice Media about Australia's 2018 Assistance and Access anti-encryption bill. It lays out in blunt terms what the law would let authorities do.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as an entertaining, accessible explanation of how bad the law is, including for non-technical audiences.
videos.q: It's very entertaining, and explains it in a way that everyday people can understand how bad it will be.

videos.t: I have APHANTASIA (and you may too...without realising it!)
videos.s: An artist describes discovering she has aphantasia, the inability to form mental images, and how it affects her work. She asks viewers about their own visualization.
videos.w: HN points to it as a vivid first-person description of aphantasia and an example of an aphantasic artist.
videos.q: this video is fantastic for describing the feeling of aphantasia

videos.t: Can you fit a whole game into a QR code?
videos.s: MattKC fits a playable Snake game into a QR code by writing tiny x86 machine code and patching the ZBar scanner so it can run the decoded data.
videos.w: HN admires it as a creative hack and cites it as the inspiration for later tiny-game and QR-code projects.
videos.q: I admire this type of content where the creator take some concepts we [all] use and understand

videos.t: The Fantastic Case of the Missing Tesla
videos.s: The final chapter of Rich Rebuilds' saga about buying a used Tesla Model X that went missing, with cameo appearances and the end of the dispute. It is part of a longer series on the problems he had with Tesla.
videos.w: HN recommends the series as a cautionary tale about buying used Teslas and dealing with Tesla service.
videos.q: Anybody involved with Tesla in any way should at least watch

videos.t: Hackfest 2015: Theo de Raadt presented "Pledge: A new security technology in openbsd"
videos.s: Theo de Raadt presents pledge, a new OpenBSD security mechanism that kills processes which exceed the system calls they declared they need. The talk was given late at night at Hackfest 2015.
videos.w: HN points to it as the canonical overview of pledge and the ideas behind OpenBSD's exploit mitigations.
videos.q: I thoroughly enjoyed Theo de Raadt recent talk

videos.t: Edward Gibson: Human Language, Psycholinguistics, Syntax, Grammar & LLMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #426
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews MIT psycholinguist Edward Gibson on human language, syntax, grammar and how large language models relate to them. The conversation runs nearly three hours.
videos.w: HN cites it for the argument that LLMs capture language form but not meaning, and for how the brain's language network works.
videos.q: I highly recommend listening to this Lex Friedman podcast episode

videos.t: F2C2012:  Aaron Swartz keynote - "How we stopped SOPA"
videos.s: Aaron Swartz's keynote at Freedom to Connect 2012 describing how ordinary people helped defeat the SOPA censorship bill. He recounts how the Senate unexpectedly united behind the bill and how grassroots action stopped it.
videos.w: HN shares it as an inspiring account of citizens changing Washington, especially after Swartz's death.
videos.q: If you haven't watched aaronsw's talk on stopping SOPA, it's well worth your time.

videos.t: I took an IQ test to explain what's wrong with them
videos.s: Veritasium takes an IQ test and examines what IQ measures, its history including military use and eugenics, its controversies, and how it correlates with life outcomes. Experts including Cecil Reynolds and Stuart Ritchie contribute.
videos.w: Recommended as a good primer on what IQ scores mean and their limited effect on life outcomes.
videos.q: Veritasium had a good primer on IQ scores and what they actually mean for your life

videos.t: David Deutsch: A new way to explain explanation
videos.s: Physicist David Deutsch's TED talk on why science took off, arguing that good explanations are those that are hard to vary. It contrasts scientific explanation with myth.
videos.w: HN points to it as a short, tight introduction to Deutsch's idea of hard-to-vary explanations.
videos.q: it's a very tight talk and you should start from the beginning

videos.t: Hans Rosling: Global population growth, box by box
videos.s: Hans Rosling's TED@Cannes talk uses boxes and animated data graphics to show how world population will grow to about 9 billion. He argues that raising living standards for the poorest is what reduces population growth.
videos.w: HN points to it as a data-driven, worldview-changing explanation of why global population will level off.
videos.q: Totally changed (well, confirmed) my world view. Start here

videos.t: Riot On Documentary (2002)
videos.s: A documentary about Riot Entertainment, a Finnish dot-com-era startup that raised millions in funding and then collapsed. It follows the hype-driven rise and implosion of the company.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an entertaining dot-com-era story and a cautionary tale about VC funding and fake-it-till-you-make-it growth.
videos.q: I highly recommend the documentary "Riot On!". Great documentary, great cinema, and great entertainment.

videos.t: The Encryption Tightrope: Balancing Americans’ Security and Privacy: EventID=104573
videos.s: A 2016 House Judiciary Committee hearing on encryption, held during the Apple and FBI iPhone dispute. It features testimony from Apple, the FBI and outside experts including Susan Landau, and runs over five hours.
videos.w: HN users cite it as primary-source testimony, especially for the argument that weakening encryption is security versus security, not privacy versus security.
videos.q: the recent House Judiciary Committee Hearing is worth the watch

videos.t: Reinventing Organizations
videos.s: Frederic Laloux presents his research on self-managing, purpose-driven organizations, followed by Q&A. He summarizes the findings of his book Reinventing Organizations and examples such as Buurtzorg.
videos.w: Recommended as the best introduction to self-management and new management paradigms.
videos.q: I can highly recommend watching this video if you're interested in self-management and the idea of a new management paradigm

videos.t: What Would You Do? Bike Theft (White Guy, Black Guy, Pretty Girl)
videos.s: A hidden-camera social experiment in a park where three people try to steal a bike in the open: a white teenager, a black teenager and a young woman. It records how bystanders react to each.
videos.w: Used in threads on bias and social engineering as a vivid example of how bystanders treat different thieves.
videos.q: There's an awesome video of three college-student-aged in a park.

videos.t: Shanghai Tower (650 meters)
videos.s: A POV video of climbers illegally scaling the 650 m Shanghai Tower while it was under construction, filmed on a helmet camera.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a gripping and vertigo-inducing watch that put rooftop climbers on the map.
videos.q: An absolutely fantastic watch.

videos.t: Oculus Connect Keynote: John Carmack
videos.s: John Carmack's keynote at Oculus Connect 2014 about the Gear VR and development stories from building it. He discusses mobile GPU optimization, latency, and display ideas like programmable interlacing.
videos.w: HN recommends it for Carmack's detailed engineering insight into VR rendering and latency challenges.
videos.q: Carmack's 2014 Oculus Connect keynote is well worth watching

videos.t: Apple's World Wide Developers Conference 1997 with Steve Jobs
videos.s: Steve Jobs at Apple's 1997 WWDC, shortly after his return, taking developer questions and describing Apple's direction. He discusses the Newton and says to start from the customer experience and work back to technology.
videos.w: Held up as a masterclass in handling a crisis and a hostile Q&A, and quoted for starting from customer experience.
videos.q: My favorite Jobs masterclass is his talk at Apple's developer conference in 1997

videos.t: Saifedean Ammous: Bitcoin, Anarchy, and Austrian Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #284
videos.s: A long Lex Fridman podcast conversation with Austrian economist Saifedean Ammous, author of The Bitcoin Standard. They cover Bitcoin, fiat money, anarchy and Austrian economics.
videos.w: Cited as a thorough statement of the bitcoin-maximalist case, with the host pushing back.
videos.q: this episode turned me from a "fuck any form of crypto" stance to an appreciation of BTC the technology

videos.t: 100%+ short interest in GameStop stock (GME) – fundamental & technical deep value analysis
videos.s: Roaring Kitty's July 2020 analysis of GameStop, arguing a bullish deep-value case when the stock was about $4 and short interest exceeded 100%. It covers fundamentals, cash balance and technicals.
videos.w: After the 2021 squeeze, HN cites it as the original thesis behind the GME story and praises its quality.
videos.q: If you haven't watched his youtube content go watch it. It's unbelievably high quality.

videos.t: How Your Brain Works & Changes
videos.s: Andrew Huberman introduces how the nervous system produces sensation, emotion and behavior, and how neuroplasticity lets us change it. It covers neurons, synapses, brain chemicals and the rhythms governing focus, learning and sleep.
videos.w: HN points to it as a foundational neuroscience primer, with some commenters crediting it for practical changes to learning and sleep.
videos.q: feeling overwhelmed and the frustration of learning are necessary to activate the neuro-chemical processes needed to change our programming

videos.t: The real reason Boeing's new plane crashed twice
videos.s: Vox explainer arguing the two Boeing 737 Max crashes were not just a software bug but the result of a company's drive to beat its rival, with a flawed MCAS design.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a concise explanation of what caused the 737 Max crashes.
videos.q: VOX has a good explainer video on what caused the 737 Max to crash twice for anyone who doesn't know the details.

videos.t: Apollo Core Rope Memory (Apollo Guidance Computer Part 30)
videos.s: CuriousMarc's Apollo Guidance Computer restoration series looks at core rope memory, the ROM that held the Moon landing programs. Mike Stewart builds a custom reader to recover lost AGC programs.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as the deepest explanation of how AGC rope memory works and how it differs from core memory.
videos.q: Here,s a deep, deep dive into AGC rope memory.

videos.t: I Saved a PNG Image To A Bird
videos.s: Benn Jordan's video about storing a PNG image in a living bird, a starling that learns to reproduce encoded sounds. It mixes ornithology, audio engineering, and data encoding.
videos.w: HN fans point to it as a fun, nerdy crossover of bird song acoustics and technology, and the story itself got its own thread.
videos.q: you might enjoy Benn Jordan's video of "saving" a PNG to a bird

videos.t: Trump's Biggest Failure
videos.s: A long video essay by Kraut arguing that Trump's biggest failure was his handling of China. It spends much of its length on Chinese history, culture, the trade war, and the rise of a communist superpower.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a well-researched explainer of the history and culture behind China's current position, despite the political title.
videos.q: Kraut has a fantastic video on the topic

videos.t: Edward Kmett - Type Classes vs. the World
videos.s: Edward Kmett speaks at the Boston Haskell meetup about type classes and the design tradeoffs of global coherence compared with other approaches to implicit instances. It covers why uniqueness of instances matters for reasoning and refactoring.
videos.w: HN points to it as the definitive explanation of why coherence and the orphan rule matter, in debates over Haskell, Rust traits, OCaml modules and Elm.
videos.q: Ed Kmett's fantastic "Typeclasses v. the World" talk covers

videos.t: Nord Stream sabotage and hybrid war on Europe
videos.s: Anders Puck Nielsen analyzes the Nord Stream pipeline sabotage using Kilcullen's theory of liminal warfare and prospect theory. He argues from the operational design that Russia is the most likely culprit, then discusses how hybrid warfare might be used against Europe.
videos.w: HN points to it as a compact, reasoned case for Russian responsibility, though at least one commenter found the argument unconvincing.
videos.q: Anders Puck Nielsen has an under 15 minute video with a compelling explanation for why Russia is most likely to have done it

videos.t: Kubernetes for SysAdmins | Kelsey Hightower at PuppetConf | Talk & Demo
videos.s: Kelsey Hightower introduces Kubernetes to sysadmins at PuppetConf 2016, with a demo. He explains the declarative model and how it changes the contract between infrastructure and applications.
videos.w: HN recommends it for Hightower's clear mental models, such as comparing the scheduler to Tetris and explaining why resource limits matter.
videos.q: Kelsey Hightower comparing the kubernetes scheduler to Tetris was awesome for cementing a mental model.

videos.t: Part 1 - Training Video for Bell Labs' Holmdel Computing Center - AT&T Archives
videos.s: A 1973 AT&T training film made for new employees at Bell Labs' Holmdel Computing Center, when Unix was in its third version and running at 16 computer centers in the Bell System. It shows how users submitted jobs and used the center's machines.
videos.w: HN commenters share it as a rare, atmospheric look at what working at an early computing center was actually like, including how code was submitted and processed.
videos.q: This is one of my favorites, about people submitting their code to get processed at their computing center

videos.t: Scammers Wanted $3,000 - They Watched Me Spend It All
videos.s: Kitboga baits tech-support scammers into believing they will get $3,000, wasting hours of their time while he plays along and screen-shares. The scammers become frustrated as it becomes clear the money will not reach them.
videos.w: HN commenters point to Kitboga as an entertaining, righteous example of wasting scammers' time.
videos.q: One of my favourite videos so far involved “driving to a store” to get google play codes

videos.t: Software Engineering's Greatest Hits
videos.s: Greg Wilson surveys what empirical research actually shows about software development, why we believe it, and how to share that knowledge more widely. It covers evidence on practices such as TDD and design patterns.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as an evidence-based counterweight to opinion in software engineering debates.
videos.q: I highly recommend watching Greg Wilson's Software Engineering's Greatest Hits[1].

videos.t: How to Get Your First Customers | Startup School
videos.s: A Startup School talk by YC partner and former Airbnb growth head Gustaf Alstromer on how startups get their first customers. It covers doing things that don't scale, founders learning sales, the sales funnel, and charging your first customer.
videos.w: Commenters recommend the whole talk as practical, tactical advice for early customer acquisition and outbound sales.
videos.q: The entire video is really good actually I recommend watching the entire thing.

videos.t: Bayes theorem, the geometry of changing beliefs
videos.s: 3Blue1Brown presents Bayes' theorem through a geometric diagram, showing how evidence should update beliefs. It works through the Kahneman and Tversky style questions and base rates.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as the most intuitive introduction to Bayes' theorem and cite it in base-rate arguments.
videos.q: There's a very cool 3Blue1Brown video [0] that helps give you an intuitive feel for Bayes Theorem.

videos.t: Living Computation: Robust-first programming in ULAM
videos.s: Dave Ackley presents robust-first computing and the ULAM programming language for the Movable Feast Machine, a cellular-automata-like architecture. It was a short video for the Future Programming Workshop 2015.
videos.w: HN points to it as an entry into Ackley's indefinitely scalable computing project, with a network-switch demo recommended as the best place to start.
videos.q: I think the best place to start is this demo of a network switch made out of cells

videos.t: How Corruption Destroys Armies - Theft, Graft, and Russian failure in Ukraine
videos.s: Perun analyzes how corruption and theft in defence procurement hollowed out the Russian military before its invasion of Ukraine. It explains the mechanics of graft and how it degrades capability.
videos.w: Recommended as a long but insightful explanation of how corruption works inside institutions.
videos.q: Both these videos are long, but they had a lot of interesting ideas and insight on this topic

videos.t: Inner Game of Tennis
videos.s: A 1970 demonstration of W. Timothy Gallwey, author of The Inner Game of Tennis, teaching a complete beginner to play tennis in about ten minutes. He chats with her, feeds balls and gives positive feedback instead of instruction.
videos.w: HN commenters use it as a vivid demonstration of learning by quieting the conscious mind, and recommend it alongside the book.
videos.q: This video of Timothy Gallwey teaching a woman how to play tennis. In 5 minutes.

videos.t: SpaceX: The Biggest Money Loser in IPO History
videos.s: Patrick Boyle analyzes SpaceX's IPO prospectus, covering its financials, speculative products, AI business, related-party dealings, compensation, and a governance structure with minimal shareholder rights.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear, roughly 30-minute summary of the problems with the SpaceX IPO.
videos.q: Patrick Boyle has an excellent presentation (YT) on the SpaceX IPO.

videos.t: Tuesday @ 1130   ISA Shootout – a Comparison of RISC V, ARM, and x86   Chris Celio, UC Berkeley V2
videos.s: Chris Celio of UC Berkeley compares the RISC-V, ARM and x86 instruction sets, with quantitative data on instruction counts and code density. It examines how the compressed extension fares against Thumb and x86.
videos.w: Cited as primary-source evidence that RISC-V code density is competitive with or better than ARM and x86.
videos.q: You should watch this video

videos.t: The US Military’s Massive Global Transportation System
videos.s: Wendover Productions explains how the US military moves people and materiel worldwide, including prepositioned equipment, sealift and airlift. It shows the scale of the logistics system behind US force projection.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear overview of military logistics, often as a contrast with civilian infrastructure efforts.
videos.q: Wendover Productions has a great video about the insane amount of logistics

videos.t: David Carr vs. Some Guys from VICE
videos.s: A clip from the documentary Page One in which New York Times reporter David Carr interviews and confronts the founders of Vice magazine over their media deal. It captures tension between old and new media in 2010.
videos.w: Brought up whenever Vice is discussed, as a memorable scene of Carr pressing its founders.
videos.q: One of the best scenes from Page One

videos.t: DIY haptic input knob: BLDC motor + round LCD
videos.s: A two-minute demo of SmartKnob View, an open-source input knob built from a brushless gimbal motor, magnetic encoder and round LCD. Closed-loop torque control gives software-defined detents and end stops.
videos.w: HN people hold it up as a polished solo hardware project and the go-to example of haptic knobs, including in discussions of physical car controls.
videos.q: I made a rotary input device that provides software-defined "virtual" detents and end-stops, implemented using a BLDC gimbal motor.

videos.t: The Absurdity of Detecting Gravitational Waves
videos.s: Veritasium explains in detail how LIGO detects gravitational waves, with a laser interferometer measuring displacements smaller than a proton. The video focuses on the extreme precision and the techniques needed rather than the general discovery story.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a good layperson explanation of how LIGO's detection works and why it is so hard.
videos.q: Here is a great video with explanations

videos.t: Zig 2026: No-AI Policy, $670K Foundation, Left GitHub & Why Zig Isn’t 1.0 - Andrew Kelley Explains
videos.s: JetBrains interviews Zig creator Andrew Kelley about why Zig has no 1.0 after a decade, why the project left GitHub, and why it bans AI contributions. He also covers what makes Zig better than C and his views on open source.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a convincing primary-source interview showing Zig's cohesive design vision and the creator's level-headed reasoning.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: convinced me more than any design doc or blogpost could

videos.t: Stanford Seminar - Generalized Reversible Computing and the Unconventional Computing Landscape
videos.s: A Stanford EE380 seminar by Michael P. Frank of Sandia National Laboratories on generalized reversible computing. It surveys unconventional computing approaches as transistor scaling nears its limits and energy efficiency stops improving.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as an informative talk from a leading researcher in reversible computing, mainly in threads on reversible computers and energy efficiency.
videos.q: his Stanford talk is extremely informative

videos.t: Accent Expert Gives a Tour of U.S. Accents - (Part 2) | WIRED
videos.s: Dialect coach Erik Singer tours a range of accents across North America with linguists in Part 2 of WIRED's accent series. It covers regional distinctions such as Southern Mississippi, Miami and Utah English.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an enjoyable, accessible tour of US accents and cite it in threads on vowel shifts and dialects.
videos.q: I loved this video which does a tour of US accents.

videos.t: Irving Kirsch:  The Emperor's New Drugs
videos.s: Psychologist Irving Kirsch gives a distinguished lecture on antidepressant trials and the placebo effect. He argues drug-placebo differences are small outside severe depression.
videos.w: HN points to it in discussions of antidepressant efficacy, the serotonin model and the power of placebos.
videos.q: I found Irving Kirsch's talk about anti-depressants vs placebo in depression [1] very interesting.

videos.t: Design Microservice Architectures the Right Way
videos.s: Michael Bryzek of Flow gives a QCon London 2018 talk on key decisions for building maintainable microservices. It covers infrastructure, continuous deployment, communication, event streaming and language choice.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it for showing the tooling possible when schemas and APIs are treated as code.
videos.q: There's a great talk that I highly recommend about some of the magic you can do

videos.t: Can Spinlaunch Throw Rockets Into Space?
videos.s: Scott Manley looks at SpinLaunch, which aims to throw launch vehicles out of a spinning launcher at hypersonic speed. He covers its recent Mach 1 test of a one-third scale launcher and the engineering problems that remain.
videos.w: HN treats it as the more informed, balanced take on SpinLaunch's tradeoffs.
videos.q: a more honest and detailed look at the company

videos.t: Genetic Engineering Will Change Everything Forever – CRISPR
videos.s: Kurzgesagt's animated explainer on CRISPR gene editing, covering how the technology works and what it could mean for curing disease, designer babies and aging. It frames genetic engineering as an irreversible change coming to humanity.
videos.w: HN commenters hand it out as a quick, accessible primer whenever CRISPR or gene editing comes up.
videos.q: I strongly recommend this quick introduction video from Kurzgesagt on YouTube

videos.t: How to Land the Space Shuttle... from Space
videos.s: Bret Copeland, in an astronaut costume, gives an energetic talk on how the Space Shuttle landed from orbit, including reentry and the unpowered glide. It includes real-time landing footage with HUD and audio.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an entertaining, technical illustration of how hard the Shuttle's one-shot dead-stick landing was.
videos.q: I highly, highly recommend this entertaining and technical presentation by Bret Copeland

videos.t: Delvon Lamarr Organ Trio - Warm-up Set (Live on KEXP)
videos.s: A live KEXP warm-up set by the Delvon Lamarr Organ Trio, recorded at Upstream Music Fest in 2017. The set includes Move On Up and Memphis.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as a great live KEXP session with standout guitar work and good sound.
videos.q: He's hands down one of the most talented guitarists alive today.

videos.t: Why is Time a One-Way Street?
videos.s: Leonard Susskind's Santa Fe Institute talk on the arrow of time: why the past differs from the future when physics equations are time-symmetric. He covers entropy, cosmology and Boltzmann brains.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a clear explanation of why time runs one way, from a leading physicist.
videos.q: Highly recommend the talk.

videos.t: Google Engineer on His Sentient AI Claim
videos.s: Bloomberg Technology interviews Google engineer Blake Lemoine about the experiments that led him to believe LaMDA was sentient and why he was placed on administrative leave. He also raises concerns about AI ethics at Google.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend watching it to hear his side directly, noting he comes across as coherent, while others dispute his sincerity.
videos.q: I'd implore anyone reading this thread to see what he had to say for yourself and form your own opinion

videos.t: Second Reality by Future Crew (pc demo)
videos.s: A capture of Second Reality, the real-time audiovisual demo by Future Crew first shown at Assembly 1993, recorded from a 486DX2-66 with a Gravis Ultrasound. It showcases the peak of early 1990s PC demoscene techniques.
videos.w: HN points to it as one of the best and most formative early PC demos, a touchstone of demoscene history.
videos.q: It is considered to be one of the best demos created during the early 1990s on the PC

videos.t: Peter Singer - ordinary people are evil
videos.s: Philosopher Jeffrey Kaplan summarizes Peter Singer's 1972 essay 'Famine, Affluence, and Morality', arguing that failing to give to save lives is morally comparable to letting a child drown. It is a short lecture on the argument's structure.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the best short exposition of Singer's argument for a duty to give.
videos.q: I think the video is the best short exposition but you could try reading the paper the video is about

videos.t: Why Japan had NO Chance in WW2
videos.s: Military History Visualized charts ship production by the United States and Japan from December 1941 to September 1945. The growing numbers show why Japan, despite a stronger starting navy, could not win a long war.
videos.w: Cited as one of the best visualizations of how overwhelmingly dominant US industrial output was in the Pacific war.
videos.q: One of the best visualizations I've come across of just how dominant the US industrial base was in the 1940s under full mobilization.

videos.t: Elite: "The game that couldn't be written"
videos.s: An hour-long video essay on Elite, the 1984 BBC Micro game by David Braben and Ian Bell. It covers how they fit a 3D engine, economy and universe into 22KB on a 2MHz 6502.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an amazing overview of the technical feats and history behind Elite, and cite it for what the 6502 could do.
videos.q: has an amazing video on this

videos.t: Breakdown of the Pentagon UFO videos with Mick West
videos.s: Astronomer David Kipping of Cool Worlds talks with Mick West to break down the three declassified Pentagon UFO videos. They explain the footage through camera artifacts, glare, and perspective effects.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the boring, convincing debunking of the Gofast, FLIR and Gimbal videos, which commenters say ended UFO hype for them.
videos.q: Mick West's breakdowns of the Pentagon UAP videos was the nail in the coffin of this era of UFO hype for me.

videos.t: Alpha Zero's "Immortal Zugzwang Game" against Stockfish
videos.s: agadmator walks through a game in which DeepMind's AlphaZero beat Stockfish, ending in a famous zugzwang that leaves the engine helpless. He gives commentary on the moves.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a striking, well-explained example of AlphaZero's play and of zugzwang.
videos.q: A great example I love showing people is Alpha Zero's infamous "Immortal Zugzwang Game" against Stockfish

videos.t: The Uncanny Valley Is Wrong
videos.s: This Place argues that the uncanny valley is a flawed concept, since 'human likeness' is too broad and the supporting evidence is cherry-picked. It proposes that the creepiness really comes from how animated characters and robots move.
videos.w: Recommended as a convincing counterargument to the widely repeated idea of the uncanny valley.
videos.q: here's an amazing video making a convincing argument that "Uncanny Valley" isn't a thing

videos.t: You Are Immune Against Every Disease
videos.s: Kurzgesagt's animated explainer on the human immune system, describing the body as an ecosystem and how immune defenses cope with the variety of invaders. It promotes their book Immune.
videos.w: HN users call it a mind-blowing and good explainer on how the immune system works, and cite it in vaccine and disease threads.
videos.q: this Kurzgeasgt video blew my mind on this topic. Our immune system really is amazing.

videos.t: Avoiding Negative Side Effects: Concrete Problems in AI Safety part 1
videos.s: Robert Miles introduces the first of several videos on the paper 'Concrete Problems in AI Safety', focusing on how AI systems can cause accidental negative side effects. It explains the problem in accessible terms.
videos.w: HN recommends Robert Miles' channel as a clear starting point for people curious about AI safety.
videos.q: For those curious about AI safety I heavily recommend Robert Miles channel on YouTube.

videos.t: Magnetohydrodynamics - Propelling Liquid Metal with Magnets!
videos.s: Tech Ingredients explains the principles of magnetohydrodynamics and builds several demonstrations, including propelling liquid metal and electrolytes with magnets and a railgun-style setup.
videos.w: It comes up as a great explainer on magnetohydrodynamic drives and pumps in threads about silent submarine propulsion.
videos.q: There's a great video from one of my favorite YouTube channels about Magnetohydrodynamic drives.

videos.t: Sacha Arnoud, Director of Engineering, Waymo - MIT Self-Driving Cars
videos.s: Sacha Arnoud, Waymo's Director of Engineering, gives a lecture in MIT's 2018 deep learning for self-driving cars course on the rise of machine learning in autonomous vehicles. It covers how Waymo uses deep learning and how it handles tricky driving situations.
videos.w: Pointed to during self-driving news threads as an insider view of Waymo's progress, deep learning's role and its limits.
videos.q: Check the lecture, its fantastic imo.

videos.t: David Deutsch on Optimism
videos.s: An excerpt from an RSA event in which physicist David Deutsch makes the case for optimism as a driver of progress in the 21st century. It is a short highlight of a longer discussion.
videos.w: Pointed to as an antidote to pessimism about the future, tied to Deutsch's ideas in The Beginning of Infinity.
videos.q: I encourage everyone pessimistic about our future to learn about David Deutsch's infinite optimism

videos.t: Generative AI for Krita - With ControlNet
videos.s: A short demo of an open-source Krita plugin that uses Stable Diffusion to generate and edit images in place. It adds ControlNet scribble and line-art support. You select an area, push a button, and new matching content appears.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a quick way to see how the Krita AI plugin works and how it matches Photoshop's generative features.
videos.q: the video is mindblowing

videos.t: DEF CON 24 - Chris Rock - How to Overthrow a Government
videos.s: A DEF CON 24 talk on how a cyber mercenary group could forge identities and create the conditions for overthrowing a government. It is entertainingly outlandish and includes a drone-mounted saw for cutting power lines.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an amazing, entertaining talk and cites it in threads on power-line sabotage and coup tactics.
videos.q: If you've not seen this amazing talk I can't recommend it enough.

videos.t: Hound Internal Demo
videos.s: SoundHound's CEO demos Hound, a voice assistant, handling fast compound natural language queries with context and detailed criteria. The video leaked before the product's official launch.
videos.w: HN viewers were impressed by its speed and saw it as a glimpse of the future of voice search; later it appears in hiring posts.
videos.q: That's insanely fast, compound natural language queries. I'm impressed.

videos.t: We Are The Art | Brandon Sanderson’s Keynote Speech
videos.s: Brandon Sanderson's keynote on AI-generated art, arguing that the artistic process and the journey matter more than the finished product. He explains why he rebels against generative AI in creative work.
videos.w: HN commenters share it as an eloquent argument that AI output is not art, and as a companion to worries about losing deep thinking.
videos.q: Here is author Brandon Sanderson eloquently explaining why AI generated slop will never be art

videos.t: Lecture 1 | Convex Optimization I (Stanford)
videos.s: The introductory lecture of Stephen Boyd's Stanford Convex Optimization I course (EE 364A). It outlines convex sets, functions and problems, and the course's coverage of least-squares, linear and semidefinite programming, duality and interior-point methods.
videos.w: HN recommends Boyd's lectures as a fantastic, often funny follow-up to linear algebra and as a step in machine learning study paths.
videos.q: These lectures are fantastic after you've mastered the basics of linear algebra

videos.t: Two Monkeys Were Paid Unequally: Excerpt from Frans de Waal's TED Talk
videos.s: A short excerpt from Frans de Waal's TED talk showing a capuchin monkey fairness experiment in which two monkeys are paid unequally, one with cucumber and one with grapes. The shortchanged monkey reacts angrily.
videos.w: HN uses it again and again as shorthand for the idea that resentment of unfair pay and inequality is built into primates, including us.
videos.q: This is the video that explains the best

videos.t: Here I Stand, at Age 80
videos.s: Ted Nelson, the originator of hypertext and Project Xanadu, gives a personal account at age 80 of his ideals, his career, and how a poor career plan led to discoveries and adventures. It works as an alternative history of personal computing and hypertext.
videos.w: HN people point to it as Nelson's candid, first-person overview of his life, Xanadu's failure, and the lessons he drew, a historical record from the man himself.
videos.q: Strongly recommended, and I'm grateful that he recorded this historical treasure.

videos.t: Steve Jobs introduces iPhone in 2007
videos.s: An excerpt from Steve Jobs's January 2007 Macworld keynote in which he introduces the original iPhone. It shows the pitch of a phone, music player and internet communicator, along with the live demo.
videos.w: HN treats it as the model product demo and MVP showcase, and as a reminder of how constrained the first iPhone hardware was.
videos.q: If you want to se the ultimate MVP demo of a product look no further than the 2007 introduction of the Apple iPhone

videos.t: Cambridge Analytica Uncovered: Secret filming reveals election tricks
videos.s: A Channel 4 News undercover investigation in which Cambridge Analytica executives are filmed discussing bribes, honeypots, fake identities and manipulating elections around the world.
videos.w: HN points to it as the primary evidence of what Cambridge Analytica was willing to do, especially in Facebook data scandal threads.
videos.q: I highly recommend watching the report, it's a fascinating watch.

videos.t: Surreal Numbers (writing the first book) - Numberphile
videos.s: A Numberphile interview with Donald Knuth about how he came to write the first book on surreal numbers after a lunch with John Conway. He tells the story casually in about 14 minutes.
videos.w: Recommended as a short, charming introduction to surreal numbers and to how Knuth wrote his book in under a week.
videos.q: This interview is excellent

videos.t: In The Bleak Midwinter - Jacob Collier
videos.s: Jacob Collier layers ten vocal parts to arrange and perform Harold Darke's carol "In the Bleak Midwinter", with inventive harmony and tuning.
videos.w: Recommended as a showcase of Collier's harmonic and microtonal skill.
videos.q: Probably the best example, especially the middle

videos.t: Keynote. Professor Steven G. Johnson | JuliaCon 2019
videos.s: Steven G. Johnson, MIT professor and FFTW co-author, gives a JuliaCon 2019 keynote on metaprogramming and staged programming in Julia, showing how it enables high-performance numerical code and when not to use macros.
videos.w: Cited for showing how Julia's metaprogramming can beat C and Fortran, along with sound advice not to overuse it.
videos.q: really interesting, informative, entertaining and well delivered.

videos.t: Glass engineering - designing and making photochromic glass
videos.s: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science shows how to make small batches of specialty glass with minimal equipment, including designing and making photochromic glass. He covers ingredients, melting and the challenges involved.
videos.w: Recommended as a hands-on introduction to glass melting and chemistry and to Krasnow's channel.
videos.q: I'd highly recommend his channel to anyone interested in science and fabrication.

videos.t: Mark Zuckerberg: First Interview in the Metaverse | Lex Fridman Podcast #398
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Mark Zuckerberg in the metaverse, with both appearing as photorealistic avatars from separate locations. They discuss Meta's AI, VR and the future of avatars.
videos.w: HN points to it as a demonstration that VR presence can feel close to talking in person.
videos.q: The Fridman - Zuckerberg VR interview really convinced me of this, if you haven't seen it, check it out, it's incredible

videos.t: The Scariest Episode Yet - Still Untitled: The Adam Savage Project - 10/30/18
videos.s: An episode of Adam Savage's Still Untitled podcast with molecular biologist Joe DeRisi. They discuss his work, including sequencing to detect rare infections, in a conversation Savage calls possibly the show's scariest.
videos.w: HN recommends it for DeRisi's fascinating stories about rare pathogens such as brain-eating amoebas.
videos.q: The stories he tells are absolutely fascinating and I thoroughly encourage everyone

videos.t: How Sugar & Processed Foods Impact Your Health | Dr. Robert Lustig
videos.s: A long Huberman Lab podcast episode with Dr. Robert Lustig on the calories-in, calories-out model and how sugar, fructose, fiber and processed foods affect insulin, liver and metabolic health.
videos.w: HN mentions it mostly as a source for the argument that sugar is toxic, though some commenters push back on claims like fructose being addictive.

videos.t: Google I/O 2011: Chrome Dev Tools Reloaded
videos.s: Paul Irish and Pavel Feldman present the newest Chrome Dev Tools features at Google I/O 2011, including live CSS editing, saving changes, breakpoints and network analysis. It also covers remote debugging.
videos.w: In 2011 HN people cited it as a convincing introduction that won them over to Chrome's developer tools.
videos.q: I am Sold. I am switching to WebDev tools.

videos.t: Rethinking CS Education | Alan Kay, CrossRoads 2015
videos.s: Alan Kay argues for rethinking how computer science is taught in schools, drawing on his work on object-oriented programming and GUIs. He discusses how poorly people understand complex systems and what education could do about it.
videos.w: HN readers cite Kay's talks for his views on programming languages as user interfaces, thinking beyond logic, and why people struggle with complex systems.
videos.q: I would really really encourage everyone here to watch Alan Kay's recent talks on how poorly we understand systems

videos.t: Toxic Propellant Hazards In Rocketry 1966 NASA
videos.s: A 1966 NASA safety film teaching workers how to handle toxic rocket propellants such as hydrazine and nitrogen tetroxide. It explains the hazards of these corrosive, flammable and toxic chemicals and what to do after contamination.
videos.w: Commenters share it as a favorite vintage NASA film with a sobering look at how dangerous hypergolic propellants are.
videos.q: provides an interesting discussion of the dangers of nitrogen tetroxide and hydrazine propellants.

videos.t: Bobby McFerrin Demonstrates the Power of the Pentatonic Scale | World Science Festival
videos.s: Bobby McFerrin uses audience participation at a World Science Festival event to demonstrate how instinctively people follow the pentatonic scale.
videos.w: HN shares it as a delightful demo of the pentatonic scale's near-universal appeal and of a crowd syncing without instruction.
videos.q: Have you seen the video where Bobby McFerrin leads a whole crowd to sync perfectly with each other

videos.t: Free Energy Principle — Karl Friston
videos.s: Neuroscientist Karl Friston gives a 15-minute talk on the free energy principle, covering Markov blankets, Bayesian model evidence and global brain theories.
videos.w: Offered as a high-level, approachable introduction to Friston's idea of the brain as a prediction machine.
videos.q: There's a great video introduction to that idea with Karl Friston from UCL here

videos.t: Chuck Moore's Fireside Chat 2011
videos.s: Chuck Moore, creator of Forth, gives his annual Fireside Chat at Forth Day 2011 at Stanford. He talks about his multi-core GreenArrays chip design and demonstrates code running on it.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a window into Moore's minimalist CPU design and the GA144 chip, despite the slow pace.
videos.q: I was blown away by this 2011 video of Charles Moore talking about his CPU design and running code

videos.t: The Computer-free Automation of a Jukebox (Electromechanics)
videos.s: Technology Connections takes apart a 1970 Wurlitzer 3400 jukebox to show how electromechanical relays and switches automated its behavior without a computer.
videos.w: Recommended as an eye-opening look at pre-computer automation and relay logic.
videos.q: The computer free automation of a jukebox from the 1970s is an eye opener

videos.t: Robert C Martin - Clean Architecture and Design
videos.s: Robert C. Martin (Uncle Bob) talks about clean architecture and design, including keeping the database and frameworks out of the center of an application. It is an hour-long conference talk.
videos.w: Recommended as a formative talk on architecture that argues against putting the database at the center of a design.
videos.q: This talk was really formative for me

videos.t: You Give REST a Bad Name
videos.s: Dylan Beattie's parody of 'You Give Love a Bad Name' about hypermedia APIs and REST, performed with his band at developer conferences.
videos.w: Shared as developer humor, with commenters insisting any Dylan Beattie mention must come with this song.
videos.q: You Give REST a Bad Name" is also excellent.

videos.t: SIMCITY 3000 - MAGNASANTI - 6 MILLION - ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM.flv
videos.s: A video tour of Magnasanti, a SimCity city built to hold six million residents, pushed to the absolute maximum and inspired by Kowloon Walled City.
videos.w: Cited as the legendary extreme SimCity build, and recommended as fascinating viewing with the creator's commentary.
videos.q: Don't miss the video

videos.t: 1.1 - Course outline
videos.s: Course outline for Stanford's online GNSS course, introducing how GPS works and the many uses of satellite navigation. The series pairs short lectures with backyard experiments using smartphones.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a thorough, free lecture series for anyone wanting the nitty-gritty of GPS and GNSS.
videos.q: If anyone wants to get into the nitty-gritty details of GPS / GNSS, there's a good series of lectures (course) available from Standford University

videos.t: The Hubble Ultra Deep Field in 3D
videos.s: A short video built around an animation of the roughly 10,000 galaxies in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, placed at their measured redshift distances. It gives a brief history of deep field images and ends with a 3D fly-through.
videos.w: Recommended as a way to grasp the scale of the universe and what the Hubble deep field image means.
videos.q: This [0] IMHO gives more perspective

videos.t: Sonification & The Problem with Making Music from Data
videos.s: Tantacrul examines sonification, the practice of turning data into sound or music, and critiques how scientists and musicians, including NASA and CERN projects, use it well and poorly.
videos.w: Recommended as an incisive look at the real potential and common misuse of data sonification, often brought up in threads on space sonifications.
videos.q: Tantacrul has a typically incisive video [1] about the real potential of sonification as a powerful technique for understanding data

videos.t: Tesla AI Day 2022
videos.s: Tesla's full AI Day 2022 presentation, covering the Tesla Bot hardware and software, Full Self-Driving planning and perception, the occupancy network, data labeling, simulation and Dojo training infrastructure.
videos.w: HN uses it as primary-source evidence on how Tesla's vision-based driving stack and training pipeline work.
videos.q: Learning about their engineering in that regard really changed my perception of the likelihood that they could solve the problem. Give it a watch

videos.t: Pieter Levels: Programming, Viral AI Startups, and Digital Nomad Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #440
videos.s: A roughly 3.7-hour Lex Fridman podcast with Pieter Levels, the solo developer behind over 40 startups. They discuss programming, viral AI products, indie hacking and digital nomad life.
videos.w: Recommended in solo-developer threads for its insights on shipping small projects with simple stacks and AI tools.
videos.q: I highly recommend checking out this podcast

videos.t: Building the Moroccan Court
videos.s: A short film following Moroccan artisans from Fez as they build a traditional 15th-century-style Moroccan court inside the Metropolitan Museum of Art. It shows zellij tilework and other traditional techniques.
