videos.w: Shared as a satisfying look at craftsmen taking pride in traditional handmade tile mosaics.
videos.q: Here’s a great video [0][17min] documenting the Met Museum’s commissioning of moroccan mosaics

videos.t: Joe Rogan Experience #1419 - Daryl Davis
videos.s: Joe Rogan interviews Daryl Davis, a Black blues musician who has befriended Ku Klux Klan members and helped many leave the group. He tells stories of how he talked with them.
videos.w: Offered as a persuasion success story in threads about polarization and online toxicity.
videos.q: His episode on the JRE is really good and his stories keep you engaged.

videos.t: 3-Sweep: Extracting Editable Objects from a Single Photo, SIGGRAPH ASIA 2013
videos.s: A SIGGRAPH Asia 2013 research demo of 3-Sweep, a tool for extracting editable 3D objects from a single photo using a few user strokes. It predates modern AI image tools.
videos.w: HN recalls it as a mind-blowing pre-AI demo of 2D-to-3D object extraction.
videos.q: this single video blew my mind back in *2013* and I find myself thinking about it often.

videos.t: The Scientific Method-Richard Feynman
videos.s: A one-minute clip of Richard Feynman describing the scientific method: guess a law, compute its consequences, and compare with experiment. If it disagrees with experiment, it is wrong.
videos.w: HN quotes it as the crispest statement of what science is, usually when a theory clashes with evidence.
videos.q: That is the scientific method. And it is presented by one of our best ever thinkers.

videos.t: Nathaniel J. Smith - Trio: Async concurrency for mere mortals - PyCon 2018
videos.s: Nathaniel J. Smith's PyCon 2018 talk introducing Trio, a Python concurrency library designed around usability and structured concurrency. He live-codes a problem and analyzes pitfalls in other async libraries.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear introduction to structured concurrency and as an explanation of subtle asyncio bugs that Trio avoids.
videos.q: one of the best explanations I've seen about what subtle bugs are easy to make with asyncio

videos.t: Rhyme: Why Eminem is one of the most impressive lyricists ever
videos.s: A re-upload of a video breaking down Eminem's rhyme schemes, showing multi-syllable and internal rhymes in songs such as Lose Yourself. It aims to show why he is considered a standout lyricist.
videos.w: Recommended in threads on rap vocabulary and rhyme generation as a clear visual explanation of Eminem's rhyming technique.
videos.q: this absolute standout of a YouTube video about the rhyme scheme in Eminem's Lose Yourself.

videos.t: Blade Runner 2049 | "Cells Interlinked" and Pale Fire (LITERALLY ME! INCELS INTERLINKED)
videos.s: A film-analysis video essay linking Blade Runner 2049's Cells Interlinked sequence to Nabokov's Pale Fire. It examines the poetry and meaning behind the film's references.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the best video essay on the film's use of Pale Fire.
videos.q: The best video essay on the movie

videos.t: Self: The Movie;
videos.s: A 1995 Sun Microsystems film about the Self programming language, a prototype-based Smalltalk relative, showing its live, graphical programming environment.
videos.w: HN uses it as the canonical demo of Self's integrated, direct-manipulation environment whenever prototypal inheritance or live programming comes up.
videos.q: This is a good demo of what could be done in the Self environment

videos.t: AlphaFold - The Most Useful Thing AI Has Ever Done
videos.s: A Veritasium video on AlphaFold, DeepMind's protein structure prediction system, and the protein design work it enabled. It features interviews with John Jumper and with David Baker's protein design group and explains why predicting protein folding matters.
videos.w: HN points to it as an accessible explainer of AlphaFold and as an example of narrow, specialized ML delivering real scientific breakthroughs.
videos.q: To learn more about AlphaFold and its importance, I would recommend the Veritasium video[0]

videos.t: Designer's Digest - Steve Jobs on the role of product and marketing people.
videos.s: A three-minute excerpt of a Steve Jobs interview in which he describes how monopolies let sales and marketing people displace product people, rotting a company's product sensibility, with Xerox as the example.
videos.w: Cited constantly on HN whenever a large company declines, as the canonical explanation of product people being pushed out by sales and marketing.
videos.q: Steve Jobs has the best explanation for this.

videos.t: Clojure for Java Programmers Part 1 - Rich Hickey
videos.s: Rich Hickey introduces Clojure to the NYC Java Study Group in the first of a two-part talk. It covers reader syntax, core data structures, code-as-data, evaluation, special operators, functions, macros and sequences, assuming no Lisp background.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear, well-paced introduction to Clojure and Lisp ideas like code as data and macros, straight from the language's creator.
videos.q: It's just a great talk.

videos.t: PAUL TAYLOR - #FRANGLAIS - FULL SHOW
videos.s: Paul Taylor's first stand-up special, recorded in Paris in 2018, in which a British comedian living in France riffs on French culture, language and bureaucracy. It is the full 70-minute show.
videos.w: Recommended as hilarious for anyone familiar with both French and British or American culture, and relevant to expats.
videos.q: I HIGHLY recommend a watch, it's hilarious especially if you're familiar with both French and British/American culture

videos.t: Building Prototypes Dan Gelbart  part 10 of 18  Flexures
videos.s: Part 10 of Dan Gelbart's prototype-building lecture series, covering flexures: flexible joints that give precise, frictionless motion. It shows how a cheap piece of aluminum can become a nanometer-accurate mechanism.
videos.w: HN recommends the series as a fascinating, practical course in precision prototyping, with the flexure episode singled out as especially impressive.
videos.q: He starts off with a $10 piece of aluminum that took maybe an hour or two to make

videos.t: HERO – Blender Grease Pencil Showcase
videos.s: HERO is a short animated film made entirely in Blender to showcase the Grease Pencil 2D animation tools in Blender 2.8. It mixes hand-drawn 2D with a full 3D pipeline.
videos.w: HN points to it as an impressive demo of Blender's open-source 2D/3D hybrid animation and as a comparison for other 2D animation tools.
videos.q: the demo the foundation commissioned was amazing. I love how seamlessly they mix the 3D in with the direct illustration.

videos.t: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb about the interstellar object Oumuamua, aliens and black holes. Loeb lays out his argument that it may be an artifact rather than debris.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a good, non-sensational presentation of Loeb's actual argument, usually linked in Oumuamua threads.
videos.q: There's a good interview with Avi Loeb on the Lex Fridman podcast about this very topic.

videos.t: Brian Springer - Spin
videos.s: Brian Springer's documentary Spin, built entirely from unauthorized satellite feeds of politicians and newscasters before they went on air during the 1992 US presidential election. It exposes the behind-the-scenes construction of media reality.
videos.w: Recommended as a revealing look at how politicians and news anchors behave off camera and how packaged news feeds were produced.
videos.q: You might like Spin , a 1995 documentary composed of unauthorized behind the scenes footage

videos.t: Ocarina of Time TAS by dwangoAC, TASBot, Savestate, Sauraen in 53:05 - Summer Games Done Quick 2022
videos.s: A tool-assisted speedrun of Ocarina of Time at Summer Games Done Quick 2022, using TASBot and arbitrary code execution to reach an alternate ending in about 53 minutes. The run is introduced by its creators and followed by an interview.
videos.w: HN points to it as a stunning demonstration of arbitrary code execution in a console game and of what speedrunners effectively do as vulnerability researchers.
videos.q: absolutely blew me away

videos.t: Unbelievably busy bicycle crossing in Amsterdam
videos.s: Nine minutes of unedited footage of a very busy bicycle and car crossing at Korte Prinsengracht and Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam. Cyclists, pedestrians and cars flow through without traffic lights.
videos.w: Cited in urbanism and self-driving threads as a vivid example of dense mixed traffic working through infrastructure and culture.
videos.q: Watching that video sooths my mind and warms my heart

videos.t: Feynman: Take the world from another point of view (1/4)
videos.s: Part one of a four-part upload of a BBC Horizon documentary featuring Richard Feynman, in which he talks about physics and looking at the world from another point of view.
videos.w: Mentioned as a fun and impressive Feynman documentary, though the mentions are brief.
videos.q: I love this old Horizon as well

videos.t: Crash Bandicoot Co-Creator Andy Gavin: Extended Interview | Ars Technica
videos.s: A two-hour extended interview in which Crash Bandicoot co-creator Andy Gavin tells how he and Jason Rubin built the game at Naughty Dog. It includes the custom Lisp tools used.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a fascinating hacker war story, especially in threads on Naughty Dog's custom Lisp languages GOOL and GOAL.
videos.q: I recently watched and loved this extended interview with him about making Crash Bandicoot

videos.t: Alcoholic Vervet Monkeys! - Weird Nature - BBC animals
videos.s: A BBC Weird Nature clip about vervet monkeys in the Caribbean that drink alcohol, and how they split into heavy drinkers, social drinkers and teetotalers.
videos.w: HN shares it as an amusing parallel to human drinking habits and as a possible window into addiction.
videos.q: might give some insight into addiction.

videos.t: Eric Schmidt and Peter Thiel - Fortune Debate, 2012
videos.s: A 2012 Fortune dinner debate between Peter Thiel and Eric Schmidt over whether technological progress is healthy or stalling and whether Google can still innovate.
videos.w: HN recalls it as one of the most interesting debates between two contrasting worldviews on progress.
videos.q: One of the most interesting debates was between Eric Schmidt and Peter Thiel back in 2012

videos.t: Vocal Fry: what it is, who does it, and why people hate it!
videos.s: Linguist Geoff Lindsey explores vocal fry: what it is, who uses it, how it relates to glottal stops and accents, and why some people dislike it.
videos.w: HN points to it as an expert correction of myths about vocal fry, showing it is a normal speech pattern across groups.
videos.q: it's not just that. It's (also?) a normal speech pattern, used by different genders, ages, and social groups, in many languages.

videos.t: The 8pen
videos.s: A demo of the 8pen, a gesture-based keyboard replacement for touchscreens that lets users enter text by moving around a circle. It is meant for phones, remotes and game controllers and mimics handwriting.
videos.w: HN commenters who used it remember it as an unusually fast and accurate touchscreen text input method and a fascinating alternative to QWERTY.
videos.q: It was absolutely, hands down without question, the most accurate way to quickly enter text into a phone using only a screen.

videos.t: Why Figure 8 knot is NOT hard to untie!
videos.s: Hard Is Easy runs experiments to show that a correctly tied figure 8 knot is not hard to untie after loading. He shows how two knots that look similar can behave differently depending on how they are dressed.
videos.w: Cited in climbing knot threads to counter the claim that figure 8s jam, by showing the correct tying method.
videos.q: Apparently there is a wrong way of tying a figure 8, that leads to a version that is much harder to untie.

videos.t: DEF CON 18 - Jason Scott - You're Stealing It Wrong! 30 Years of Inter-Pirate Battles
videos.s: Jason Scott's DEF CON 18 talk tells the history of software piracy over thirty years, centered on the feuds and drama among rival warez groups. It is full of archival material and insider lingo.
videos.w: HN brings it up in threads on warez, cracktros and the demoscene as a funny, informative history of the piracy scene.
videos.q: Related, and a personal favorite of mine

videos.t: How the US Is Destroying Young People’s Future | Scott Galloway | TED
videos.s: Scott Galloway's TED talk uses data to argue that young Americans are financially worse off than earlier generations, calling it a great intergenerational theft. He covers root causes and what could change it.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it for hard data on millennials versus boomers and the economic reality facing young workers.
videos.q: covers a lot of the current reality young people face entering the workforce.

videos.t: The Default Mode Network & End of Suffering - Gary Weber
videos.s: A dialogue with Gary Weber on the default mode network, meditation and non-dual awakening, with discussion of psychedelics, thought and time. It is part of the Non-Dual Couch series.
videos.w: Cited to explain the default mode network and how meditation may quiet it.
videos.q: I highly recommend this talk given by a physicist exploring what spirituality does to the brain

videos.t: Fermi Paradox: The Dyson Dilemma v2.0
videos.s: Isaac Arthur examines the Dyson Dilemma, the puzzle of why we see no Dyson spheres or megastructures if growth-oriented civilizations should build them. He covers detectability and whether such structures could hide.
videos.w: Recommended in Fermi paradox threads as a thorough and reasoned treatment of Dyson sphere detectability.
videos.q: He describes the Fermi Paradox and related concepts 100x better than anyone else.

videos.t: "Uncle" Bob Martin
videos.s: Robert 'Uncle Bob' Martin speaks at Yale School of Management about clean, well-written code and what makes good software development. The talk covers his views on OOP, architecture and professional practice.
videos.w: HN cites it as a formative talk on what OOP really is, and on why teams write code that slows them down.
videos.q: This talk was really formative for me

videos.t: Tom Lehrer Full Copenhagen Performance
videos.s: A full-length recording of Tom Lehrer's 1967 concert in Copenhagen, mixing his satirical songs with spoken comedy between numbers. It runs about 51 minutes with good audio for its age.
videos.w: Posted whenever Lehrer comes up, as the best way to see him perform, and treated as a complete stand-up-style set.
videos.q: He intersperses song and spoken comedy, with the whole performance hanging together masterfully.

videos.t: The Strangest Implication of Quantum Mechanics
videos.s: A Veritasium video that follows the principle of least action from Bernoulli and Newton to quantum mechanics, asking whether light takes all possible paths at once. It includes experiments showing quantum waves.
videos.w: HN commenters call it eye-opening and deeper than typical layman explanations, linking it in double-slit and mechanics threads.
videos.q: this veritasium video is quite eye opening

videos.t: Understanding the Honda CR-V Hybrid E-Drive
videos.s: WeberAuto explains how the Honda E-Drive (i-MMD) hybrid transaxle works in the CR-V, Accord, Insight and Clarity hybrids. It walks through the system's three modes of operation.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of a mind-blowingly simple power-split hybrid design.
videos.q: Some of these designs are mind-blowingly simple. My favorite is Honda's E-drive

videos.t: Into Eternity - Official trailer
videos.s: Official trailer for the documentary Into Eternity, about Finland's Onkalo repository, built to store high-level nuclear waste safely for 100,000 years. It raises how to warn and communicate with far-future humans.
videos.w: Recommended as a thought-provoking film on deep-time nuclear waste storage, though one commenter found it unenlightening.
videos.q: Highly recommended.

videos.t: #Earth 🌏 Will we survive this ?  Amazing⚡️ #crashcourse on #collapse & #environment by #ArthurKeller
videos.s: Arthur Keller gives a roughly half-hour crash course on environmental collapse, covering exponential growth, carrying capacity and ecological overshoot.
videos.w: HN commenters post it in climate threads as a clear explanation of overshoot and declining carrying capacity.
videos.q: you should really spend some 30 mins here

videos.t: Militarizing Your Backyard with Python: Computer Vision and the Squirrel Hordes
videos.s: A PyCon 2012 talk by Kurt Grandis on building an automated water-squirting turret that uses Python and computer vision to detect and drive off squirrels from a bird feeder.
videos.w: HN loves it as a funny, inspiring hobby project and calls it one of the best conference talks ever.
videos.q: Perhaps the best presentation to a programming language conference in history.

videos.t: Alan Kay Demos GRaIL
videos.s: Alan Kay demonstrates GRaIL, a graphical input language system from around 1968 in which hand-drawn strokes become boxes, connections and dataflow-style programs.
videos.w: HN points to it as proof that the 1960s already had modeless, sketch-based interfaces that remain impressive today.
videos.q: Pretty amazing stuff, even today.

videos.t: Justin Bieber 800% Slower
videos.s: A Justin Bieber song slowed down 800% with the PaulStretch program, turning a pop track into a long ambient drone.
videos.w: HN points to it as the canonical example of extreme audio stretching making pop music into something entirely different and relaxing.
videos.q: I'm not even kidding. It's superb.

videos.t: The Ridiculous Engineering Of Jet Engines
videos.s: Veritasium explains how jet engines run hotter than their components' melting points, using cooling air and single-crystal superalloy turbine blades. It covers how the blades are grown as aligned crystals.
videos.w: Commenters send it to people asking how engines survive such temperatures, and call it fascinating and worth watching.
videos.q: is absolutely fascinating & well worth a watch

videos.t: Why Gifted Kids Are Actually Special Needs
videos.s: Dr. K of HealthyGamerGG argues that gifted kids can be seen as special needs, tracing a path from the gifted label to burnout and perfectionism.
videos.w: HN commenters call it enlightening for understanding the emotional challenges of gifted kids, especially those who struggle later in school or college.
videos.q: It is a truly excellent video for helping to understand some of the psychological/emotional challenges of being

videos.t: Louis CK honors George Carlin
videos.s: Louis CK speaks at a 2010 NYPL tribute to George Carlin about how Carlin's habit of discarding material and writing a new hour each year changed his own career. He becomes emotional describing it.
videos.w: HN finds the story inspiring beyond comedy: getting good by throwing out your old work and starting over.
videos.q: His story is not only inspiring, it transcends comedy.

videos.t: Don't Buy Stuff - Saturday Night Live
videos.s: A 2006 Saturday Night Live fake infomercial with Steve Martin and Amy Poehler selling the sure-fire way out of debt: don't buy stuff.
videos.w: HN posts it as a favorite comic summary of debt avoidance and spending discipline, and as a joke in buy-now-pay-later threads.
videos.q: This is my favorite video that explains it all

videos.t: Makepad: Designing modern UIs with Rust - Rik Arends - RustNL 2023
videos.s: Rik Arends presents Makepad, a Rust UI framework, at RustNL 2023. The talk covers designing modern, GPU-fast UIs with Rust and includes live-coded demos of an IDE and a synthesizer.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it for the live-coded demos running at high frame rates, calling the performance impressive.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: Greg Johnston, creator of Leptos, has made a video with performance comparisons

videos.t: Distinguished Lecturer Series: Building Science - Adventures in Building Science
videos.s: A Berkeley Lab Distinguished Lecturer talk on building science, with an expert covering control layers, insulation and vapour barrier placement, and how buildings fail. The delivery is humorous.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as an authoritative, entertaining source on building science, such as insulation placement and why LEED point priorities miss the mark.
videos.q: Presentation on control layer (especially starting around 15m)

videos.t: RustConf 2020 - Closing Keynote by Siân Griffin
videos.s: RustConf 2020 closing keynote by Sian Griffin that dives into Pokemon Blue glitches, notably Missingno and arbitrary-code-execution tricks. It uses them to explain how memory unsafety works and how memory-safe languages like Rust prevent such bugs.
videos.w: HN points to it as a fun, technically deep talk that makes memory-safety bugs vivid through a beloved game.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: I really enjoyed the RustConf 2020 Closing Keynote

videos.t: Nathan Barley - Episode 1
videos.s: The first episode of Nathan Barley, Chris Morris and Charlie Brooker's British sitcom satirizing hip media and startup scenesters in mid-2000s Shoreditch. Cynical writer Dan Ashcroft finds himself idolized by the moronic Nathan Barley.
videos.w: Recommended as a savage, ahead-of-its-time parody of startup and tech culture.
videos.q: I can highly, highly , recommend Nathan Barley which was ahead of its time

videos.t: Why 90% of Managers Are GARBAGE (The Professional Lie) | Steve Jobs
videos.s: A short clip of Steve Jobs arguing that the best people are self-managing and that professional managers who cannot do the work add little. He says leadership is about a shared vision.
videos.w: Cited in threads on management, hiring and company culture for Jobs's views on self-managing people and small, self-policing core teams.
videos.q: My favorite Steve Job's video on the subject

videos.t: HC2023-K2: Hardware for Deep Learning
videos.s: Bill Dally of NVIDIA gives a Hot Chips 2023 keynote on the challenges of building hardware for deep learning. He traces how GPUs have been adapted for machine learning, especially training.
videos.w: HN points to it for an insider view of why NVIDIA's AI gains came from design rather than process, and for data-movement power costs.
videos.q: The whole talk is brilliant and worth watching.

videos.t: PAW Patrol's Dark Secret, Explained
videos.s: A long video essay by Skip Intro asking what vision of policing the kids' show PAW Patrol suggests. It mixes comedy with serious critique and features guest voices.
videos.w: Recommended as a funny but serious critique of the show's portrayal of authority and policing.
videos.q: It’s a superb video essay and absolutely worth the watch!

videos.t: Bringing the Unix Philosophy to Big Data by Bryan Cantrill: FutureStack13
videos.s: Bryan Cantrill presents Manta, an object store with in-situ compute that lets tools like grep, awk, and sed run map-reduce style over huge data. He frames it as bringing the Unix philosophy to big data.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an elegant argument for simple Unix tools replacing heavyweight Hadoop-style pipelines.
videos.q: The Bryan Cantrill talk is definitely worth your time

videos.t: Jacques Pepin omelette omelet
videos.s: Jacques Pepin makes a classic French omelette in a short uncut demonstration. The video contrasts it with the American style.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as a simple method that makes omelettes approachable, while noting that the technique is harder than it looks.
videos.q: Watch this, incredibly simple method that made me actually like omelettes.

videos.t: The Iroquois Confederacy
videos.s: Historia Civilis explains the origins and governing system of the Iroquois (Haudenosaunee) Confederacy. It covers the Great Law and the league's surprisingly intricate legal and political structure.
videos.w: HN recommends it for anyone interested in legal systems, governance, or history.
videos.q: Highly recommend for anyone interested in legal systems or history in general

videos.t: 2017/08/08: James Damore and his Google Memo on Diversity  (complete)
videos.s: Jordan Peterson's roughly 50-minute interview with James Damore, the fired Google engineer, going through his diversity memo nearly line by line. The description links the scientific literature behind the claims.
videos.w: During the 2017 memo controversy, HN commenters pointed to it as Damore's own account and a detailed walk-through of the memo's sources.
videos.q: See Jordan Peterson's interview with James Damore, where he goes through the memo almost line-by-line.

videos.t: 2023 LLVM Dev Mtg - Mojo 🔥: A system programming language for heterogenous computing
videos.s: A 2023 LLVM Developers' Meeting keynote by Abdul Dakkak, Chris Lattner and Jeff Niu introducing Mojo, a Python-family systems language built on MLIR and LLVM for heterogeneous computing.
videos.w: HN points to it as the best deep dive into Mojo's design, including MLIR use and SIMD-first scalars.
videos.q: this video totally changed my view

videos.t: Why I don't use Apple products
videos.s: Louis Rossmann, an independent Apple repair shop owner, explains why he does not use Apple products, drawing on his experience of repairing devices he considers designed to fail and hard to fix.
videos.w: Cited in right-to-repair and Apple threads as an insider's view of Apple hardware design and repairability.
videos.q: I love Louis Rossman's video about why he does not use Apple products.

videos.t: Computer Science - Brian Kernighan on successful language design
videos.s: Brian Kernighan gives a talk at the University of Nottingham on how to succeed in language design without really trying. He draws on his experience with awk and other languages.
videos.w: HN cites it as a practical talk on language design and for background on awk from one of its authors.
videos.q: This is an excellent talk on designing successful programming language by Brian Kernighan

videos.t: Pragmatic Unicode, or, How do I stop the pain?
videos.s: Ned Batchelder's PyCon 2012 talk gives a quick overview of what Unicode is, then focuses on what a Python programmer needs to handle text correctly. It presents the 'Unicode sandwich' strategy: decode bytes at input, work with Unicode internally, encode at output.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as the clearest explanation of Python's bytes versus Unicode model and the Unicode sandwich, which finally makes the confusion click.
videos.q: After A TON OF PAIN I decided to put the time in to watch the talk

videos.t: OpenAI Codex Live Demo
videos.s: OpenAI's 2021 live demo of Codex translating natural language into code, from Hello World to building a game and a Microsoft Word plugin.
videos.w: HN points to it as an early, impressive demonstration that LLMs could write working code.
videos.q: Kind of changed my whole view about programming and it's future.

videos.t: Eduard Artemyev - Siberiade theme (1979)
videos.s: The main theme from Eduard Artemyev's score to the 1979 Soviet film Siberiade, an electronic piece that features the ANS synthesizer.
videos.w: Shared as an example of Artemyev, called the Russian Vangelis, and of great Soviet electronic film music.
videos.q: it hit me back hard how great this music is, even genius-like, I would say.

videos.t: Chris Sacca of Lowercase Capital Pt. 2- TWiST #295
videos.s: Part two of Jason Calacanis's long interview with investor Chris Sacca on This Week in Startups. Sacca discusses his investments in Facebook, Twitter and Uber, and how he hustled his way to the top.
videos.w: HN calls it a favorite startup video because it is packed with candid stories about Facebook, Twitter and Google.
videos.q: My favorite, because it's so full of great stories, is the Chris Sacca interview with Jason Calacanis

videos.t: re:publica 2012 - Eben Moglen - Freedom of Thought Requires Free Media
videos.s: Eben Moglen's re:publica 2012 talk argues that media which spy on and data-mine the public threaten freedom of thought, and that free technology and free culture are needed to protect it.
videos.w: HN users recommend Moglen as a brilliant speaker and a top introduction to free software philosophy, and cite this talk in privacy and crypto-wars discussions.
videos.q: none seems to beat those from Stallman's lawyer, Eben Moglen.

videos.t: The Fermi Paradox — Where Are All The Aliens? (1/2)
videos.s: Kurzgesagt introduces the Fermi paradox: with so many stars and planets, why do we see no sign of aliens? It sets up the question and what it might imply for our own future. It is part 1 of 2.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend the two-part Kurzgesagt pair as an engaging, accessible introduction to the Fermi paradox and the Great Filter.
videos.q: I find the pair of videos by Kurzgesagt on YouTube to be much more appealing for me.

videos.t: Making logic gates from transistors
videos.s: Ben Eater shows how to build logic gates out of transistors, including NOR gates. It is part of his clear hardware-from-scratch teaching style.
videos.w: HN people recommend Ben Eater's videos for easy, clear explanations of digital logic and building computers.
videos.q: All his videos are amazing, and super easy to understand.

videos.t: They're Made Out Of Meat
videos.s: A 2004 short film adaptation of Terry Bisson's story "They're Made Out of Meat", in which aliens discuss the astonishing discovery of meat-based intelligent life. It stars Tom Noonan and Ben Bailey.
videos.w: HN points to it as the best filmed version of the story whenever aliens or the nature of intelligence come up.
videos.q: O'Reagan's short is the best take on it.

videos.t: The People's Republic of The Future
videos.s: Bloomberg's Hello World episode in which Ashlee Vance visits Shenzhen, a hub of electronics manufacturing and cloning. He meets tech-fueled entrepreneurs working under an authoritarian regime.
videos.w: HN recommends it for a view of Shenzhen's hardware ecosystem and as a documentary pick on China's tech scene.
videos.q: ran across this video and it absolutely blew me away.

videos.t: Jordan Peterson - Pareto Distributions
videos.s: A short clip of Jordan Peterson explaining Pareto distributions, using Soviet farm collectivization and the resulting famine as context. It also covers how outcomes concentrate in a few people.
videos.w: HN points to it for an accessible explanation of why wealth and creative output are so unevenly distributed.
videos.q: Jordan Peterson has an excellent lecture on describing this phenomenon.

videos.t: Atlas | Partners in Parkour
videos.s: Boston Dynamics shows its Atlas humanoid robots running a parkour course with jumps, balance beams and vaults, demonstrating whole-body athletic control.
videos.w: HN uses it as the benchmark for state-of-the-art humanoid robot mobility in discussions of Tesla Bot and robotics progress.

videos.t: Pitfall: A Classic Game Postmortem
videos.s: David Crane's 2011 GDC postmortem of Pitfall, the classic Atari 2600 game. He explains how he created the game under the severe hardware limits of the console.
videos.w: Recommended as an entertaining, technical look at squeezing a game into a tiny Atari 2600, told by the original developer.
videos.q: I'm linking at the relevant timestamp, but the whole video is pure Atari 2600 goodness.

videos.t: Mark Blyth - A Brief History of How We Got Here and Why
videos.s: Political economist Mark Blyth gives a lecture tracing two versions of capitalist 'software': the postwar Great Compression era and the neoliberal era from 1980 to 2008. He explains the bug that crashed the first and the design of the second.
videos.w: Recommended as a great primer on how neoliberalism developed and why the postwar order broke down.
videos.q: Mark Blyth gives a great primer called "A brief history of how we got here and why

videos.t: Scale By The Bay 2019: Bryan Cantrill, Was He Wright All Along? Software After Moore's Law
videos.s: Bryan Cantrill's Scale By The Bay 2019 talk on software after Moore's Law. He covers the end of easy scaling and the move toward specialized, emerging architectures.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a history and analysis of the end of scaling from a well-regarded systems speaker, and lists it among the best talks of 2019.
videos.q: Bryan Cantrill has a great talk on this and the end of scaling

videos.t: Why Static Typing Came Back • Richard Feldman • GOTO 2022
videos.s: Richard Feldman's GOTO Copenhagen 2022 talk on why dynamic languages like Python, Ruby, PHP and JavaScript rose in the 1990s and why each now has a popular static type checker. It argues that modern static typing recovers the advantages that made dynamic languages attractive.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as a clear account of the trade-offs between static and dynamic typing and why the industry is swinging back to types.
videos.q: It gives the major reasons why one would prefer one over the other

videos.t: Rick Reed - WhatsApp: Half a billion unsuspecting FreeBSD users
videos.s: Rick Reed of WhatsApp speaks at MeetBSD about running a messaging service on FreeBSD and Erlang at huge scale. He covers the stack, tuning and the challenges of millions of connections per host.
videos.w: Pointed to as a rare look at how a tiny engineering team ran WhatsApp's massive scale on FreeBSD and Erlang.
videos.q: Their technology stack (FreeBSD/Erlang) is pretty interesting, more info here: 2014 talks by Rick Reed

videos.t: illumos day 2014: The Dream is Alive! Running Linux containers on an illumos kernel
videos.s: Bryan Cantrill's illumos Day 2014 talk on running Linux containers on an illumos kernel via LX-branded zones. He covers emulating Linux syscalls on SmartOS and compares Linux and Solaris-derived systems.
videos.w: HN points to it as an entertaining deep dive on Linux emulation on SmartOS and on how the Solaris kernel and libc are tightly coupled.
videos.q: I really enjoyed this talk[1] by Bryan Cantrill

videos.t: How Will You Measure Your Life? Clay Christensen at TEDxBoston
videos.s: Clayton Christensen's TEDx talk applying business theory to personal life. He argues that career success is not the right measure of a life and urges attention to relationships and values.
videos.w: HN commenters share it as an inspiring reflection on what to optimize in life beyond career, especially in threads on burnout and meaning.
videos.q: This is a very inspiring presentation, especially towards the end.

videos.t: EEVblog #555 - 555 Timer Kit
videos.s: Dave Jones builds the Evil Mad Scientist discrete-component 555 timer kit, then tests it and explains the internal circuitry of the 555 at transistor level. He finishes with scope waveforms.
videos.w: Recommended as a deep, hands-on explanation of how a 555 timer works inside.
videos.q: Please watch this clip as Dave dives deep into how a simple 555 chip works at the transistor level

videos.t: The Great Stranding: How Inaccurate Mainstream LCOE Estimates are Creating a Trillion-Dollar Bubble
videos.s: RethinkX summarizes its report arguing that mainstream LCOE estimates are inflating a bubble in coal, gas, nuclear and hydro assets. It claims solar, wind and batteries will strand conventional energy investments.
videos.w: Cited in nuclear-versus-renewables debates to support the argument that cheap renewables undercut new nuclear.
videos.q: Eye-opening video

videos.t: Joe Rogan Experience #1342 - John Carmack
videos.s: A long Joe Rogan podcast conversation with John Carmack covering his career, work habits, open source, AGI, quantum computing and CPUs.
videos.w: Recommended as a wide-ranging Carmack interview, noted for his views on work ethic and AGI.
videos.q: Fantastic listen for anyone honestly.

videos.t: Spider With Three Super Powers | The Hunt | BBC Earth
videos.s: A BBC Earth clip from The Hunt showing Portia jumping spiders, which leap many times their body length and ambush prey larger than themselves.
videos.w: HN recommends it as striking footage of how cleverly jumping spiders plan their attacks.
videos.q: Well worth the watch if it’s new to you! Quite the perspective shifter

videos.t: Erlang: The Movie
videos.s: A short film about the Erlang language, showing telecom systems built from lightweight processes and demonstrating hot code swapping. It is an edited version of the original Ericsson video.
videos.w: HN treats it as a classic that shows what Erlang was built for: robust, concurrent telecom systems with live upgrades.
videos.q: this is truly a gem

videos.t: Microsoft "Courier" secret tablet
videos.s: A short concept video of Microsoft's unreleased Courier, a dual-screen tablet designed as a digital notebook with clippings and annotation. It was first leaked by Gizmodo in 2009.
videos.w: HN treats it as a gold-standard concept demo and a what-might-have-been for dual-screen and digital notebook devices.
videos.q: It has also been my personal gold standard of a superb video demo.

videos.t: SLAPP Suits: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver explains SLAPP suits, lawsuits designed to silence critics through legal costs, after his show's legal fight with coal executive Bob Murray. It covers how such suits work and why state anti-SLAPP laws matter.
videos.w: HN recommends it whenever legal threats against critics or open-source authors come up, often as the best accessible primer on SLAPP suits.
videos.q: In my opinion, it's the best one they've ever done with an absolutely magnificent ending

videos.t: What is Concrete?
videos.s: Practical Engineering gives a short introduction to concrete, covering the difference between concrete and cement, the ingredients, and reinforcement. It includes a hydraulic press demonstration of compressive strength.
videos.w: Commenters link it as an approachable explanation of concrete basics in threads about Roman concrete, construction and sand supply.
videos.q: You're going to love this playlist from Practical Engineering [1].

videos.t: This Invention Made Disney MILLIONS, but Then They LOST It!
videos.s: Corridor Crew tracks down Disney's lost sodium vapor prism process, used for Mary Poppins-era transparency mattes. They explain how a narrow sodium wavelength and a beam splitter enabled better compositing than green screen.
videos.w: Recommended as a fun, informative rediscovery of a lost film-effects technique.
videos.q: is a fantastic watch.

videos.t: GENERAL MAGIC - Official Trailer
videos.c: General Magic and the Soul of Tech
videos.s: The official trailer for the documentary General Magic, about the secretive Apple spinoff that tried to build a handheld communicator in 1990 and whose ideas shaped the smartphone era.
videos.w: HN recommends the documentary itself as a story of an epic early failure in mobile computing, and the trailer is the linked entry point.
videos.q: Highly recommend the documentary on General Magic.

videos.t: Norm Macdonald on Germany
videos.s: Norm Macdonald's 2015 appearance on Letterman's final Late Show, delivering a deadpan bit about Germany and its military history. Jerry Seinfeld reportedly called it Norm's best joke.
videos.w: HN shares it as one of the greatest stand-up bits ever, and pulls it out whenever Germany, war or trade come up.
videos.q: will easily go down as one of the greatest stand-up bits ever written and performed

videos.t: Soyuz Launch Escape Tower System
videos.s: Short footage of the 1983 Soyuz T-10-1 pad fire, in which the launch escape tower pulled the crew away seconds before the rocket exploded.
videos.w: HN cites it as the one dramatic real-world proof that a launch escape system works.
videos.q: here is a neat video of a launch escape system working as intended during Soyuz T-10-1

videos.t: Object-Oriented Programming is Garbage: 3800 SLOC example
videos.s: Brian Will critiques object-oriented programming and rewrites a roughly 3800-line OO program in a procedural style, cutting code and complexity. It is part of a series of OOP critiques.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a concrete, worked example of the case against heavy OOP rather than abstract argument.
videos.q: I recommend the whole series

videos.t: Exposing the Honey Influencer Scam
videos.s: MegaLag investigates PayPal's Honey browser extension, showing how it swaps affiliate attribution and was promoted by large YouTube influencers. It includes technical demonstrations of the affiliate tag replacement in browser dev tools.
videos.w: HN treats it as top-tier investigative journalism on YouTube and the video that triggered lawsuits against Honey.
videos.q: one of the best pieces of investigative journalism I've seen on youtube

videos.t: RimWorld: Contrarian, Ridiculous, and Impossible Game Design Methods
videos.s: RimWorld creator Tynan Sylvester explains at GDC 2017 how Ludeon framed the game as a story generator rather than a game. He covers the design methods that came out of that frame.
videos.w: Recommended as an accessible talk on emergent narrative and on how RimWorld was designed, and cited in threads on simulation games.
videos.q: Strong recommend, if only to understand how RimWorld was designed and built.

videos.t: Elon Musk - CEO of Tesla Motors and SpaceX | Entrepreneurship | Khan Academy
videos.s: Sal Khan interviews Elon Musk in a 2013 Khan Academy entrepreneurship series. Musk discusses PayPal, rocket efficiency and reusability, and how he approaches education and learning.
videos.w: HN cites it as a source for specific Musk anecdotes and as an immensely interesting full conversation.
videos.q: I highly recommend watching the full conversation as it's immensely interesting

videos.t: Steve Jobs Stanford Commencement Speech 2005 high definition.flv
videos.s: Steve Jobs's 2005 Stanford commencement address, in which he tells three stories about connecting the dots, love and loss, and death, including his remarks on typography.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as personal inspiration for perseverance and for keeping perspective by remembering mortality.
videos.q: I suggest you see Steve Jobs' Stanford Commencement Speech (2005)

videos.t: Steve Jobs iPhone 2007 Presentation (HD)
videos.s: The full January 2007 Macworld keynote where Steve Jobs unveils the first iPhone. It covers the touch interface, multitouch gestures, the browser, maps and the pitch as an iPod, phone and internet communicator.
videos.w: HN points to it as a landmark product presentation and as primary-source evidence of what the original iPhone was meant to do and how people reacted.
videos.q: this is one of the best presentations ever

videos.t: The Vegas Loop Is Getting Progressively More Stupid
videos.s: CityNerd critiques the Las Vegas Loop, the Boring Company's tunnel transit system, arguing its design and operation are poor. The video covers how the system actually runs.
videos.w: Used as the go-to critical, first-hand overview of the Vegas Loop in threads about the Boring Company.
videos.q: This video gives a first hand experience that seems to cover everything

videos.t: Extremely Large Numbers 1 - Introduction
videos.s: The first video in a series on extremely large numbers, introducing the topic with examples. Later parts go deep into the fast-growing hierarchy.
videos.w: Recommended in large-number threads as going further than other popular videos on Graham's number and ordinals.
videos.q: I would also recommend Giroux Studios' 'Extremely Large Numbers'[1]

videos.t: Gall--Peters Projection
videos.s: A short clip from The West Wing in which characters argue for the Gall-Peters map projection over Mercator. It dramatizes how standard maps distort the relative size of countries.
videos.w: It is the go-to link in any HN thread on map projections, usually posted as the obligatory West Wing reference.
videos.q: one of the best ways to teach someone about how different our classic maps are from reality

videos.s: A Numberphile video in which physicists Tony Padilla and Ed Copeland show a seemingly astounding result that 1+2+3+4+... equals -1/12. The argument is informal and has drawn criticism for glossing over what the result actually means.
videos.w: HN uses it as the standard reference for the -1/12 meme, with commenters split between enjoying it and calling it a cheat.
videos.q: Watch this entertaining Numberphile video about this topic

videos.t: Browser hacking: Let's make "Cookie Clicker" playable in Ladybird!
videos.s: In a long live-coding session, Andreas Kling works on making the Cookie Clicker game playable in the Ladybird browser from SerenityOS. He tracks down bugs in the browser engine and fixes them.
videos.w: HN loves the Browser hacking series for its clear debugging method of reducing bugs to minimal reproductions, which people say influenced their own testing.
videos.q: At one point, he deletes half the HTML file to isolate where in the site the problematic code is.

videos.t: How Wolves Change Rivers [REMASTERED HD] - George Monbiot
videos.s: A short narrated video describing how reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone triggered a trophic cascade that changed wildlife, vegetation and even river courses. This is a remastered HD version of George Monbiot's viral piece.
videos.w: HN cites it as a compelling example of unforeseen ecosystem effects and rewilding.
videos.q: probably one of the most fascinating videos on YouTube

videos.t: Extreme transformer home in Hong Kong: Gary Chang's 24 rooms in 1
videos.s: Kirsten Dirksen visits architect Gary Chang's 32 square meter Hong Kong apartment, which he has redesigned over decades. Sliding walls and transformable furniture turn it into 24 different room configurations.
videos.w: Held up as the ultimate example of small-space design and a beautiful compact home.
videos.q: I can't recommend Kirsten Dirksen's channel enough to people interested in architecture, energy efficiency, tiny homes

videos.t: David Deutsch on Physics Without Probability
videos.s: A 2015 talk by David Deutsch with slides and audio about constructor theory and how physics, in particular the many-worlds interpretation, can be framed without probability.
videos.w: Cited in threads on probability and quantum theory as a strong argument that probabilities can be eliminated from physics.
videos.q: Worth a watch especially if you balk at this idea just to to see a strong counter argument.

videos.t: Iowa Swine Day 2022: Agriculture at the End of the World
videos.s: Peter Zeihan speaks at Iowa Swine Day 2022 on geopolitics, the end of globalization and agriculture. He argues that supply chains, energy and farm inputs are all about to be disrupted.
videos.w: Recommended for its bleak take on globalization, energy and food supply, though some commenters question how objective it is.
videos.q: The audio is a little rough, but it's worth the watch (in my opinion).

videos.t: Feynman: Magnets  FUN TO IMAGINE  4  But see NEW UPDATED file at https://tinyurl.com/ycphc432
videos.s: A clip from the BBC Fun to Imagine series in which Richard Feynman is asked how magnets work and explains why 'why' questions depend on a shared framework of understanding and cannot always be answered in layman's terms.
videos.w: Cited constantly when discussing explaining to non-experts, the limits of explanation and what a 'why' question really asks.
videos.q: mhartl has already posted this excellent video

videos.t: The Brexit effect: how leaving the EU hit the UK | FT Film
videos.s: A Financial Times film examining how Brexit hurt the UK economy, with FT writers and business people. It looks at trade effects, political silence about the costs, and the absence of a convincing Brexit dividend.
videos.w: Pointed to as an in-depth, journalistic account of Brexit's economic aftermath.
videos.q: watch this excellent documentary from the Financial Times (FT)

videos.t: Oral History of Donald Knuth Part 1
videos.s: A roughly three-hour Computer History Museum oral history interview of Donald Knuth by Edward Feigenbaum, recorded in 2007. Knuth covers his family, music, early programming, his thesis, The Art of Computer Programming, and the detour into TeX and METAFONT.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a superb, personal long-form look at Knuth's life and work habits.
videos.q: It's a _really_ long interview, +7 hours. But it's also superb.

videos.t: Everything is a Remix Part 3 (Original Series, 2011)
videos.s: Part 3 of Kirby Ferguson's Everything is a Remix series, using Apple and the iPhone to show how invention builds on copying and combining prior ideas. It argues that creativity and innovation are inseparable from copying.
videos.w: Cited in copyright and patent debates to argue that creative works and inventions evolve by building on earlier ones.
videos.q: Then watch this rather insightful video titled 'Everything is a Remix'

videos.t: Joscha: Computational Meta-Psychology
videos.s: Joscha Bach's 32C3 talk applies computational theories of mind to questions of meaning, emotion, and love, asking how computation can explain irrational-seeming human experience.
videos.w: Recommended as one of the best bridges between mind and computation, and as a sample of Bach's thinking on AI and philosophy.
videos.q: Recommend watching this video on Computational Meta-Psychology

videos.t: Why Are Emulators Legal? Dolphin vs. Nintendo, and the Fate of Emulation [Great Emu War Pt. 1]
videos.s: Moon Channel, run by a lawyer, explains the legal basis for emulation, including the history of emulation case law and Nintendo's takedown of Dolphin's Steam release. It argues the legality of emulators is more fragile than most people assume.
videos.w: HN points to it as a clear, lawyer-made summary during Nintendo emulator disputes like Yuzu.
videos.q: I really recommend folks watch this, from a lawyer

videos.t: The Origins of Linux—Linus Torvalds
videos.s: Linus Torvalds tells the story of Linux in a 2001 talk at the Computer History Museum, from writing code as a graduate student in Helsinki in the early 1990s to becoming an icon of open source. It covers the project's origins, its growth, and his views on licensing and kernel design.
videos.w: HN points to it as the long first-person account of Linux history, including Linus on the GPL's role and on microkernels.
videos.q: There's a great (long) video about Linus and Linux history from 2001. Watch the whole thing if you can

videos.t: Susan Kare explains Macintosh UI ergonomics on the Computer Chronicles (1984)
videos.s: A 1984 Computer Chronicles segment in which Susan Kare explains the ergonomics and interface design of the original Macintosh. She introduces the interface step by step for newcomers.
videos.w: Praised as a lesson in explaining technology to non-technical people and as a window into early Mac design.
videos.q: I think some of us (me included) would do well to keep this video in mind when explaining technology to non-technical people.

videos.t: CppCon 2014: Jeff Preshing "How Ubisoft Develops Games for Multicore - Before and After C++11"
videos.s: CppCon 2014 talk by Jeff Preshing on how Ubisoft Montreal developed games for multicore hardware, before and after C++11 concurrency support. It goes into atomics and lock-free programming in practice.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear, practical introduction to atomics and lock-free programming in C++.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: Jeff Preshing gave a really good introduction to atomics at CppCon 2014.[1]

videos.t: George Carlin - Germs, Immune System
videos.s: A clip from George Carlin's "You Are All Diseased" special in which he riffs on germs, the immune system and white blood cells. It argues that modern obsession with cleanliness is misplaced.
videos.w: HN brings it up as comic relief and as a funny take when immunity, dirt and germs come up.
videos.q: You've reminded me of this George Carlin rant

videos.t: 1993 interview re: Paul Rand and Steve Jobs
videos.s: A 1993 interview in which Steve Jobs talks about designer Paul Rand, who created the NeXT logo. He recounts Rand's insistence on presenting a single design and his uncompromising professionalism.
videos.w: HN commenters share it for Jobs's account of Rand's single-option approach and as a lesson in trusting designers.
videos.q: I really enjoyed his uncompromising attitude

videos.t: Stadiums: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on cities spending public money on privately owned sports stadiums, including how tax-exempt municipal bonds subsidize them.
videos.w: Pointed to in debates over stadium subsidies as a persuasive case that cities should not pay for stadiums.
videos.q: After watching it, it's pretty clear that cities should not pay for stadiums.

videos.t: Sir Roger Penrose & Dr. Stuart Hameroff: CONSCIOUSNESS AND THE PHYSICS OF THE BRAIN
videos.s: A 2020 UC San Diego event with Roger Penrose and Stuart Hameroff presenting their Orch OR theory that consciousness arises from quantum processes in brain microtubules, followed by a conversation with Roger Bingham.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a presentation of the Penrose-Hameroff theory of consciousness, which some find compelling.
videos.q: for the first time I think a truly compelling idea of what consciousness is in a scientific way that could potentially be empirically measured.

videos.t: A Conversation with Bertrand Russell (1952)
videos.s: A 1952 filmed interview in which Romney Wheeler talks with philosopher Bertrand Russell at his home in Surrey. Russell discusses his outlook and reflects on how the world changed over the first half of the century.
videos.w: HN users share it as a chance to hear Russell speak himself and get a sense of his values and outlook.
videos.q: This is a wonderful interview with him that gives a great sense of what he was all about

videos.t: The Alt-Right Playbook: The Card Says Moops
videos.s: An Innuendo Studios video essay from the Alt-Right Playbook series that uses the Seinfeld 'the card says moops' scene to explain bad-faith argument tactics. It describes how reactionaries use sincerity and irony as shields in online debate.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend the series for understanding bad-faith 'just kidding' dynamics and trolling online.
videos.q: I can only recommend watching Innuendo Studios' _Alt-Right Playbook_ series for a deeper understanding of the dynamics

videos.t: George RR Martin asks Stephen King: "How do you write so Fast?!"
videos.s: A short clip of George R.R. Martin asking Stephen King on stage how he writes so fast. King describes setting daily page goals, around six pages a day, and keeping focused hours.
videos.w: Shared in productivity and writing threads for King's simple daily-quota approach to producing a lot of work.
videos.q: One of my favorite videos is when George RR Martin asks Stephen King on stage

videos.t: Episode 1: Introduction - The Mechanical Universe
videos.s: The first episode of Caltech's The Mechanical Universe, a 52-part introductory university physics series. David Goodstein introduces ideas from Copernicus to Newton, linking the physics of the heavens and the earth with computer animation.
videos.w: HN rates the series as one of the best physics lecture courses on YouTube, with an engaging format and historical context.
videos.q: Hands down best: David Goodstein, CalTech,

videos.t: Rowan Atkinson on free speech
videos.s: Rowan Atkinson speaks against the word 'insulting' in the UK Public Order Act, as part of the Reform Section 5 campaign. He argues for robust free speech and against the slippery slope of criminalizing offense.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as an eloquent defense of free speech with concrete examples of the slippery slope.
videos.q: Rowan Atkinson explained it more eloquently that I ever could

videos.t: The Charming Genius of the Apollo Guidance Computer - Brian Troutwine
videos.s: Brian Troutwine's Code Mesh 2015 talk on the Apollo Guidance Computer. It covers the AGC's design, core rope memory, its interrupt and software behavior, and the pioneering engineering effort behind it.
videos.w: Recommended as a wonderful overview of the AGC architecture, though one commenter found it uninspiring.
videos.q: The Charming Genius of the Apollo Guidance Computer" is a wonderful talk

videos.t: Strange answers to the psychopath test | Jon Ronson | TED
videos.s: Jon Ronson, author of The Psychopath Test, gives a TED talk on the blurry line between sane and crazy and on psychopathy as a spectrum, with stories of how the label gets applied.
videos.w: Praised as one of the great non-technical talks, appearing in best-talk lists.
videos.q: In my opinion it is one of the greatest talks of all time and it gave me goosebumps.

videos.t: Death to Pennies
videos.s: CGP Grey's short animated argument for abolishing the US penny, covering its cost and history.
videos.w: Pointed to as the canonical concise case against pennies whenever coin abolition comes up.
videos.q: CGP Grey has an excellent youtube video on the whole issue for the US.

videos.t: How We Diagnosed and Fixed the 2023 Voyager 1 Anomaly from 15 Billion Miles Away
videos.s: JPL's David Cummings presents at the 2025 Flight Software Workshop how the team diagnosed and fixed the 2023 Voyager 1 anomaly from billions of miles away. It walks through the flight computer and the memory fix.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for the remarkable remote reverse engineering done on decades-old hardware with no simulator.
videos.q: Blows my mind of the reverse engineering done to achieve this

videos.t: Diatoms: Tiny Factories You Can See From Space
videos.s: An episode of Journey to the Microcosmos, hosted by Hank Green, about diatoms, single-celled algae with glass shells. It covers their role in producing a large share of Earth's oxygen and their uses in beer filtering, paint and kitty litter.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend the series as an excellent, accessible introduction to microscopic life, using this episode as the diatom primer.
videos.q: I recently learned about them from an excellent Journey to the Microcosmos video

videos.t: Yacht Rock 1 HD
videos.s: The first episode of the Yacht Rock web series, a comedic parody about the smooth soft-rock musicians of the late 1970s and early 80s. It is a short, scripted sketch set at Koko's Boat House.
videos.w: HN commenters point the uninitiated to it as a beloved parody series, often in threads that mention yacht rock.
videos.q: Also don't miss this wonderful parody series

videos.t: BUSTED: The Citizen's Guide to Surviving Police Encounters
videos.s: A 45-minute Flex Your Rights documentary on how to deal with police in three situations: traffic stops, encounters at home, and on the street. It presents practical advice on asserting constitutional rights and refusing searches.
videos.w: Recommended as a practical guide to knowing your rights during police encounters, alongside the well-known advice to not talk to the cops.
videos.q: Excellent 45 minute ACLU documentary on how to interact with police in three situations: traffic stop, in your house, and on foot.

videos.t: Quick-sort with Hungarian (Küküllőmenti legényes) folk dance
videos.s: Hungarian folk dancers from Sapientia University act out the quicksort algorithm step by step, with music. It is part of the AlgoRythmics series of sorting algorithms performed as dance.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a memorable and fun way to visualize how sorting algorithms work.
videos.q: my very favorite visualizations of sorting algorithms are the Hungarian dancers

videos.t: How Google's Self-Driving Car Works
videos.s: Part 2 of the IROS 2011 keynote by Sebastian Thrun and Chris Urmson on Google's self-driving car. It shows how the car perceives its surroundings with a lidar point cloud and recognizes traffic lights and pedestrians. The audio is poor because it was recorded on a pocket camcorder.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a technical talk aimed at a real engineering audience, with live demos of perception and pre-mapped roads.
videos.q: The whole talk is awesome and a presentation for an actual technical audience, too.

videos.t: Decaf Explained
videos.s: James Hoffmann explains how decaf coffee is made, how the decaffeination processes differ, and why decaf is roasted and stales differently. He also discusses decaf quality and health questions.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a well-researched overview of decaf processes and quality, and cite it for the claim that decaf stales faster.
videos.q: his video about decaf sold me on the idea

videos.t: Dan Britt - Orbits and Ice Ages: The History of Climate
videos.s: Dan Britt lectures on the history of climate, covering orbital cycles, ice ages and conditions millions of years ago. It frames current climate debate with deep-time context.
videos.w: Strongly recommended as a clear explanation of 50-60 million years of climate history that clears up confusion.
videos.q: For anyone interested in finding out more about the last 50-60 million years of climate history I would strongly recommend this talk

videos.t: Earth-cooled, shipping container underground CA home for 30K
videos.s: Kirsten Dirksen profiles Steve Rees, who buried two shipping containers to build an earth-cooled, off-grid 640 sq ft home in Northern California for about $30,000, solar included.
videos.w: Recommended as an example of earth-sheltered housing and as part of a channel HN loves for architecture and efficiency.
videos.q: I can't recommend Kirsten Dirksen's channel enough to people interested in architecture, energy efficiency, tiny homes

videos.t: Build an electroluminescent glass panel display -- an Apollo DSKY
videos.s: Applied Science builds a replica Apollo DSKY using an electroluminescent driver circuit and screen-printed conductive ink, with source and PCB files published.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as a fantastic maker project among Apollo anniversary builds.
videos.q: This video of building a custom Apollo electroluminescent glass panel DSKY display is also fantastic!

videos.t: The Man Who Took LSD and Changed The World
videos.s: Veritasium tells the story of Kary Mullis, the surfer and LSD user who invented PCR and won a Nobel Prize. It explains how PCR works and how it was developed at Cetus.
videos.w: Recommended as one of the most accessible introductions to PCR and its history.
videos.q: It's one of the most accessible videos on PCR I've ever come across

videos.t: Glenn Vanderburg of LivingSocial on why software development is an engineering discipline
videos.s: Glenn Vanderburg argues at the O'Reilly Software Architecture Conference that software development is an engineering discipline, even if immature. He contends the discredited body of knowledge called software engineering has led people to wrongly reject the label.
videos.w: Recommended in debates over whether software is real engineering, as a well-argued case that building is cheap relative to simulating.
videos.q: Required viewing

videos.t: Stanford Professor Andrei Linde celebrates physics breakthrough
videos.s: A short Stanford video in which Chao-Lin Kuo surprises Professor Andrei Linde with BICEP2 evidence supporting cosmic inflation, the first apparent images of primordial gravitational waves.
videos.w: Shared for its moving moment of scientific discovery, and later cited as a cautionary example after the BICEP2 result was retracted.
videos.q: They made a nice video of the researcher surprising Prof Linde with the news

videos.t: COLLAPSE of Personal Computing | Investigation Into the Destruction of Ownership
videos.s: A roughly 3.5-hour Gamers Nexus investigation into rising PC component prices, driven largely by AI data-center demand for memory and other hardware. It draws on interviews with industry figures to argue that personal computing and ownership are being eroded.
videos.w: Recommended as a documentary on the hardware shortage told from the perspective of consumer-facing companies, and cited in threads on RAM prices and ownership.
videos.q: GN did a documentary on the situation from the perspective of consumer-facing companies.

videos.t: violin plots should not exist
videos.s: Physicist Angela Collier rants for 42 minutes about why violin plots are a poor way to show data, citing papers on violin and bean plots. It is part lecture on how to read distributions and part opinionated critique.
videos.w: HN links it in data-visualization threads as an entertaining case against violin plots.
videos.q: Here is a great rant (borderline lecture) from Angela Collier on why they aren’t [0]

videos.t: Sophie Wilson - The Future of Microprocessors
videos.s: Sophie Wilson, designer of the ARM instruction set, discusses the future of microprocessors, including the economics of scaling below 28nm and why much of a chip must stay powered off.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it for the claim that process scaling beyond 28nm is uneconomic and for dark silicon.
videos.q: Highly recommend watching this video

videos.t: The Future Of Reasoning
videos.s: Vsauce explores how human reasoning works, drawing on the social theory of reason and the extended mind thesis, made in partnership with Bill Gates around climate change.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it for the social theory that reasoning evolved as a collaborative activity, and one lists it as a favorite video.
videos.q: is a fascinating pre-AI-era breakdown of how human reasoning works

videos.t: Marco Baringer's SLIME Tutorial Video
videos.s: Marco Baringer's tutorial video on SLIME, the Emacs mode for developing Common Lisp. It demonstrates the interactive workflow of working against a live Lisp image.
videos.w: HN points to it to show what the Lisp REPL workflow is like and as a good tour of SLIME.
videos.q: This is what the lisp repl is like. There's not much else like it

videos.t: Daniel Schmachtenberger on The Portal (with host Eric Weinstein), Ep. #027 - On Avoiding Apocalypses
videos.s: A long conversation between Eric Weinstein and Daniel Schmachtenberger on whether humanity can flourish long term on a single planet, introducing the Game A versus Game B framing. It covers catastrophic risk and alternatives to rivalrous systems.
videos.w: Commenters recommend the whole interview as a wide-ranging discussion of existential risk.
videos.q: I'd highly recommend watching the whole interview

videos.t: David Foster Wallace reads "Consider the Lobster" (on the 2003 Maine Lobster Festival)
videos.s: A reading of David Foster Wallace's essay Consider the Lobster, about the 2003 Maine Lobster Festival and the ethics of boiling lobsters alive. The reading runs about 50 minutes.
videos.w: Linked in threads about lobster welfare as an easy way to take in Wallace's essay.
videos.q: here's a video of DFW reading it out

videos.t: Tomb Raider on the Nintendo Game Boy Advance is incredible | MVG
videos.s: Modern Vintage Gamer looks at OpenLara, an open source Tomb Raider engine, running on the Game Boy Advance. The video explains how the port achieves playable speeds on the GBA's slow ARM CPU, with input from the developer XProger.
videos.w: HN points to it as coverage of an impressive 3D game port on very limited hardware.
videos.q: I found some fascinating coverage of the OpenLara project, specifically for the port of Tomb Raider to the GBA.

videos.t: Moon Landings Faked? Filmmaker Says Not!
videos.s: A filmmaker explains why the Apollo moon landing footage could not have been faked in a studio, based on the video and film technology of the late 1960s. He walks through the limits of cameras, frame rates and effects of the era.
videos.w: HN points to it as a concise, technically grounded rebuttal to moon-hoax claims.
videos.q: This video goes through why the video technology at the time simply wasn't even good enough to enable faking the moon landing.

videos.t: Teletype Model 19 - Part 1: A Teletype Arrives for Restoration
videos.s: CuriousMarc inspects a newly arrived Teletype Model 19, an early military unit built around a Model 15 keyboard and printer, after an initial rough cleaning. It is the first part of a restoration series and touches on 5-bit Baudot code.
videos.w: HN commenters point to this restoration series as a thorough explanation of how teletypes work at every level.
videos.q: Well worth the watch.

videos.t: Sloane's Gap - Numberphile
videos.s: A Numberphile video with Dr James Grime on Sloane's Gap, the observation that integers in the OEIS are not evenly represented and some numbers are underrepresented. It explains the clusters of 'interesting' numbers.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a concise, quick explanation of the OEIS pattern when threads touch the integer sequence encyclopedia.
videos.q: Very good video on Sloane's Gap, for the impatient

videos.t: He started a computing REVOLUTION—then the shortage hit
videos.s: Jeff Geerling interviews Raspberry Pi co-founder Eben Upton about the Pi shortage, the RP2040, RISC-V, the Sony investment and the origin of the name.
videos.w: HN recommends it to explain why Pi supply favored business customers during the shortage, straight from a founder.
videos.q: This interview with one of the founders from Jeff Geerling was quite insightful, definitely check it out if you haven't already!

videos.t: Stanford Seminar - Unethical Algorithms of Massive Scale
videos.s: Psychologist Robert Epstein presents a Stanford EE380 colloquium on how internet algorithms such as search rankings can manipulate opinions, purchases and votes at massive scale. He also describes a new monitoring system for tracking such influence.
videos.w: Cited in threads about search bias, election influence and big-tech data practices as the most comprehensive video of Epstein's research.
videos.q: It's worth watching even if it's 1 hour and 23 minutes.

videos.t: Douglas Crockford: The JSON Saga
videos.s: Douglas Crockford tells how JSON was discovered rather than invented, and how its simplicity made it a dominant data interchange format. He also covers surrounding history such as earlier Netscape usage and the 'Good, not Evil' license story.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as Crockford's first-hand account of JSON's origins and of the no-evil license anecdote.
videos.q: JSON by being so simple actually became really easy to use.

videos.t: Guido van Rossum: Python and the Future of Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #341
videos.s: A roughly three-hour Lex Fridman podcast conversation with Guido van Rossum, the creator of Python. Topics include Python's design, the GIL, asyncio, the future of programming and AI coding tools.
videos.w: HN points to it for Guido's own views on the GIL, Python internals and using Copilot, especially in Python-related threads.
videos.q: I recommend this interview to get a slightly better glimpse of the guy

videos.t: Pete Hunt - The Secrets of React's Virtual DOM (FutureJS 2014)
videos.s: Pete Hunt explains why React's virtual DOM was built, how it compares with databinding-style systems, and what it means for future browser technology. Recorded at FutureJS 2014 in Barcelona.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as the clearest explanation of why re-rendering beats tracking data changes, and say it sold them on React.
videos.q: Pete Hunt did a great talk on what actually makes React / virtualdom different from other databinding approaches.

videos.t: Smarter than a Smart TV! (Raspberry Pi Inside)
videos.s: Jeff Geerling looks at a Sharp NEC commercial display with a slot for a Raspberry Pi Compute Module. It is a large screen without built-in smart TV features or tracking.
videos.w: Brought up in smart TV complaint threads as a real-world 'dumb display' alternative.
videos.q: Jeff Geerling talks about how great a TV his non-TV is.

videos.t: The Most Unwanted Song (FULL VERSION)
videos.s: The 1997 novelty song by Komar and Melamid with composer Dave Soldier, built from survey results on what listeners dislike most in music. It features bagpipes, an opera singer rapping, and a children's choir urging shopping at Wal-Mart.
videos.w: Cited in threads about taste and terrible music as a famously engineered 'worst song', mostly for its curiosity value.
videos.q: They surveyed people to find the things they liked least in music and put it all together.

videos.t: Excel 97 Easter Egg - Flight Simulation
videos.s: A short screen recording of the flight simulator Easter egg hidden in Excel 97, with the steps to trigger it. The uploader notes the mouse controls are hard to handle.
videos.w: HN commenters link it as a fond example of elaborate hidden Easter eggs in old Microsoft Office.
videos.q: Check out

videos.t: Using JSLint For Evil
videos.s: A three-minute clip in which Douglas Crockford explains why he allowed the JSLint reference implementation to be used for evil. It recounts the license clause and how corporate lawyers reacted.
videos.w: Linked in licensing threads as a short, funny story about the 'no evil' clause and IBM's request for an exception.
videos.q: This reminds me of Douglas Crockford's classic story about the JSLint license

videos.t: Video from Jeff Bezos about Amazon and Zappos
videos.s: A short 2009 video of Jeff Bezos talking about Amazon and Zappos. He discusses customer focus, invention and long-term thinking.
videos.w: HN commenters like his candid, authentic delivery and the lessons on customer obsession and thinking long term.
videos.q: I always remember Jeff Bezos' 3 lessons: obsess over customers, invent, think long term.

videos.t: Dmitry Vyukov — Go scheduler: Implementing language with lightweight concurrency
videos.s: Go runtime contributor Dmitry Vyukov looks inside the Go scheduler, explaining how goroutines and channels are implemented. He covers the main scheduler components and overall operation, then goes into details such as preemption and stacks.
videos.w: Recommended as a good watch on how Go's M:N:P scheduler works and why it was designed that way compared with alternative schemes.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: This one notably also explains the design considerations for golangs M:N:P in comparison to other schemes

videos.t: Let's teach for mastery -- not test scores | Sal Khan
videos.s: Sal Khan of Khan Academy argues that schools push students forward with gaps in their foundations, and that students should instead master concepts at their own pace. He compares it to building a house on an unfinished foundation.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it when discussing how gaps in basic knowledge pile up and how mastery learning could fix that.
videos.q: Here is a TED talk where Sal Khan of Khan Academy talks about this

videos.t: A simple trick to design your own solutions for Rubik's cubes
videos.s: Mathologer shows a simple idea, the commutator, that lets anyone who can solve the first layer design their own full Rubik's cube solution. The same idea carries over to other symmetric twisty puzzles such as the Megaminx.
videos.w: Recommended as an accessible explanation of how Rubik's cube solving relates to group theory.
videos.q: This 15 minute video is a pretty accessible explanation of a technique for solving Rubik's-type puzzles

videos.t: Generative AI is a Parasitic Cancer
videos.s: Freya Holmer delivers a long critique of generative AI, arguing it degrades the internet by flooding it with machine-generated junk. The video grew out of her frustration finding reliable information about a technical file format.
videos.w: HN people link it when discussing AI-generated spam clogging search results and the broader harm of generative AI to the web.
videos.q: She talks at length about how pages of AI-generated nonsense text are cluttering search results on Google and all other search engines.

videos.t: URBEX | Abandoned Soviet Space Shuttles (Buran) in Baikonur
videos.s: Urban explorers break into the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan to film the abandoned Soviet Buran space shuttles. The video shows the decaying orbiters and the dangerous trip to reach them.
videos.w: Linked in space and Soviet-history threads as striking footage of the rotting Buran shuttles.
videos.q: There's video on youtube of people sneaking in (it's a guarded base), flying drones around them and climbing around in and out of them. It's pretty cool.

videos.t: Identity After Authenticity: Abigail Thorn's Profile
videos.s: A philosophy lecture by Professor Moeller on the philosophy of identity. It builds on a discussion of Abigail Thorn's video and covers authenticity, sincerity and how online profiles reshape identity.
videos.w: Cited in threads on social media and online identity as a framework of sincerity, authenticity and profilicity.
videos.q: it is interesting to see some meta perspective on identity creation

videos.t: Stephen Wolfram: Fundamental Theory of Physics, Life, and the Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #124
videos.s: A roughly four-and-a-half-hour Lex Fridman podcast conversation with Stephen Wolfram about his Wolfram Physics Project and a fundamental theory of physics, computation, life and the universe.
videos.w: HN points to it as a detailed explanation of Wolfram's physics hypothesis, and for Wolfram's evident passion, though some find it long.
videos.q: He has three long interviews on Lex Fridmans youtube channel! I greatly enjoyed watching those those.

videos.t: Assholes are Ruining Your Project. Donnie Berkholz (RedMonk).
videos.s: Donnie Berkholz of RedMonk gives a Monki Gras talk arguing that abusive, toxic contributors damage open source projects. He makes the case for removing them from communities.
videos.w: Cited as the go-to evidence that rudeness drives contributors away and that toxic people must be removed from projects.
videos.q: Assholes will ruin your project[1], you need to get rid of them

videos.t: This is the WORST Monitor Ever...ON PURPOSE! - Dasung PaperlikeU E-Ink Monitor
videos.s: Linus Tech Tips reviews the Dasung Paperlike E-Ink monitor, asking whether an e-paper display makes sense as a computer monitor. The video covers its slow refresh rate, eye-comfort claims and day-to-day usability.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as a realistic demonstration of E-Ink monitor refresh rates and how such displays feel in use.
videos.q: I do think the videos do a a good job of showing how the monitors feel.

videos.t: Humans can't read URLs. How can we fix it? - HTTP 203
videos.s: Jake Archibald argues that URLs are nearly impossible for humans to interpret, especially for security. He walks through what browsers do about it, including highlighting the registrable domain, and floats a possible better design.
videos.w: Referenced in debates over Chrome hiding URLs as a compelling case for why full URLs are hard even for experts.
videos.q: I think they make a compelling argument for hiding most of the url in part to prevent phishing

videos.t: R. P. Feynman on the difference between knowing the name of something and knowing something.
videos.s: A two-minute clip of Richard Feynman on the difference between knowing the name of something and actually knowing it. He uses the example of knowing a bird's name in every language and still knowing nothing about the bird.
videos.w: It is the standard reference whenever a thread turns to rote labels versus real understanding.
videos.q: Feynman also knows the difference "between knowing the name of something and knowing something"

videos.t: How Budget Airlines Work
videos.s: A Wendover Productions explainer on how budget airlines can sell tickets for under 10 euros. It covers the costs airlines face and how low-cost carriers structure their business.
videos.w: HN points to it as a short, clear answer to why budget airlines are so cheap.
videos.q: Wendover has a short 8 minute video
