videos.t: TEDxCopenhagen - Mikael Colville-Andersen - Why We Shouldn't Bike with a Helmet
videos.s: Copenhagen's bicycle ambassador Mikael Colville-Andersen argues in a TEDx talk that bicycle helmets threaten bicycle culture. He says they distract from road design and make cycling look dangerous.
videos.w: Pointed to in helmet-law debates as a watchable argument that helmet mandates may cost lives by discouraging cycling.
videos.q: If you would rather watch than read, there's this

videos.t: Wim Hof Method Guided Breathing for Beginners (3 Rounds Slow Pace)
videos.s: A guided Wim Hof breathing session of three rounds at a slow pace, building from a 30 second to a 90 second breath hold. An on-screen bubble animation helps you keep the rhythm.
videos.w: HN commenters share it as a gentle beginner session and as a way to wind down before sleep.
videos.q: i did send her this one which is a bit easier

videos.t: Complete Solution To The Twins Paradox
videos.s: A minutephysics explainer on the twins paradox in special relativity. It shows why the traveling twin ends up younger and how acceleration resolves the paradox.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an easy-to-digest explanation of time dilation and the twin paradox.
videos.q: Minute Physics did a good couple of videos on this

videos.t: The Story of Another World on the Amiga | MVG
videos.s: Modern Vintage Gamer explains how Eric Chahi built Another World on the Amiga 500, using 2D polygons, rotoscoping and clever techniques to run well on a stock 7MHz machine.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear overview of Another World's graphics and programming and what the Amiga could do.
videos.q: A great video about Another World's graphics and the capabilities of the Amiga

videos.t: TikTok in China versus the United States | 60 Minutes
videos.s: A 60 Minutes segment in which Tristan Harris contrasts TikTok with its Chinese counterpart Douyin. He argues that Chinese children get wholesome, time-limited content while the rest of the world gets the addictive version.
videos.w: HN cites it in TikTok ban debates as the accessible summary of how Douyin and TikTok differ.
videos.q: tl;dw: Chinese users get more wholesome content, particularly children, along with usage limits.

videos.t: Is Nuclear Energy Green?
videos.s: Sabine Hossenfelder weighs the arguments for and against nuclear power, covering waste, fuel supply and newer reactor designs. She is skeptical that fast breeders and thorium solve the problems.
videos.w: Cited in nuclear energy debates, especially for uranium supply limits and why new reactor types fall short of claims.
videos.q: It's quite well researched

videos.t: Zero to $10 Million with React Native + Next.js - Fernando Rojo - (Next.js Conf 2021)
videos.s: Fernando Rojo explains how BeatGig reached $10M in sales with one frontend engineer by sharing code between React Native and Next.js, covering navigation, animation, theming and performance.
videos.w: Linked as the origin story and rationale for Solito and for sharing code between web and mobile.
videos.q: His video at Next.js Conf was really informative

videos.t: Sand Castle Holds Up A Car! - Mechanically Stabilized Earth
videos.s: Practical Engineering explains Mechanically Stabilized Earth, where layers of reinforcement make soil strong enough to hold heavy loads, shown with a sand structure supporting a car. It notes that MSE walls are everywhere in infrastructure.
videos.w: Often named as a great first video from Practical Engineering and as the explanation of reinforced earth.
videos.q: Practical Engineering has a great video on this simple but pervasive technology.

videos.t: How Smoking vs Vaping Affects Your Lungs  ● You Must See This ! !
videos.s: A demonstration comparing what a month of vaping versus a month of smoking cigarettes does to the lungs, using a filter to show the residue. It is part of a series of similar experiments.
videos.w: HN commenters send it to people who think vaping is as harmful as smoking, for its graphic comparison.
videos.q: Anyone who tries to tell me vaping might be worse I send them to this YouTube video

videos.t: BOLTR: KitchenAid Mixer. SURPRISE!
videos.s: AvE tears down a high-end KitchenAid stand mixer, looking at its castings, large DC motor and gear train. He also picks apart some design trade-offs.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as an entertaining teardown and as evidence that KitchenAid mixers are stoutly built.
videos.q: I thought the BOLTR teardown of one was entertaining

videos.t: Gaiman on Copyright Piracy and the Web
videos.s: Neil Gaiman tells the Open Rights Group how the internet and piracy affect books and publishing. He describes how free web copies of his books boosted sales.
videos.w: HN commenters use it as the standard example of an author who found piracy helped rather than hurt sales.
videos.q: He has a fantastic interview clip regarding his outlooks on piracy of his books

videos.t: Brain Crack (Explicit Version) :: Best of the Show :: 07-11-06
videos.s: A short Ze Frank piece from his 2006 show about "brain crack", the rush of exciting new ideas that feel great but tend to fall apart once you start executing them.
videos.w: Shared as reassurance and a reality check for people with idea overflow who keep planning instead of doing.
videos.q: Most ideas kinda of suck when you do them.

videos.t: What is the best diet for humans? | Eran Segal | TEDxRuppin
videos.s: Prof. Eran Segal's TEDx talk on research showing that people's blood sugar responses to identical foods vary widely. It describes an algorithm that predicts individual responses and why one best diet for everyone does not exist.
videos.w: HN points to it as an accessible case that diets work differently for different people, partly due to gut bacteria.
videos.q: It was not just about the food, it was also about the person eating it

videos.t: Stuart Sierra - Components Just Enough Structure
videos.s: Stuart Sierra presents the Component library for Clojure, a way to manage stateful services like database connections and thread pools without global mutable state. He draws on both functional and object-oriented principles.
videos.w: Pointed to as a thought-provoking talk on structuring large systems, including outside Clojure.
videos.q: it is a tiny clojure framework but the ideas should be thought provoking

videos.t: Munk Debate on Artificial Intelligence | Bengio & Tegmark vs. Mitchell & LeCun
videos.s: A Munk Debate on the proposition that AI research and development poses an existential threat. Yoshua Bengio and Max Tegmark argue for it, and Melanie Mitchell and Yann LeCun argue against.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a good debate with leading figures on both sides of the AI existential risk question.
videos.q: Tis a good one

videos.t: Why ChatGPT Can't Draw a Full Glass of Wine
videos.s: Alex O'Connor shows that ChatGPT cannot draw a wine glass filled to the brim, and ties the failure to David Hume's missing shade of blue. It asks what the failure says about how image models learn.
videos.w: HN treats it as the origin of the full-wine-glass meme and an illustration of how models lack concepts missing from their training data.
videos.q: this video is where the "AI can't draw a full glass of wine" meme got traction

videos.t: Reballing flip chip GPUs is BULLSHIT - the truth about dead laptop GPUs & repairing them.
videos.s: Louis Rossmann argues that reballing flip-chip GPUs is not a real fix for dead laptop GPUs. He explains why such repairs and oven reflow tricks fail and what is actually happening with failing hardware.
videos.w: HN people cite it to debunk oven-reflow and reballing repair folklore, and as part of Rossmann's critiques of Apple hardware quality.
videos.q: It's pretty funny. He thinks oven reflows are a bad idea.

videos.t: "Pixie - A Lightweight Lisp with 'Magical' Powers" by Timothy Baldridge
videos.s: Timothy Baldridge presents Pixie, a lightweight Lisp built on RPython, at Strange Loop 2015. It covers C interop, immutable data structures, fast startup and async-by-default IO.
videos.w: HN mentions it as the author's own overview of Pixie, with an interesting implementation technique near the end.
videos.q: There's a talk by the author online worth it

videos.t: In Norway, Everyone Can Know How Much You Earn
videos.s: Tom Scott explains how in Norway and other Nordic countries tax returns, and so individual incomes, are public. He looks at the effects of wage transparency and whether it is a good idea, with sources listed in the description.
videos.w: HN points to it in discussions of salary transparency as a short, well-sourced overview of how public tax records work in Nordic countries.
videos.q: Interesting video about somewhat public tax returns, and hence salary, in Norway and other Nordic countries.

videos.t: Lyle Bickley explains the PDP-1 (and we play the original Spacewar!)
videos.s: Lyle Bickley of the PDP-1 restoration team tours the 1959 DEC machine at the Computer History Museum and plays the original Spacewar! He covers its graphics display and the MIT student programs written for it.
videos.w: Linked in Spacewar and vintage computing threads as a charming demo on real hardware.
videos.q: it's quite an impressive machine.

videos.t: HandmadeCon 2015 - Pat Wyatt
videos.s: Pat Wyatt, a veteran game programmer who worked at Blizzard and ArenaNet, speaks at HandmadeCon 2015 in a conversation with Casey Muratori. He discusses network code and architecture in games he worked on, including mistakes on Diablo and the success of Guild Wars.
videos.w: HN points to it as a first-hand account of game netcode and engineering lessons from a Blizzard and Guild Wars developer.
videos.q: good interview with him talking about screwing up Diablo and doing a good job on Guild Wars

videos.t: This Is Your Brain On Stale Air
videos.s: Tom Scott features Kurtis Baute inside a sealed homemade biodome as carbon dioxide builds up, showing how stale air with elevated CO2 affects cognitive function. Sources include studies on CO2 and cognitive scores.
videos.w: HN links it as a popular, accessible introduction to indoor CO2 and its effect on thinking, in air quality threads.
videos.q: Tom Scott did a great video on it a while back

videos.t: Pinging The Voyager 2 Probe (PART 2)
videos.s: Part two of EEVblog's visit to the NASA/CSIRO Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex, showing the control room and how operators contact Voyager 2. It includes live data and spectrum displays.
videos.w: Commenters recommend the series for hearing an operations supervisor explain how Voyager signals are actually received.
videos.q: Dave Jones of EEVBlog has a nice series of videos talking to Richard Stephenson, Operations Supervisor at the DSN's Canberra site.

videos.t: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Bryan Johnson, founder of Kernel and previously Braintree, about brain-computer interfaces and Kernel's non-invasive brain monitoring hardware. It covers what the devices can do today and the company's plans.
videos.w: Cited as an accessible overview of Kernel's technology whenever its brain-sensing helmets come up.
videos.q: this recent podcast episode with the CEO is a good start

videos.t: The Geometry of Causality
videos.s: PBS Space Time explains how spacetime geometry and light cones determine the order of events and what can cause what. It visualizes causality in special relativity.
videos.w: Used as a go-to reference for relativity arguments, such as spacetime intervals being the same for all observers, and as a suggested follow-up for physics fans.

videos.t: SymbOS MP3MSX Demostration
videos.s: A demonstration of SymbOS, a multitasking operating system for 8-bit Z80 machines, running on a real MSX turboR with an MP3MSX card and a CF IDE interface. It shows the OS playing audio and running a graphical desktop on very old hardware, captured from the real machine and not an emulator.
videos.w: HN points to it as a vivid showcase of how much a modern-feeling GUI OS can do on slow 8-bit hardware.

videos.t: Andrew Ng: Artificial Intelligence is the New Electricity
videos.s: Andrew Ng speaks at the Stanford MSx Future Forum about how AI is transforming industry after industry, comparing its impact to electricity. The talk also touches on evil-AI worries, jobs and basic income.
videos.w: Recommended as a broad, practical view of AI's near-term impact from a leading practitioner, with his argument that worrying about evil AI is premature.
videos.q: I really enjoyed this Andrew Ng talk

videos.t: Don't Be a Sucker - 1947
videos.s: A 1947 US military film that deconstructs how the Nazi regime used divisive propaganda and prejudice to split and control a population. It teaches viewers to recognise demagoguery tactics.
videos.w: Shared in political threads as a timeless warning about divisive manipulation and demagogues.
videos.q: Here's a good video from 1947 explaining the whole thing

videos.t: Oral History of Dave Cutler Part 1
videos.s: A Computer History Museum oral history interview with Dave Cutler, covering his youth, early work on operating systems at DuPont and Digital Equipment, and his path toward VMS and Windows NT. This is part one of a long-form interview.
videos.w: Recommended as a rare long-form interview with a legendary operating system designer, though some find it light on technical detail.
videos.q: The Computer History Museum oral history interview with David Cutler is also very good

videos.t: Donald Knuth: Algorithms, Complexity, and The Art of Computer Programming | Lex Fridman Podcast #62
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Donald Knuth about algorithms, complexity, The Art of Computer Programming, and his work habits. The conversation covers his approach to verifying algorithms and how he organises his time.
videos.w: Cited as an excellent look at Knuth's thinking and working style, and as a likely source for quotes about his habits.
videos.q: It's fascinating to learn how much energy he still spends at verifying and investigating each aspect of newly published algorithms.

videos.t: Yehuda Katz - Why Rails is Hard (Railsberry 2012)
videos.s: Yehuda Katz's Railsberry 2012 talk on why Rails is hard to learn and use. He explains that the framework's many features reflect real complexity in web applications that newcomers do not yet see.
videos.w: Recommended to people who call Rails bloated, as an argument that its size comes from features you eventually need.
videos.q: I've seen an interesting talk[1] by Yehuda Katz: "why rails is hard".

videos.t: How to use uBlock Origin to protect your online privacy and security | uBlock Origin tutorial 2018
videos.s: A 2018 tutorial explaining uBlock Origin's advanced user mode, including how to block scripts and use the dynamic filtering settings. It positions the extension as a replacement for tools like uMatrix.
videos.w: HN points newcomers to it as the thing to watch before tackling uBlock Origin's advanced mode and filter syntax.
videos.q: Here is a good tutorial on how to use ublock origin in advanced mode.

videos.t: Thiel: Google has $50B, doesn't innovate
videos.s: A short CNN clip of Peter Thiel telling Google chairman Eric Schmidt that Google has huge cash reserves and does not know how to invest them. Thiel argues this signals a lack of innovation.
videos.w: HN reaches for it whenever big tech cash hoarding, buybacks or stagnating innovation come up.
videos.q: I strongly encourage you to watch the 4 min clip.

videos.t: Lisp Editing in the 80s - Interlisp SEdit
videos.s: A short demo of SEdit, the structure editor for Interlisp-D on Xerox Lisp machines in the 1980s, which edits code as trees rather than text.
videos.w: Linked as the clearest view of the legendary structural editor in threads about Lisp environments and structure editing.
videos.q: Dan Ingalls (one of the original authors of Smalltalk) in a 2017 demo of Smalltalk 76

videos.t: Robotic Liberation by PWP (VIC-20)
videos.s: Robotic Liberation by PWP is a music video demo performed entirely by an unexpanded Commodore VIC-20 and a 1541 disk drive, using only a few kilobytes of RAM and a 16 KB disk. It uses demoscene effects to tell a story.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a showcase of what skilled demoscene programmers can squeeze out of extremely limited hardware.
videos.q: I like that the demo effects are used here to tell a story in addition to being a pure display of coding prowess.

videos.t: Rick Roderick on Baudrillard - Fatal Strategies [full length]
videos.s: Rick Roderick's 1993 lecture on Baudrillard, the last in his series The Self Under Siege. It covers hyperreality, simulation and what Baudrillard calls fatal strategies.
videos.w: Recommended as a much easier way into Baudrillard's ideas than reading his own writing.
videos.q: here's an excellent presentation summarizing the idea

videos.t: DEBUNKING STARLINK
videos.s: A 43-minute skeptical critique arguing that Starlink fails to live up to its promises, covering satellite lifespan, costs, bandwidth and viability. The creator later added an update about FCC grant requirements.
videos.w: A few commenters recommend it as a skeptical take on Starlink economics, though others see it as dishonest.
videos.q: watching Common Sense Skeptic’s video, which I recommend

videos.t: Eric Weinstein: Revolutionary Ideas in Science, Math, and Society | Lex Fridman Podcast #16
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews mathematician and economist Eric Weinstein about science, mathematics, and society. The conversation ranges across physics, academia, AI and job displacement.
videos.w: HN refers to it for Weinstein's views on advanced math and physics and academia's problems, though some find him a bit kooky.
videos.q: Eric Weinstein (a bit kooky) explains his view on the trenches of advanced mathematics/physics

videos.t: Well There's Your Problem | Episode 28: Goiânia Incident
videos.s: An episode of the Well There's Your Problem podcast on the 1987 Goiania radiological accident in Brazil, based largely on the IAEA report. It goes through the event day by day.
videos.w: HN points to it as a good, detailed podcast account whenever the Goiania incident or lost radioactive sources come up.
videos.q: Goes into detail day by day about the events

videos.t: FreeBSD optimizations used by Netflix serving at 800Gb/s - Drew Gallatin - EuroBSDcon 2022
videos.s: Netflix engineer Drew Gallatin's EuroBSDcon 2022 talk quantifies the older FreeBSD optimizations that let Netflix serve web traffic at 800Gb/s, including TSO, LRO, VM page cache zones, asynchronous sendfile and unmapped mbufs.
videos.w: HN points to it as the recorded talk behind the Netflix 800Gb/s slides and as a deep look at kernel-level optimizations for high throughput.
videos.q: this might be a little lower level that you may be interested in as it relates to kernel optimizations to jack bit throughput rates

videos.t: Kilim: Fast, lightweight, cheap message passing in Java.
videos.s: A Google Tech Talk by the author of Kilim, a Java library for lightweight actor-style message passing. It argues that message passing can replace shared-memory concurrency and claims performance competitive with or better than Erlang for huge numbers of actors.
videos.w: Pointed to as evidence that Java can do fast, cheap message-passing concurrency, as an alternative to Erlang or Scala actors.
videos.q: Kilim's author did a nice Google Talk

videos.t: How a TV Works in Slow Motion - The Slow Mo Guys
videos.s: The Slow Mo Guys film a TV and screens with a high-speed camera to show how displays build an image. The footage includes CRT-style scanning and how pixels light up over time.
videos.w: Frequently linked as visual proof of how a CRT's raster scan and phosphor decay work.
videos.q: This YouTube video by "The Slow Mo Guys" shows this in action

videos.t: Behind the scenes of iOS and Mac Security
videos.s: Ivan Krstic's Black Hat talk on Apple platform security, including the Find My design that uses elliptic curve key diversification to locate offline devices privately. It also covers hardware features such as the T2 chip and secure boot hardening.
videos.w: Recommended as a rare insider look at Apple's security architecture and the reasoning behind its hardware choices.
videos.q: Good talk behind the reason for the T2 chip and some other Apple security stuff

videos.t: CppCon 2014: Zaika Antoun "Microsoft w/ C++ to Deliver Office Across Different Platforms, Part I"
videos.s: A CppCon 2014 talk from Microsoft engineers on using portable single-source C++ to deliver Office across iOS, Android, Windows and Mac. It covers architectures, techniques and lessons from real cross-platform projects.
videos.w: Cited as evidence that large production apps share a C++ core with native UI, in cross-platform and React Native or Flutter debates.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: There's a pretty interesting video of how the Office team uses C++ for their cross-platform efforts

videos.t: Internet of food: Arduino-based, urban aquaponics in Oakland
videos.s: A short documentary about Eric Maundu's Arduino-controlled aquaponics setup in West Oakland, where contaminated soil rules out ordinary farming. Fish and circulating water grow plants without soil.
videos.w: HN cites it as a neat example of urban aquaponics and as a plausible alternative path for people leaving programming.
videos.q: I recall watching was pretty neat.

videos.t: NSA operation ORCHESTRA Annual Status Report - FOSDEM 2014
videos.s: Poul-Henning Kamp's FOSDEM 2014 talk presents a fictitious NSA program called ORCHESTRA, satirizing how intelligence agencies could influence startups and open source. It is a humorous but pointed look at surveillance and subverted software.
videos.w: Recommended as an entertaining talk showing that targeting software projects and introducing bugs is nothing new.
videos.q: It’s pretty entertaining and illustrates that this is nothing new.

videos.t: Kevin Systrom: Instagram | Lex Fridman Podcast #243
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Instagram co-founder and former CEO Kevin Systrom about building the product, its early days and its pivot story.
videos.w: Pointed to for the founder's own account of Instagram's pivot, early scaling on Django with a small team, and avoiding overengineering.
videos.q: you can hear about it from the founder in this really good Lex Fridman podcast

videos.t: Joe Rogan Experience #1309 - Naval Ravikant
videos.s: Joe Rogan interviews entrepreneur and angel investor Naval Ravikant on happiness, work, technology platforms, AI and society. Naval revisits ideas from his well-known tweets.
videos.w: Mostly cited to support specific points Naval makes, such as platforms and free speech, rather than as a general must-watch.
videos.q: Naval Ravikant got this exactly right on his Rogan Interview

videos.t: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange
videos.s: A short Art of the Problem clip explaining Diffie-Hellman key exchange, using a paint mixing analogy for one-way functions and touching on modular arithmetic and discrete logarithms.
videos.w: Recommended as a simple, non-mathematical way to understand key exchange.
videos.q: Diffie-Hellman explained to me like I'm 5 using colors.

videos.t: Fred Dibnah How to climb a chimney overhang at 50+
videos.s: Footage of British steeplejack Fred Dibnah climbing a chimney overhang at over fifty years old, without a harness. It is a short clip from his steeplejack work.
videos.w: HN shares it as a dizzying example of Dibnah's fearless chimney work, in threads about heights and climbing.
videos.q: the overhang climb in this is enough to make you feel dizzy

videos.t: AI "Stop Button" Problem - Computerphile
videos.s: Rob Miles explains on Computerphile why implementing an off switch for a general AI is hard. A capable agent would resist being stopped because shutdown prevents it from achieving its goal.
videos.w: HN points to it as the standard response to the argument that we can just unplug a dangerous AI.
videos.q: here’s an interesting video response to the “just unplug it” argument on the Compuerphile channel

videos.t: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Douglas Lenat, founder of Cyc, a decades-long project to encode common-sense knowledge and reasoning for AI. They discuss symbolic AI and how it may complement neural networks.
videos.w: Pointed to as the long-form interview for understanding Lenat's work, especially after his death.
videos.q: If anybody wants to hear more about Doug's work and ideas, here is a (fairly long) interview with Doug by Lex Fridman

videos.t: Dark Matter: The Situation has Changed
videos.s: Sabine Hossenfelder explains how her opinion on dark matter has shifted, weighing the evidence for and against it and the case for modified gravity. It runs through what dark matter is and why it has not been detected.
videos.w: Recommended as an accessible, curious-undergraduate-level overview of dark matter and its alternatives.
videos.q: Here’s Sabine Hossenfelder’s curious-undergraduate-level history of Dark Matter theories

videos.t: Here's What Happens When an 18 Year Old Buys a Mainframe
videos.s: Connor Krukosky, an 18-year-old college student and vintage computer collector, tells how he bought an IBM z890 mainframe and got it running at home. The talk was given at SHARE in San Antonio in March 2016.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as an entertaining example of a teenager buying, hosting and booting a real mainframe.
videos.q: it's an entertaining 45 minutes

videos.t: Using Emacs - 1 - setting up the package manager
videos.s: The first episode of Mike Zamansky's Using Emacs series, covering setting up the package manager for new Emacs users as a start toward customization and efficient editing.
videos.w: Recommended as a practical, step-by-step video path for learning Emacs.
videos.q: I learned a lot from this CS prof's videos, and it's a good, practical learning path I'd recommend

videos.t: Sebastian Markbage: Minimal API Surface Area | JSConf EU 2014
videos.s: Sebastian Markbage explains how React is moving toward a minimal API surface by leaning on language features and patterns instead of dedicated framework APIs. He also touches on JSX and syntax proposals for future JavaScript.
videos.w: HN cites it as a statement of React's early design philosophy of keeping APIs small and understanding JavaScript itself.
videos.q: I found this talk on the topic very interesting

videos.t: We Solved Nuclear Waste Decades Ago
videos.s: Kyle Hill explains what nuclear waste actually is and how it is stored, arguing that the problem was effectively solved decades ago. It covers solid shielded waste and deep geological storage.
videos.w: Cited in nuclear power debates to argue that waste storage is a political rather than technical problem.
videos.q: Kyle Hill did a great video on this

videos.t: This Swiss Builder uses NO INSULATION...
videos.s: Builders Matt Risinger and Jordan Smith visit a Swiss cross-laminated timber factory that makes thick all-wood walls with no traditional insulation and wooden nails instead of glue or chemicals. The video is sponsored by Siga.
videos.w: HN cites it in mass timber and construction threads as an example of insulation-free, glue-free all-wood building in Europe.
videos.q: where Matt Risinger is visiting a Swiss factory where they use wooden (berch?) nails and dowel pins in stead of glue.

videos.t: First-stage landing | Onboard camera
videos.s: Sped-up onboard camera footage of the Falcon 9 first stage landing on a drone ship during the THAICOM 8 mission on May 27, 2016. It shows the descent from grid fin deployment to touchdown.
videos.w: HN links it in SpaceX landing threads as the best first-person view of how hard a booster landing is.
videos.q: The landing video from the rocket[0] really puts into perspective how much this truly is 'rocket science'.

videos.t: Psp collections: views and more by Paul Phillips
videos.s: Paul Phillips, a major Scala compiler contributor, gives a long talk on Scala collections and views, using it to critique Scala's design and direction.
videos.w: Cited in Scala debates as an insider's critique that persuaded many the language's problems were deep.
videos.q: Then I watched this Paul Phillips talk, which convinced me that the problems were deep, not superficial

videos.t: The Truth about Rust/WebAssembly Performance
videos.s: Leptos creator Greg Johnston examines Rust/WebAssembly frontend frameworks against JavaScript frameworks using the JS framework benchmark. He argues that WASM is no longer too slow for DOM-heavy rendering.
videos.w: Cited as evidence that DOM access is not the bottleneck for WebAssembly, and as an explanation of signals-based updates versus virtual DOM.
videos.q: did a pretty good video about this a few weeks ago[0]

videos.t: We need to talk about failing keyboards on these new Macbooks.
videos.s: Louis Rossmann discusses failing keyboards on newer MacBooks, comparing a Dell keyboard repair with an Apple keyboard repair and explaining why Apple's design is costly and hard to fix.
videos.w: Cited in MacBook keyboard and repairability threads for its clear teardown of what a replacement involves.
videos.q: Its eye opening seeing a keyboard replacement being performed

videos.t: A Possible Future of Software Development
videos.s: Sean Parent of Adobe argues that object-oriented frameworks ultimately fail to deliver scalable, high quality software and proposes combining generic and declarative programming instead. It draws on Stepanov's Elements of Programming.
videos.w: Frequently cited for the claim that Photoshop's codebase could shrink dramatically with generic programming.
videos.q: Watch this Sean Parent video

videos.t: Making Sense of VRChat, the "Metaverse" People Actually Like
videos.s: People Make Games explores VRChat, the social virtual world that many consider the metaverse people actually like, interviewing users and covering its communities and uncertain future.
videos.w: Recommended as a mini documentary that explains VRChat's culture and contrasts it with Meta's Horizon Worlds.
videos.q: There's a great video[1] on VRChat

videos.t: The Myth of the Robber Barons with Burt Folsom
videos.s: Hillsdale historian Burt Folsom lectures at a 2011 seminar on the 'robber barons' of the Gilded Age. He argues that figures like Vanderbilt and Rockefeller were market entrepreneurs rather than monopolists.
videos.w: HN people offer it as a free-market counterpoint to the standard robber baron narrative.
videos.q: Burton Folsom on the myth of robber barons and the great american entrepreneurs of the 19th century.

videos.t: Dr. Robert Sapolsky's lecture about Biological Underpinnings of Religiosity
videos.s: Robert Sapolsky's Stanford lecture on the biological underpinnings of religiosity, from his human behavioral biology course. It covers theories linking religion to stress, and schizotypal traits.
videos.w: Recommended when religion, mental health or psychedelics come up, for Sapolsky's biological framing.
videos.q: Here's a lecture by Robert Sapolsky where he goes into some theories involving schizotypal individuals

videos.t: NeWS: A Networked and Extensible Window System, lecture by James Gosling
videos.s: A 1990 lecture by James Gosling on NeWS, Sun's networked window system in which clients send PostScript programs to the server for execution. It covers the high-level imaging model and compares NeWS with similar systems.
videos.w: Shared in threads on window systems and X11 history as a primary-source talk on why NeWS was technically ahead of X.
videos.q: Here's James Gosling (you know, guy that invented Java) talking about it for an hour or so from 1990

videos.t: What Eating the Rich Did For Japan
videos.s: Asianometry traces how the Japanese zaibatsu families grew into vast industrial combines and how postwar reforms abruptly broke up their wealth and control.
videos.w: Recommended as a look at how Japan's monopolies were dismantled and how that shaped later industry.
videos.q: here’s a look at Japan’s monopolies, how they were broken up, and partly how that effected the future of their industry

videos.t: EEVblog 1547 (Part 1) - Contacting the Voyager 2 Space Probe
videos.s: EEVblog interviews Richard Stephenson of NASA's Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex about how the 70m DSS-43 dish is used to contact Voyager 2. It covers the ground antenna and low-noise receiver side of deep space communication. This is a 2023 re-release of a 2017 video.
videos.w: Shared in Voyager news threads as an accessible look at the real equipment used to talk to the probes.
videos.q: These three videos by EEVblog detail the ground based antennas and how it is contacted

videos.t: Introducing SILE: A New Typesetting System
videos.s: The SILE author's FOSDEM 2015 talk introducing SILE, a TeX-inspired typesetting system with frame-based layout, Unicode, OpenType and a Lua-based extensible design.
videos.w: Pointed to as the standard introduction to SILE as a modern TeX alternative, though possibly dated.
videos.q: was nice introduction, although I don't know how up to date it is

videos.t: How I Boarded a US NAVY NUCLEAR SUBMARINE in the Arctic (ICEX 2020) - Smarter Every Day 237
videos.s: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day documents boarding a US Navy nuclear submarine in the Arctic during the ICEX 2020 under-ice exercise. It is the first of a series on life aboard a fast attack submarine.
videos.w: Recommended in submarine threads as the start of an access-rich series on life aboard a US fast attack sub.
videos.q: you will enjoy Destin's series on Smarter Every Day spending time on a US fast attack submarine

videos.t: The Daily Mail Song
videos.s: A comedy song by Dan and Dan that summarizes the British newspaper The Daily Mail using only its headlines. It satirizes the paper's habit of claiming everything causes or cures cancer.
videos.w: Used as a running joke or satirical shorthand whenever the Daily Mail is cited or criticized.
videos.q: there is a good (and humorous) summary of the paper made into a song using only their headlines

videos.t: AI can't cross this line and we don't know why.
videos.s: A Welch Labs explainer on neural scaling laws and the compute-efficient frontier, asking why model loss seems to hit a line it cannot cross. It draws an analogy to an ideal gas law for AI.
videos.w: Recommended as a well-made, digestible introduction to scaling laws and why models cluster along a similar efficiency frontier.
videos.q: see eg for a well made/easily digestable intro

videos.t: Four Horsemen - Feature Documentary - Official Version
videos.s: An independent feature documentary in which 23 economists, advisers and financiers discuss how the financial system works and what a more just economic model might look like. It covers money creation, debt and the aftermath of the financial crisis.
videos.w: Mentioned as a one-package overview of heterodox views on money creation and debt, though some find it unsurprising.
videos.q: goes into these topics at length, especially money creation

videos.t: Thomas Thwaites: How I built a toaster -- from scratch
videos.s: Designer Thomas Thwaites describes his attempt to build a toaster from scratch, from mining ore and deriving plastic from oil. It is a short TED talk on how much civilization a simple object depends on.
videos.w: HN uses it as the standard illustration of hidden complexity and supply-chain dependencies behind everyday objects.
videos.q: a great example of the hidden complexities of

videos.t: Oxide and Friends 7/3/2023 -- Shipping the first Oxide rack: Your questions answered!
videos.s: A two-hour Oxide and Friends session answering questions after shipping the first Oxide rack. Topics include making hardware as a startup and why Oxide chose illumos.
videos.w: HN cites it as Oxide's own explanation of how they ship hardware as a startup and why they picked illumos.
videos.q: We have talked quite a bit about what it's like to be making hardware as a startup

videos.t: Axis of Awesome - 4 Four Chord Song (with song titles)
videos.s: Australian comedy group Axis of Awesome perform a sketch showing that dozens of pop hits share the same four chords. It was recorded at the 2009 Melbourne International Comedy Festival.
videos.w: The go-to reference in threads on chord progressions, pop music similarity and music copyright.
videos.q: well worth watching

videos.t: Machine with Concrete - Arthur Ganson
videos.s: Arthur Ganson's kinetic sculpture chains twelve 1:50 worm gear reductions so the final gear, embedded in concrete, would take over two trillion years to turn once.
videos.w: Shared whenever gear reductions, exponential scaling or playful kinetic art come up.
videos.q: I quite like how a lot of his work seems to have a punchline to it.

videos.t: Corruption is Legal in America
videos.s: A short RepresentUs explainer arguing that US politics is shaped by money, citing the Gilens and Page Princeton study on how little average citizens influence policy.
videos.w: Frequently linked as a compact summary of the Princeton study when commenters argue Congress ignores public opinion.
videos.q: It's pretty compelling and well made.

videos.t: Professional SMT Soldering:   Hand Soldering Techniques - Surface Mount
videos.s: A three-minute demonstration of professional hand-soldering techniques for multi-lead surface mount parts, to IPC class 3 criteria.
videos.w: HN points to it as proof that SMD soldering is simpler than people fear.
videos.q: Great demo, showing simplicity

videos.t: "Eve" by Chris Granger
videos.s: Chris Granger presents Eve, a programming environment designed to be approachable for humans, at Strange Loop 2015. The talk covers the project's approach and design ideas.
videos.w: HN mentions it as one of the talks on Eve, usually as related prior work in discussions of end-user and visual programming.

videos.t: "Transactions: myths, surprises and opportunities" by Martin Kleppmann
videos.s: Martin Kleppmann's Strange Loop talk on database transactions, covering why they were dropped by NoSQL, their reputation for being slow, and newer algorithms that make serializable transactions perform and scale. It touches on consistency, linearizability and the CAP theorem.
videos.w: Recommended as a compact preview of Kleppmann's data systems material, including from his book on the subject.
videos.q: I recommend watching this talk from him to give a little glimpse of the book

videos.t: Conrad Wolfram: Teaching kids real math with computers
videos.s: Conrad Wolfram argues that the part of math taught in schools, hand calculation, is tedious and mostly irrelevant to real mathematics. He proposes teaching math through computer programming so students can tackle real problems.
videos.w: Cited in HN discussions of math and CS education reform as an argument that school math is boring because it is taught wrong.
videos.q: But isn't maths boring at school because we're teaching it wrong?

videos.t: Genetics and Intelligence
videos.s: Steve Hsu's 2011 Google Tech Talk reviews psychometric measurement of intelligence and the heritability of adult IQ, then discusses genome-wide association studies seeking the genes behind cognitive ability.
videos.w: Pointed to as a well-cited hour on IQ and genetics whenever intelligence and heritability come up.
videos.q: You can also choose to spend an hour on this talk by Stephen Hsu who does research on IQ and genetics

videos.t: Kylie Minogue - Come Into My World (Official Video) [Full HD Remastered]
videos.s: The official music video for Kylie Minogue's Come Into My World, directed by Michel Gondry, built around a looping scene with multiplying copies of Kylie.
videos.w: Cited as a landmark looping music video, a reference point for creative video and editing tricks.
videos.q: One of the best music videos, in my opinion.

videos.t: Cody's Algae Panel
videos.s: Cody's Lab builds a prototype algae growing panel as an experiment before making more. The channel also shows growing algae for consumption.
videos.w: Pointed to as a cheap, hands-on example of home algae cultivation.
videos.q: Cody'sLab has a few videos about growing his own algae for consumption which are pretty interesting

videos.t: The next outbreak? We’re not ready | Bill Gates | TED
videos.s: Bill Gates's 2015 TED talk, given after the 2014 Ebola outbreak, argues the world is unprepared for the next fast-spreading epidemic. He calls for scenario planning, vaccine research, and trained health workers, in the way countries prepare for war.
videos.w: During COVID-19 HN commenters cited it as a prescient pandemic warning.
videos.q: It's impressive how the details are similar to coronavirus.

videos.t: Sand Flea Jumping Robot
videos.s: A short Boston Dynamics clip of the Sand Flea, an 11-pound RC-car-style robot that can jump about 30 feet into the air. An onboard stabilization system keeps it oriented in flight and for landings.
videos.w: Brought up as a favorite and as an inspiration for small, cheap jumping robots for obstacle crossing and planetary exploration.
videos.q: My favorite is the Sand Flea, a small car which can jump 9 meters (30-feet) into the air

videos.t: A Day Made of Glass... Made possible by Corning. (2011)
videos.s: Corning's 2011 concept video showing a future where specialty glass surfaces and touchscreens are woven into everyday life.
videos.w: Referenced as an inspiring example of a vision-of-the-future video with believable everyday uses.
videos.q: has far more every day examples we can all believe in

videos.t: Dtrace Review
videos.s: A 2007 Google Tech Talk in which Bryan Cantrill demonstrates DTrace and explains how it improves debugging of both development and live production systems.
videos.w: Recommended as the DTrace creator's own demonstration and a reference for dynamic tracing.
videos.q: A video demostration of DTrace, by the creator of DTrace.

videos.t: The Secret Life of components. A series of eight guides for designers and makers by Tim Hunkin
videos.s: The trailer for Tim Hunkin's series The Secret Life of Components, eight guides to mechanical and electromechanical parts for designers and makers.
videos.w: Recommended to people who like building things, as part of Hunkin's body of practical engineering explainers.
videos.q: It is really great stuff if you enjoy building things.

videos.t: What Happens When Maths Goes Wrong? - with Matt Parker
videos.s: Matt Parker's Royal Institution talk based on his book Humble Pi, covering everyday mathematical mistakes and spurious patterns that went wrong in engineering and software. It mixes stand-up comedy with stories of coincidence and error.
videos.w: Used as a funny, accessible reference for coincidences, spurious patterns and maths errors.
videos.q: It also comes with an entirely different set of interesting stories for anyone inclined to listen

videos.t: Elon Musk Mahalo Mentor Interview
videos.s: A roughly 40-minute Mahalo mentor interview with Elon Musk, covering his background from Zip2 and PayPal to SpaceX, Tesla and SolarCity, along with advice for entrepreneurs.
videos.w: Shared as an early long-form Musk interview, notably for his answer about what motivates him.
videos.q: His answer on motivation was striking to me

videos.t: A simple guide to electronic components.
videos.s: Big Clive gives a 38-minute beginner's guide to identifying common electronic components and what they do. He keeps the maths minimal and aims to fill gaps for people just starting out.
videos.w: Suggested as a gentle starting point for beginners in electronics.
videos.q: And then some bigclivedotcom to get going

videos.t: Death Magnetic Retail vs Guitar Hero 3
videos.s: A short comparison of the retail release of Metallica's Death Magnetic against the Guitar Hero 3 version of the same song. It switches between the two so you can hear and see the heavy clipping in the retail master.
videos.w: HN uses it as the go-to demonstration of the loudness war and what over-compressed mastering does to music.
videos.q: A comparison between these two versions was the eye opener for me.

videos.t: Just Intonation vs Equal Temperament
videos.s: A short demonstration comparing just intonation with equal temperament, played so you can hear how the tuning compromise changes intervals and chords. It includes a Bach prelude played in both tunings.
videos.w: Shared as a quick audible demonstration of the errors that equal temperament introduces compared with pure intervals.
videos.q: this video is a great demonstration of the errors between just intonation intervals and our equal temperament compromise

videos.t: Quantum Expert Insight:  Peter Shor
videos.s: Peter Shor tells the story of how he discovered Shor's Algorithm, from his early mathematics days to the quantum factoring breakthrough. It was recorded at MIT at the Physics of Computation conference.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an oral history of the algorithm straight from its inventor.
videos.q: Shor (yes the one who invented Shor's Algorithm) gave a create 30 min presentation here

videos.t: Dabble DB demo
videos.s: A short product demo of Dabble DB, a web tool for importing, entering and manipulating structured data with little effort. It was built in Smalltalk and later acquired by Twitter.
videos.w: Used as a reference for an ahead-of-its-time end-user database tool, brought up in threads on Access clones, Smalltalk and data-entry tools.
videos.q: If you haven't heard of DabbleDB, this video is a good introduction

videos.t: GraphQL: The Documentary
videos.s: A documentary on how GraphQL came to be at Facebook, featuring its co-creators Lee Byron, Dan Schafer and Nick Schrock. It covers the problems it solved and its adoption at companies like Twitter, Airbnb and GitHub.
videos.w: HN recommends it for understanding the original motivation behind GraphQL before judging whether it fits your problem.
videos.q: Listen to what the developers tell which problems they had to solve when they invented GraphQL.

videos.t: Cory Benfield - Building Protocol Libraries The Right Way - PyCon 2016
videos.s: Cory Benfield's PyCon 2016 talk on building protocol libraries that can be reused widely, using the Python Hyper HTTP project as the example. He argues for separating protocol parsing from I/O.
videos.w: HN points to it as the foundational argument for sans-I/O protocol library design.
videos.q: give some really great brainfood about the way currently all kinds of network protocols are implemented

videos.t: If money was no object, should you run every medical test?
videos.s: A doctor from Medlife Crisis explains in under three minutes why even a rich patient should not simply order every medical test, touching on pre-test probability and Bayesian reasoning. False positives make blanket testing counterproductive.
videos.w: HN people link it as a short, funny and accurate explanation of why over-testing and over-screening can do harm.
videos.q: An under 3-minute video by a funny and informative doctor explaining this

videos.t: iMUSE Demonstration 2 - Seamless Transitions
videos.s: A two-minute demonstration of LucasArts' iMUSE adaptive music system in Monkey Island 2. It shows music layers and transitions changing seamlessly as the player moves.
videos.w: HN points to it as the clearest short demo of iMUSE, considered a high point in video game music.
videos.q: considered a high point in video game music. 1. A video demo

videos.t: Jet Fuel VS Diesel VS Gasoline how they burn and what color are they.
videos.s: A hands-on comparison of how jet fuel, diesel, heating oil, kerosene, avgas and gasoline burn and what color they are. It shows that gasoline ignites more easily than jet fuel.
videos.w: HN cites it as a practical demonstration that kerosene-type fuels are hard to ignite compared with gasoline.
videos.q: Great practical demonstration of the different flammability characteristics of some common fuels.

videos.t: Why Asimov's Laws of Robotics Don't Work - Computerphile
videos.s: Rob Miles explains for Computerphile why simple rule sets like Asimov's Three Laws cannot make robots and AI safe. Terms like harm and human are too ambiguous to specify precisely.
videos.w: Pointed to in AI safety debates as a short explanation of why encoding human values as simple rules is so hard.
videos.q: I found this video insightful on the matter from Computerphile

videos.t: Physics in Clojure - Colin Smith
videos.s: Colin Smith introduces Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics and his Clojure port, sicmutils. He shows how higher-order functions and a symbolic algebra system can represent Lagrangian mechanics.
videos.w: Recommended as the best introduction to SICM and sicmutils and a showcase of what such symbolic systems can do.
videos.q: The Strange Loop talk [3] is a good showcase of the power and simplicity of these kind of systems.

videos.t: George Carlin - Saving the Planet
videos.s: George Carlin's stand-up routine arguing the planet will be fine and it is people who are in trouble. It mocks the idea of saving the planet.
videos.w: HN quotes it in environmental threads as a famous, darkly funny take that the planet will outlast humanity.
videos.q: I cannot explain it better than George Carlin [1]. Enjoy!

videos.t: Solar Powered Air Conditioner!
videos.s: Tech Ingredients builds a larger solar-powered desiccant air conditioner that uses a calcium chloride liquid desiccant with evaporative cooling to cool their lab. The video includes the engineering calculations.
videos.w: HN points to it as a detailed, DIY-able design for desiccant-based cooling.
videos.q: built a dessicant-based air conditioning system with enough info to DIY one.

videos.t: Major Brian Shul, USAF (Ret.) SR-71 Blackbird 'Speed Check'
videos.s: Retired Major Brian Shul tells the story of a ground speed check with LA Center while flying the SR-71 Blackbird. He recounts it live at the Hiller Aviation Museum.
videos.w: Shared as the pilot's own telling of a famous, amusing SR-71 anecdote that never gets old.
videos.q: it's pretty amusing. As told by the pilot

videos.t: IPFS Alpha Demo
videos.s: Juan Benet gives an overview and demo of the go-ipfs alpha. It shows the peer-to-peer content-addressed protocol in action, including streaming video from a home computer.
videos.w: HN lists it among the best early resources for learning what IPFS is and does.
videos.q: Watch a demo of this @ 7:00 in this video

videos.t: The Implementation of Rewind in Braid
videos.s: Jonathan Blow's GDC talk explains how the time-rewind mechanic in Braid was designed and implemented, including the technical hurdles such as memory limits and state history. It covers both design and engineering concerns.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as the reference for how a rewind system works and as a point of comparison for undo and serialization approaches.
videos.q: Here's a GDC talk about the rewind system in which he explains some of the hurdles he had to deal with

videos.t: SpaceX reaches orbit with Falcon 1 - Flight 4 (full video including Elon Musk statement)
videos.s: The full webcast of SpaceX's Falcon 1 Flight 4, the first privately developed liquid-fueled rocket to reach orbit, on 28 September 2008. It includes the crew's cheering and Elon Musk's statement afterward.
videos.w: HN shares it as a nostalgic, historic moment, noting the cheers at each milestone and Musk's address to employees.
videos.q: The series of cheers at each milestone, as the article mentions, is pretty awesome.

videos.t: Stephen Fry on American vs British Comedy
videos.s: A short clip of Stephen Fry explaining the differences between American and British comedy. He attributes them to cultural attitudes such as optimism versus pessimism.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as an insightful short explanation of why US and UK comedy differ.
videos.q: Actually very insightful, and explains why I have never been fond of the cool guy

videos.t: The Origins of APL - 1974
videos.s: A 1974 talk-show-style interview with the original developers of APL, including Iverson, Falkoff and Breed. They discuss how the language originated.
videos.w: Recommended as a vintage TV segment on APL's origins, and quoted for Iverson's view of APL as notation.
videos.q: a video from 1974, where Iverson, Falkoff, and others discuss the origins of APL. It was a pleasure to watch.

videos.t: Florian Grunow, Niklaus Schiess: Lifting the Fog on Red Star OS
videos.s: A 32C3 talk dissecting Red Star OS, North Korea's state-built operating system. The speakers explain its internals and how it invades users' privacy, including file watermarking.
videos.w: HN points to it as a deep dive into the surveillance features of North Korea's OS and the extent of that state's digital tracking.
videos.q: A deep dive into the surveillance features of North Korea's operating system

videos.t: Is Organic Really Better? Healthy Food or Trendy Scam?
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt explainer asking whether organic food is really healthier or better for the environment. It defines what organic means and looks at pesticide use, nutrition and environmental impact, with sources.
videos.w: Cited as a sourced overview of what organic means and how it compares on pesticides and nutrition.
videos.q: Kurzgesagt has a pretty great video[0] about organic food, and goes a little bit into what the definition of "organic" means.

videos.t: Everythings Amazing & Nobodys Happy
videos.s: A clip of Louis C.K.'s bit "Everything's Amazing and Nobody's Happy," about how quickly people take modern technology for granted and complain about it. It is a comedic riff on impatience with air travel and gadgets.
videos.w: Posted constantly in threads about tech complaints as a reminder to appreciate how remarkable modern technology is.
videos.q: Maybe we need to watch this tube to see things in a more balanced way

videos.t: SpaceX IPO Scandal
videos.s: Patrick Boyle examines SpaceX's planned IPO at a roughly $1.75 trillion valuation. He covers the merging of other Musk companies, orbital data center claims and the fast-track index rules that may help the listing.
videos.w: HN users cite it as the explanation of the tricks around the IPO and the index-inclusion rule changes.
videos.q: Informative and entertaining.

videos.t: Vampire 2 Review - The Fastest Amiga Ever?!
videos.s: Dan Wood reviews the Vampire 2 FPGA accelerator for the Amiga 600. He covers how much faster it makes the machine and what it can run.
videos.w: Recommended as a decent introduction to the Vampire accelerator and a cheaper way to modernize classic Amigas.
videos.q: This is a decent introductory video

videos.t: BlueHat IL 2023 - David Weston - Default Security
videos.s: David Weston's BlueHat IL 2023 talk traces the evolution of Windows security and previews Windows 11 and hardware advances. It ends with upcoming changes such as Rust in the kernel and fonts, signed binaries and adminless Windows.
videos.w: HN uses it as the primary source for Microsoft's Rust adoption and its reasoning on TPM and security requirements.
videos.q: The speaker covers a bunch of areas and the final part of the talk (around 10 minutes) is about Microsoft introducing Rust in some self-contained areas in Windows.

videos.t: It's Quieter in the Twilight | Trailer | SF48
videos.s: Trailer for the documentary It's Quieter in the Twilight, shown at the Boston SciFi Film Festival. The film follows the engineers who keep the Voyager spacecraft running.
videos.w: Recommended in Voyager threads as a documentary about the team keeping the probes alive.
videos.q: about the team keeping the Voyager missions alive

videos.t: No Body Steering Bike of the California Superbike School
videos.s: California Superbike School demonstrates its 'No B.S.' bike, which has fixed handlebars so riders can only steer with body lean. It illustrates how little control that gives compared with countersteering.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an eye-opening demonstration of why countersteering matters on two wheels.
videos.q: It is really eye opening on how little control you have without countersteering.

videos.t: What Fossils Will We Leave Behind in 65 Million Years?
videos.s: Curious Droid asks what traces human civilization would leave in the geological record 65 million years from now. It considers how thin the fossil record of humanity might be.
videos.w: HN points to it in discussions of whether a past industrial civilization would leave detectable evidence.
videos.q: There is a nice curious droid video on the topic

videos.t: Freeman Dyson: Heretical Thoughts About Science and Society
videos.s: Freeman Dyson's 2005 Boston University talk on heretical views about science and society. He questions prevailing dogmas, including his argument that climate and CO2 are a land management issue.
videos.w: HN cites it for Dyson's contrarian take on global warming and soil carbon.
videos.q: I encourage you to listen to videos of him. I found him quite enjoyable to listen to.

videos.t: Imba is Underrated: Building a counter in 49 seconds
videos.s: A five-minute video showing how to build a counter in the Imba web programming language in under a minute, then style it.
videos.w: HN links it in Imba threads as a quick demonstration of how the language combines code, HTML and CSS.
videos.q: It demonstrates how CSS styling, code, and HTML works together in this language

videos.t: I Think Faster Than Light Travel is Possible. Here's Why.
videos.s: Sabine Hossenfelder explains why she thinks faster-than-light travel may not be ruled out. She argues that the standard objections from special relativity are inconclusive.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for a compelling, accessible case against treating the speed of light as a hard limit.
videos.q: She does seem to have a pretty compelling argument that the speed of light may not be the maximum speed.

videos.t: Net Neutrality II: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on net neutrality, explaining the stakes of the FCC's push to roll back the rules and urging viewers to file comments. It is a comedic but substantive explainer.
videos.w: HN points people to it as a good plain-language explanation of net neutrality during the 2017 FCC fight.
videos.q: John Oliver found a good way to explain it

videos.t: Naive empiricism, terrorism & Ebola.
videos.s: Nassim Taleb argues that evidence on terrorism risk presented in media is statistically naive, using extreme value theory without math to separate fat-tailed risks like Ebola and terrorism from thin-tailed ones.
videos.w: HN cites it when arguing that different risks follow different distributions and should be judged by growth rates and tails rather than current counts.
videos.q: Watch this to understand that we're talking about two different distributions

videos.t: 10 Reasons to Ignore AI Safety
videos.s: Robert Miles goes through ten common reasons people give for dismissing AI safety, adapted from Stuart Russell's list, and answers each one. It is aimed at skeptics and newcomers.
videos.w: HN commenters link it as a compact rebuttal to dismissive arguments and as a way to see why people consider AI safety important.
videos.q: This video might be interesting to see some arguments for why people think it’s important

videos.t: David Sinclair | Why We Age and Why We Don't Have To | Talks at Google
videos.s: Harvard geneticist David Sinclair discusses his book Lifespan at Google. He covers the biology of aging, lifestyle interventions and possible future ways to slow or reverse it.
videos.w: Shared as the author's own hour-long overview of his aging research, though some commenters doubt that the book's claims hold up.
videos.q: Google talk: Why We Age and Why We Don't Have To (55:13) - By the author of the book

videos.t: Tiny meteorites are everywhere. Here’s how to find them.
videos.s: Verge Science's pilot of its Trial & Error series follows amateur scientist Jon Larsen on a hunt for micrometeorites. It shows how tiny space rocks can be found on rooftops and confirmed under a microscope.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an accessible demonstration of how anyone can collect micrometeorites at home.
videos.q: Here's a good video running through one way to do this at home

videos.t: Professor Jeff Dahn | WIN Seminar Series
videos.s: Professor Jeff Dahn lectures on why lithium-ion batteries die and how chemistry changes could make them last decades.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a detailed look at battery degradation, in threads on EV and grid storage lifetimes.
videos.q: This lecture (1h, 13m) goes into it in detail, including how it can be prevented, ways of testing, and more

videos.t: LESSON 1: Do Not Obey In Advance
videos.s: The first lesson from Timothy Snyder's short video series accompanying On Tyranny, arguing that most of the power of authoritarianism is freely given when people comply in advance. It runs about eight minutes.
videos.w: Linked in political threads as a short, accessible companion to Snyder's book and as a reminder not to obey in advance.
videos.q: I also recommend the short Youtube series Snyder recorded before the release of the graphic edition

videos.t: Armadillo Aerospace - Mod free flight, engine restart, 4 views
videos.s: A four-pane view of Armadillo Aerospace's Mod vehicle on a June 2010 boosted hop. The flight includes engine shutdown, drogue chute deployment, an engine restart and a safe landing.
videos.w: Cited as an example of impressive amateur-scale rocket work, and as a vertical-landing test that predates and rivals SpaceX's Grasshopper.
videos.q: this [1] test by Armadillo was more impressive in my opinion for the additional complexity involved

videos.t: Marble Marcher - A Fractal Physics Game
videos.s: A demo of Marble Marcher, a game using a fractal physics engine and fully procedural ray-marched rendering. The player rolls a marble through shifting fractal levels.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a striking example of rendering with distance-estimated fractals and non-standard graphics approaches.
videos.q: He has a YouTube channel as well

videos.t: I recently learned that waste heat will boil the oceans in about 400 years.
videos.s: Sabine Hossenfelder explains that waste heat from ever-growing energy use could eventually boil the oceans in a few centuries, whatever the energy source. She discusses proposed ways to cool the planet.
videos.w: HN cites it in energy debates as an illustration of the long-term thermal limits of exponential energy consumption growth.
videos.q: You might enjoy Sabine Hossenfelder's video exploring this

videos.t: Sassy Justice with Fred Sassy (Full Episode) | Deep Fake and Deep Fake: The Movie
videos.s: Full episode of Sassy Justice, a satirical local-news show from the South Park creators starring a deepfaked consumer advocate, Fred Sassy. It uses face-swapped public figures to comment on the dangers of manipulated video.
videos.w: Brought up in every deepfake thread as a funny and technically convincing early example of synthetic media used for satire.
videos.q: A hilarious take on deepfakes

videos.t: Sir Roger Penrose & William Lane Craig • The Universe: How did it get here & why are we part of it?
videos.s: Physicist Roger Penrose and philosopher William Lane Craig discuss the origin of the universe on the Unbelievable? show. Topics include Penrose's three realms of reality, conformal cyclic cosmology and whether fine tuning points to a creator.
videos.w: Pointed to for Penrose's own explanations of the Big Bounce and his three-worlds idea.
videos.q: this video might serve as a quick introduction to Penrose's three world idea for those interested.

videos.t: Are we in control of our decisions? | Dan Ariely
videos.s: In a TED talk, behavioral economist Dan Ariely uses visual illusions and his research to show that people are less rational in their decisions than they think. He covers defaults, such as organ donation rates, and how choice framing steers decisions.
videos.w: Used to illustrate predictable irrationality, such as defaults and the effect of the middle option among three choices.
videos.q: talks about the very significant differences in organ donation rates between countries

videos.t: The Black Hole Information Paradox
videos.s: PBS Space Time episode on the black hole information paradox, covering how black holes seem to destroy information, the no-hair conjecture and the proposed role of the event horizon. It is part of a series on black holes.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of how information may be encoded on a black hole's surface.
videos.q: There's a great PBS Space Time youtube video on this concept

videos.t: Glenn Gould and Leonard Bernstein: Bach's Keyboard Concerto No. 1 (I) in D minor (BWV 1052)
videos.s: A 1960 CBS clip in which Leonard Bernstein introduces and conducts Bach's Keyboard Concerto No. 1 in D minor with a 28-year-old Glenn Gould at the piano. Gould's performance starts around 5:08.
videos.w: Recommended as a definitive Gould interpretation whose playing makes Bach's counterpoint clear.
videos.q: Have a look/listen at Glenn Gould's version, which makes the counterpoint really clear [1].

videos.t: The Braitenberg Vehicles
videos.s: Brian Douglas introduces Braitenberg vehicles, simple robots whose sensors are wired directly to motors yet show surprisingly lifelike behavior. He draws on Valentino Braitenberg's book Vehicles.
videos.w: Recommended as a short, fascinating introduction to how simple sensor-actuator machines can appear intelligent.
videos.q: Fascinating thought experiments.

videos.t: Falcon Heavy & Starman
videos.s: SpaceX's recap of the Falcon Heavy debut launch, with side booster landings and a Tesla Roadster with Starman sent into orbit.
videos.w: HN references it for launch footage and the atmosphere of the first Falcon Heavy flight, including the center core landing failure.
videos.q: is my favorite way to watch that launch, just because of the way it integrate the people watching.

videos.t: Tree-sitter: a new parsing system for programming tools - GitHub Universe 2017
videos.s: Max Brunsfeld of GitHub presents Tree-sitter, a parsing system for programming tools that supports incremental, error-tolerant parsing. He demos its integration into GitHub.com and Atom for syntax highlighting and code navigation.
videos.w: Recommended as the canonical introduction to tree-sitter and why fast incremental parsing enables live editor support.
videos.q: There is a long (42 minutes) but worth to watch talk about tree-sitter

videos.t: Boards of Canada - Dayvan Cowboy
videos.s: The official video for Boards of Canada's Dayvan Cowboy, built from reassembled documentary footage. It forms a dreamlike journey from space to the sea and shore, including Kittinger's 1960 high-altitude jump and surfing footage.
videos.w: HN mentions it as a favorite ambient track and as a nicely edited tribute to Kittinger's jump.
videos.q: you can watch nicely edited footage of Kittinger's 1960 record of 100,000 feet

videos.t: RSA ANIMATE: The Secret Powers of Time
videos.s: An RSA Animate illustrating a lecture by psychologist Philip Zimbardo on how people's perspectives on time (past, present, future) shape work, health and well-being.
videos.w: Recommended in threads about culture and time orientation as an accessible presentation of Zimbardo's framework.
videos.q: another approach I found interesting is the one proposed by Philip Zimbardo neatly presented in this video

videos.t: Why hierarchy creates a destructive force within the human psyche (by dr. Robert Sapolsky)
videos.s: A short clip of Robert Sapolsky on how social hierarchy generates chronic stress, drawing on baboon research. It links rank-related stress to heart health and life expectancy.
videos.w: HN shares it as a compact explanation of how hierarchy and stress affect health, pointing to the longer full lecture.
videos.q: Here's Sapolsky explaining how stress in an hierarchical social arrangement impacts heart health and life expectancy.

videos.t: Are WILD cockatoos smart enough to solve this puzzle?
videos.s: Maker's Muse designs a 3D-printed and laser-cut puzzle box to test whether wild sulphur-crested cockatoos can solve it. He documents how the birds work it out.
videos.w: Recommended in cockatoo threads as a fun and remarkable demonstration of the birds' problem-solving ability.
videos.q: it's really remarkable to watch them figure it out

videos.t: Cities Without People
videos.s: Jacob Geller's video essay on empty cities and what they say about our relationship to places, using games, literature and aerial imagery. It touches on works such as Invisible Cities.
videos.w: HN points to Geller's essays as accessible companions to literary works and as a good summary of a story.
videos.q: Jacob Geller provides a fun and effective summary within this video at 9 minutes in

videos.t: What prevents the poor from reaching the middle class?  | VISION TALKS
videos.s: Megan McArdle's AEI Vision Talk 'Capital and Poverty' argues that social and financial capital work differently in low-income communities, and that this explains barriers to reaching the middle class.
videos.w: Cited to explain why poor people's seemingly irrational financial decisions can rationally protect their social safety net.
videos.q: poor people make seemingly dumb decisions because if they don't help their social network when it comes knocking

videos.t: This 1970s tank simulator drives through a tiny world
videos.s: Tom Scott visits the Swiss Military Museum to see the last surviving 1970s tank-driving simulator. It uses a real camera moving over a miniature model landscape rather than any computer graphics.
videos.w: Recommended as a great example of early VR and pre-computer simulation.
videos.q: This tank simulator from the 1970s is a great example of early VR

videos.t: Tom Lehrer - The Elements - LIVE FILM From Copenhagen in 1967
videos.s: A 1967 live film of Tom Lehrer performing his patter song "The Elements" in Copenhagen, reciting the chemical elements to a Gilbert and Sullivan tune. It is a short, polished example of his satirical piano-and-voice style.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as a favorite Lehrer song and invoke it as a joke whenever elements or science-themed wordplay come up.
videos.q: is the Tom Lehrer song that made the biggest impression on me.

videos.t: The Bizarre Truth About Purebred Dogs (and Why Mutts Are Better) - Adam Ruins Everything
videos.s: An Adam Ruins Everything segment arguing that purebred dogs suffer from inbreeding and genetic disorders, and that mutts are healthier. It follows the show's comedic debunking style.
videos.w: Shared in dog-breeding threads as a snappy summary of the genetic-diversity problem.
videos.q: this video sums up my feelings nicely

videos.t: Perhaps Ben Shapiro Shouldn't Be Taken Seriously By Anyone About Anything - SOME MORE NEWS
videos.s: An hour-plus Some More News episode that critiques Ben Shapiro's arguments and record of errors. It is a long, comedic and opinionated breakdown.
videos.w: Occasionally recommended as an in-depth critical take on Shapiro, though mentions are sparse and partisan.
videos.q: you should watch this in-depth breakdown of his perspectives and ideals

videos.t: New vs Old Room Fire Final UL
videos.s: A short NIST-based demonstration places a room furnished with old natural-material furniture beside one with modern synthetic furnishings and burns both. The modern room reaches full flashover in a few minutes while the legacy room is only starting to spread.
videos.w: HN uses it as vivid proof that modern fires develop much faster, which is the argument for working smoke detectors and early escape.
videos.q: Not many more words needed. Just watch

videos.t: Black Hole Star – The Star That Shouldn't Exist
videos.s: Kurzgesagt explains black hole stars, a hypothesized kind of giant star with a black hole at its core that could be a route to early supermassive black holes.
videos.w: HN uses it as a quick, accessible introduction to the black hole star concept in threads about early-universe black holes.
videos.q: Just in case you somehow don’t know what a Black Hole Star is, check out Kurzgesagt’s video about them

videos.t: SpaceX Seattle 2015
videos.s: Full recording of Elon Musk's January 2015 presentation and Q&A at the SpaceX Seattle office announcement. He lays out plans for a satellite constellation to provide low-latency global internet, tied to funding Mars ambitions. Pauses between questions have been edited out.
videos.w: It is the primary source for the original Starlink concept, so commenters cite it for Musk's stated goals on latency, hops, pricing and timelines.
videos.q: Here is a video where elon explains the system very well in 2015.

videos.t: MIX08 Microsoft Office 2007: The Story of the Ribbon
videos.s: A MIX08 session from Microsoft's Office team on how the Office 2007 ribbon was designed. It explains the user-feedback and telemetry behind it and the alternatives that were rejected.
videos.w: HN recommends it for its in-depth view of a major UI redesign process driven by user data.
videos.q: some guys from MS actually talk through the design process and everything that went into it with a lot of depth

videos.t: The Problem With Human Rights
videos.s: A philosophy video critiquing the concept of human rights from a Marxist perspective, drawing on Locke, Marx, Nietzsche, Hegel and Rawls. It examines what human rights actually mean and presuppose.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a deeper philosophical look at human rights from a critical Marxist angle.
videos.q: Jonas Čeika has philosophical deep dive [0] into the topic of human rights worth watching.

videos.t: Reading Silicon: How to Reverse Engineer Integrated Circuits
videos.s: Ken Shirriff walks through how to reverse engineer integrated circuits from die photos, using famous chips as examples, in a Hackaday SuperConference talk.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear account of the craft of reading chips from photographs.
videos.q: The craft is explained nicely in this video

videos.t: Boeing 777 Wing Test
videos.s: A short video of a Boeing 777 wing being tested to destruction, finally breaking at 154 percent of its designed limit load. The wing is flexed upward until it fails.
videos.w: HN links it constantly as vivid evidence of how much margin aircraft structures have and that destructive testing is real.
videos.q: you might find this really interesting

videos.t: The Ultimate V60 Technique
videos.s: James Hoffmann demonstrates his recommended technique for brewing coffee with a Hario V60 or other cone-shaped dripper, with notes on water and filter papers.
videos.w: HN coffee fans recommend it as the reliable, simple recipe for much better pour-over coffee.
videos.q: I highly recommend trying out a V60

videos.t: How to power ANYTHING using USB-C Power Delivery and the ZY12PDN PD Trigger Board
videos.s: Kenneth Finnegan shows how USB-C Power Delivery trigger boards like the ZY12PDN negotiate 5V to 20V so you can power projects from a USB-C charger, including the color coding for each voltage.
videos.w: Recommended as a practical way to get 12V or other voltages from USB-C for hobby projects.
videos.q: These little boards are ultra handy

videos.t: GopherCon 2015: Go GC: Solving the Latency Problem - Rick Hudson
videos.s: Rick Hudson's GopherCon 2015 talk on Go 1.5's new low-latency concurrent garbage collector. It covers the motivation, performance numbers, technical challenges and why the approach fits Go.
videos.w: Pointed to as the authoritative source on Go's GC pause improvements, and later revisited when GC latency claims were challenged.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: you might also find Rick Hudson's talk on GC improvements in Go 1.5 interesting

videos.t: Aldous Huxley interviewed by Mike Wallace : 1958 (Full)
videos.s: Mike Wallace interviews Aldous Huxley in 1958 about the warnings in Brave New World, including mass persuasion, overpopulation and voluntary totalitarianism.
videos.w: Recommended as more thought-provoking than the usual pill-popping take on Huxley.
videos.q: Aldous's pill popping from Brave New World isn't as interesting as what he said in his interview with Mike Wallace

videos.t: Three Beautiful Quicksorts
videos.s: Jon Bentley walks through three implementations of Hoare's Quicksort, from a dozen-line C function to a series of systematic code transformations that make the program ever simpler and more powerful. It is a Google Tech Talk on code elegance and program derivation.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as programming inspiration and as a source of Bentley's anecdotes about adding function by deleting code.
videos.q: If you're looking for programming inspiration I love these videos

videos.t: Making a heart with Maths
videos.s: Inigo Quilez shows step by step how to build a simple heart shape from mathematics and shaders, with code on Shadertoy. It is an introduction to procedural graphics and signed distance functions.
videos.w: HN commenters call it a great beginner-friendly introduction and enjoy watching Quilez work through graphics.
videos.q: is a great introduction for beginners and younger people

videos.t: Unconditional Code • Michael Feathers • GOTO 2018
videos.s: Michael Feathers' GOTO Chicago 2018 talk on reducing error checks and conditional logic in code. He offers a framework for handling errors and decisions at the level of code and architecture.
videos.w: HN recommends it for the idea of giving data instead of asking for it, and ties it to zero values and exception-free design.
videos.q: giving data instead of asking for data avoids error conditions

videos.t: The Secret Reason We Eat Meat - Dr. Melanie Joy
videos.s: Social psychologist Melanie Joy introduces the concept of carnism, the belief system that conditions people to eat some animals but not others.
videos.w: HN offers it as a short, light introduction to carnism and the language bias around eating animals.
videos.q: see this [2] for a light introduction

videos.t: Do these scatter plots reveal fraudulent vote-switching in Michigan?
videos.s: Matt Parker of Stand-up Maths examines scatter plots that were claimed to show fraudulent vote-switching in Michigan's 2020 election. He recreates the analysis and shows that the pattern arises from comparing percentages across different bases, not from fraud.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as a clear debunking of election-fraud statistics and as a warning against comparing percentages without context.
videos.q: here's a video that debunks many of his claims

videos.t: Boeing 737 Unable to Trim!! Cockpit video (Full flight sim)
videos.s: Mentour Pilot, a 737 captain, demonstrates in a full flight simulator why a Boeing 737 can become impossible to trim manually at high speed. He explains the jackscrew forces and the roller-coaster manoeuvre.
videos.w: HN pointed to it during the 737 MAX discussions to show how hard manual trim is when severely out of trim.
videos.q: I had no idea how bad it can actually get

videos.t: These tunnels are designed for 100,000 years
videos.s: Tom Scott visits Onkalo in Finland, the planned deep geologic repository for high-level nuclear waste intended to be sealed for 100,000 years.
videos.w: Recommended in nuclear waste threads as a short, clear look at a real long-term storage solution.
videos.q: Tom Scott has a great video[0] about the Onkalo spent nuclear fuel repository in Finland[1]
