videos.t: DEFCON 19: Bit-squatting: DNS Hijacking Without Exploitation (w speaker)
videos.s: Artem Dinaburg's DEF CON 19 talk on bit-squatting, where flipped bits in DRAM cause devices to contact domains that differ by one bit from legitimate ones. He shows how registering such domains can hijack traffic without exploiting any software bug.
videos.w: HN cites it in ECC memory debates and bit-flip discussions as concrete evidence that memory errors have real security consequences.
videos.q: There was a good Defcon talk about some security implications of this phenomenon

videos.t: We all move at the Speed of Light
videos.s: ScienceClic explains why nothing can go faster than light by treating motion through space and time together, so everything moves at the speed of light through spacetime. It uses animated visuals to cover relativity basics in 12 minutes.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a helpful way to conceptualize why light speed is a limit.
videos.q: I know a lot of people find this video helpful in conceptualizing things.

videos.t: The horrible truth about Apple's repeated engineering failures.
videos.s: Louis Rossmann, a Macbook repair shop owner, goes through a long list of Apple hardware engineering failures, from GPU defects to keyboards and repair practices.
videos.w: Mostly cited by critics of Apple hardware quality, and as a rabbit hole for people curious about laptop repair.
videos.q: Louis Rossmann made a video highlighting a lot of the engineering problems with Apple laptops.

videos.t: How to Make a DIY Air Filter | Ask This Old House
videos.s: This Old House's Ross Trethewey explains MERV filter ratings and how air filtration works, then shows how to build a localized DIY air filter, including a box fan with multiple filters.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a practical breakdown of filtration versus air volume and a clever box-fan filter design.
videos.q: This Old House has a really good breakdown on filtration and air volume and have a pretty clever DIY box fan approach using multiple filters.

videos.t: How To Visit STARBASE // A Complete Guide To Seeing Starship!
videos.s: Everyday Astronaut's guide to visiting Starbase, Texas to see Starship, covering what and where it is, which areas close during launches, where to watch from, where to fly into and stay, and things to do.
videos.w: Recommended as the practical guide for anyone planning to attend a Starship launch in person.
videos.q: Everyday Astronaut did a great writeup on seeing a launch in South Texas

videos.t: Why We Can't Have Small Trucks Anymore - Blame the EPA
videos.s: All Cars with Jon explains how EPA fuel economy rules, especially the footprint-based CAFE formula, push automakers away from small trucks.
videos.w: Cited in threads on vehicle bloat as the explanation for why small pickups disappeared in the US.
videos.q: explains why small pickup trucks can't really be sold in the USA anymore

videos.t: Why There are Now So Many Shortages (It's Not COVID)
videos.s: Wendover Productions explains the wave of supply shortages in 2021, arguing the causes go beyond COVID. It covers how just-in-time manufacturing was applied, container imbalances and the chip shortage.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a better explanation of just-in-time versus the Toyota Way and of container and chip shortages.
videos.q: see for a much better explanation than I could provide

videos.t: Chris Seaton @ VMSS16: JRuby+Truffle: Why it’s Important to Optimise the Tricky Parts
videos.s: Chris Seaton talks about JRuby+Truffle, explaining how the Truffle and Graal combination optimises the tricky parts of Ruby and why it outperforms other Ruby implementations.
videos.w: HN recommends it for specifics on how Truffle and Graal achieve strong dynamic-language performance.
videos.q: Chris Seaton gave this talk recently about JRuby+Truffle and some specifics about how it optimises so well compared to other Ruby implementations.

videos.t: Apple - iMac G4 "Lamp" ad (2002)
videos.s: Apple's 2002 television ad for the iMac G4 "Lamp", showing the adjustable-arm design in a playful way.
videos.w: Cited in iMac G4 threads as a charming ad reminiscent of Pixar's Luxo Jr.
videos.q: I still remember this ad for the G4 which feels very similar to Luxo Jr. from Pixar. Really fun.

videos.t: Springboard: the secret history of the first real smartphone (Full Documentary)
videos.s: The Verge's documentary on Handspring and its Treo, a smartphone that came a decade before the iPhone. It tells how a small team tried to build the modern smartphone and was held back by carriers and timing.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an interview-rich history of Handspring, Palm OS and why telcos hurt early smartphones.
videos.q: Nice documentary about this with interviews

videos.t: Amazon Sells Fake Electrical Fuses
videos.s: Louis Rossmann examines fuses sold on Amazon that fail to trip at their rated current, including a 2A fuse surviving 8 amps. He uses it to criticize Amazon's lax control over safety-relevant products.
videos.w: HN cites it as the key example of Amazon selling dangerous counterfeit goods and warns people to test their fuses.
videos.q: This video gives a good overview of how Amazon's NGAF attitude about safety needs to be reigned in.

videos.t: PHILOSOPHY - Michel Foucault
videos.s: A School of Life short introducing Michel Foucault, who questioned assumed progress in how society treats madness, medicine and sexuality.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a simple entry point to Foucault, especially on mental health and institutionalization.
videos.q: I recommend you watch the following video on Foucault

videos.t: Billion Dollar Bully: Yelp documentary producers Kaylie Milliken & Mellissa Wood
videos.s: Louis Rossmann interviews Kaylie Milliken and Mellissa Wood, producers of the documentary Billion Dollar Bully, about Yelp's alleged practices toward businesses.
videos.w: Recommended as a good conversation and starting point on Yelp's alleged bullying of businesses.
videos.q: he talks with two of the people behind the movie Billion Dollar Bully.

videos.t: International Colloquia #26:  Fusion Reactor First Wall Cooling
videos.s: An MIT colloquium by Dennis Whyte on power exhaust and first-wall cooling in fusion reactors, including recent innovations and the SPARC and ARC designs.
videos.w: Recommended for realistic engineering detail on extracting heat from a tokamak.
videos.q: This is the best recent video I've seen, about SPARC and ARC.

videos.t: Colonizing Venus
videos.s: Isaac Arthur examines options for colonizing Venus, from vast floating habitats in the temperate upper atmosphere to full terraforming of the planet. It is a long-form speculative futurism episode in his solar system colonization series.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as the go-to reference for the idea of living in Venus's atmosphere rather than on the surface.
videos.q: Caution: don't click unless you have nothing else to do today.

videos.t: How To Uninstall McAfee Antivirus
videos.s: A bizarre, tongue-in-cheek video in which John McAfee himself supposedly shows how to uninstall McAfee antivirus. It is known for its NSFW sex and drug references.
videos.w: HN mostly cites it as a notorious piece of McAfee lore, usually jokingly, whenever John McAfee or antivirus uninstallation comes up.
videos.q: At least he's got a sense of humor.

videos.t: Web Development in Emacs, Common Lisp and Clojurescript - Emacs SG
videos.s: Elias Martenson presents his Emacs-based workflow for building a web application (the Potato chat platform) with Common Lisp on the backend and ClojureScript on the frontend. He demonstrates SLIME, Paredit, CIDER and debugger-driven interactive development. The talk is 79 minutes and was given at Emacs SG.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a live demonstration of interactive Lisp development, including compiling single functions in a running program and debugger-driven workflows.
videos.q: This video also has great examples of other crazy interactive development workflows and is worth watching in its entirety

videos.t: How to design an actually good toaster with lessons from the 1940's
videos.s: Technology Connections praises a 1940s-50s Sunbeam toaster and explains what makes a toaster well designed, drawing on a vintage Sunbeam video.
videos.w: Recommended as a passionate take on good appliance design and cited in toaster threads.
videos.q: This one about Sunbeam toasters from 50+ years ago is particularly great

videos.t: Bill Hader impersonates Arnold Schwarzenegger [DeepFake]
videos.s: A deepfake in which Bill Hader, impersonating Arnold Schwarzenegger on a talk show, visibly morphs into Schwarzenegger. It was made with DeepFaceLab by Ctrl Shift Face.
videos.w: Pointed to as one of the most impressive early deepfakes, where a good impersonation makes the effect convincing and funny.
videos.q: this DeepFake video (SFW) is the most impressive I've seen so far

videos.t: Nest Protect is a terrible buggy product
videos.s: Brad Fitzpatrick records himself struggling to silence a set of first-generation Nest Protect smoke alarms that keep beeping and triggering one another.
videos.w: HN cites it as the famous example of how over-clever smart-home devices can fail at something as basic as a smoke alarm.
videos.q: on an artistic level it is really well done, it is an epic battle between human and machine.

videos.t: How to Become TripAdvisor’s #1 Fake Restaurant
videos.s: VICE's Oobah Butler spends eight months using fake reviews to push a nonexistent restaurant, The Shed at Dulwich, to number one on TripAdvisor in London. The short documentary shows how easily review systems can be gamed.
videos.w: Cited as the canonical example of fake reviews and gamed rating platforms.
videos.q: I'd recommend watching the Vice video I found in another comment

videos.t: BeOS DEMO VIDEO
videos.s: The official demo video from Be, Inc. showing BeOS running multiple videos, media applications and a responsive desktop on 1990s hardware.
videos.w: HN people cite it as evidence of how fast and responsive a well-designed microkernel desktop could be on modest hardware.
videos.q: Tell me why microkernels are too slow when they can only do this on 90's era hardware

videos.t: Blue Bubbles vs Green Bubbles: Explained!
videos.s: Marques Brownlee explains why iMessage's blue and green bubbles matter, covering the technical, commercial and social side of Apple's messaging lock-in. It also discusses RCS and what could be done about it.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as an eloquent, well-rounded summary of the blue-versus-green bubble issue.
videos.q: Marques Brownlee has a video[0] that discusses the technical, commercial, and social aspects.

videos.t: Passion | David Mitchell's SoapBox
videos.s: David Mitchell's Soapbox rant on employers who demand passion and enthusiasm from workers, using satire to skewer fake workplace passion.
videos.w: HN people share it as a funny and apt take whenever job postings or recruiters demand passion.
videos.q: David Mitchell had a very good take on it.

videos.t: Node.js Is Bad Ass Rock Star Tech
videos.s: A short satirical sketch in which a Q&A about web servers turns into a profane rant about threads, blocking and non-blocking I/O. It lampoons the hype around Node.js and async programming.
videos.w: HN mostly drops it as a joke in async, Node and concurrency threads, and some call it hysterically funny.
videos.q: Watch the very NSFW (lots of swearing) but hysterically funny video

videos.t: David Kriesel: Lies, damned lies and scans
videos.c: Free and Open Source Software Conference (FrOSCon) e.V.
videos.s: David Kriesel's FrOSCon talk on how Xerox scancopiers, due to JBIG2 compression, silently replaced digits in scanned documents. He walks through how he discovered the bug and why it is so dangerous.
videos.w: The standard reference whenever HN discusses the Xerox scanner bug or AI and compression that fabricates content.
videos.q: There a few videos of David Kriesel explaining the bug for the curious

videos.t: MOLTEN GLASS VS Prince Rupert's Drop - Smarter Every Day 285
videos.s: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day explores molten glass and Prince Rupert's drops with a glass artist, including a process that freezes the moment glass shatters and an artisan who makes the drops.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for the striking glass-shattering visuals and the artist's attitude of treating failure as a space for discovery.
videos.q: Learn about and see how it’s made

videos.t: Dispelling the Myths of Nuclear Energy (Live Lecture)
videos.s: A lecture for high school seniors and college freshmen making the case for nuclear power and answering common objections. It is an overview of the channel's more detailed videos on each topic.
videos.w: Pointed to as a lay-audience explanation of nuclear waste, safety and economics.
videos.q: Not only is it solvable, it's basically been solved for years.

videos.t: Problems with gas stovetops | weak, dirty and dangerous
videos.s: Food YouTuber Adam Ragusea argues that gas stovetops are weaker than electric burners, dirty to clean, and a health risk from indoor air pollution. He cites Consumer Reports ratings and a literature review on gas stove health effects.
videos.w: Cited as an accessible overview of the case against gas cooktops in threads on cooking, induction and indoor air quality.
videos.q: Great coverage of this entire issue

videos.t: Why Web Filters Don't Work: Penistone and the Scunthorpe Problem
videos.s: Tom Scott visits Penistone to explain the Scunthorpe problem, showing why naive web and profanity filters block innocent words.
videos.w: The go-to explainer whenever content filters wrongly flag innocent words, well made and short.
videos.q: He talks about how it's impossible to implement with all edge-cases, easy to circumvent

videos.t: Agile Project Management with Kanban | Eric Brechner | Talks at Google
videos.s: Eric Brechner, a Microsoft Xbox development manager, presents his Kanban approach for agile project management at Talks at Google. He covers using sticky notes to organize work, estimate and meet deadlines.
videos.w: Recommended as a clear description of how Kanban works and a practical alternative to sprints.
videos.q: Eric Brechner of Microsoft (of all possible places...) gives a great talk on his team's approach

videos.t: Exact Instructions Challenge - THIS is why my kids hate me. | Josh Darnit
videos.s: A family video in which kids write instructions for making a peanut butter and jelly sandwich and a parent follows them exactly as written, with comic results. It demonstrates how precise instructions must be.
videos.w: HN uses it to teach kids computational thinking and as a joke whenever specs, requirements, or LLM prompts are taken too literally.
videos.q: this video is a great way to show how difficult it is to teach a machine to do something and how clear instructions can help get things done

videos.t: U.S. Territories: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: A Last Week Tonight segment on how century-old Supreme Court decisions left U.S. territories such as Puerto Rico, Guam and American Samoa without meaningful representation. It mixes comedy with a history of their legal status.
videos.w: HN people use it as a quick, entertaining primer on territory status, citizenship versus nationality, and voting rights.
videos.q: John Oliver has a great, 13-min segment on U.S. territories

videos.t: Why Western Designs Fail in Developing Countries
videos.s: A design essay on why products designed in Western contexts often fail when deployed in developing countries. It covers expert blindness and cultural assumptions, with examples such as malaria nets and the One Laptop Per Child project.
videos.w: Commenters cite it to explain expert blindness and the difficulty of solving problems from inside your own cultural context.
videos.q: explains a general problem (that of trying to solve problems that are more prevalent elsewhere in the world, from within your own cultural context)

videos.t: A conversation with Elon Musk about Starship
videos.s: Tim Dodd of Everyday Astronaut talks with Elon Musk right after Musk's 2019 Starship presentation. Musk discusses Starship's design, why SpaceX favors conventional engines over aerospikes, and how deleting parts and processes speeds up development.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as evidence of Musk's engineering thinking, on questioning requirements, organizational errors mirroring product errors, and Conway's Law, and to argue about whether he is a strong engineer.
videos.q: Here's an interesting interview the author did with Elon Musk

videos.t: "Systems that run forever self-heal and scale" by Joe Armstrong (2013)
videos.s: Joe Armstrong's Strange Loop 2013 talk on building large scalable systems from small isolated parallel components. It covers detecting and correcting errors at run time, changing code while it runs, and how Erlang embodies these principles.
videos.w: Pointed to as the canonical pitch for Erlang's fault-tolerance and self-healing model.
videos.q: is a great talk too.

videos.t: Thermoelectric cooling: it's not great.
videos.s: Technology Connections explains in 33 minutes why thermoelectric (Peltier) cooling is far less efficient than compressor-based refrigeration.
videos.w: It is the standard link whenever a new Peltier or thermoelectric cooling breakthrough is posted.
videos.q: they are _massively_ less efficient.

videos.t: Everything Is A Remix (Full Film)
videos.s: Kirby Ferguson's film argues that creativity is built from copying, transforming and combining existing works, examining music, film and technology. It makes the case that everything is a remix.
videos.w: HN brings it up in discussions of originality, invention, copying and attribution, including AI art.
videos.q: You will enjoy this documentary (Everything a Remix).

videos.t: 15 Lazygit Features In Under 15 Minutes
videos.s: The author of lazygit demos 15 features of his terminal UI for git, such as staging individual lines and easier rebasing, aimed at making common git tasks simpler.
videos.w: Recommended as the author's own quick intro to lazygit, a TUI that makes git workflows more natural.
videos.q: There is a nice video from the author that introduces a lot of its features.

videos.t: Duolingo -- the next chapter in human computation |  Luis von Ahn | TEDxCMU 2011
videos.s: Luis von Ahn, creator of CAPTCHA and reCAPTCHA, presents Duolingo at TEDxCMU 2011. The idea is to have millions of people translate the web for free while learning a language, an example of human computation.
videos.w: HN people recommend it as a look at how to get people to eagerly do useful collective work, and as the origin of Duolingo.
videos.q: First thing: Watch this video from Luis von Ahn

videos.t: [Linux.conf.au 2013] - The real story behind Wayland and X
videos.s: A linux.conf.au 2013 talk by a Wayland developer who previously worked on X, telling the history of X and why Wayland was created. It covers X's hardware abstraction and architecture and why they became problematic for modern graphics.
videos.w: Whenever Wayland versus X comes up, HN points to this talk as the authoritative explanation from an X maintainer of why X was replaced.
videos.q: a great presentation by one of the guys behind wayland, who worked on X a lot before

videos.t: Ralph Langner: Cracking Stuxnet, a 21st-century cyber weapon
videos.s: In an 11-minute TED talk, Ralph Langner explains how his team reverse-engineered the Stuxnet worm and worked out that it targeted industrial control systems, with a covert state origin. It is a compact look at cyber-forensics.
videos.w: HN points people to it as the short, accessible account of how Stuxnet was dissected, usually when Stuxnet or state-sponsored malware comes up.
videos.q: The Stuxnet TED talk [0] was really interesting

videos.t: 2017 LLVM Developers’ Meeting: “Implementing Swift Generics ”
videos.s: Swift compiler engineers explain how Swift implements generics using dictionary-passing with reified type metadata. They compare it with Java-style uniform representation and C++ or Rust monomorphization.
videos.w: Recommended as the clearest explanation of how Swift generics compile and how that differs from other languages.
videos.q: there's a very nice talk on how Swift's generics compile.

videos.t: RustConf 2017 - Closing Keynote: Safe Systems Software and the Future of Computing by Joe Duffy
videos.s: Joe Duffy's RustConf 2017 closing keynote on his experience at Microsoft building Midori, an operating system written in a Rust-like safe systems language. He covers the technical and cultural challenges of applying those lessons to Windows.
videos.w: HN repeatedly cites it for Midori lessons: compatibility matters for adoption, and the Windows team stayed sceptical even with Midori running real workloads.
videos.cn: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.q: I summarized this excellent talk here [1], but one of the main points is that compatibility with existing systems is important for adoption.

videos.t: Money creation in the modern economy - Quarterly Bulletin
videos.s: A short Bank of England video accompanying its 2014 Quarterly Bulletin article on money creation. It explains that most money is bank deposits and that commercial banks create new money by making loans, which simultaneously create matching deposits.
videos.w: HN people use it as an authoritative, plain-English source from a central bank that loans create deposits, rather than banks lending out saved money.
videos.q: Some of the content is in this short video

videos.t: The Great 202 Jailbreak - Computerphile
videos.s: Computerphile with Professor Brailsford on how a 1979 Bell Labs team reverse engineered a Linotron 202 phototypesetter over a summer to get high-quality print output. It covers typesetting history and the later 2013 rebuild of the famous vacation memo.
videos.w: Recommended alongside the original paper and Unix history threads as an engaging account of the typesetter hack.
videos.q: explained the brilliant and exiting history of this paper and its recreation, as well as the history of Phototypesetters.

videos.t: J.S.Bach "The Goldberg Variations" [ Glenn Gould ] (1955)
videos.s: Glenn Gould's 1955 recording of Bach's Goldberg Variations, uploaded as a continuous performance of about 39 minutes.
videos.w: Recommended as the best-known and most famous recording of the Goldberg Variations.
videos.q: Glenn Gould's 1955 recording is perhaps the best known recording of this work

videos.t: 5 Hours of The Shipping Forecast on BBC Radio 4!
videos.s: Five hours of the late-night BBC Radio 4 Shipping Forecast, uploaded to mark its 150th anniversary. It can be used as sleep audio or to learn the sea areas named in the broadcast.
videos.w: Offered as a calming, dry, familiar broadcast, fitting for a crowd that enjoys ambient and lofi radio.
videos.q: Obligatory BBC Shipping Forecast, because it seems right up this crowd's alley

videos.t: How Semiconductors Ruined East Germany
videos.s: Asianometry examines how East Germany tried and failed to build a native semiconductor industry despite heavy investment, including the espionage involved in acquiring Western microelectronics technology.
videos.w: HN commenters share it in chip fab and industrial espionage threads as a well-researched account of East Germany's failed microelectronics effort.
videos.q: this is a well researched video by Asianometry, which actually contains a couple of details (unlike the Politico article) about the spycraft involved

videos.t: Container Hacks and Fun Images
videos.s: Jessie Frazelle's DockerCon SF 2015 talk on running Docker containers for desktop applications, with fun container hacks and images. It shows how far containers can be pushed beyond servers.
videos.w: HN points to it as an illuminating look at what containers really are and as a video companion to running desktop apps in Docker.
videos.q: If you prefer video format, Jessie also has a talk at DockerCon SF 2015

videos.t: Experiment! How Does An Owl Fly So Silently? | Super Powered Owls | BBC
videos.s: A BBC Earth clip from Super Powered Owls in which the team uses sensitive sound equipment to compare owl flight with other birds. It shows why owls fly almost silently.
videos.w: Linked in owl-feather and quiet-flight threads as a clear audio comparison.
videos.q: To really appreciate how silent Owls are as compared to other birds, see this excellent video from BBC

videos.t: Does It Make Sense To Put Data Centers In Space? Can They Really Cost Less To Operate?
videos.s: Scott Manley analyzes the idea of putting data centers in orbit, prompted by Lumen Orbit's funding. He examines the claimed advantage of constant solar power against launch cost, cooling and mass.
videos.w: Recommended in orbital data center threads as a sober explanation of why the idea doesn't work out economically or thermally.
videos.q: The great Scott Manley did a video about that

videos.t: SpaceX's plan to fly you across the globe in 30 minutes | Gwynne Shotwell
videos.s: A TED conversation with SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell about the company's race to put people in orbit and the BFR rocket. It also covers the idea of using the rocket for fast point-to-point travel on Earth.
videos.w: Pointed to in SpaceX threads as a window into the company's ambitions and leadership.
videos.q: Another interesting watch is the TED talk by SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell earlier this year.

videos.t: Why Everyone Is Talking About Data Centers In Space
videos.s: Scott Manley examines why SpaceX, Google and others are looking at orbital data centers. He walks through the economics, heat rejection and solar power arguments, with links to the Lumen/Starcloud and Google Suncatcher papers.
videos.w: Pointed to as a credible, engineering-informed answer to whether space data centers are feasible, from someone with deep space knowledge.
videos.q: Scott Manley had a really good video on it

videos.t: 36C3 -  The ecosystem is moving
videos.s: Moxie Marlinspike's 36C3 talk examines why distributed and decentralized technology is hard to build into consumer products, from the perspective of developing Signal. It argues that ecosystems move slowly and federation causes problems.
videos.w: Cited in decentralization and federation debates as the key talk on the practical challenges, though some found it defeatist.
videos.q: A talk by Moxie at CCC deals with this exact question.

videos.t: Planes clouds and vortices
videos.s: A short compilation of aircraft flying through clouds and moist air, showing the spiraling vortices that wings leave behind. The footage shows wingtip vortices and the way planes disturb cloud layers.
videos.w: HN commenters link it as a visual illustration of wingtip vortices and wake turbulence when discussing lift and aircraft wakes.
videos.q: the spiraling wingtip vortices which can be observed in this neat video

videos.t: What Happened Before History? Human Origins
videos.s: Kurzgesagt's animated overview of human origins and the vast prehistory before recorded history. It covers how modern humans emerged and spread.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a compact, well-sourced intro to human evolution that even led one viewer to read Sapiens.
videos.q: there is a great 10 minute video from the Youtube Kurzgesagt channel that lead me to read Sapiens.

videos.t: Apollo 11 Saturn V Launch Camera E-8
videos.s: Raw 500 fps footage from Camera E-8 on the launch tower for the Apollo 11 Saturn V liftoff, transferred in HD from the 16mm original. More than eight minutes of film covers about 30 seconds of real time.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it for its slow-motion view of the first seconds of liftoff and cite it when comparing launch pads and engine behavior.
videos.q: It explains the sequence of events over the course of 8+ minutes (30 seconds real time).

videos.t: JuliaRobotics: Making robots walk with Julia | Robin Deits
videos.s: Robin Deits presents the JuliaRobotics organization and shows how Julia is used to visualize, simulate and control a humanoid robot. The talk touches on real-time performance and composability across packages.
videos.w: Julia fans point to it as a concrete example of Julia working for soft real-time robotics, especially when avoiding heap allocation.
videos.q: There's a nice talk here [1] about using julia in soft-real-time for robotics.

videos.t: Elm Europe 2017 - Richard Feldman - Scaling Elm Apps
videos.s: Richard Feldman's Elm Europe 2017 talk on how to structure and scale large Elm applications, including when to nest messages.
videos.w: The standard pointer for anyone asking how to organize larger Elm codebases.
videos.q: Just watch rfeldman's talks about how to structure large Elm projects

videos.t: Departing Space Station Commander Provides Tour of Orbital Laboratory
videos.s: In her final days as ISS commander, Sunita Williams gives an extensive tour of the station's modules and research facilities, narrating the work done aboard.
videos.w: Recommended as a great, understandable tour of life and equipment aboard the International Space Station.
videos.q: There's a great 25 minute tour of the ISS by Sunita Williams on NASA's YouTube channel

videos.t: Jolene at 33 rpm
videos.s: Dolly Parton's song Jolene, slowed down to 33 rpm so that it sounds deeper and more drawn out. The short clip is a well-known example of how pitch-shifting changes a song's mood.
videos.w: HN people point to it as a slowed-down song that sounds more plaintive and haunting.
videos.q: Hearing it at 33 rpm [0] is a different experience still: it's almost more plaintive, more haunting. Worth a listen IMO.

videos.t: China's 7nm Chips: SMIC N+2
videos.s: Asianometry's short analysis of SMIC's N+2 node, China's 7nm leap forward. It considers how far behind the competition SMIC still is.
videos.w: Recommended as a high-level, in-depth take on SMIC's 7nm progress and Asian chip manufacturing.
videos.q: Probably one of the best high level insights into tech mfg in Asia.

videos.t: "Code is the Easy Part" by Evan Czaplicki
videos.s: Evan Czaplicki, creator of Elm, gives an elm-conf 2016 talk on the non-code side of building a language. It covers the philosophy behind Elm's development approach, including batching work and the priorities of different language communities.
videos.w: HN points people to it to understand Elm's design philosophy, such as favoring simplicity over type classes, when they question its choices.
videos.q: great talk by Evan Czaplicki and his approach to Elm development

videos.t: 27c3: Console Hacking 2010 (en)
videos.s: The fail0verflow team (bushing, marcan, sven) present console hacking at 27C3, covering Wii, Xbox 360 and PS3 exploits. They explain how the PS3 was cracked after Sony removed Other OS.
videos.w: HN recommends it as the primary source on Sony's ECDSA nonce-reuse blunder and the history of console cracking.
videos.q: I recommend watching the Console Hacking talk at 27c3 by the fail0verflow team

videos.t: How are Microchips Made? 🖥️🛠️ CPU Manufacturing Process Steps
videos.s: Branch Education walks through a semiconductor fab and the dozens of steps used to turn silicon wafers into microchips, with 3D animation. It covers lithography, deposition and etching at a high level.
videos.w: Pointed to as a clear visual reference for chip manufacturing steps.
videos.q: the Branch Education YouTube channel has great videos detailing the manufacturing process as well

videos.t: Tinder Experiment: 18 Yr Old Woman Tries Being A Man!!!
videos.s: A social experiment in which an 18-year-old woman runs a Tinder profile as a man and sees how differently the dating experience plays out for men.
videos.w: HN brings it up in dating app threads as a real-world illustration of how hard Tinder is for men.
videos.q: I loved the Youtube video where a woman tries to impersonate a man and get a date with women on a dating app.

videos.t: The hidden background noise that can catch criminals
videos.s: Tom Scott explains Electrical Network Frequency analysis, where hum from the power grid in a recording is matched against grid logs to date and place it. He talks to a researcher and sets them a challenge.
videos.w: The go-to short, accessible explainer for mains hum forensics, linked whenever recording authenticity or timestamps come up.
videos.q: less detailed but pretty accessible video [1] explaining how mains hum forensics work

videos.t: How We Should Vote (Range Voting)
videos.s: A six-minute explainer from Undefined Behavior on range (score) voting. It follows an earlier video on Arrow's Theorem and shows how range voting seems to satisfy the criteria Arrow's Theorem says no ranked system can.
videos.w: HN commenters link it in voting-reform discussions as a concise explanation of range voting versus other systems.
videos.q: The following video covers 'Range Voting' in relation to Arrow's Theorem

videos.t: Touché: Enhancing Touch Interaction on Humans, Screens, Liquids, and Everyday Objects
videos.s: Disney Research presents Touche, a swept frequency capacitive sensing technique that recognizes complex hand and body configurations, and adds touch sensitivity to humans, liquids and everyday objects.
videos.w: Brought up as an early example of context-aware touch sensing and as part of Disney Research's wider interaction prototypes.
videos.q: Basically the idea is to make devices aware of the physical context of user interactions.

videos.t: Shenzhen: A New Breed of Intellectual Property (Part 3) | Future Cities | WIRED
videos.s: Part 3 of WIRED's Future Cities series on Shenzhen. It examines how attitudes toward patents and intellectual property differ from the West, and how shanzhai (copycat) manufacturing created an ecosystem of rapid iteration and distribution.
videos.w: HN commenters point to it as a snapshot of Shenzhen's hardware and IP culture, including counterfeit electronics and fast iteration.
videos.q: A shoutout to a new video series from WIRED on Shenzhen.

videos.t: The 100 Year Flood Is Not What You Think It Is (Maybe)
videos.s: Practical Engineering explains what a 100-year flood actually means, combining statistics, hydrology and how society treats risk. Grady walks through local drainage infrastructure and the caveats in estimating flood probability.
videos.w: HN points to it as a clear explanation of what flood return periods really mean.
videos.q: Grady (of the Practical Engineering YouTube channel) has a great video on this topic

videos.t: The KGB, the Computer, and Me (Complete)
videos.s: The 1990 NOVA documentary follows astronomer Clifford Stoll as he tracks a hacker through military and research computer networks, a story that involved the CIA and KGB. It is based on The Cuckoo's Egg.
videos.w: HN lists it among favorite nerdy documentaries and enjoys hearing Stoll tell the story himself.
videos.q: It was really great, getting to hear it from Mr. Stoll's mouth directly.

videos.t: Quants | The Alchemists of Wall Street | VPRO documentary
videos.s: A VPRO documentary on quantitative analysts who designed the mathematical models and high-speed trading systems behind modern finance. It features figures such as Paul Wilmott and asks what risks come from treating markets as a machine.
videos.w: HN recommends it as an insider-style look at quants and high-frequency trading and their effect on markets.
videos.q: just to get an insider look into quant traders and the effect HFT can have on the market, I also recommend these two short documentaries

videos.t: The RIGHT Way to Handle a Police Stop
videos.s: A short video advising how to handle a police stop by politely refusing searches and not answering questions, citing Fourth and Fifth Amendment rights.
videos.w: HN points to it as a companion to Don't Talk to the Police for knowing your rights during stops.
videos.q: This video is also useful,

videos.t: Nuclear Propulsion in Space
videos.s: A 1968 NASA film from the US National Archives explaining why the US needed a nuclear rocket and how the engine works. It also shows combined nuclear and chemical stages for a manned Mars mission.
videos.w: HN people link it as an old-timey explainer for nuclear thermal propulsion, and as evidence these engines were already built and tested.
videos.q: This video is worth checking out if you haven’t seen it yet.

videos.t: Ryan Dahl: Node JS
videos.s: Ryan Dahl's JSConf EU talk introducing Node.js to the world. He explains the motivation for event-driven, non-blocking I/O, with JavaScript chosen mainly for its asynchronous nature.
videos.w: Cited as the primary source for why Node exists and why JavaScript was chosen, in debates about async models and language choice.
videos.q: it's kind of refreshing to see the original node.js presentation, where using javascript is sort of a side-note

videos.t: The benefits of deploying IPv6 only
videos.s: A NANOG 64 panel with speakers from Comcast, APNIC, T-Mobile and Facebook on deploying IPv6-only networks, including performance data showing IPv6 outperforming NAT-ed IPv4.
videos.w: Cited as real operator data that IPv6 is faster than IPv4 and that large networks are already going IPv6-only.
videos.q: Watch Paul Saab from Facebook talk about how much better IPv6 performs at NANOG 64

videos.t: Alan Kay: A powerful idea about teaching ideas
videos.s: Alan Kay's TED talk on teaching ideas, in which he argues the world is not what it seems and shows children learning through programming and building their own lessons with Etoys/Squeak.
videos.w: Recommended as a condensed version of Kay's ideas on education and computing, showing kids using software to explore physics and robotics.
videos.q: You'll see kids using the software to explore robotics and do physics of gravitation.

videos.t: Swami Sarvapriyananda at IITK - "Who Am I?" according to Mandukya Upanishad-Part 1
videos.s: A lecture by Swami Sarvapriyananda at IIT Kanpur on the Mandukya Upanishad and the question 'Who am I?'. It explains the four states of consciousness in Advaita Vedanta.
videos.w: Recommended in threads about consciousness and reality as a clear exposition of the Vedantic view of waking, dreaming and deep sleep.
videos.q: These two lectures were very good

videos.t: Game Theory: How PewDiePie Conquered YouTube
videos.s: The Game Theorists analyze how PewDiePie rose to become the most subscribed channel on YouTube. The video looks at why let's plays and gaming channels thrive on the platform.
videos.w: HN commenters cite it as an analysis of PewDiePie's popularity and of how YouTube's recommendations favored gaming content.
videos.q: Here's a video with some interesting theories about how PewDiePie, and other gaming channels, are so popular

videos.t: 1. Introduction for 15.S12 Blockchain and Money, Fall 2018
videos.s: The opening lecture of MIT's Blockchain and Money course taught by Gary Gensler, covering the course plan, the history of failed digital currencies, cryptography and what a blockchain is.
videos.w: Recommended as a solid, level-headed academic introduction to blockchain, often noted because Gensler later led the SEC.
videos.q: I've been enjoying a playlist of blockchain lectures by Gary Gensler

videos.t: The Wright Brothers DID Invent the Airplane
videos.s: A long rebuttal arguing that the Wright Brothers truly invented the airplane, responding to other YouTubers who credit others. It walks through the engineering breakthroughs the Wrights achieved, such as control and wind tunnel work.
videos.w: HN commenters use it as a well-researched account of what the Wrights actually solved, in threads on airplane physics and invention credit.
videos.q: This video has a nice delineation of the collection of breakthroughs needed

videos.t: ShaderToy LiveCoding - The Drive Home - 1. Basic Setup
videos.s: The first part of a ShaderToy live-coding series that lays the groundwork for The Drive Home, a rainy night-traffic shader. It covers basic setup and builds toward rain and bokeh effects.
videos.w: Recommended in shader and rain-simulation threads as an engaging tutorial from a well-liked graphics-programming channel.
videos.q: The accompanying video tutorial[2] is super interesting too

videos.t: Vibe coding complex changes in Rust
videos.s: Jon Gjengset spends about three hours livecoding complex changes in a Rust codebase with agentic AI tools, testing his hypothesis that AI is weak at non-pattern work. He documents where Claude Code helps and where it struggles.
videos.w: Pointed to as a non-promotional, realistic long session of an experienced engineer working with AI on non-trivial code.
videos.q: I found this one and sat down and watched the whole three hours.

videos.t: The Fall of Minecraft's 2b2t
videos.s: FitMC tells how the Nocom exploit let griefers track players across Minecraft's oldest anarchy server, 2b2t, and the fallout that followed.
videos.w: Cited as the original, accurate account of the Nocom exploit, a story of years of player tracking and impressive technical work.
videos.q: it details a story of gaslighting, 3 years of player data, and some really really impressive technical work

videos.t: Strong Towns | Charles Marohn | Talks at Google
videos.s: Charles Marohn of Strong Towns presents, in a Talks at Google session, the ideas from his book on why many North American towns struggle financially despite decades of growth. He argues for incremental, bottom-up city building as a path to local prosperity.
videos.w: HN commenters link it in housing and urbanism threads as a clear explanation of unsustainable car-oriented development and fragile systems.
videos.q: It has a great explanation of the difference between complex and complicated

videos.t: React.js Conf 2015 - Beyond the DOM: How Netflix plans to enhance your television experience
videos.s: Jafar Husain of Netflix explains at React.js Conf 2015 how Netflix runs React-style rendering without the DOM on smart TVs and game consoles. It uses a canvas-like API for performance.
videos.w: Cited as the primary source on React with a custom rendering backend and on Netflix's Gibbon engine.
videos.q: There's an interesting video by Netflix where they discuss using React in their stack.

videos.t: Oral History of Chuck Peddle
videos.s: A Computer History Museum oral history of Chuck Peddle, the engineer behind the 6502 and the Commodore PET, covering his career from GE through Motorola and MOS Technology. It runs nearly four hours.
videos.w: Used as a primary source for 6502 origins, pricing strategy and Commodore history.
videos.q: You might also like the Computer History Museum interview w/Bill Mensch

videos.t: [Highlight] StarCraft Remastered Rant
videos.s: Day9 gives a passionate first look at what his StarCraft: Brood War Remastered series will teach. He argues Brood War is primarily a real-time game and only secondarily a strategy game, making the commander fantasy a matter of mechanics.
videos.w: HN uses it to argue that mechanical difficulty and limited attention are integral to RTS strategy, especially in StarCraft AI threads.
videos.q: day[9] (ex Broodwar pro, current caster of many games) probably makes the argument better than I can here

videos.t: Evidence-Based Weight Loss: Live Presentation
videos.s: Dr. Michael Greger gives a live presentation on evidence-based weight loss, previewing his book How Not to Diet. He focuses on foods that aid weight loss while also supporting health and longevity.
videos.w: HN commenters share it as a helpful lecture on plant-based weight loss and which foods to experiment with.
videos.q: I also find this lecture helpful for thinking about foods to experiment with

videos.t: The Battle of the Diets: Is Anyone Winning (At Losing?)
videos.s: Stanford's Christopher Gardner presents his large, long comparison of four popular diets under real-world conditions, in which the lowest-carbohydrate Atkins diet came out on top.
videos.w: Recommended as a researcher presenting actual diet-study results, including a trial with 311 women on different diet books.
videos.q: Here's a researcher presenting the results of their study as well as discussing several others[1].

videos.t: Jacob Collier Explains Music in 5 Levels of Difficulty ft. Herbie Hancock | WIRED
videos.s: WIRED's 5 Levels format with Jacob Collier explaining harmony to a child, a teen, a college student, a professional and Herbie Hancock.
videos.w: Recommended as a gentle explanation of harmony for beginners and cited as the model of the 'explain at five levels' format.
videos.q: If you really know nothing you might enjoy this attempt at explaining harmony at five different levels from a child to Herbie Hancock

videos.t: The most important lesson from 83,000 brain scans | Daniel Amen | TEDxOrangeCoast
videos.s: Psychiatrist Daniel Amen discusses lessons from 83,000 brain scans, arguing that brain activity patterns relate to psychological symptoms and that you can improve your brain.
videos.w: HN cites it in depression and brain health threads for its message that the brain can be improved, and that brain injury is common and overlooked.
videos.q: I think this talk is relevant.

videos.t: Tesla Model 3's motor - The Brilliant Engineering behind it
videos.s: An engineering explainer on why Tesla abandoned the induction motor for the Model 3 and used an IPM-SynRM design. It covers the reluctance torque and permanent magnet principles behind the choice.
videos.w: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of the Model 3 motor and reluctance rotor design.
videos.q: This youtube video describes it rather well, and I'd recommend giving it a watch

videos.t: The man who faked human cloning
videos.s: BobbyBroccoli's first of two long documentaries about Hwang Woo-suk, the South Korean scientist who faked human cloning results. It tells the story of the scandal that shook a country.
videos.w: Recommended as a gripping account of scientific fraud and the history of cloning research.
videos.q: I'd recommend watching this video [1].

videos.t: Why do Biden's votes not follow Benford's Law?
videos.s: Matt Parker examines claims that Biden's 2020 vote counts violate Benford's Law, explaining the law and why it often does not apply to precinct-level election data.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a visual debunking of Benford-based election fraud claims and as a guide to when Benford's Law does and does not apply.
videos.q: Matt Parker did a good video with lots of visuals to explain why Benford's Law works in general, but why it cannot always be simply applied to election results.

videos.t: Don't Make Me Click
videos.s: A Google Tech Talk arguing that the best interface requires the fewest clicks and choices, with Google search, Facebook, the iPod and Firefox as examples. It shows how minimizing interaction makes interfaces easier to learn.
videos.w: HN commenters recommend it as a companion to Steve Krug's usability advice and as a talk on minimal interface design.
videos.q: Read Don't Make Me Think! by Steve Krug. Also watch this talk titled

videos.t: Melt your circuit boards
videos.s: mitxela shows his KiCad plugin that rounds PCB tracks to give circuit boards organic, melted-looking layouts instead of rigid geometric ones.
videos.w: Recommended as a great creative PCB-design video and linked in threads on KiCad and artistic boards.
videos.q: mitxela did a great video on this topic recently and wrote a plugin for kicad to make the regular geometric layouts more organic.
